In Sardinia, the monastery of St Michael of Plajano, with its churches, estates, and other appurtenances; the ecclesiastical office and the benefice of the people of Pisa in the harbour [Col. 0990B] of the towers.

Moreover, embracing your mother church with the arms of fullest affection, we confirm its ancient and reasonable customs: namely, the anointing of the sick; and the tithes of the Pisan parish—of grain and *jussio* [variant: *eladae*, “of all wine”]; and, of all monies, three payments in full, both from the city itself and from the villages, boroughs, and territories which receive baptism from the greater church; and the offerings of the living and the dead which are brought to the greater church. These are never to be taken away from you or your successors by anyone’s cunning or violence, but are to remain whole and secure for the common use and benefit. The same we decree concerning the offerings of the episcopal Mass, which is celebrated in the presence of the canons, excepting gold or its monetary equivalent. [Col. 0990C]

Furthermore, no canon may be introduced or ordained in the greater church unless with the consent of all the canons, or of the greater part of them; and no bishop whatsoever may deprive an ordained canon of office or benefice except by canonical judgment. Nor may anyone presume, apart from the common will of the canons or of their greater part, to ordain or harass the churches which are the property of the chapter of the greater church, or their clergy. No church in the city or boroughs, except the mother church and monasteries—and in monasteries, except for the use of the monks and household—may presume to bless olives or candles, save where this is known to have been granted from most ancient times. [Col. 0991A]

Baptism, however, shall be celebrated in the greater church, as has been observed from ancient times, except in fear of death. On Holy Saturday no one may presume to sing Mass or ring bells until they are rung at the greater church. Nor are public processions to be held except in the greater church. Moreover, by authority of this present privilege we decree that the goods of deceased canons, now and in the future, shall be taken by no one, but shall be left peacefully and entire for the benefit of the brethren living in common.

Further, those accustomed to be buried at the greater church shall not abandon their customary burial places. But those who transfer to burial places of other churches, whether in the city or in the boroughs, shall leave one fourth of their estates to the mother church. [Col. 0991B] In all churches in which you attend the funerary rites of the dead, we grant you the celebration of Masses together with their offerings. To be sure, elections of pious canons and appointments of monks and chaplains—those, namely, who administer divine offices to the people—shall take place with the consent of the bishop and canons.

Moreover, by authority of the apostolic see we decree that the division of the wood of the mound, as it is known to have been made by our venerable brother Villanus, archbishop of Pisa, by mandate of our now Lord predecessor Pope Eugenius, and assigned to us, shall remain valid and unshaken in future times; and no one, having discovered this division, may ever presume to infringe or disturb it on any pretext against you or your successors. [Col. 0991C]

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person rashly to disturb the aforesaid church, or take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole, to be of every benefit for the uses for whose governance and support they were granted, saving in all things the authority of the apostolic see. If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowingly, attempts rashly to act against this page of our constitution, after a second warning, unless he corrects himself by fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his former power; and moreover let him know that he is answerable before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed, and let him be estranged from the most holy [Col. 0991D] body and blood of God and of our Lord Redeemer Jesus Christ, and be subject at the last judgment to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve justice in that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge find the reward of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Anastasius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have signed. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum, have signed. I, Hugh, bishop of Ostia, have signed. I, Gregory, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Callixtus, have signed. I, Guy, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Chrysogonus, have signed. [Col. 0992A] I, Ubaldus, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Praxedes, have signed. I, Jordan, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Susanna, have signed. I, Octavian, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Cecilia, have signed. I, Artaldus, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Prisca, have signed. I, John, priest-cardinal of the title of Equitius, have signed. I, Otto, deacon-cardinal of the title of St. George at the Golden Veil, have signed. I, Hyacinth, deacon-cardinal of the title of SS. Sergius and Bacchus, have signed. I, Otto, deacon-cardinal of the title of St. Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have signed.

[Col. 0992B] Given at the Lateran through the hand of Roland, priest-cardinal of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the sixth day before the Ides of September, in the first indiction, in the year 1153 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Pope Anastasius IV.

## II. He undertakes the protection of the Church of Benevento and confirms the rights of Archbishop Peter.  
*(Lateran, September 22.)*

[UGHELLI, *Italia Sacra*, VIII, 113.]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother PETER, archbishop of Benevento, and to his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

Placed by the disposing [Col. 0992C] Lord upon the lofty watchtower of the universal Church, we are bound, by the office of apostleship entrusted to us by God, to love our brother bishops and to strengthen, by the protection of the apostolic see, the churches committed to their governance. Therefore, venerable brother in Christ Peter, archbishop of Benevento, graciously granting assent to your petitions, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves, and strengthen by the patronage of this present writing, the Church of Benevento over which, by God’s appointment, you are known to preside. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by God’s favor, acquire through grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names. [Col. 0992D]

Namely, the bishoprics of Avellino, Monte Marano, Frequentinum, Ariano, Monte di Vico, Bovino, Ascoli, Lucera, Florentinum, Tortibulum, Montecorvino, Vulturaria, Civitate, Dragonara, Larino, Termoli, Guardina, Trivento, Boiano, Alife, Telese, and Sant’Agata.

Within the city of Benevento: the church of St. Peter Paccadosso; the church of St. Thecla; the church of St. Martin; the church of St. Mary *ante horam*; the church of St. Peter situated beside the church of St. Peter of the Medici; the church of St. Mary of Ancona; the church of St. Arthelaus; the church of St. Januarius [Col. 0993A] of the Greeks; the church of St. Maurus; the church of St. Paschasius; and the church of St. Angelo, which is beside the church of St. Mary Rotunda.

Outside the city: the church of St. John of the Plain; the church of St. Mary of the Rock; the church of St. Mary of Venticano; the church of St. Peter of Cardito; the church of St. Peter in Planisio; the church of St. Theodore; and the church of St. Mary in Gildone. The abbey of St. Mary in Strata; the abbey of St. Mary of Corate; the church of St. Mary in Gradelli; and whatever right you have in the castle of Monte Sarculo and in the Caudine Valley.

Moreover, we grant you the use of the pallium, according to custom, for performing the solemnities of Mass: that is, you may use it only within the church on the following days: at the Nativity of the Lord, Epiphany, [Col. 0993B] the Purification of Holy and Ever-Virgin Mary, and her Annunciation; the Lord’s Supper; the Easter feasts; the Ascension of the Lord; Pentecost; the feast of St. John the Baptist; the feasts of the Apostles Peter and Paul; and the Assumption and Nativity of blessed Mary, ever Virgin and Mother. You may also use it at the dedication of your archbishopric; on the anniversary of your consecration; at gatherings of bishops; at ordinations of clergy and consecrations of churches; and, further, at the translation of the body of blessed Bartholomew, when your Fraternity is to put it on in the secretarium and then proceed to the solemnities of Mass.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb that church, [Col. 0993C] take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with arbitrary exactions; but that all things shall be preserved whole, to be of every benefit for the uses for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the apostolic see. If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, etc.

I, Anastasius, bishop of the Lateran Church. I, Hugh, bishop of Ostia. I, Guarinus, bishop of the Church of Palestrina. [lacuna] I, James, cardinal of St. Callixtus. I, [lacuna], priest-cardinal. [Col. 0993D] I, Ubaldus, priest-cardinal of St. Praxedes. I, Julius, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Marcellus. I, Octavian, priest-cardinal of St. Cecilia. I, Astaldus, priest-cardinal of the title of Prisca. I, John, priest-cardinal of SS. John and Paul. I, Cencius, priest-cardinal of St. Lawrence in Lucina. I, Henry, priest-cardinal of SS. Nereus and Achilleus. I, [lacuna], deacon-cardinal of St. George. I, Hyacinth, deacon-cardinal of St. Mary in Cosmedin. I, John, deacon-cardinal of SS. Sergius and Bacchus. [lacuna]

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Roland, priest-cardinal of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the Kalends of October, in the first indiction, [Col. 0994A] in the year 1153 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Anastasius IV.

## III. Privilege for the monastery of St. Antimo.  
*(Rome, at St. Mary Rotunda, October 31.)*

[UGHELLI, *Italia Sacra*, I, 993.]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son GUIDO, abbot of the monastery of St. Antimo, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

Although, by the office of apostleship entrusted to us by God, we stand in obligation to all churches and ecclesiastical persons, we ought nevertheless to give more earnest attention to those known from ancient foundation to pertain to the right and property of blessed Peter. [Col. 0994B] Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, graciously granting your just petitions and following in the footsteps of our predecessor, Pope Innocent of happy memory, we strengthen by the privilege of the apostolic see and the page of this present writing the monastery of blessed Antimo, over which, by God’s appointment, you are known to preside. We decree that whatever goods and possessions this monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by the grant of popes, the gifts of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, acquire through the Lord’s providence, shall be preserved firm and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Moreover, that you may more freely devote yourselves to divine service according to the rule of your profession, we likewise decree that no priest of any church, except the Roman pontiff alone, may claim any jurisdiction, power, or authority in your monastery. Indeed, unless invited by the abbot of that monastery, he may not even dare to celebrate the solemnities of Mass there. [Col. 0994C] We also forbid any bishop to have leave to constrain or excommunicate the priests—monks or canons—of the same monastery, or to forbid them the divine office. We decree likewise that they shall remain free and absolved from every episcopal synod.

Furthermore, we wish that the place itself be free from every yoke of any powers—bishops, marquises, counts, viscounts, *castaldiones*, and all other Lombards—and that none of them may presume, upon any pretext, to hold any court or assembly, or to exercise coercive jurisdiction, in possessions belonging to the aforesaid monastery. Rather, both these things and all others known to pertain to the right of the same monastery shall remain under the free power and disposition of you and your successors. [Col. 0994D]

We further grant to that venerable place tithes and first-fruits from all its own holdings, whether held by mandate or otherwise, which have already been acquired by the monastery or are hereafter, by God’s favor, to be acquired. Upon your death, therefore—you who are now abbot of the same place—or upon the death of any of your successors, no one may be set over it by any crafty deception or violence, except one whom [Col. 0995A] the brothers by common consent, or the sounder part of the brothers, foresee should be elected according to the fear of God and the aid of blessed Benedict. The elected man, moreover, shall be consecrated by the Roman pontiff.

As for chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and ordinations of priests, deacons, or others, whether monks or canons, who are to be advanced to sacred orders: you shall receive these either from the apostolic see or from any Catholic bishop who is vested with authority and grants what is requested. And if at any time you wish to invite to your monastery one of our bishops or some other person, as may seem more fitting to us, to celebrate the sacred ministry or perform a consecration, [Col. 0995B] you shall have full power to do so without anyone’s opposition. In addition, we decree that, if necessity requires, baptism shall be celebrated in the parish church of St. Saviour, in the parish church of St. John, and likewise in the other churches belonging to your monastery, as is known to have been established by the enactments of our predecessors John XV, John XIII, Benedict, Stephen VII, Sergius, Adrian, and other Roman pontiffs.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb your monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any molestations; but that all things [Col. 0995C] shall be preserved whole, to be of benefit for the uses for whose support and governance they were granted.

If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person, etc.

Given at Rome, at St. Mary Rotunda, through the hand of Roland, priest-cardinal of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the second day before the Kalends of November, in the year 1153 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Anastasius IV.

## IV. He confirms to the monastery of Monte Cassino the church of St. Julian in the territory of Faresenonis and the church of St. Caesarius of Anagni.  
*(Rome, at St. Mary Rotunda, October 31.)*

[GATTULA, *Historia Casinensis*, 337.]

[Col. 0995D] ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son RAINALD, priest-cardinal of the Holy Roman Church and abbot of Monte Cassino, and to his brethren: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Among all the churches of the world, the monastery of Monte Cassino has always adhered to the apostolic see as a special member; and, as it was near it in locality, so it has zealously endeavoured to render it devoted services. Hence those who before us, through the bounty of the divine gift, held the chair of blessed Peter, loved that monastery with sincere affection and constantly sought to enlarge it with temporal and spiritual benefits. They showed themselves so solicitous for its advancement that through their zeal and action it continually received new increases, [Col. 0996A] and firmly retained what it had received.

We likewise, imitating their footsteps out of reverence for blessed Benedict and his church, confirm by apostolic authority to your monastery the church of St. Julian situated in the territory of Fresonensis with its appurtenances, which our venerable brother Leo, bishop of Veroli, granted to you; and the church of St. Caesarius situated in the suburb of Anagni above the place called Claranum, which our brother Eleutherius, bishop of Anagni, granted to you through our intercession; together with as much land at Pulliano as will suffice each year for two yokes of oxen to plough.

Therefore no person whatsoever may lawfully infringe this page of our confirmation and grant by rash boldness, or oppose it by any presumption. [Col. 0996B] If anyone presumes to attempt this, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his offence by suitable satisfaction, let him incur the indignation of almighty God and of his apostles blessed Peter and Paul, and at the last judgment be subject to severe vengeance.

Given at Rome, at St. Mary Rotunda, on the second day before the Kalends of November.

## V. Privilege for the Milanese church of St. Thecla.  
*(Lateran, November 13.)*

[GIULINI, *Memorie di Milano*, V, 602.]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons AZO, provost of the church of St. Thecla at Milan, and his brethren both present [Col. 0996C] and future, canonically appointed in perpetuity.

The rigor of equity and the order of present reason require that just petitioners be granted their request, when piety supports the will of those who ask and truth does not oppose it. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, graciously granting your just petitions and following in the footsteps of our predecessor Pope Eugenius of happy memory, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves, and strengthen by the patronage of this present writing, the aforesaid Church in which you are devoted to divine service. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, through the grant of popes, the gifts [Col. 0996D] of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, by the Lord’s favor, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names.

The cemetery of that church, with the houses and buildings which have been built for the benefit and service of that church and of the brethren there, or which will hereafter be reasonably built by you or your successors, just as you have hitherto reasonably and peacefully held and possessed them. Moreover, by apostolic authority we confirm to you the reasonable custom in that church of singing, reading, preaching, and performing the office for the faithful departed—namely at vigils, lauds, and vespers; [Col. 0997A] and we wholly forbid anyone there to alter this or introduce anything new. We likewise grant that burial at that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated. We therefore decree, etc.

In the monogram: “Fare well.”

In the circle:

“KEEP ME, O LORD, AS THE APPLE OF THE EYE.”

I, Anastasius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Otto, deacon-cardinal of St. Gregory at the Golden Veil, have signed. I, Guy, deacon-cardinal of St. Mary in Portico, have signed. [Col. 0997B] I, Hyacinth, deacon-cardinal of St. Mary in Cosmedin, have signed. I, Gerard, deacon-cardinal of St. Mary in Via Lata, have signed. I, Odo, deacon-cardinal of St. Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have signed. I, Gregory, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Callixtus, have signed. I, Cencius, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Lawrence in Lucina, have signed. I, Henry, priest-cardinal of the title of SS. Nereus and Achilleus, have signed.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Roland, priest-cardinal of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, [Col. 0997C] on the Ides of November, in the second indiction, in the year 1153 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Anastasius IV.

(A yellow cord appears; the seal is missing.)

## VI. Privilege for the monastery of Vallombrosa.  
*(Lateran, November 22.)*

[LAMI, *Ecclesiae Florentinae Monumenta*, I, 544.]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son AMBROSE, abbot of Vallombrosa, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

The authority of the apostolic see, which by the Lord’s bounty we serve, and the unity of brotherhood urge us to consent to the just wishes of religious persons and graciously to grant their reasonable petitions. Accordingly, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Ambrose, in consideration of charity, granting your reasonable petitions, we receive under the guardianship and protection of the apostolic see the monastery of Vallombrosa, over which, by God’s appointment, you preside, together with all monasteries subject to it; and we strengthen it by the page of this writing. We decree that every immunity and liberty granted to the aforesaid monastery by our predecessors of happy memory—Victor, Gregory VII, Urban, Paschal, and Innocent, Roman pontiffs—shall remain firm, whole, and unimpaired in perpetuity for you, your successors, and the Vallombrosan congregation.

[Col. 0998A] We further add that whatever possessions and goods the aforesaid monastery now justly and lawfully possesses, or may hereafter reasonably acquire, by the grant of popes, gifts of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s favor, shall be preserved peaceful and entire for you. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The monastery of St. Salvi; the monastery of the Holy Trinity of Florence; the monastery of Struma; the monastery of Usella and of St. James of Castello; the monastery of Passignano, and of St. Michael of Siena, and of Alpiano; the monastery of Coltibuono and of Monte Pisano; the monastery of Monte Scalario and of Nerano; the monastery of Ficiclo and of Capiano; [Col. 0998B] the Pisan monastery of St. Paul; the monastery of Plaiano and of St. Venereus in Sardinia; the monastery of St. Angelo of Pistoia, of Pacciano, and of St. Mary of Prato; the monastery of Vaiano, of Opleto, and of Montepiano; the monastery of Fonte Taona; the monastery of Musceto, of Monte Armato, and of St. Cecilia; the monastery of St. Reparata, of Trecento, of Crespino, of Razolo, of Rivo Cesare, of Cuneo, of Turri, and of Caprilia; the monasteries of Piacenza, Pavia, and Cremona; the monastery of Capanna and of St. Prosper; the monasteries of Novara, Vercelli, Genoa, Tortona, and Turin; the monasteries of Brescia and Verona, and of St. Vigilius; and the monasteries of Bergamo and Milan, of St. Carpophorus, and of Asti.

[Col. 0998C] Indeed, no person whatsoever may rashly dare to seize converts or monks of the aforesaid monastery or of the whole congregation, retain them when seized, or harass them with any burdens. We decree that you may hold and possess, free from opposition by bishops, episcopal officials, or parish priests, the tithes of your produce which you gather anywhere by your own expense and labor, to be rendered to your hospice. You may also receive, without anyone’s prohibition, clerics fleeing the secular life or laypersons for conversion; and may receive, without prejudice to other churches, the offerings of both those who vow to be buried in your cemetery and all other faithful persons.

[Col. 0998D] We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb that monastery, take away or diminish its subject churches or possessions, or harass them with arbitrary vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole, to be of every benefit for the uses for whose support they were granted. If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, etc.

I, Anastasius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have signed. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum, have signed. I, Manfred, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Sabina. [Col. 0999A] I, Aribert, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Anastasia. I, John, priest-cardinal of SS. John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius, have signed. I, Otto, deacon-cardinal of St. George at the Golden Veil. I, Guy, deacon of St. Mary in Portico, have signed. I, Hyacinth, deacon-cardinal of St. Mary in Cosmedin. I, Gerard, deacon-cardinal of St. Mary in Via Lata. I, Odo, deacon-cardinal of St. Nicholas in the Prison, have signed.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Roland, priest-cardinal [Col. 0999B] of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the tenth day before the Kalends of December, in the second indiction, in the year 1153 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Anastasius IV.

## VII. At the request of Bishop Guido, he confirms the boundaries of the Abruzzo bishopric and the Church’s possessions.  
*(Lateran, November 27.)*

[UGHELLI, *Italia Sacra*, I, 357.]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother GUIDO, bishop of the Church of Abruzzo, and to his successors canonically appointed.

Just as no effect should be granted to those asking for what is unjust, so the petition of those desiring what is lawful ought not be delayed. Therefore, beloved brother in Christ and bishop, granting your prayers, we decree by the firmness of this present decree, for the perpetual peace and dignity of the Holy Church of Abruzzo, that all the boundaries of the parish—as they have been possessed by your predecessors until this day—shall be preserved entirely in perpetuity for you and your successors. [Col. 0999C]

These boundaries are seen to run from the head of the Vomano, along the very summit of the mountain, as far as the stream flowing between the county of Ascoli and Abruzzo; through Carrufo as far as beyond the river Tronto; to the boundary there established and thence to the sea; and along the sea as far as the river Vomano. Within these boundaries, whatever towns, villages, parish churches, and churches are situated, or shall in future be situated, shall remain under the episcopal care and administration of you and your Catholic successors. From all of them episcopal dues shall be paid to you, both at the ordination of clergy and consecration of churches, and in the receipt of tithes and offerings, as well as in the correction of offenders.

We now prohibit the wrongful presumption of monks which has grown up within the Abruzzese boundaries—partly because of bishops’ absence and partly because of their obstinacy—so that henceforth they may neither perform baptism in monasteries, dare to leave their cloisters for anointings of the sick, admit lay persons for the imposition of penance, receive into communion persons excommunicated by the bishop, [Col. 1000A] nor receive persons under interdict for sacred offices.

Furthermore, we decree that the church of Blessed Mary shall always be regarded as the mother church, as it has hitherto been regarded, and that the episcopal see shall remain there. We confirm to you and your successors whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by God’s favor, acquire through grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, to remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The abbey of St. Benedict at Carrula; the abbey of St. Mary at Cataneto; the abbey of St. John at Pesula; the abbey of St. John at Scorcione; the church of St. [Col. 1000B] Flavian, with Castro, Portus, and all its appurtenances; the chapter of St. Sylvester at Salino; the parish churches of St. Mary in Vico, St. Mary in Vellete, St. Peter in Romano, St. Peter in Abrelio, St. Victorinus in Canali, St. Mary in Brazzano, St. Saviour in Pagliarolo, St. Lawrence in Festiniano, St. Martin in Junipero, St. Mary in Predi, St. Paul in Ablata, and St. Lawrence in Civitella; the monastery of St. Sebastian at Gomano; the city of Interamne, with Vitica Carticula; the suburb of St. Flavian, with the island; Montone; the riverbank of Tortoreto and Lauro; half of Pretuli Lavaroni; Neretum; Turanum; Gusbert’s share at Oforiano; the land of the sons of Montacellus, Walter, and Rayner; Lucum; Colle Vetulum; Rapinum; Mianum; the lands of the sons of Albertion; [Col. 1000C] Forcella; Caprafico; the land of the canon of Guictariis, namely the hill of Cantalupo; half of Germaniano; Bizino’s share; the little town of Colonia; a share of Gazino; and of the whole land of St. Nicholas.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid Church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, claim for his own use things granted unjustly, diminish them, or harass it with arbitrary vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole, to be of benefit for the uses both of it and of its clergy and poor, saving in all things the authority of the apostolic see. If, therefore, in future an archbishop, bishop, emperor, king, prince, duke, count, viscount, judge, *castaldio*, or ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts rashly to act against this page [Col. 1000D] of our constitution, etc. Amen.

I, Anastasius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Gregory, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Callixtus. I, Manfred, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Sabina. I, Albert, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Anastasia. I, Octavian, priest-cardinal of St. Cecilia. I, John, priest-cardinal of the title of SS. John and Paul of Pammachius. I, Cencius, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Lawrence in Lucina. I, Odo, deacon-cardinal of the title of St. George at the Golden Veil. [Col. 1001A] I, Guy, deacon-cardinal of the title of St. Mary in Portico. I, John, deacon-cardinal of the title of SS. Sergius and Bacchus.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Roland, priest-cardinal of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the fifth day before the Kalends of December, in the second indiction, in the year 1153 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Anastasius IV.

## VIII. He confirms the rights and privileges of the monastery of St. Lawrence in Campo and of its abbot Albert.  
*(Lateran, November 27.)*

[MURATORI, *Antiquitates Italicae*, V, 487.]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son ALBERT, abbot of the monastery of St. [Col. 1001B] Lawrence in Campo, situated in the diocese of Fano, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity. [Lacuna] ought to embrace with zealous affection, so that both the sincerity of devotion may be worthily made known and that what utility requires may undoubtedly acquire force.

Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Albert, we graciously admit your petitions. Following also in the footsteps of our predecessors John, Alexander, Paschal, and Innocent, Roman pontiffs, we decree that the monastery of blessed Lawrence called “in Campo” shall remain, with the Lord’s help, [under the Holy Roman Church; the syntax is defective in the source]. We decree that whatever goods and possessions it is known now justly and canonically to possess, and all things which hereafter may be offered to that monastery, with the Lord’s help, through episcopal grant, royal or princely gift, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. [Col. 1001C] Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names.

The monastery of St. Angelo of Monte, with its churches and all things pertaining to it; the monastery of St. Paternianus of Mampullo, with its appurtenances; the monastery of St. Michael of the sons of Alfedo; the church of St. John of Montecalvo; the church of Mauriana in Lucioli, with the estate of Paleano; St. Cecilia, with the estate of Ferbula; St. Stephen, with the estate of Fenilio; the monastery of St. Hippolytus [Col. 1001D] with its cells, namely St. Sabinus with its estate at Pratalia, St. Mauritius, St. Michael, and St. Damian; the cell of St. Stephen; the church of St. Gerontius; the estate of Vallelunga with its appurtenances; the monastery of St. Adrian, with the castle of Gajo itself and the island of Arvosiccho as far as the river Metauro; the cell of St. Martin at Britholi; St. John Major, situated at Fano; St. Gregory; SS. Philip and James of Cavallaria; the estate called Canna Domestica; the estate called Gurgo Fusco; the church of St. Mary at Crutide; St. Paternianus; the estate of Numero; the estate of Urciano; Massa Barthi with its appurtenances; the estate of St. Peter at Vettelago; the estate of Roverate with the church of St. John; [Col. 1002A] the greater and lesser *antudina* [meaning uncertain]; the estate of St. Peter of Bolagaria; the castle of Cerquacupa with its appurtenances; the church of St. Severus; St. Donatus, with the estate of Ortaria; the estate of Montecalvo with its appurtenances; and the monastery of St. Lawrence situated at Urbitalia, with its appurtenances, estates, and castles.

It is therefore decreed that no person whatsoever may lawfully rashly disturb that church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, sell off things unjustly given for his own use, diminish them, or harass it with arbitrary vexations. All these things shall be preserved whole, to be of every benefit for the uses for whose support and governance they were granted. If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular [Col. 1002B] person—

I, Anastasius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have signed. I, Gregory, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Callixtus, have signed. I, Aribert, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Anastasia, have signed. I, Julius, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Marcellus, have signed. I, Ubaldus, priest-cardinal of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have signed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Roland, priest-cardinal of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the fifth day before the Kalends of December, in the second indiction, in the year 1153 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Anastasius [Col. 1002C] IV.

## IX. At the request of Bishop Blancone, he undertakes the protection of the Church of Treviso and confirms its goods.  
*(Fragment.)*

[UGHELLI, *Italia Sacra*, V, 523.]

Dated at the Lateran, through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the Kalends of December, in the second indiction, in the year 1153 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Pope Anastasius IV.

## X. Privilege for the monastery of St. Denis. (Lateran, 6 December.)

[DOUBLET, *History of Saint-Denis*, 498.]

[Col. 1002D] ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the monks of Saint Michael: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our beloved son Odo, abbot of Saint-Denis, and your abbot, appeared before us concerning the payment of five marks which you had raised against the monastery of Saint-Denis, not so much on grounds of right as by your own choice. Both having been granted a hearing, each set forth his reasons before our tribunal. Having heard and considered the arguments of both parties with our brethren, we decree that this payment is owed by you to the aforesaid abbot and to the monastery entrusted to him; and we have commanded your abbot to restore in full whatever has hitherto been withheld from it by you. We therefore enjoin upon you by these present letters that, together with him, you take care to restore to the aforesaid abbot whatever you have withheld up to this time from the said payment, and that henceforth you pay it to him without objection, as it is known to have been established of old between your monasteries. But if, within forty days after your abbot has returned to you, the said payment has not been paid by you in full to the aforesaid abbot, you shall know that thereafter you are suspended from your offices by our authority, and that the celebration of divine offices is interdicted in your monastery.

Dated at the Lateran, on the eighth day before the Ides of December.

## XI. To Peter, Archbishop of Bourges.—That he restore to the abbot of Saint-Denis the church of Casa Maior and the property of the deceased archpriest, as Pope Eugenius had admonished him once and again. (Lateran, 7 December.)

[D. BOUQUET, *Recueil*, XV, 655.]

[Col. 1003B]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother PETER, Archbishop of Bourges: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We believe that the office of the pontificate you have undertaken has bound you so closely to obedience to the Apostolic See that it ought to seem shameful and dishonourable to you to await a second or third command of the Roman pontiff concerning the same matter. Our beloved son Odo, abbot of the venerable monastery of Saint-Denis, appearing before us, represented to our hearing that, when he had formerly resolved to approach the Apostolic See, you took from him the church of Casa Maior after he had set out on the journey; and that, when the archpriest of that church—who, when he assumed its pastoral care, is said to have bestowed upon that same church everything which he should acquire there in the course of time—had entered upon the way of all flesh, you appropriated all his goods to your own uses. And although Pope Eugenius, our predecessor of happy memory, as has been said, twice sent you written commands rebuking this act, you have hitherto taken no care to give effect to his commands.

We are the more astonished at this because you see yourself to have strayed further from the path of justice. Therefore, laying aside all agitation, you ought to have thought more vigilantly of correcting the matter. But because it is necessary for us at least by apostolic power to bend this hardness toward what is right, we command you by the authority of these present letters that, if his complaint does not depart from the order of truth, you restore to the oft-mentioned abbot, with fitting amends and satisfaction, both the church and whatever from the goods of the aforesaid priest, acquired in the service of that church, has come into your hands; and that you cause what has been taken away to be restored to him in full. Take diligent care that he is not compelled further to lodge a complaint concerning these matters in our ears, nor we required again to send you our letters. Otherwise, you shall know that we shall consider how to soften this hardness in such a manner that you will always be found more ready to carry out what is enjoined upon you by the Roman pontiff.

For you should know with what love and diligence our predecessors protected the possessions of Blessed Denis, knowing that he—Blessed Denis, I say—is able not only to confer many benefits upon them, but also to bestow much greater ones. Therefore, do not delay, for the love of God and of so great a martyr, and for the salvation of your soul, to fulfil what they devoutly performed; and do not cease to restore to us what belongs to our right. Let no person whatsoever therefore presume rashly to disturb this page of our decree or, by reckless daring, to oppose it. But if anyone should attempt this, let him know that he will incur the wrath of God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Dated at the Lateran, on the seventh day before the Ides of December.

## XII. Privilege for the monastery of Saint-Denis. (Lateran, 8 December.)

[DOUBLET, *History of Saint-Denis*, 497.]

[Col. 1004B]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ODO, abbot of Saint-Denis, and his brethren: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Whenever we are asked to confirm for any church those things which it possesses justly and reasonably, it is fitting that we grant it with willing mind and give suitable assent to the petitioners’ desires, lest, if we should perhaps deny it our protection in safeguarding its possessions, we might seem to afford the audacity of wicked men an opportunity to plunder ecclesiastical goods—an audacity which our office rather admonishes us to resist.

Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, wishing to provide for your peace and advantage, by apostolic authority we confirm to you the *personatus* of Villiacum, the church of Calvomons, and the church of Cergiacum, belonging to the right of your monastery. Moreover, we confirm to your church of Corbolium a certain tithe at Chamoila, which our venerable brother Hugh, Archbishop of Sens, granted to it by a reasonable arrangement. We likewise confirm to your church of Vallis Cressonis the tithe of that village itself, and decree that it shall remain unimpaired to it for all time.

Let no person whatsoever therefore presume to infringe this page of our confirmation or, by reckless daring, to oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Dated at the Lateran, 6 December.

## XIII. He confirms ancient privileges to Pacificus, abbot of Saint Genesius at Brixellum. (Lateran, 9 December.)

[MURATORI, *Antiquities of Italy*, V, 1021.]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son PACIFICUS, abbot of the monastery of Brixellum, and to his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

[Col. 1005A] Although by the authority and goodwill of the Apostolic See we stand indebted to all religious places and persons, it is especially fitting that we provide for those which it is beyond doubt belong to the right of Blessed Peter. Indeed, the necessity laid upon us to watch with paternal care over the monastery of Saint Genesius at Brixellum, over which, beloved son Pacificus, by God’s appointment you are known to preside, is all the greater because that place is known to pertain to the right and property of the Holy Roman Church.

Following the example of our predecessors of happy memory, Paschal and Innocent, Roman pontiffs, we receive the same monastery under the protection of Blessed Peter; preserving its former liberty both for itself and for its settlers, we fortify it by the privilege of the Apostolic See. We decree that no priest may exercise any authority whatsoever in that monastery or the adjoining village, and that none of them may have power to subject that place, its monks, or its clerics to interdict or excommunication. You may receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of churches or altars, and the ordinations of monks or clerics who are to be promoted to sacred orders in those places, from whichever Catholic bishop you prefer.

But upon the death of you, now abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed over it by any craft of intrigue or violence, except the person whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall provide to be elected, from their own community or, if necessary, from another, according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict. The person elected shall then come to the Roman pontiff to be consecrated.

Furthermore, by this present decree we establish that whatever estates, possessions, or goods were bestowed, from their own lawful property, upon the right of the same monastery by Count or Margrave Atto, of noble memory, its founder; or by his son Tedald, or his grandson Boniface, margraves; and by Mathilda, countess, daughter of Boniface, the singular daughter of the Apostolic See; or by other faithful persons; and whatever it now possesses justly and lawfully, or may hereafter acquire, by grant of pontiffs, offering of the faithful, generosity of kings or princes, or by other just means, the Lord granting it, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names.

[Col. 1005D] The church of Blessed Michael at Ferraria; the church of Saint Christopher at Ponticellum; the church of Saint Michael at Maximatica; the church of Saint Mary at Gurzaneticum; the church of Saint Philip at Bibianum; the church of Saint Mary at Caldo; the church of Saint George with its estate; the church of Saint Mary at Gurgo; the church of Saint Fabian with its estate; half the estate of Gavasetum, with the chapel of Saint Peter within the castle; the estate of Saint Martin with its chapel; the hospital of Saint Lawrence at Calerno; also your rights in the port of Brixellum, the German road, the toll, and the customary due which is usually received from it; whatever you possess at Gonzaga, Piconiaca, Castel Nuovo, Butrion, Herbera, Bletulum, Sacca, the head of the Incia, and Beruptum; the estate called Mercorina and half the estate of Pellanum, with the church of Saint Andrew; the *stedia* adjoining the castles of Godi, with the church of Saint Mary at Caldone; and Rivalta, with its port on the river Mincio; likewise Oliveta in the county of Brescia or Verona.

[Col. 1006A] Certainly, no one whatsoever shall presume to exact tithes from you upon the produce which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or upon the fodder of your animals. If any free and independent person, in life or at death, should wish to give himself to your monastery for the redemption of his soul, you shall have free power to receive him, saving the right of the mother church.

Let no person whatsoever therefore presume rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations. Rather, let all things be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted—saving, in the aforesaid churches, the canonical right of the diocesan bishop.

As a token of the liberty received from the Roman Church, you shall annually pay to us and to our successors one gold Byzantine coin, as was established in the charter of offering of the aforesaid Countess Mathilda, so that, in accordance with her devotion, the brethren of the monastery of Brixellum may be secure from every molestation of secular service and free from every burden of worldly oppression, being subject on no grounds to anyone other than the Roman and Apostolic See, to whose right that place belongs. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, etc.

I, Anastasius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.  
I, Imarus, Bishop of Tusculum, have subscribed.  
I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Callixtus, have subscribed.  
I, Manfred, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina, have subscribed.  
I, Aribert, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia, have subscribed.  
I, Julian, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus, have subscribed.  
[Col. 1006D] I, Octavian, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia, have subscribed.  
I, Altaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Prisca, have subscribed.  
I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.  
I, Jacynthus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin, have subscribed.

Dated at the Lateran, through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Ides of December, in the second indiction, in the year 1153 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Pope Anastasius IV.

## XIV. Bull for the Church of Maguelone. (Lateran, 10 December.)

[*Gallia Christiana*, VI, Documents, 357.]

[Col. 1007A]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother RAYMOND, Bishop of Maguelone, and to his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Placed, by the Lord’s ordering, upon the lofty watchtower of the Apostolic See, we are bound by the office entrusted to us to love our brother bishops, whether near at hand or far away, and to preserve their due rights to the churches committed to them by God. Therefore, beloved brother bishop in Christ, graciously assenting to your just petitions, we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid Church of Maguelone, over which by God’s appointment you are known to preside, following the example of our predecessor Urban II of good memory; and we fortify it by the protection of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and goods it now possesses justly and canonically, or may hereafter acquire, God favouring it, by grant of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and, through you, for that Church. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names.

[Col. 1007B] We confirm to you and your successors the Church of Maguelone itself, to be canonically governed and administered; the church of Saint Baudilus of Montesevo; and everything known justly to belong to the Bishop of Maguelone or to the common fund of the brethren living there. Moreover, following in the footsteps of the same predecessor of ours, we entrust to you the administration of the county of Melgueil: you shall exact the annual payment from those who hold it from the hand of the Roman pontiff; and if the succession of the counts and heirs of that county should fail, you shall govern and administer that county on behalf of us and our successors. We decree, therefore, etc.

Dated at the Lateran, through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Ides of December, in the second indiction, in the year 1153 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Pope Anastasius IV.

## XV. Privilege for the Church of Saint Victor of Marseille. (Lateran, 20 December.)

[*The Antiquity of the Church of Marseille*, I, 471.]

[Col. 1007D]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brethren R. [RAYMOND], Archbishop of Arles; P. [PONCE], Archbishop of Aix; and G. [WILLIAM], Archbishop of Embrun; and to the other bishops established throughout the province, etc.

(The pope’s decision is expressed in these terms:) Therefore, we request and command your brotherhood that you leave undisturbed to the same monastery, even henceforth, all possessions which it is known to have held peacefully for forty years or more; and also the tithes which, after the lapse of that same period, it is shown to have held peacefully at the episcopal see of Cereste, [Col. 1008A] Almis, Nantis, or other places established throughout the province, etc.

## XVI. To Andrew, Archbishop; Count P.; and the clergy and people of Ragusa. (Lateran, 25 December.)

[FARLATI, *Illyrian Ecclesiastical History*, VI, p. 65.]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother A., archbishop, and his beloved sons P., count, and the whole clergy and people of the Ragusans: greeting and apostolic blessing.

“He here commends them for the honour shown to Henry, subdeacon of the Holy Roman Church and papal legate, and for the obedience rendered to his commands and to the precepts conveyed in the pope’s name; then [Col. 1008B] he adds:”

And because it would be lengthy to commit to the present writing everything which must be said to you, you shall know that we hold ratified the sentence of deposition and interdict pronounced by his authority against certain of our brother bishops, because, though summoned, they scorned to come to his council: deposition against the Bishop of Tristina [Drivasto] and of Dulcigno; and interdict against the Bishop of Cattaro. We also ratify the sentence of excommunication which he promulgated against the Count of Cattaro, and command that it be observed by your whole community until he permits your Church to obey its bishop as it ought. Furthermore, concerning devotion, etc.

Dated at the Lateran, on the eighth day before the Kalends of January, etc.

## XVII. To the bishops of Gaul.—Against the Count of Nevers and the townsmen of Vézelay. (Lateran, 25 December.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 777.]

[Col. 1008C]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, to the bishops of Gaul.

When, at the devil’s instigation, some commit sins in which it is blameworthy to relax punishment, correction should be imposed upon them so severely that they themselves, taught by the penalty, may recognize how grave was what they perpetrated, and that fear of ecclesiastical correction may restrain others from like presumptions. Hence our predecessor Pope Eugenius of blessed memory commanded you, brother Bishop of Langres, by apostolic letters, strictly to warn the Count of Nevers to repent of the monstrous tyranny which he had exercised with barbarous ferocity against the monastery of Vézelay, which indeed belongs to the right of Blessed Peter. If he refused to desist from such wickedness, you were to pronounce a sentence of excommunication against him and the burgesses of Vézelay, and a sentence of interdict in the lands of the count himself.

But, as we have heard, for certain reasons that command—which greatly astonishes us—has not yet been carried out in full. Therefore we, who by the ordering of divine clemency have succeeded him in the office of the apostolate, are bound to defend the aforesaid monastery as the special patrimony of Blessed Peter. Following in the footsteps of our said predecessor, we have given our venerable brother Peter, Archbishop of Bourges, the command that, unless the aforesaid count, warned by him, fully makes good the damage he has inflicted on the monastery and leaves that place in peace and its liberty, he shall subject both the count himself and the burgesses of Vézelay, who are perpetrators of such wickedness, to excommunication by our authority; and throughout all his land, apart from baptism of infants and penances for the dying, he shall prohibit the celebration of all divine offices.

By the authority of these present letters we command you, therefore, firmly to observe that sentence after it has been announced to you by that same brother, and to cause it to be inviolably observed throughout your dioceses.

[Col. 1009B] Dated at the Lateran, on the eighth day before the Kalends of January.

## XVIII. To Ponce, Abbot of Vézelay.—On the same matter. (Lateran, 25 December.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 777.]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, to Ponce, Abbot of Vézelay.

We sympathize with your devotion in paternal affection concerning the affliction, persecution, and distress which you suffer for the church entrusted to you and for justice; and in the matters in which we can act according to God, we wish to furnish you welcome assistance. Therefore, in accordance with your wish and petition, we have taken care to send our letters both to the archbishops and bishops of the kingdom of the Franks, and to the king, counts, and barons, as your devotion requested. From copies you will be able clearly to ascertain their contents.

If therefore, beloved son in Christ, you endure tribulations for the house of Israel, you ought to hope that the Lord will give help out of tribulation and, to those trusting in His mercy, will bring deliverance from every affliction and lead them by His grace to the harbour of peace. Act, therefore, son, and do not be slow, as hitherto so henceforth, to set yourself as a most secure wall in defence of your church. Indeed, strive courageously to fight against those who have wholly renounced faith and whom we have also commanded to be bound by the bond of excommunication. Until they have been excommunicated, if they should perhaps wish to summon you before a court concerning any matter, do not answer them at all without consulting us.

We further command you and prohibit you by apostolic authority from daring to make any grant, except by our command, to the Count of Nevers in our church of Vézelay, which is known to be the freehold of Blessed Peter.

Dated at the Lateran, on the eighth day before the Kalends of January.

## XIX. To Odo, Duke of Burgundy, that the excommunicated townsmen of Vézelay be treated as excommunicate. (Lateran, December?)

[DU CHESNE, *Genealogical History of the Dukes of Burgundy*, Proofs, p. 40.]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the noblemen ODO, Duke of Burgundy; [Col. 1010A] H., count; A. of Bourbon; WILLIAM, Count of Chalon; RAYMOND, brother of the duke; R., Count of Joigny; G. of Donzy; R. of Rubeomont; D. of Luzy; A. of Montréal; S., Viscount of Sens, and his sons G. and B.; G., Viscount of Châtillon; G. of Vergy; O. of Til; and HUGH of Mont-Saint-Jean: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We believe that it has long since come to your knowledge that, because of the monstrous cruelty and barbarous tyranny which the perjured and treacherous burgesses of Vézelay exercised, and still do not cease to exercise, against their lord, our beloved son Ponce, Abbot of Vézelay, and against the monastery itself, they have been cut off from the body of Christ, which is the Church, as limbs infected with decay, by the sword of the divine word at the command of Pope Eugenius of holy memory.

They make light of this, and, as though they believed themselves able to prevail against the Lord by deceitful power, they persist obstinately in their wickedness, though not with impunity; perhaps thinking that the protection of the Apostolic See will at some point be withdrawn from that church. We, therefore, strictly weighing their iniquity, yet tempering our wrath with mercy, have judged that for the present we should not lay a heavier hand upon them. Nevertheless, by apostolic letters we command your nobility entirely to forbid the aforesaid burgesses, as perjurers, traitors, and excommunicates, to be received at fairs and markets in your lands; indeed, wherever they may be found by any of your men, they are to be seized and completely despoiled of their goods, which are to be cast away.

## XX. To Hugh, Archbishop of Sens; Geoffrey of Langres; Theobald of Paris; and Henry of Troyes, bishops: he gives the same orders concerning the burgesses of Vézelay as in the preceding letter. (Lateran, December?)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 774.]

It has come to your knowledge, etc.

## XXI. To Peter, Archbishop of Bourges.—That he excommunicate the Count of Nevers unless he repents. (Lateran, December?)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 775.]

[Col. 1010D] ANASTASIUS, bishop, to P., Archbishop of Bourges.

Your brotherhood, we believe, recognizes, at least by its magnitude, the monstrous cruelty and barbarous savagery which the Count of Nevers still does not cease to exercise against the monastery of Vézelay, as though by his power he ought to prevail against the Lord, against His sacred bride the Church. Although our predecessor Pope Eugenius of holy memory had prepared the remedies of the Apostolic See against him and desired to correct him, he did not deserve to be cured of so great a disease, because it passed into the inclination of his heart and his foolish heart was darkened, so that, in accordance with the prophetic word, seeing he does not see, and understanding the things of God, he understands them not at all.

[Col. 1011A] We therefore, who by the ordering of divine clemency have succeeded our said predecessor in the apostolic see, are compelled to defend the aforesaid monastery of Vézelay as the freehold of Blessed Peter. We also thirst, in paternal charity, for the salvation of the aforesaid count and of all Christians; and we possess no little confidence in the prudence and integrity of your brotherhood. By these present letters we command your charity, without delay, strictly to warn him to repair in full the damage which he has inflicted upon that monastery and to leave that place in peace and its liberty.

Also announce to the same count on our behalf that he must not compel the Abbot of Vézelay to come before him in order to render justice to any of his men, unless it has first been established in the court of that abbot that justice has been denied to any of his men. But if, within thirty days after your warning, he neglects to perform what we have said above, go with religious and prudent men to a place from which it may readily resound in his ears. When a gathering of the people has assembled in church, with candles lit, solemnly pronounce by apostolic authority, without any remedy of appeal, the sentence of excommunication against him and the faithless burgesses of Vézelay; and, excepting the baptism of infants and penance for the dying, prohibit the celebration of all divine offices in all the lands of that count.

We further command you to announce by your letters, on our behalf, that the same sentence must be firmly observed by our venerable brethren H., Archbishop of Sens; G., Bishop of Nevers; G., Bishop of Langres; H., Bishop of Autun; Henry, Bishop of Troyes; and A., Bishop of Auxerre. For we have commanded them by apostolic letters to cause that sentence, after your announcement, to be inviolably observed throughout their dioceses. Cause the letters which we sent to our aforesaid brethren, the Bishops of Langres, Autun, Nevers, and Auxerre, to be delivered to them by your messengers.

## XXII. To Louis VII, King of the Franks.—Against the Count of Nevers and the townsmen of Vézelay. (Lateran, December?)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 776.]

[Col. 1011D]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, to King LOUIS.

Since many good reports have reached us from former times concerning your royal magnificence toward us and the most holy Roman Church, both those who have preceded us in the apostolic office and we ourselves have cherished your nobility in every way. And we who, by the divine will, still survive, cherish you now and desire, insofar as we can do so according to God, that your honour may be increased.

Therefore, dearest son in Christ, as our predecessor Pope Eugenius of holy memory did, so we also send you apostolic letters on behalf of the monastery of Vézelay. We command and exhort you in the Lord strictly to admonish the Count of Nevers, who does not cease to rage with barbarous ferocity against that monastery, to make full amends to the said monastery for the damage he is known to have inflicted and to leave its place in peace and its liberty. If he believes that he has any right in that monastery, he may afterward obtain his justice by our command.

But if, hardened in his obstinacy, he should scorn to carry this into effect, we command that a sentence of excommunication be pronounced against him and the burgesses of Vézelay without remedy of appeal, and that throughout all his land the celebration of all divine offices be completely prohibited, excepting baptism of infants and penances for the dying. Accordingly, through the bearer of these letters we command you thereafter to abstain from him as an excommunicate; and, wholly barring the burgesses themselves from every fair in your kingdom under your ban, zealously to command that, wherever they may be found, they be seized and despoiled of their goods as perjurers and disturbers of the Church.

Moreover, we command your diligence that you do not in any way burden the aforesaid monastery of Vézelay upon any false allegation. Rather, for reverence toward Blessed Peter and us, strive to defend it from every enemy as the patrimony of that prince of the apostles. Furthermore, we do not wish it to escape your devotion that we have commanded our beloved son, the Abbot of Vézelay, not to dare to make any concession whatsoever to the said count in our monastery. Farewell.

## XXIII. He confirms the privileges and goods of the Church of Arles. (Lateran, 26 December.)

[*Gallia Christiana*, new ed., I, Documents 97.]

[Col. 1012C]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother RAIMOND, Archbishop of Arles, and to his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

Both the ancient evidence of the city itself and the authoritative testimony of ancient writings make clear that the metropolitan see of Arles was once famous and distinguished, and flourished in the regions of Gaul with many titles of dignity and glory. But because it pleased divine providence to correct the sins of the people dwelling in it, wars breaking in from every side greatly diminished that metropolis in both dignity and temporal possessions. We, though unworthy, sit by the Lord’s ordering in the watchtower of the chief apostles Peter and Paul, as cultivators and guardians of justice in the Church [read: ecclesiastical], and sympathize with its desolation in kindly affection; as far as we can with God, we desire beneficially to provide for its peace and dignity.

For it is fair and reasonable that those who are known to be more devoted to Blessed Peter and his vicars, and who desire to be cherished by the protection of the most holy Roman Church, should be nourished at the breasts of that pious mother and heard in their reasonable petitions. Therefore, beloved brother and fellow bishop Raimond in Christ, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive under the protection of the prince of the apostles himself and ourselves the aforesaid Church of Arles. To this church Saint Trophimus, bishop—indeed, from the fountain of whose faith all Gaul received its streams—was sent from this Holy Roman and Apostolic See by Blessed Peter, as is clearly shown from the statements of Blessed Pope Zosimus, called a martyr [Note: We conjecture that the title “martyr” has entered erroneously.]. We fortify it by the privilege of this present document, decreeing that whatever possessions or goods that Church now possesses justly and canonically, or may hereafter acquire, God favouring it, through cession by pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm for you and your successors and, through you, for that Church. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

[Col. 1013B] The monastery of Saint Caesarius with all its appurtenances, which the same Blessed Caesarius, bishop of Arles, is said to have founded on the freehold of that Church and enriched from its goods; the right of ordering and correcting that place; the church of Blessed Mary of Fos, with its tithes and all appurtenances; the church of Blessed Mary of Château-Vieux, with tithes and other appurtenances; the castle of Célon; the castle of Saint-Amans; the castles of Avernico and Avalon; the castles of Mornas and Montdragon; revenues from the bridge of Saint-Genès; the Jews; the right which you have in the coinage of that city; and everything which you possess in the shares and tolls of Arles.

Moreover, we confirm by authority of the Apostolic See the settlement concluded between you and Anfos, Count of Toulouse, by reasonable provision and put into writing, if it is shown to be reasonable. We also confirm for you and your successors the island called Boscus-comitalis, which the aforesaid count restored to your Church.

Furthermore, by a prerogative of a broader and more special kind [read: “by a broader and more special prerogative”], we establish by this present decree that the province of Arles shall be subject to no legate whatsoever except only one sent from the side of the Roman pontiff.

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations. Rather, let all things be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly attempts rashly to act against this page of our constitution, etc. Amen.

I, Anastasius, bishop of the Catholic Church.  
I, Ymarus, Bishop of Tusculum.  
I, Hugh, Bishop of Ostia.  
I, Gobert, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Callixtus.  
[Col. 1014A] I, Manfred, cardinal of the title of Saint Sabina.  
I, Guido, cardinal of Saint Pastor.  
I, Jordan, cardinal of Saint Susanna, etc.

Dated at the Lateran, through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Kalends of January, in the second indiction, in the year 1153 of the Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Pope Anastasius IV.

## XXIV. He confirms the goods of the Church of Marseille to Bishop Peter. (Lateran, 30 December.)

[*Gallia Christiana*, new ed., I, Documents 112.]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother PETER, Bishop of Marseille, and to his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

[Col. 1014B] Placed, by the Lord’s ordering, upon the lofty watchtower of the Apostolic See, we ought to love our brother bishops, both those nearby and those far away, with brotherly charity, and to preserve for the churches in which they are known to serve the Lord their due rights. Therefore, beloved brother in Christ Peter, bishop, we graciously grant your reasonable requests; and, following in the footsteps of our predecessors of happy memory, Innocent and Eugenius, Roman pontiffs, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the Church of Marseille of the blessed Mother of God Mary, over which, by God’s appointment, you are known to preside, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, whether churches, tithes, castles, [Col. 1014C] villages, or other things, and whatever it may, God being favourable, acquire in the future by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these, we have considered it proper to specify the following by their proper names:

The monastery of Saint Saviour of La Sachoas, situated within the walls of the city of Marseille; the episcopal city with all its territory; Rocambarbara, with the ditch surrounding that rock and with the valleys encircling the same city from its walls; the harbour from the Gallic Gate, and whatever you possess in the old harbour between the monastery and the city; the lands of Fontecooperto; the *pedaticum* levy from the territory [Col. 1014D] of Alaugi and Nertii; whatever you possess in the harbour of Banneriis; whatever you possess in Leonio; the castle of Saint Canat; the castle of Nertii; the castle of Alaugi; the village of Saint Julian; the share which you possess in the castle of Pennes; the castle of Mairanegas; the castle of Melna; the castle of Aurovenes; the castle of Balcet, with its territory and appurtenances; the castle of Albania; and two *rocetos* for it at Christmas and Easter. Whatever, moreover, Pontius of Podio-nigro granted to your church on behalf of his son Aichard in the aforesaid castle of Alaugi; your share of the castle of Evene; the hill which is called the castle of Guimbert.

Furthermore, by apostolic authority we forbid anyone to presume, without the consent and will of the bishop of Marseille, to build the castle of Turen or any fortification upon that hill or upon any other possessions [Col. 1015A] of the same Church of Marseille. Moreover, we confirm by the protection of this present charter, and decree to remain valid in future times, the settlement made, with both sides consenting, in the presence of our venerable brother Raymond, archbishop of Arles, and of other bishops, concerning the dispute between you and Geoffrey of Marseille and his brethren, as is contained in their document.

The church of Saint Canat; the church of Mairanegas; and the churches of Melna, with their tithes and appurtenances; the churches of Pennes, Nertii, Alaugi, Saint Julian, Saint Mary in the episcopal town, and Saint Martin [Col. 1015B] in the vicomital town, with their tithes and appurtenances; Saint Mary of La Sachoas; Saint Martin of Arogno; Saint Lawrence; Saint Andrew; in the territory of Marseille, the churches of Septimo, Saint Thyrsus of Cula, Saint Mitrius at the castle of Gumbert, and Solobiis, with their tithes and appurtenances; the church of Saint Michael in the territory of Marseille; the churches of Saint Marcellus, with tithes; the churches of Albania, Saint Peter in Chains, Saint John of Gargerio, Saint Clarus, Saint Pontius, Saint Mary of Gemenas, Saint Mary of Ros, Saint John of Podio, in the valley of Tritis, the church of Saint Martin of Insol, with tithes. In the churches of Auriol, one third of the tithes; in the churches of Saint Zacharias, seven *solidi* and two measures of honey; the churches [Col. 1015C] of Villariis and Rochafort, and of Chuia, with tithes; the church of Saint Peter and Saint John of Signa; the church of the old castle, with tithes; the churches of Aurovones, Baucet, Castellet, Saint Victor in the territory of Madalgas, with tithes; and the church of Laza with its appurtenances.

We also forbid any abbot, monk, or other person whatsoever to receive persons excommunicated or placed under interdict who are known by parochial right to belong to the Church of Marseille.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person at all rashly to disturb the aforesaid church or to take away its possessions, etc. Amen.

I, Anastasius, bishop of the Catholic Church. [Col. 1015D] I, Ymarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Ugo, bishop of Ostia. I, Oddo, cardinal deacon of Saint Gregory at the Golden Veil, etc.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Kalends of January, in the second indiction, in the year 1153 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Anastasius.

## XXV. Privilege for the Church of Fiesole.  
*(Lateran, 31 December.)*

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, III, 244.]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother RODULPH, bishop of Fiesole, and to his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

[Col. 1016A] The authority of our office exhorts us to love our brother bishops with the charity due to them and to preserve the due rights of the churches entrusted by God to their governance. Therefore, beloved brother and fellow bishop in Christ Rodulph, we graciously grant your reasonable requests; and, following in the footsteps of our predecessor, Pope Eugenius of holy memory, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the Church of Fiesole, over which, by God’s appointment, you are known to preside, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may in the future, by gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, the Lord granting it, acquire, [Col. 1016B] shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these, we have considered it proper to specify the following by their proper names:

The monastery of Saint Bartholomew, situated at Fiesole; the monastery of Saint Martin at Maiano; the monastery of Saint Gaudentius at the foot of the Alps; the monastery of Saint Mary of Rosano; the parish church of Saint Peter of Romena, with the tithes and possessions belonging by right to the bishopric of Fiesole; the parish church of Saint Peter of Cassia; the parish church of Saint John of Capolia; the parish church of Saint Leoninus in Collina; the parish church of Saint Martin of Vado; the parish church of Saint Mary of Sco; the parish church of Saint Mary of Spaltinna; and all other parish churches and churches known to belong by right to the Church of Fiesole; the city and fortress of Fiesole; the castle of Monte Lauri with [Col. 1016C] its manor; the castle of Cisalo with its manor; the castle of Monte Bonelli with its manor; the castle of Gregnanellum with its manor; whatever you possess in the manor of Acone and in the manor of Lancisa, and within the parish of Panzano, Saint Mary of Novola, and Saint Justus in Salice; the manor of Agna; the church of Saint Alexander, with its manor, beside the castle of Monte Carboli; and likewise the other castles, villages, and possessions which were confirmed to you by name in the privilege of our predecessor Pope Innocent of good memory.

No one shall presume to usurp without your consent the appointment of the aforesaid monasteries and baptismal churches subject to the Church of Fiesole. In the chapels [Col. 1016D] of your parish churches, however, the parish priests shall have free appointment and due obedience without contradiction from anyone, as was granted to them by the privilege of Pope Paschal of happy memory, while preserving the due reverence owed to their own bishop. We confirm to you, throughout your bishopric and according to the provisions of the canons, the share of tithes, offerings, wills, and other ecclesiastical revenues. We forbid any church to be built in the same bishopric or, once built, to be subjected to anyone without your permission—while in all things preserving the right and authority of the Apostolic See.

We therefore decree that no one at all, etc. If anyone therefore, etc. But to all, etc. Amen.

I, Anastasius, bishop of the Catholic Church. [Col. 1017A] I, Ugo, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, GG., cardinal priest of Saint Calixtus. I, Guido, cardinal priest of Saint Chrysogonus. I, Manfred, cardinal priest of Saint Sabina. I, Aribert, cardinal priest of Saint Anastasia. I, Julius, cardinal priest of Saint Marcellus. I, Ubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Astaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Prisca. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, the title of Pammachius, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Sylvester and Martin, have subscribed. I, Otho, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. [Col. 1017B] I, Martin, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Kalends of January, in the second indiction, in the year 1153 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Anastasius IV.

## YEAR 1153–1154

## XXVI. To Peter, Archbishop of Tarentaise.  
*(Lateran, 24 November.)*

[*Hist. patriae Monum.*, *Chart.*, I, 804.]

[Col. 1017C] ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brothers P[ETER], archbishop of Tarentaise, and AR., bishop of Aosta, greetings and apostolic blessing.
