We wish your brotherhood to know that we have taken care to confirm for our beloved sons G., prior of Saint Ursus, and his brethren—and, through them, for the church committed to them—the gift of Strata which our beloved son, the nobleman Hu., count of Maurienne, is known to have made to those brethren out of piety. Therefore, by apostolic letters we command you that, if anyone should perhaps presume to act against the charter of our confirmation and, after being warned, refuses to make amends, you shall bind him with a sentence of excommunication.

[Col. 1017D] Given at the Lateran, on the eighth day before the Kalends of December.

## XXVII. To Engebald, Archbishop of Tours.—He orders him to summon G., bishop of Tréguier, and investigate his life.

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 773.]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother E., archbishop of Tours, greetings and apostolic blessing.

If you had devoted to the honourable exercise of the pontifical office entrusted to you the diligence which it requires, and if you had applied due concern to correcting the grave abuses reported concerning those who live under your oversight, the life and conduct of our brother G., bishop of Tréguier, would not until now have remained [Col. 1018A] unexamined before your eyes. For reports of such deeds of his have reached our ears that it would seem shameful to hear them, and lamentable to repeat them, of any person established in the clerical order. He is alleged to be a squanderer of his church’s goods and to have conferred holy orders contrary to the decrees of the holy Fathers. Moreover, he is said to be so entangled in the crimes of simony, perjury, and many other offences that—what we cannot say without profound distress of mind—according to the prophet’s words (Hosea 7), he has become “like a cake not turned.”

In this matter he has reason to fear concerning the commission of these transgressions, while you have reason to fear concerning your silence. Though you have been placed by the Lord as a watchman over the house of Israel, you leave so great offences uninvestigated and uncorrected that, in the prophet’s words, you seem rather to plaster over [Col. 1018B] the wall of sins which you ought to tear down. Since, therefore, we neither wish nor ought to endure that the life of the aforesaid bishop should remain any longer unexamined, we command your brotherhood by these present letters to summon prudent and religious men; or to order the said bishop and the clergy of his church to appear before you; and, after a diligent investigation of his conduct and deeds, if he should be found implicated in even one crime, or found to have performed holy orders contrary to the statutes of the canons, to send him, suspended from his office, to the presence of our apostolic see, so that we may punish in him whatever ought to be punished according to canonical constitutions. We wish, moreover, that both you and the other bishops or abbots whom you summon to investigate his conduct should take care fully to report to us in writing whatever truth you discover in the matter.

Certainly, since such rumours concerning him had, it is said, reached even the ears of our predecessor Pope E. of happy memory through the reports of many worthy persons, he has until now omitted to consider [lacuna] his governance. We must take care lest we seem to be reproved by the strict Judge for disregarding such grievous reports.

## YEAR 1154

## XXVIII. To Gregory, Bishop of Lucca.

[BALUZ., *Miscellanies*, ed. Mansi, IV, 595.]

[Col. 1018D]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother G., bishop of Lucca, greetings and apostolic blessing.

If we sometimes depart from the rigour of the canons out of mercy, deal mercifully with those in distress, and become weak with the weak, we do not do so because we wish to curtail the due rights of others or abandon the path of the royal road which is most strictly enjoined upon us to observe. For we have heard something at which we cannot but marvel. We have heard, indeed, that the clergy of the church of Saint Pantaleon, because we treated them mercifully and absolved them—not so much through justice as through mercy—from the interdict under which that church had [Col. 1019A] suffered for a long time, almost to destruction, now raise their horns and seek to have a prior placed over them, not as is fitting but according to their own pleasure; and they attempt to take from our beloved sons, the canons of Saint Fridian, the right which those canons are known to possess in that church.

Although we too mercifully remitted the sentence of interdict, we did not understand the church of Blessed Fridian to be deprived of its right, nor did we intend to infringe the privileges of our predecessors, so that we might sing to the Lord the song of mercy and justice and say with the Prophet: “I will sing to you, O Lord, of mercy and judgment.” Therefore, by apostolic letters we command your brotherhood not to allow the aforesaid clergy of Saint Pantaleon [Col. 1019B] to proceed to the election of a prior without the consent and will of our aforesaid sons, the canons of Saint Fridian; nor are you yourself to proceed improperly. But if either you or those clergy of Saint Pantaleon are confident that you have any right by which you hope to be able to proceed in appointing a prior, you may establish your right in our presence on the next Sunday when “I am the Good Shepherd” is sung (18 April).

## XXIX. To the Regular Canons of the Lateran.—He confirms their statutes.

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 778.]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 1019C] sons JOHN, prior of the most sacred patriarchal basilica of the Lord Saviour, called the Constantinian, and likewise of John the Baptist and John the Evangelist, and to his brethren, canons present and future who profess the regular life, in perpetuity.

The Church recognizes that the power of binding and loosing in both heaven and earth was principally entrusted by the Lord to blessed Peter and his successors in the words by which that same Lord addressed Peter: “Whatever you bind upon earth shall be bound also in heaven, and whatever you loose upon earth shall be loosed also in heaven” (Matthew 16). By the working of the same God, the steadfastness of his own faith and the strengthening of another’s faith were likewise granted to him, when it was said to him: “I have prayed for you, Peter, that your faith may not fail; and when you have turned again, strengthen your brethren” [Col. 1019D] (Luke 21).

It is therefore fitting that we, although unworthy, who sit in blessed Peter’s place, should, insofar as divine mercy grants us knowledge and ability, correct what is wrong, strengthen what is right, and make such dispositions in his Church, according to the judgment of the Judge, that our judgment may proceed from his countenance and our eyes may behold equity. It is therefore just and reasonable that each church should retain its own honour and dignity. And as, in the structure of a human body, natural reason, providing for the well-being of each member, assigns particular and proper functions and preserves to the more noble members their dignity, so apostolic providence governs all churches in the body of the Church according to the ordinances of the sacred canons; and it guards those that are more [Col. 1020A] worthy and renowned in the prerogative of their rank.

Moved, therefore, by this obligation of reason, although the concern and care of all churches rests upon us, we ought nevertheless to provide with fuller and more attentive care for the aforesaid holy Lateran Church. Through it we are enabled to watch over all the others, and it is known to pertain more especially and intimately to the ordering of the Roman pontiff. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, following the example of our predecessor, Pope Alexander II of blessed memory, we strengthen the same church, in which you are dedicated to divine service, by the privilege of the Apostolic See. First, we decree that the order of canons known to have been established there according to God and the Rule of blessed Augustine [Col. 1020B] shall be preserved there inviolate for all time.

Furthermore, whatever possessions and whatever goods the same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may in the future, God being favourable, acquire through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these, we have considered it proper to specify the following by their proper names: one half of all offerings at the high altar, wholly and without any deduction; the payment or revenue called *Glandaticum* or *Herbaticum*, from our swine and cattle; and every benefit granted to that church by the same our predecessor.

Upon the death of you, the prior of the same place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed over it by any craft of fraud or force. Rather, they shall first agree upon a suitable person from your own college, if one can be found, or from another religious community; and thereafter, with the counsel, deliberation, and judgment of the Roman pontiff, they shall elect him. The person elected shall be bound in obedience or subjection to no one except the Roman pontiff alone. Moreover, you may receive into conversion, without opposition from anyone, clergy fleeing from the world or free laymen, from wherever they come, provided they are not excommunicated or under interdict. Those who have been received with the common counsel of the prior and brethren shall be bound in obedience to no one except the Roman pontiff and the prior [Col. 1020D] of the same church. Should any writing at any time appear contrary to this your privilege, we deem it void.

We forbid any of the brethren, after having made profession in that place, to leave the cloister without the permission of his prior; and no one shall dare retain a person who has left without letters of such authorization. At the petition and by the will of our brother cardinal bishops, we decree that the same church, as principal, mother, and mistress, shall be wholly free and subject to absolutely no one except the Roman pontiff alone. The same bishops, by salutary provision, as our co-workers and vicars, shall provide for the welfare and dignity of that venerable basilica.

[Col. 1021A] We further command that the provision made by our aforesaid predecessor Alexander be observed with the greatest care: namely, that altar vessels, altar vestments, and all ornaments of the sacred mystery shall not be touched, brought out, put away, or that offerings of any kind shall not be taken from upon the altar by ministers not consecrated to God. When bishops celebrate there the sacred solemnities of Mass, you shall be present in clerical tunics, begin the chant, and always ensure that a priest, deacon, subdeacon, and acolyte are provided from among yourselves. Moreover, Mass shall not be celebrated in that church, even on ordinary days, unless at least four brethren are present. On Sundays and feast days of saints, your whole community, however numerous, shall be present.

[Col. 1021B] So that, with God’s help, the vigour of regular order and discipline may be guarded and preserved inviolate in that church, we decree that each of the cardinal bishops appointed to the service of the high altar shall hold chapter with the brethren of that place once a week concerning observance of the Rule. If anything serious requires correction, it shall be amended by them in our stead with the common counsel of the prior and brethren. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly [acts against] this charter of our confirmation and constitution, etc.

## XXX. To the Abbess of Saint-Deodat.—That she render obedience to the Abbot of Vulturno.

(MURATORI, *Rerum Italicarum Scriptores*, I, II, 520.)

[Col. 1021C]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to A., abbess of Saint-Deodat.

Our beloved son Elias, abbot of Saint Vincent, declares that you deny him—at which we marvel—the obedience which his predecessors are known always to have possessed in the church entrusted to you, and which you yourself formerly rendered. Since we wish the same abbot, as our special son, to retain his rights unimpaired, we command you by these present letters always, with charity preserved, to render him the due obedience and reverence which those who held the governance of the church entrusted to you before you rendered to his predecessors, [Col. 1021D] and which you yourself rendered to him and to his predecessors; and do not presume to take away anything from his right.

## XXXI. He confirms certain possessions of the Monastery of Saint Bertin at Sithiu.

(See Iperius, *Chronicle of Saint Bertin*, in MARTÈNE, *Thesaurus Anecdotorum*, III, 647.)

## XXXII. He commands [Gerald], bishop of Tournai, not to arrogate to himself authority over the churches of the Monastery of Saint Bertin at Sithiu.

(Iperius, *Chronicle*, in the place cited.)

## XXXIII. Privilege for the Monastery of Agnano.  
*(Lateran, 13 January.)*

[MITTARELLI, *Annales Camaldulenses*, III, appendix, 469.]

[Col. 1022A]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons SAXO, abbot of the monastery of Saint Mary of Agnano, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

A petition of pious desire ought to be fulfilled by the ensuing effect, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth worthily and the requested benefit may assuredly acquire force. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously grant your just requests; and we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid monastery, in which you are dedicated to divine service, [Col. 1022B] and strengthen it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may in the future, God being favourable, acquire through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these, we have considered it proper to specify the following by their proper names:

The monastery of Saint Mary at Graticciata near the city of Arezzo; the church of Saint Blaise in that city; the monastery of Saint Gaudentius; the church of Saint Quiricus of Vicione; the hospital of that place; the church of Saint Michael of Caphajora; the church [Col. 1022C] of Saint Michael of Tuntinano; the church of Saint Stephen of Crovule; and the church of Saint Cecilia of Ferrata, with their appurtenances; the manor of Vertige; the manor of Saint Soterius; whatever right you possess in the castle of Pergine; the mill which you possess on the River Arno near Monte di Valle; the mill on the River Ambra at Poce; and the mill on the River Elsa at Pedemontis.

We also grant that the burial ground of that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who decide to be buried there, while preserving the right of the mother church.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no one at all rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, or to take away, retain, diminish, or harass with any vexations its possessions; but that all things shall be preserved intact for the full benefit of the uses for which they were granted, namely the governance and support [Col. 1022D] of those concerned, while preserving the authority of the Apostolic See.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, etc.

“LORD, KEEP ME AS THE APPLE OF THE EYE.” ANASTASIUS, POPE IV.

I, Anastasius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Hugo, bishop of Ostia. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Calixtus. [Col. 1023A] I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus. I, Manfred, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina. I, Aribert, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, Ubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, John, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Oddo, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Octavian, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill. [Col. 1023B] I, John, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, the title of Pammachius.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the Ides of January, in the second indiction, in the year 1153 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Anastasius IV.

## XXXIV. He takes the Monastery of Glanfeuil under protection and confirms its goods and rights.  
*(Lateran, 13 January.)*

[GATTULA, *History of Monte Cassino*, 299.]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son WILLIAM, abbot of the monastery of Glanfeuil, [Col. 1023C] and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

Whenever a request is made to us which is known to accord with reason and propriety, we willingly grant it and offer suitable assistance to the petitioners’ desires. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, we graciously grant your just requests; and, following in the footsteps of our predecessor Pope Urban of happy memory, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid monastery over which, by God’s appointment, you are known to preside, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may in the future, through grants of pontiffs, [Col. 1023D] gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God being favourable, acquire, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these, we have considered it proper to specify the following by their proper names:

Namely, the church of Saint Martin of Saint-Maur; the church of Saints Gervasius and Protasius at Bateaco, with its appurtenances; the church of Blessed Mary of Molo, with its appurtenances; the island of Saint Maurus, with its appurtenances; the church of Saint Mary in Dane; the church of Saint Simplicius on the Loire; the church of Saint Peter at Vodda; Saint Peter with the village of Fabrensis; Saint Lambert of Curalo; Saint Hilary of Concorzo, with its appurtenances; and Saint Martin of Sorech; the land of Aymeric of Averoim; the churches of Saint [Col. 1024A] Justa of Verce, with their appurtenances, and of Saint Mary of Doado; the village of Solonge, with its appurtenances; the village called Gru, with its appurtenances; the church of Saint Vetorinus of Gena, with its mill and other appurtenances; the church of Saint Quiricus in Salmossa, with its tithes; the church of Saint Maurus in Lauduna; the church of Saint Mary Magdalene of Vareno; the village of Sindremont, with its appurtenances; the church of Saint Martin in Burno; the village of Panes, with its appurtenances; the village of Lambri, with its appurtenances; the island of Blazon in Normandy; the church of Saint Mary of Cingla; the church of Saint Maurus situated in the castle of Laudun; the church of Saint Anianus and the village of Sindremont; and the church of Saint Peter in Culturis.

[Col. 1024B] We also decree that the burial ground of that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who decide to be buried there, while preserving the right of the mother church. Upon the death of you, the present abbot of the same place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed over it by any artifice of fraud or force, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall determine is to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict. The person elected shall be presented to the abbot of Monte Cassino for confirmation and consecrated by a Catholic bishop whom that abbot requests by his letters. He and his successors shall promise obedience to the abbot of Monte Cassino and, every five years, shall visit that monastery of Monte Cassino, as their head, with due humility.

[Col. 1024C] We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no one at all rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery or take away, retain, diminish, or harass with any vexations its possessions; but that all things shall be preserved intact for the full benefit of the uses for which they were granted, namely the governance and support of those concerned, while in all things preserving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical rights of the diocesan bishops. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, etc.

I, Anastasius, bishop of the Catholic Church. [Col. 1024D] I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Calixtus. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Jacynthus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, Ubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Octavian, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Henry, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. I, Cencius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina. [Col. 1025A] I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Sylvester and Martin.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the Ides of January, in the second indiction, in the year 1154 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Anastasius IV.

## XXXV. To Gregory, Bishop of Lucca, and the Canons of Lucca.  
*(Lateran, 16 January.)*

[BALUZ., *Miscellanies*, ed. Mansi, IV, 595.]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother G., bishop, and to our beloved sons, the canons of Lucca, greetings and apostolic blessing.

From the time when sacred religious life was established in the church of St. Fridianus, the brethren of that place have diffused such a fragrance by their manner of life [Col. 1025B], and have so illumined the Church of God by their religion, that many who seemed to have rotted away like beasts in their own dung have run, through them, after the fragrance of their ointments, and have received in their life the splendor of the true light, under whose guidance they might return to the homeland of blessed brotherhood. Hence it was that our predecessors have hitherto loved that same church as a special daughter, and have taken continual care to exalt it both temporally and spiritually.

Following, indeed, in their footsteps, we embrace that place with no lesser affection and no unequal charity; and, insofar as divine grace grants, we desire to foster, exalt, and defend it [Col. 1025C], holding its dear brethren in such regard that whoever should offend them would offend the Roman Church, and whoever should touch them would be accounted as touching the pupil of our eye. Therefore we have conceived great bitterness in our heart because we have heard that certain of your parishioners, at the prompting of him who [lacuna] all the sons of pride, have been driven to such violence that, having assembled a crowd in the church of St. Saviour of Mustolio, which is recognized as belonging to their jurisdiction, they made an attack, broke open the doors of the church, and wished shamefully to mistreat the persons of the clergy. We are greatly astonished and grieved with all our heart at this—not so much for the destruction of those who, at the instigation of the devil, are hurled into the precipice of such pride [Col. 1025D], as for your peril, since, making light of the injury done to religious persons, you have not been inflamed with any zeal for justice against these wicked men.

Therefore, because we regard the injuries and molestations of the oft-mentioned brethren as our own, and because we can in no way leave such presumption unpunished, by these present letters we command you that you rise more zealously in vengeance for so great a wickedness; and that, when the congregation of the church is assembled on a solemn day, with candles lighted, you, brother bishop, bind with the bond of excommunication all those who were the ringleaders of this evil, and cause them throughout your entire diocese to be avoided as excommunicated persons until they present themselves before the apostolic presence with your letters in order to make satisfaction for so great a presumption. You shall also sternly rebuke the others and compel them [Col. 1026A] to make satisfaction. Let your brotherly discretion take care that you are not found to neglect this iniquity by any dissimulation, but pursue it more watchfully, with assistance and truth, as the duty of your office requires. Otherwise, not in gentleness but in severity, God being the author, we shall make you know that we have concern and care for them as our special sons; nor do we permit priestly protection against their wrongdoers to be denied them by any of our brethren.

Given at the Lateran, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of February.

### XXXVI. He grants Berald, abbot of the monastery of St. Sixtus at Piacenza, the use of the mitre.  
*(Lateran, January 23.)*

[CAMPI, *History of Piacenza*, II, 353.]

[Col. 1026B]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son BERALD, abbot of St. Sixtus, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Both the obligation of charity urges us, and the kindness and benevolence of the Apostolic See incite us, to render honor to brethren and to bestow upon the special sons of the Holy Roman Church the favor of a more special prerogative, so that they may appear more distinguished to men, may govern more securely the churches committed to them when supported by the familiar favor of apostolic love, and their subjects may show them greater reverence and honor. Thus, beloved son in the Lord Berald, abbot of St. Peter’s, we have resolved to honor you by the favor of our affection. Therefore, on the principal feasts [Col. 1026C] of your church, both in procession and during the sacred solemnities of Mass, we grant to your church, out of the liberality of the Apostolic See, the use of the mitre.

Given at the Lateran, on the tenth day before the Kalends of February.

### XXXVII. Privilege for the Church of Rieti.  
*(Lateran, January 24.)*

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, I, 1198.]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother DODO, bishop of the Church of Rieti, and to his successors canonically instituted, in perpetual memory.

Placed, by the Lord’s disposition, on the lofty watchtower of the Apostolic See [Col. 1026D], we ought to love our brethren, the bishops, with brotherly charity and to provide with paternal solicitude for the churches committed to them by God. Therefore, venerable brother in Christ Dodo, bishop of the Church of Rieti, graciously assenting as is due to your just petitions, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the aforesaid Church over which, by God’s authority, you are known to preside; and we fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by the favor of God, acquire through grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors [Col. 1027A]. Among these we have judged that the following should be expressly named:

The parish church of St. Thomas in Grumulo; the parish church of St. Susanna; St. Vitus; St. Mary at Gisoni; St. Mary at Testoni; St. Rusticus; St. Mary in Valliocrina; St. Mary in Cornu; St. Mary in Sigilli; St. Rufina; St. Mary in Baccigno; St. Sylvester in Fallarino; Holy Cross in Burbone; St. Peter in Laculo; St. Mary and St. Peter in Pantano; St. Peter in Dura; St. John in Clarino; St. Sixtus in Amiternum; St. Peter in Popleta; St. Victorinus; St. Peter in Precoro; St. Valentine in Collectario; [Col. 1027B] St. Mark and St. Donatus in Teria; St. Julian in Foce; St. Paul at the head of Amiternum; St. Cosmas in Cagnano; St. Anthimus in Cassina; St. Thomas in Villano; St. Peter in Cornu; St. Eutychius in Marana; St. Stephen in Cluvano; St. Lawrence and St. Leopardus in Cartoro; St. Mary in Mareri and St. Pastor; St. Peter in Canapinula; St. Elpidius; St. Andrew and St. Paul; St. Mary in Rivogatti; St. Andrew in Laceto; St. Lucy on the high hill; St. Andrew in Capradosso; St. Mary in Valle; St. Agatha in Plaja; St. Justin in Rocca Sinibaldi; St. Anatolia in Tore; St. Angel [Col. 1027C] in Ceruja; St. Victoria in Tripula; St. Felix in Octavo; St. Nicholas and St. Helena in Lubriculo; St. John in the valley of Rieti; St. Sabinus on Mount Gurzo; St. Mary in Casa Roperti; St. Lawrence in Quintiliano; St. Mary in Anglise; St. Donatus of the Tower of Carpasso; and St. Mary della Sala.

And in these parish churches, the oratories called monasteries, namely: St. Peter in Anglise; Holy Cross at Aqua de Solangio; St. Juvenal at Lacu; St. Mary in Consonano; St. Saviour; the Trinity; St. Gregory of Cacalici; St. Valentine della Pureja; Holy Cross in Lognano; St. Eleutherius in the Rieti plain; St. Pastor in Alatro; St. Angelicus in Vetica; St. Mary in Lupicino; St. Peter in Madito; St. Sylvester [Col. 1027D] in Petra Battuta and St. Sylvester in Perulo; St. Severinus and St. Avita in Amiternum; St. John the Baptist of St. Victorinus; St. Leontius in Classina; St. Lawrence in Fasso; St. [lacuna] in Nura; St. Maurus; St. Castilion of Valle de Petra; St. Leonard of Colle Fecati; and St. Paul of Cocotha.

Likewise, within the city or suburb of Rieti: the church of St. John and St. Eleutherius; St. Rufus; St. Juvenal; St. Marina; St. Peter at the Roman gate; St. Saviour; St. Nicholas in Acupentu; St. Leopardus; St. Bartholomew; St. Eutychius; St. Maro; St. Severus; St. Fortunatus; St. Peter and St. Andrew in the Rieti plain; the Holy Apostles and St. Donatus; St. Sebastian in Scaje; St. Saccinus in Berrico; St. Clement; St. Nicholas in Forfone; St. Mary at Capite Aquae; St. Mary in Pugillo; St. Flavian [Col. 1028A] in Novera; St. Mary in Burbone, in the valley of Lumbricola; St. Hilary in Racciolo; St. Mary in the city at Amiternum; and St. Barotus: from all of these episcopal dues are to be paid to you.

Moreover: the castle of Collis Vaccarii; the castle of Veneruba; the castle of Mount Guizzi; the castle of Catrico; the castle of Casalis Lie; the castle of Rocca in Prece; the castle of Verano; the castle of Butri; and the castle of Monte Secco, with their appurtenances.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no one at all to hold, disturb, or take away the same [lacuna], or retain what has been taken away, diminish it, or harass it with rash vexations; but that all things be preserved whole, for the benefit both of you and of the clergy and poor, saving in all things the authority of the Apostolic See. [Col. 1028B] But if any ecclesiastical or secular person, etc.

I, Anastasius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, G., cardinal priest of the title of St. Calixtus, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of St. Chrysogonus, have subscribed. I, Hubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of St. Praxedis, have subscribed. I, Manfredus, cardinal priest of the title of St. Sabina, have subscribed. I, Astaldus, cardinal priest of the title of St. Prisca, have subscribed. I, John Paparo, cardinal priest of St. Lawrence in Damaso, have subscribed. I, Cencius, cardinal priest of the title of St. Lawrence in Lucina, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Roland, priest of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the ninth day before the Kalends of February, in the first indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation [Col. 1028C] 1153, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Anastasius IV.

### XXXVIII. Privilege for the nunnery of the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete.  
*(Lateran, January 26.)*

[ABAELARD, *Works*, 353.]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ HELOISE, abbess, and the other sisters devoted to divine service, present and future, in the oratory of the Holy Spirit situated in the district of Troyes, in the parish of Quincey above the river Arducon, etc. (as in the preceding letter of Eugenius III, given 1 November 1147—see *Patrologia*, vol. CLXXX [Col. 1028D]). From the gift of Walter Rungifer: four arpents of meadow and four arpents of land, forty solidi of rent, and labor-services, etc. From Godfrey the moneyer: ten solidi of rent; from Fulcher Pentecost: whatever he had in the oven of the freehold. Fifty solidi of rent from the deceased Stephen the vicar and his nephew Andrew. Five solidi of rent from the deceased Aalis. Ten solidi of rent from Peter of the Gate. Whatever you possess at Sulimatum and at Pontem. From the wife of Walter of Fontenay: twenty solidi of rent in the lands of Coriletum. The places of Triagnel, Pomarium, and Leavalle, as they have reasonably been granted to you, etc.

[Col. 1029A] Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Kalends of February, in the second indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1153, in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Anastasius IV.

### XXXIX. He confirms to the Church of St. John of Kaltenbrunn the church of Revigne and other goods, donations, tithes given, acquired, or to be acquired.  
*(Lateran, January 29.)*

[*Thuringia sacra*, 307.]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GODESCALC, provost, and his brethren in the church of St. John the Evangelist of Kaltenbrunn [Col. 1029B], who profess the canonical life, present and future, in perpetual memory.

As the authority of the sacred canons teaches, holy places are to be transferred for three reasons. Recognizing that two of these applied to the church of Revigne—namely, the inconvenience of the place and the danger posed by robbers—Otto, formerly bishop of Halberstadt, of good memory, transferred and changed the estates of the aforesaid church to Kaltenbrunn, with the common consent of the brethren, for the greater fruit of divine service. Therefore we, whose particular concern it is reasonably to confirm what is done by our brethren and to promote pious desires with fitting support, confirm by this present decree that transfer made for the aforesaid reasons, and decree that it shall remain ratified [Col. 1029C] in future times.

Moreover, following in the footsteps of our predecessors of blessed memory, Calixtus, Honorius, Innocent, and Eugenius, Roman pontiffs, we decree that the order of canonical life which you have professed in that church shall be observed there for all time, and we fortify the same place, with all its appurtenances, under the protection of blessed Peter. Furthermore, whatever possessions or goods have lawfully been bestowed upon that place from their own right by the noblemen Hermann and Wichmann, or by any other faithful persons, or may hereafter, by God’s gift, be justly and canonically bestowed, shall remain forever firm and inviolate for you and your successors. We also confirm for you, and through you for the church itself, by the strength of our favor, the tithes which Rainard, Otto, and Udelric, bishops of Halberstadt [Col. 1029D], are known to have granted to your church.

Upon the death of you, the provost of that place, or of any one of your successors, let no one be placed over it by any craft of deception or violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall provide to be elected according to God and the Rule of Blessed Augustine.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish it, or harass it with any rash vexations; but that all things be kept whole for the uses of those for whose governance and support they were granted [Col. 1030A], with every benefit, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the bishop of Halberstadt.

But if any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, etc. I, Anastasius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of St. Calixtus. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of St. Chrysogonus. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of St. Angel. I, Aribertus, cardinal priest of the title of St. Anastasia. I, Octavianus, cardinal priest of the title of St. Cecilia. I, John, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, title of Pammachius. [Col. 1030B] I, Hugh, bishop of Ostia.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the sixth day before the Kalends of February, in the second indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1153, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Anastasius.

### XL. He confirms the goods, possessions, and immunities of Saint-Germain-des-Prés.  
*(Lateran, January 31.)*

[BOUILLARD, *History of Saint-Germain-des-Prés*, Documents, p. 38.]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons JOSFRED, abbot of St. German, formerly bishop of the city of Paris [Col. 1030C], and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

The granting of effect to just petitioners is required alike by the force of equity and the order of reason, especially when piety aids the petitioners’ wish and truth does not abandon it. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the monastery of Blessed German of the Meadows, in which you are devoted to divine service; and we confirm it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by God’s favor, acquire through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings [Col. 1030D] or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Moreover, we confirm by apostolic authority to you, and through you to your church, every liberty and dignity bestowed upon your monastery by Childebert, Clothar, and other kings of the Franks and confirmed by their privileges; and we decree that it shall remain ratified forever. We command, moreover, that chrism, holy oil, consecrations, ordinations, and whatever else you may require from pontifical ministry shall not be denied to you or your successors by any Catholic bishop. We strictly forbid any bishop or clergy of the Church of Paris to conduct Masses, ordinations, or stations in that monastery [Col. 1031A] contrary to the will of the abbot or the community. Nor do we grant them authority to perform anything there, to forbid them divine offices, to excommunicate them, or to summon to synod the abbot or monks, priests or clerics of the churches of that place.

We add also that, in the parish churches which you hold, priests shall be chosen by you and presented to the bishop; if they are suitable, the bishop shall commit the care of souls to them, so that they answer to him concerning the care of the people, but render to you due subjection concerning temporal matters belonging to the monastery. Every abbot, beloved son in the Lord Josfred, who after you is elected by the community of the monastery entrusted to you according to the Rule of Blessed Benedict [Col. 1031B], shall receive blessing from the Roman pontiff or from whichever Catholic bishop he prefers who enjoys the favor and communion of the Apostolic See.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish it, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things be preserved unimpaired and whole, for the uses of those for whose governance and support they were granted, with every benefit, saving, of course, the authority of the Apostolic See.

But if any person in the future, etc.

I, Anastasius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have signed. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum, have signed. [Col. 1031C] I, Hugh, bishop of Ostia, have signed. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of St. Calixtus, have signed. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of St. Chrysogonus, have signed. I, Hubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of St. Praxedis, have signed. I, Aribertus, cardinal priest of the title of St. Anastasia, have signed. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of St. Marcellus, have signed. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Pastor, have signed. I, Octavianus, cardinal priest of the title of St. [Col. 1031D] Cecilia, have signed. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, have signed. I, Rodulfus, cardinal deacon of St. Lucy in Septa Solis, have signed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of St. Angel, have signed. I, Guido, cardinal of St. Mary in Portico, have signed. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of St. Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have signed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Kalends of February, in the sixth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1153, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Anastasius IV.

### XLI. He grants Wibald, abbot of Stavelot, the use of a ring for life only.  
*(Lateran, February 7.)*

[MARTÈNE, *Amplissima Collectio*, II, 572.]

[Col. 1032A]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son, the abbot of Corbie, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The Apostolic See has always bestowed more abundant honor upon prelates of churches whom it has recognized as bound to itself by fuller charity, and has more readily assented to their honorable requests. Accordingly, moved by the ancient devotion which you are known to have borne toward the Apostolic See, and inclined by the prayers of certain of our brethren, we have judged that the use of a ring [Col. 1032B] should be granted to you alone for your lifetime, out of the customary kindness of the Apostolic See; and, as an increase of our affection, we also send you a ring through our beloved son G., cardinal deacon, whom we are dispatching to the regions of the German kingdom for the interests of the Church. Therefore let your devotion receive this benefit with such thanksgiving, and always show yourself so fervent in reverence for your most holy mother, the Roman Church, that we may rejoice to have bestowed upon you this sign of charity and beneficence, and that you may at all times be found worthy of obtaining other benefits.

Given at the Lateran, on the seventh day before the Ides of February.

### XLII. He confirms the regular discipline, possessions, and privileges of the canons of Pistoia.  
*(Lateran, February 8.)*

[ZACHARIA, *Anecdota medii aevi*, 232.]

[Col. 1032C]

ANASTASIUS, etc., to his beloved sons GERO, provost, and the other brethren of the canonry of Pistoia, etc.

The desires of petitioners must always be fulfilled whenever they seek things that do not depart from reason. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and, following the examples of our predecessors of blessed memory, Alexander, Urban, Lucius, and Eugenius, Roman pontiffs, fortify by the authority of our privilege the order of canonical life which you have professed [Col. 1032D]. By this present decree, therefore, we establish that no living person may separate you and your successors from the communion of the canonical life; nor may any one of you, after profession, freely depart from the community and follow the precepts of a more relaxed life. Accordingly, we decree that if any of you should depart from his purpose, no person ought to oppose you or your successors, or the others who preside, in correcting him and restraining him according to the discipline of the Rule.

Upon the death of you or of the other rulers of your canonry, let no one be placed over it through any craft of deception or violence, except one whom the regular brethren, in the fear of God, shall elect—whether from among themselves, if they find such a man among themselves, or from outsiders if necessary—with the counsel of the bishop who [Col. 1033A] has been canonically elected and ordained through the Roman Church, etc. [Note: [Col. 1033D] The remainder is the same as in the privilege of Eugenius III for these same canons. See *Patrologia*, vol. [Col. 1034D] CLXXX, no. 456.]

I, Anastasius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, GG., cardinal priest of the title of St. Calixtus. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of St. Chrysogonus. I, Ubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of St. Praxedis. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of St. Marcellus. I, Wido, cardinal priest of the title of Pastor. I, John, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul and Pammachius. I, Cencius, cardinal priest of the title of St. Lawrence in Lucina. I, Henry, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil. [Col. 1033B] I, Guido, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Portico. I, John, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Oddo, cardinal deacon of St. Nicholas in the Tullian Prison.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Roland, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the sixth day before the Ides of February, in the second indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1153, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Anastasius IV.

### XLIII. To the clergy and people of Dol.—Confirmation of Hugh, elected of Dol.  
*(Lateran, February 13.)*

[MARTÈNE, *Anecdota*, III, 896.]

[Col. 1033C]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the clergy, barons, and people of Dol, and to those established throughout the entire diocese of Dol, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Moved by the example of him who bore our infirmities and carried our sorrows in his compassion, we have judged that the bowels of pity should be opened to you and that, insofar as at present we could do so without prejudice to the peace of the Church, the grace of paternal consolation should be extended to your contrition and grief. Therefore, lest—God forbid—your church should utterly fail in temporal matters, we have entrusted their care and governance to our beloved son Hugh, your elect; and we command him diligently both to preserve the possessions it now has and to recover those which have hitherto been lost through the lack of pastoral care [Col. 1033D].

Since your assistance is known to be necessary to him for this purpose, by these present letters we command you to stand by our said son more diligently and assist him with all zeal in recovering and preserving the goods of your church. And just as R., your late archbishop of good memory, held those goods in peace, so may this man, with your support, be able to retain them. If any one of you has occupied anything from the goods of that church, let him restore it to our said son without trouble or contradiction. Otherwise let him know that he will incur the judgment of the strict Judge and the indignation of his apostles, blessed Peter and Paul [Col. 1034A].

Given at the Lateran, on the Ides of February.

### XLIV. To the archbishop of Tours.—That he observe the settlement made by St. Bernard.  
*(Lateran, February 13.)*

[Ibid.]

The pains and groans of the Church of Dol invite our mind to sorrow and compassion, and do not permit us long to withhold from it the consolation of charity. Moved by consideration of its lament, Pope Eugenius, our predecessor of happy memory, commanded by his letters the late Bernard, abbot of Clairvaux, of holy memory, to labor [Col. 1034B] for the establishment of peace between you and the Church of Dol and, according to the wisdom bestowed upon him from above, to allay in brotherly charity the controversy long agitated on both sides.

Therefore, after receiving assurance from your party and that church that what he should establish between you would be observed, that abbot, in the presence of our beloved sons [Note: [Col. 1034D] Perhaps Geoffrey, St. Bernard’s secretary.] G., a monk, and Nivard, the abbot’s brother, [lacuna; the following words are corrupt: “ger vi dit”] he established what he judged expedient. By these present letters we command your brotherhood to lay aside the severity of your will, considering that charity seeks not its own things but those of others, and to observe that settlement. Otherwise, since, while we have long withheld the water of mercy, all its spiritual goods are drying up [Col. 1034C], we do not wish your brotherhood to be ignorant that we shall open to that church the bosom of pity and, with the Lord as author, cure and heal its affliction. For the office of charity does not permit us, by preferring severity to gentleness, wholly to suffer so great a church to fail under this contention.

Given at the Lateran, on the Ides of February.

### XLV. He takes the Church of Pistoia under protection and confirms its goods and rights.  
*(Lateran, February 4.)*

[ZACHARIA, *Anecdota medii aevi*, 243.]

Anastasius, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother THRACIA and his successors canonically appointed [Col. 1034D], in perpetuity.

Since, by God’s disposition as has pleased him, we have undertaken the care of the universal Church, we ought to love our brethren, the bishops, with fuller charity and to fortify, with the protection of the Apostolic See, the churches entrusted to their governance. Thus, while both they and the churches committed to their rule remain under apostolic protection and obtain the patronage of the Prince of the Apostles against the assaults of evil men, they may devote themselves more earnestly to the discharge of their office, and the Lord’s sheep entrusted to their pasture may continually gather more abundantly and peaceably with them for the food of life, the vexations of evil men having ceased [Col. 1035A].

Therefore, venerable brother in Christ Thracia, bishop of Pistoia, induced both by consideration of your integrity and of the ancient devotion by which the Church of Pistoia has always continued in reverence and veneration of the Apostolic See, and following the example of our predecessors of happy memory, Innocent II, Anastasius, Alexander, Urban III, and Innocent III, Roman pontiffs, we receive that same church under the protection of blessed Peter and our own and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions or goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, with the Lord’s aid, acquire through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings [Col. 1035B] or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm, whole, and unimpaired for you and your successors.

We also decree that the bishopric of the diocese of Pistoia shall continue, without the molestation or disturbance of others, in the right and jurisdiction of the bishop of Pistoia, just as its boundaries have been defined by the privileges of our aforesaid predecessors. Within those boundaries the following chapels and churches are known to be situated: the chapel of Capraria; the chapel of the Hospital of Rosaria; the parish church of Massa; the chapel of Vincio; the chapel of Bucuniano; the chapel of Castello Nuovo; the chapel of St. Martin on Monte Culli; the chapel of St. Mary Magdalene in Colle; the chapel of Varezzano; the chapel of Venua, concerning which the sentence of our aforesaid predecessor Urban was issued after the third and fourth hearing; the chapel of the Hospital of Fanano; the chapel of the bishop’s meadow; the chapel of Rotie; the chapel of Cerbaria; the chapel of Monte Acuto; the chapel of Insula; the chapel of St. Saviour situated in a meadow by the river Bisenzio [Col. 1035C]; at Cojano; and also the estate called Pavana in the county of Pistoia, with the castle of Sambuca built on the boundaries of the estate. We confirm these to the holy Church of Pistoia, as they are known to have been restored, after an action long examined by many judges and jurists, from Countess Matilda of venerable memory, daughter of blessed Peter, by the judgment of Bernard, then cardinal priest of the Holy Roman Church and vicar of the aforesaid Pope Paschal, into the hands of Ildebrand, your predecessor of worthy memory [Col. 1035D], and his brethren.

Furthermore, let no one ever presume to alienate from the right of the church and the uses of the clergy the tithes of Monte Murlo, Prato, St. Paul, Colonica, Monte Magno, Lamporecchio, Creti, and Spanarecchio, which the diligence of your aforesaid predecessor recovered from the hands of laymen. We command the same regarding the other estates and properties which today remain in the possession of the Church of Pistoia: namely, Lizzano, Mammiano, Cavinana, Batoni, Saturnana, Groppule, Pescia, Vinacciano, Tobiana, Publica, Silva Mortua, Petanense, Celleri, and the land situated within the bishopric of Bologna, which was held by the men of Valle Liderla, and the estate of Spallioffo.

Furthermore, we confirm to you [Col. 1036A] the parish church of St. Hippolytus in Alpe; St. Lawrence; that on Monte Murlo; that of Viliano; St. Quiricus; that on Monte Spanarecchio; that in Saturnana; that of Brandellio; that of Cavinana; St. Marcellus; that of Lizzano; that of Popillio; that of Piteglio; that of Furfalo; that of Celle; that of Calloria; that of Vinacciano; that of Massa; that of Creti; that of Lamporecchio; that of Limite; that of Artimino; that of Saiano; that of Quarrata; that of Montemagno; that of Tobiano; St. Hippolytus; St. Paul; that of Aiolo; St. Justus; that of Colonica; and, at Prato, the parish church of St. Stephen.

In addition, we decree that, by occasion of the privilege which the people of Prato rejoice to have obtained from us [Col. 1036B], no injury, diminution, or disobedience shall be inflicted upon their mother, the Church of Pistoia, or upon any of the aforesaid parish churches—namely St. Paul, St. Hippolytus, St. Peter of Aiolo, St. Justus of Colonica—or upon any other in any respect. Nor may the Church of Prato or the clergy of that place use that writing against the right, dignity, or obedience due to the Church or bishop of Pistoia. Rather, as was the case in the time of our predecessors Urban, Paschal, Innocent II, and others, and also of Peter and Ildebrand, bishops of Pistoia of good memory, so the aforesaid Church of Prato shall remain obedient and subject in all things to the Church of Pistoia or its bishop, without any diminution of authority or dignity.

We further prohibit anyone from daring to establish anew a church or oratory in your bishopric without the assent of you or your successors, saving the privilege of the Roman Church. It shall also be lawful for you and your successors to establish baptismal churches in the same diocese if necessity appears to require it [Col. 1036C].

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no one at all rashly to disturb the aforesaid Church of Pistoia, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish it, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things be preserved whole and unimpaired for the benefit of you, your brethren, and the poor, saving the authority of the Apostolic See. But if any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, etc. [Col. 1036D]

I, Anastasius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Hicmarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Ugo, bishop of Ostia. I, BB., cardinal priest of the title of St. Calixtus. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of St. Chrysogonus. I, Manfredus, cardinal priest of the title of St. Sabina. I, Aribertus, cardinal priest of the title of St. Anastasia. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of St. Marcellus. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Pastor. I, Octavianus, cardinal priest of the title of St. Prisca. I, Henry, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. [Col. 1037A] I, Oddo, cardinal deacon of the title of St. George at the Golden Veil. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Portico. I, Yacynthus, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Cosmedin, have signed. I, Gerardus, deacon of St. Mary in Via Lata. I, Oddo, cardinal deacon of St. Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have signed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of March, in the fourteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1153, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Anastasius IV.

XLVI. Privilege granted to Peter the Venerable concerning the controversy that had existed between the abbot of Miratoire and the brethren of the monastery of Gigny, judicially settled by the supreme pontiff himself. (Lateran, 16 February.)

*[Bullarium Cluniacense, 63.]*

[Col. 1037B]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son PETER, abbot of Cluny, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Whenever any matters are concluded judicially in our presence, it is fitting, lest what is done be brought into doubt, that they be committed to the record of letters for the security of the parties. For concerning the controversy which was being conducted between our beloved son Eustorgius, abbot of Miratoire, and your brethren of Gigny, over the injuries inflicted upon them by the brethren themselves, both you and the abbot himself appeared in our presence [Col. 1037C], and the case was for a long time handled and diligently examined before us and our brethren. Therefore, having heard the allegations of both parties and fully understood their arguments, after taking counsel with the brethren we have adjudged that the aforesaid abbot of Miratoire shall restore to you and to your monastery, without objection, by the first Kalends of August, seventeen thousand solidi of Lyons currency, which you had given him, although for peace, yet under compulsion. Thereafter, he shall cause the things carried off by the same brethren of Gigny to be restored by the judgment of our beloved son Odo, cardinal deacon and legate of the Apostolic See; and we nevertheless command that compensation be made for the injuries inflicted upon that abbot, or that justice concerning them be rendered to him. [Col. 1037D]

Let absolutely no person, therefore, be permitted to infringe or in any way disturb the ruling of this our determination by rash presumption. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, unless, having been admonished a second or third time, he corrects his presumption by due satisfaction, let him suffer the loss of his rank or be punished by the penalty of excommunication.

I, Anastasius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Calixtus. I, Hicmarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Censius, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina. [Col. 1038A] I, Rodulphus, cardinal deacon of Saint Lucy in Septa. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Hubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Manfredus, cardinal priest of Saint Sabina. I, Julius, cardinal priest of Saint Marcellus. I, Bernardus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Pastor. I, Aribertus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia. I, Jordanus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna. I, Astaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Prisca. I, Geraldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, Octavianus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, GG., in the Roman Church. [Col. 1038B] I, John, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, John, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Silvester and Martin.

Given at the Lateran by the hands of Roland, cardinal priest of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of March, in the second indiction, in the year 1154 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of lord Pope Anastasius IV.

XLVII. Privilege granted to the bishop of Bergamo. (Lateran, 23 February.)

*[Lupi, Codex diplomaticus Bergomensis, II, 1119.]*

[Col. 1038C]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother GIRARD, bishop of Bergamo, and to his successors canonically appointed, in perpetual remembrance.

Established, by the Lord’s disposal, on the lofty watchtower of the Apostolic See, we ought, by the office entrusted to us, to love our brother bishops and preserve for the churches committed to them by God their rights. Therefore, beloved brother in the Lord, Bishop Girard, following the example of our predecessor of blessed memory, Pope Innocent, and providing with paternal concern for the Church of Bergamo over which, by God’s authorship, you preside, we decree that whatever possessions and goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter, by the Lord’s bounty, acquire by reasonable means, shall remain secure and inviolate to you and your successors. [Col. 1038D] Moreover, the present and future canons of Saints Vincent and Alexander shall render canonical and due obedience to you and your successors, nor shall they withhold it under pretext of a privilege received from the Apostolic See. They, indeed, and all other clerics of your bishopric are to know that by this document of our decree all power is forever removed from them to alienate in any manner, without the knowledge and consent of you and your successors, the possessions of churches pertaining to your jurisdiction. Yet this is to be understood so that you ought not, through malice or perversity, to refuse your consent if the clear and evident advantage and necessity of those churches requires it.

[Col. 1039A]

We decree, therefore, that absolutely no person may rashly disturb the Church entrusted to you, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass them with any vexations; but that all things be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, etc.

I, Anastasius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, GG., cardinal priest of the title of Calixtus, have subscribed. I, Astaldus, cardinal priest of Saint Prisca, [Col. 1039B] have subscribed. I, Oddo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Roland, cardinal priest of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the seventh day before the Kalends of March, in the second indiction, in the year 1153 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of lord Pope Anastasius IV.

A lead seal suspended on silk threads.

XLVIII. To the bishop of Toulon—on behalf of the monks of Saint Victor, toward whom he had shown himself hostile. (Lateran, 1 March.)

*[Marten, Amplissima Collectio, I, 826.]*

[Col. 1039C]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother W. [Note: [Col. 1039D] William II of that name, who governed the bishopric of Toulon from 1117 to 1165, having been taken from the monastery of Saint Victor at Marseille, as appears from this letter—a fact hitherto unknown to the historians of Provence.] bishop of Toulon, greeting and apostolic blessing.

If any spark of charity had remained in you, and if you had not forgotten the Rule of monastic profession, you would love your brethren, the monks of Marseille, and would strive to inflict no injury upon them. For behold, as we have learned from their account, you unjustly take from them the tithes of the church of Saint John of Petrafoci; and furthermore, concerning the church of Saint Pontius of Colubreira, you do not fear to inflict considerable injury upon them, since, although those who choose to be buried have free burial in their churches, you rashly oppose it. Since, therefore, you appear to depart from the union of brotherly charity, [Col. 1039D] and do not cease to persecute those whom you ought, as far as you are able, to defend against others, we command you by apostolic letters that, if what the aforesaid brethren have laid before our ears is true, you shall henceforth not presume to inflict on the aforesaid brethren any injury or annoyance in the churches mentioned, or in any manner prevent those who have chosen burial among them. Otherwise, know that for their defense, as persons known to belong properly to the right of blessed Peter, we shall set ourselves up as a most secure wall against those [Col. 1040A] who presume to assail them.

Given at the Lateran, on the Kalends of March.

XLIX. At the request of Archbishop Engelbald, he confirms the Church of Tours as metropolitan of Dol and of the other bishops of Lesser Brittany. (Lateran, 3 March.)

*[Marten, Thesaurus Anecdotorum, III, 894.]*

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother ENGELBALD, archbishop of Tours, and to his successors canonically appointed, in perpetuity.

The order of justice and reason counsels that he who desires his commands to be observed by his successors should preserve the will and enactments of his predecessors. For our predecessor of blessed memory, Pope Innocent, committed to Geoffrey, formerly bishop of Chartres and then legate of the Apostolic See, for investigation and decision the controversy long disputed between the pastors of the Churches of Tours and Dol over the primacy of the Church of Tours and the subjection of Dol. [Col. 1040B] Although it had been argued in his presence in several places in Gaul and had not yet been duly concluded, the archbishop of Dol came before that same predecessor of ours, complaining that he had often been burdened by delay in the case and had incurred many expenses on that account. He therefore humbly requested that our predecessor recall the case to his own presence and impose its due conclusion. Assenting to his petition, our predecessor commanded your predecessor Hugh by apostolic letters to present himself before the apostolic tribunal, prepared to demonstrate the right of his church on this matter. [Col. 1040C]

When meanwhile, by divine judgment, he had entered upon the way of all flesh, both that archbishop and the bishop of Dol presented themselves before our predecessor of blessed memory, Pope Lucius, for the settlement of the same controversy. After many arguments, documents, and proofs concerning the right of his church had been produced, there was at last brought forward the privilege of our predecessor of good memory, Pope Urban. It plainly contained that, after many discussions and reconsiderations of this matter in [Col. 1040D] his own presence and also in that of legates of the Apostolic See, after carefully examining the writings of the Roman pontiffs Nicholas, John, Leo IX, and Gregory VII, and after thoroughly investigating everything on both sides, that pope had decreed, by the common counsel of his brother bishops and many clerics of the Roman Church, and confirmed by the authority of his writing, that henceforth both the bishop of Dol and the other Breton bishops should recognize the Church of Tours as their metropolitan and always show it due reverence; and that, after the death of Roland, then presiding over the Church of Dol, no bishop of Dol should aspire to the use of the pallium at any time thereafter.

To this the bishop of Dol answered nothing supported by reason, nor could he defend his side by the authority of any Roman pontiff. Therefore, after hearing the allegations of both parties and carefully examining the writings of the Roman pontiffs on behalf of the Church of Tours, the aforesaid Pope Lucius, our predecessor, having taken counsel in an assembly of his brother bishops, cardinal priests and deacons, and many other noble Roman citizens, confirmed the same judgment by apostolic authority; and he invested both the archbishop and the Church of Tours by his own hand, with the staff, with obedience from those bishops. [Col. 1041B] He commanded, in accordance with the tenor of that judgment, that both the bishop of Dol and all the bishops of Lesser Brittany thereafter should be subject to the Church of Tours as to their own metropolitan, and should humbly render it due obedience and reverence; and that no bishop of Dol should thereafter presume to aspire to the use of the pallium, but, as has been said, should recognize the Church of Tours as his own metropolitan and reverently obey it. Pope Eugenius of holy memory confirmed the same thing by a document of his own.

Therefore we, who, though unworthy, have been established by the Lord’s ordering in the seat of justice, neither wish nor ought to depart from the path of truth; following in the footsteps of those same predecessors of ours, we confirm the same judgment by the authority of the Apostolic See granted to us by God and strengthen it by the protection of this present writing. [Col. 1041C] If, therefore, etc.

SAINT PETER. SAINT PAUL.

POPE ANASTASIUS IV.

Place of the monogram.

KEEP ME, O LORD, AS THE APPLE OF THE EYE.

L. Privilege to the brethren of Cluny concerning the church of Rocaboviscurti, over the controversy between them and the clerics. (Lateran, 4 March.)

*[Bullarium Cluniacense, 64.]*

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the monks of Cluny dwelling in the church of Rocaboviscurti, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The controversy being conducted between you and the clerics of the church in which you are established, concerning the right of ownership of that church, we have committed to our venerable brethren G. . . bishop of Limoges and B. . . bishop of Saintes for hearing and decision. Therefore, by these present letters we command you that, when you are summoned by them on this matter, putting aside all pretext you shall appear before them and shall accept and observe without objection whatever they shall judge between you.

Given at the Lateran, on the fourth day before the Nones of March.

*[Ughelli, Italia Sacra, IV, 365.]*

[Col. 1042D]

The subscriptions are as follows.

LII. To the monks of Nonantola—so that, upon the death of Albert, they may elect a new abbot. (Lateran, 8 March.)

*[Tiraboschi, Storia di Nonantola, II, 265.]*

[Col. 1043B]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons A., prior, and the whole convent of the monastery of Nonantola, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We sympathize with paternal affection over the ruin and destitution of your monastery, and, according to the duty of our office, so far as with God we are able, we exercise diligent care and attentive concern for its restoration. We have learned from your letters and from brother R., whom you sent to our presence, that after the death of A., your abbot of good memory, you have carefully considered appointing a pastor for yourselves [Col. 1043C] and wish to unite in support of a person. This is pleasing to us, and we commend your zeal in the Lord. But because we do not have the requisite knowledge of the person whom you wish to elect, and our brethren, who knew him more fully, advised that they should by no means consent to him; and because the aforesaid brother R. was in no way adequate to pursue so important a business, we could neither receive nor ought to have received your petition at present.

Therefore, by these present letters we command you to unite in choosing a learned and honorable person fit to govern so great a monastery, and, through W., one of the worthier persons of your monastery, take care to make known to us your unanimous and concordant election concerning that person. Confer also upon them authority and power, if perhaps you cannot assemble in the aforesaid meeting, to elect or receive from us a person who may profit and preside over you, and to bring him back to you after he has been confirmed and blessed by us in the office of abbot. [Col. 1043D]

Given at the Lateran, on the eighth day before the Ides of March.

LIII. He confirms the possessions and immunities of the Church of Gerberoy. (Lateran, 14 March.)

*[Louvet, Antiquités du Beauvoisis, I, 665.]*

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons EUSTACE, dean of the church of Gerberoy [Col. 1044A], and his brethren, present and future, canonically appointed, in perpetuity.

Whenever a request is made to us that is recognized as suitable to religion and uprightness, it is fitting that we grant it willingly and give consent appropriate to the petitioners’ desires. Therefore, beloved sons, we graciously assent to your petitions and take the aforesaid church, in which you are devoted to divine service, under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and strengthen it by the present document; decreeing that whatever possessions or goods it now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings and princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, with the Lord’s permission, acquire, shall remain secure and inviolate to you [Col. 1044B] and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by name:

The church of Rotengy, with the great and small tithe and all its appurtenances; half the tithe of Collignie; the tithe of Tillet; a third part of the tithe of the estate of Saint-Denis; the churches of Vuabesio, of the chapel, of Sullies, of Saint Samson, and of Saint Audoenus; the jurisdiction which you possess at Sonions and at [lacuna], and the estate called Ons at Senentes and at Wuardes. In the estate of Bray and at Curteum, likewise the tithe on transport dues, the toll on passage at Gerberoy, Sonions, and Ons, and the earthworks in the suburbs.

Furthermore, we confirm by apostolic authority the freedom which Guy, formerly bishop of Beauvais, of good memory, granted to you, the canons, and to your church, and confirmed by his document, so that it may not be displaced from its condition by the rash assault of anyone or by the passage of time. [Col. 1044C]

By this present decree we also establish that no one shall have a prebend in your church except one who is willing to serve it in person. Likewise, a chaplain, in the place of the lord who may be there at the time, shall not altogether cease from the office of chaplain; and we forbid him to hold the chaplaincy and a prebend of your church together with that chaplaincy. Moreover, we decree, confirm by apostolic authority, and forbid that your prebends be divided; rather, they shall remain in their full integrity.

We decree that absolutely no person may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass them with any vexations; but that all things be kept intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and instruction they were granted. [Col. 1044D]

We forbid anyone ever to impose new and unlawful exactions upon your church or its chapels, or to burden your persons with unlawful levies and services, saving, of course, the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. As a sign of the protection received from the Roman Church, you shall pay one bezant each year to us and our successors.

If, however, etc.

[Col. 1045A] I, Anastasius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Hicmarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Hugh, bishop of Ostia. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of the Church of the Savior. I, Hubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of the Church of Praxedes. I, Manfredus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Firmina. I, Ausbertus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia. I, Octavianus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint [lacuna]. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Rodulphus, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Lucy [lacuna]. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Mary in Portico [lacuna]. I, Oddo, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Nicholas [lacuna]. I, Astaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Prisca. [Col. 1045B] I, John, cardinal priest of the title of the Brethren [lacuna].

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Roland, cardinal priest of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the second day before the Ides of March, in the second indiction, in the year 1155 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of lord Pope Anastasius IV.

LIV. He confirms the very generous donation of the monastery of Saint Peter of Landelina, of the Order of Saint Benedict, in the diocese of Nocera, made to the prior and canons of the cathedral church of Foligno by the counts Monaldus, son of Bucci, Rodulfus, son of Lambert, and Count Gentilis, son of Alberic.

[Col. 1046A]

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Roland, cardinal priest of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of April, indiction [lacuna], in the year 1153 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of lord Pope Anastasius IV.
