LVII. Privilege for the nunnery of Saint Firmus of Plorizano. (Lateran, 19 March.)

*[Lupi, Codex diplomaticus Bergomensis, II, 1117.]*

[Col. 1046C]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, LICIA, abbess of the monastery of Saint Firmus of Plorizano, and her sisters, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetual remembrance.

To prudent virgins who, under the religious habit, render a service pleasing to God, our protection ought to be afforded, so that they may persevere more firmly in their religious purpose insofar as they have been more earnestly fortified by apostolic protection against the storms of worldly waves. Therefore, beloved daughters in [Col. 1046D] Christ, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the patronage of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God being favorable, acquire, shall remain secure and inviolate to you and to those who succeed you. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by name:

[Col. 1047A]

The church of Saint Martin; the land which you possess in the place called Plorizano; other land in the place called Istrata; the land which you possess at Redona; the house which you possess at Somvicum, with its vineyard. We also forbid absolutely any layman to presume to demand tithes from you or take them forcibly. But if anyone should presume to attempt this and, after admonition, scorn to make amends, let him be struck by the sentence of anathema.

We decree, therefore, that absolutely no person may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass them with any vexations; but that all things be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. [Col. 1047B]

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, etc.

I, G., cardinal priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus, have subscribed. I, Hubaldus, cardinal priest of Saint Praxedes, have subscribed. [Col. 1047C] I, Manfredus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina, have subscribed. I, Bernardus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement, have subscribed. I, Aribertus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Pastor, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Susanna and Felicity, have subscribed. I, Henricus, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal priest of Saint John, of the title of Pammachius, have subscribed. I, Octavianus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia, [Col. 1047D] have subscribed. I, Oddo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Rodulphus, cardinal deacon of Saint Lucy in Septisolium, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Angelo, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed. [Col. 1048A] I, John, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Oddo, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Roland, cardinal priest of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of April, in the second indiction, in the year 1153 of the Lord’s Incarnation [Note: [Col. 1047D] Although this bull of Anastasius gives the year 1153 in its chronological notes, it nevertheless belongs to the following civil year, 1154. Both the name of the supreme pontiff and the second indiction, which was then current in that year, indicate this beyond doubt. The Florentine year [Col. 1048D] did not begin until the eighth day before the Kalends of April, or later; this was the year employed in this pontiff’s diplomas.], in the first year of the pontificate of lord Pope Anastasius IV.

LVIII. He confirms the possessions and rights of the monastery of Saint Mary of Pomposa. (Lateran, 19 March.)

*[Muratori, Antiquitates Italicae, V, 431.]*

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons JOHN, abbot of the monastery of Saint Mary, [Col. 1048B] situated on the island of Pomposa, and to his brethren, present and future, regularly appointed, in perpetuity.

Apostolic protection ought to be present for those choosing the religious life, lest perhaps the assault of any rashness either recall them from their purpose or—God forbid—break the strength of sacred religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, and, following in the footsteps of our predecessors of blessed memory, Celestine and Eugenius, Roman pontiffs, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the monastery of Pomposa of the Blessed Mother of God and ever-Virgin Mary, in which you are devoted to divine service, [Col. 1048C] and fortify it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions and places that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, with the Lord’s aid, acquire, shall remain secure and inviolate to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by name: namely, the whole of Massacella [Note: [Col. 1048D] As in the bull of Pope Calixtus II. See *Patrologia*, vol. CLXIII.], etc.

Furthermore, in the diocese of Concordia, the church of Saint Martin in Phana. In the diocese of Ceneda, the church of Saint Peter in Colosis and that of Saint Daniel. In the same diocese, the church of Saint Andrew in Bosco with its chapels; another church of Saint Martin in Cambernardi; [Col. 1048D] Saint Mary in Ronchu Marzollu; Saint Mary in Vidore; Saint Bona with its chapels; Saint Mary in Castello; and others which you possess in those regions. In the diocese of Vicenza, the church of Saint Mary in Teupisse. In the city of Verona, the church of Saint Matthew. In the diocese of Brescia, the churches of Saint Mary of the See of Marculfus, Saint Mary of Cucumare, and Saint Mary of Suxiliano. In the diocese of Cremona, the church of Saint [Col. 1049A] Stephen in Caballaria. In the diocese of Asti, the churches of Saint Mary of Flexu and Saint John of Cerro. In the diocese of Bologna, the churches of Saint Mary of Arzellata, Saint Venantius, Saint Blaise of Luzaco, Saint Mark in Turrixella, Saint John in Castagnolo, Saint Blaise in Saliceto, and another church in Granarolo. In that same city, the church of Saint Syrus. In the city of Modena, the church of Saint Mary. In the castle of Soliera, the church of Saint John, and in its village the church of Saint Michael. At Ferrara, the church of Saint Agnes. At Finale, that of Saint Michael. At Ustulati, the church of Saint Peter. At Faenza, the church of Saint Clement. At Prato, the church of Saint Lawrence. In the diocese of Livy, the church of Saint Mary in Manumizola, the church [Col. 1049B] of Saint Michael, and Saint Mary the New with its chapels. At Rimini, Saint Mary in Tribbo. In the diocese of Urbino, the church of Saint Leo of Folia, Saint Angelo of the Island, Saint Mary of Petra, Saint Martin in Ulmeta, Saint Raclianus, and Saint Angelo in Preverzum; the church of Saint Mary in Castagneto with its chapels; the church of Saint Mary of Viculo with its chapels; the church of Saint John of Prugneto with its chapels; and the church of Saint Mary of the castle, Saint Martin, with its chapels. But chrism and holy oil from the bishop of Comacchio [Note: [Col. 1049D] See the same work.], etc.

I, Anastasius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed.

Fare well.

[Col. 1049C] I, Hicmarus, bishop of Tusculum, have subscribed. I, the bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Callixtus, have subscribed. Given at the Lateran through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of April, in the second indiction, in the year 1153 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Anastasius IV.

## LIX. He confirms the regular discipline and possessions of the churches of Carcassonne. (Lateran, April 5.)

[BOUGES, *History of Carcassonne*, 528.]

[Col. 1050B]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother PONTIUS, bishop of Carcassonne, and to his successors canonically instituted, for perpetual remembrance.

The order of justice and reason urges that one who desires his own ordinances and commands to be observed by his successors should preserve, strengthen, and confirm by his own stability the ordinances and commands of his predecessor. Therefore, graciously assenting to the just petitions of the regular canons of your church, after the example of our predecessor Pope Urban of blessed memory, we confirm by the authority of the Apostolic See the establishment of the regular order which your predecessor Peter, bishop of good memory, is known, with the Lord’s help, to have ordained at the mother church of Saint Nazarius and [Col. 1050C] at the churches of Saint Mary or Blessed Stephen; and we decree that it shall remain valid for all time.

We establish that whatever possessions or goods the aforesaid churches now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter acquire, by grant of pontiffs, bounty of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, with God’s favor, shall remain firm and unimpaired for those churches, to benefit in every way the needs of the clergy and of those serving God there under the observance of the regular life. Moreover, we forbid either you, your successors, or any ecclesiastical or secular [Col. 1050D] person to overthrow those canonries or remove the order of regular life established there, without prejudice to the authority of the Apostolic See. If, therefore, anyone, etc.

SAINT PETER. SAINT PAUL. POPE ANASTASIUS IV.

I, Anastasius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Hicmarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Hugh, bishop of Ostia. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Laboch. I, Octavianus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. [Col. 1051A] I, Joannes, cardinal priest of Saints John and Lamachius.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the Nones of April, in the second indiction, in the year 1154 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Anastasius IV.

## LX. He receives the monastery of Fruttuaria under the protection of Blessed Peter, confirms its goods—among which he enumerates the church of Saint Daniel at Venice—and grants other privileges. (Lateran, April 6.)

[CORNELIUS, *The Church of Venice*, IV, 187.]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons RUFINUS, abbot of Fruttuaria, and his [Col. 1051B] brethren, both present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

[Note: [Col. 1051D] Neither Mabillon in the *Annals of the Order of Saint Benedict* nor Ugh. in his treatment of the bishops of Ivrea makes any mention of this diploma. From it we learn that in ancient times the more illustrious monasteries had the form of a congregation, comprising numerous smaller monasteries subject to their jurisdiction. [Col. 1052D]]

A pious request should be brought to its intended effect by a favorable fulfilment, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth laudably and the benefit sought may assuredly gain strength. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves the monastery of Fruttuaria, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing.

We establish that whatever goods and possessions that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by grant of pontiffs, bounty of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, [Col. 1051C] with the Lord’s help, shall be preserved firm and unimpaired to you and your successors forever. Among these we have added the following, to be specified by their proper names: in the city of Asti, the church of Saint Secundus; near the village of Sollariense, the church of Saint John; near Morozio, the church of Saint Blaise; near Quadraginta, the church of Saint Benignus; at Villa Nuova Faloa, in the city of Pavia, the church of Saint Matthew; in the archbishopric of Milan, near the castle of Paternianum, the church of Saint Nicholas; near the castle of Cantorium, the church of Saint James; near Cuzatum, the church of Saint Gervasius; at Ganne, the church of Saint Gemulus and the church of Vulturnus; in the bishopric of Lodi, near the castle of Paudum, the church of Saint Peter; in the city of Vercelli, [Col. 1051D] the church of Saint Faith; near Genoa, at Cape Faro, the church of Saint Paul; in the city of Savona, the church of Saint George; in the bishopric of Alba, the castle of Serre-Longue and, by the wall, the church of Saint Mary; in the district of Ivrea, near the castle of Clevascio, the church of Saint Martin; near Ferrara, the church of Saint Romanus; in the bishopric of Bologna, the monastery of Saint Bartholomew, the church of Saint Peter Decaron, the church of Saint Mary of Villa Nova, and the church of Saints Simon and Jude. Above the bank of the Ticino, in the place called Brinate, the church of Saint Martin; in the place [Col. 1052A] of Paternianum, the church of Saint Martin of Ublate; the church of Daniel at Venice; and the church of Saint Agatha in the bishopric of Treviso.

Upon the death of yourself, the abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it by any artifice of intrusion or by violence, except one whom the brethren, by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall provide to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict. The person elected shall be ordained by the Roman pontiff or by whichever Catholic bishop he may prefer.

You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and ordinations of monks to be promoted to holy orders, or of clerics belonging to the monastery, from whatever Catholic bishop you choose, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what is requested. [Col. 1052B] We grant the same also concerning the cells situated under the said monastery, if the bishops of the respective dioceses should refuse to provide freely and without abuse those things which belong to the episcopal office.

Furthermore, we establish that no bishop shall have authority to impose any burdens upon the aforesaid place of Fruttuaria, or to pronounce a sentence of excommunication or interdict against the abbot, monks, or clerics of that monastery. We also forbid tithes of revenues from demesne lands cultivated either at Fruttuaria or elsewhere by you or your brethren to be exacted from you by bishops or their officials. We decree that burial in that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and [Col. 1052C] last will of those who have decided to be buried there, unless they happen to be excommunicated.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all things be preserved intact, for the complete benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, without prejudice nevertheless to the authority of the Apostolic See. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, etc.

I, Anastasius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint Sergius at the Golden Veil. [Col. 1052D] I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Callixtus. I, Guido, cardinal priest of Saint Chrysogonus. I, Hubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes, have subscribed. I, Manfredus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina. I, Aribertus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Pastor. [Col. 1053A] I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest of the holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the eighth day before the Ides of April, in the second indiction, in the year 1154 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Anastasius IV.

## LXI. He commands the archbishop of Braga to render due obedience to J[oannes], archbishop of Toledo, as primate, within thirty days. (Lateran, April 8.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 782.]

How great a crime contempt of the Apostolic See is held to be is shown by the prophetic words where it is written: “To rebel is the sin of divination, and [Col. 1053B] refusal to comply is as the crime of idolatry” (1 Kings 15). Likewise, Blessed Gregory says concerning those disobedient persons who stubbornly resist the commands of the Apostolic See: “Whoever refuses obedience to apostolic commands ought to be cast down in sorrow at his own ruin; he should have no place among priests, but should be excluded from the sacred ministry.”

How frequently and how strictly you were admonished by our predecessor Pope Eugenius of holy memory to render to the archbishop of Toledo, as your primate, due reverence and obedience, and how you obeyed him—on account of which, before complying with his commands, you incurred a second sentence of suspension for your disobedience and stiff-neckedness—ought not to have [Col. 1053C] escaped your memory. But, as we have learned from the complaint of our venerable brother I. . . . . ., now archbishop of Toledo, after you had become certain of the death of that same predecessor of ours, you utterly refused to render him the obedience which you had rendered to R., the predecessor of the same archbishop; failing to consider that by the death of one man the firmness of the apostolic Rock is neither broken nor changed.

Accordingly, by these present letters we command and direct you to approach our aforesaid brother I. . . . . ., archbishop of Toledo, without excuse, and render him the obedience due to him as your primate. If you neglect to fulfil this within thirty days after receiving these letters, know that from that time you are suspended from episcopal office.

Given at the Lateran, on the sixth day before the Ides of April.

[Note: [Col. 1053D] There follow other letters of the same pontiff to the same archbishop of Braga and to the archbishop of Tarragona, in which he most severely rebukes them for having withdrawn themselves from the authority of the archbishop of Toledo, primate of the Spains; and then letters to Hyacinthus, cardinal deacon and legate in Spain, concerning the recall to duty of those archbishops who refused to obey the archbishop of Toledo as primate. [Col. 1054D]]

## LXII. He commands Hyacinthus, cardinal and legate, concerning the submission of the archbishop of [Saint James] of Compostela to the primacy of the archbishop of Toledo.

[MANSI, ibid.]

[Col. 1053D]

Since we have commanded our brother of Compostela either to obey him as his primate or, under your judgment, to render him full satisfaction in justice, we nevertheless command your charity that, should this our brother refuse to submit to the uncertainty of judgment, [Col. 1054A] you summon both parties before you; and, after fully hearing and ascertaining the arguments of each side, determine that what accords with equity and reason shall be observed. Otherwise, make him humbly obey that man as his primate.

## LXIII. To Richard, abbot of Savigny.—He confirms to him the abbeys subject to the monastery of Savigny. (Lateran, April 20.)

[MARTÈNE, *Thesaurus Anecdotorum*, I, 433.]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son RICHARD, abbot of Savigny, and to his successors to be regularly promoted, in perpetuity.

The authority of the Apostolic See, over which by divine grace we preside, admonishes us to establish religion pleasing to God and, once established, to preserve it with diligent care. Accordingly, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Richard, we graciously assent to your just petitions and strengthen, by the protection of our writings, the monastery of Savigny, over which, by God’s grace, you are known to preside. We establish that the monastic order according to the order of the Cistercian brethren shall be inviolably observed in future times both in the aforesaid monastery and in those houses which stand under its authority and discipline; and that the abbeys known to belong by right to your monastery shall remain in the obedience and subjection of you and your successors. Their names are set down as follows:

[Col. 1054C] The abbey of Belbreh, and the abbey of Briostel with their appurtenances; the abbey of Sarnago; the abbey of Brollio; and the abbey of La Trappe with their dependencies; the abbey of Saint Andrew of Goffert; and the abbey of Saint Clement of Tyrunhel with their dependencies; the abbey of Falcardimont with its dependencies; the abbey of Luncuiler with its appurtenances; the abbey of Chalocheio with its appurtenances; the abbey of Busseria with its appurtenances; the abbey of Fontibus with its appurtenances; the abbey of Veteri-Villa with its appurtenances; the abbey of Alnetum with its appurtenances; the abbey of Fuanesium; the abbey of Holanda; the abbey of Caldra; and the abbey of Man with their appurtenances; the abbey of Bella-Lauda; and the abbey of Joreval with their appurtenances; [Col. 1054D] the abbey of Cumbra-mara; the abbey of Basinwerch; the abbey of Saint Mary of Durelina; and the abbey of Pultuna with their appurtenances; the abbey of Bildwas with its appurtenances; the abbey of Neth with its appurtenances; the abbey of Buffestren with its appurtenances; the abbey of Quarraria; and the abbey of Drogonis-fonte with their appurtenances; the abbey of Straforth with its appurtenances; and the abbey of Quoquosala with its appurtenances.

We therefore confirm these abbeys with all their appurtenances to you and your [Col. 1055A] successors forever, after the example of our predecessor Pope Eugenius of holy memory. Let no person, therefore, dare to disturb your monastery with respect to this our confirmation or inflict upon it any opposition on that account; rather, let all things be preserved forever unimpaired, as the charter of our aforesaid predecessor is known to have established, without prejudice in all things to the authority of the Apostolic See.

If anyone knowingly presumes rashly to contravene this page of our privilege, after a second or third warning, unless he makes suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer; and at the last judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance. [Col. 1055B] But may those who preserve for that place what belongs to it obtain, through the merits and intercession of Blessed Peter and Paul, the rewards of eternal life from the Lord, the rewarder of all good things. Amen, amen, amen.

KEEP ME, O LORD, AS THE APPLE OF THE EYE. SAINT PETER. SAINT PAUL. POPE ANASTASIUS IV.

I, Anastasius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Hicmarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Oddo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Callixtus. I, Hugh, bishop of Ostia. I, Cencius, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina. [Col. 1055C] I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Hubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon and bishop-elect of Sabina. I, Joannes, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, have subscribed. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus, have subscribed. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, Wido, cardinal priest of the title of Pastor, have subscribed. [Col. 1055D] I, Astaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Prisca, have subscribed. I, Henricus, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of May, in the second indiction, in the year 1154 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Anastasius IV.

## LXIV. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Mary of Prato. (Lateran, April 20.)

[*Bullarium Cluniacense*, 64.]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 1056A] sons Theobald, prior of Saint Mary of Prato, and his brethren, both present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

It is fitting to give ready assent to religious desires, so that faithful devotion may attain a swift result. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, graciously assenting to your just petitions, we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We establish that whatever possessions and goods the monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by grant of pontiffs, bounty of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, with God’s [Col. 1056B] favor, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have considered it proper to specify the following by their proper names.

The borough in which the monastery itself is situated, together with Mount Curio and all its other dependencies; and whatever parochial benefice you possess throughout the whole parish of the castle of Donzy and the village of Saint Mary of Prato, together with the chapel of Bronzilia and everything that you possess in that village and the other surrounding hamlets; whatever you possess by parochial right in the village of Poniaco and certain other neighboring hamlets; half the tithe of your whole parish; the entire lesser tithe of lambs and wool from your village; the chapel of Saint Mary in the castle of Donzy, with the adjoining houses in which the priest [Col. 1056C] Vitalis resides; half the salt revenue from the market of that same castle of Donzy; the church of Saint Martin with half the tithe of the holding of Merillus; half the whole territory of Lueth, with the tithe which belonged to Bernard de Galis; two mills and one [lacuna] at the bridge; two parts of the mill of Bumont, both in grain and fishing rights; two new mills; the mill of Albicastellum; the land of Saint Martin; the land of Tripaldus; the tithe of Cartis, together with that which belonged to Arnulf; the tithe of Chevenci; the tithe of Bergenis; the tithe of Paludis; the wood called Chassaneium; the forest called Solua; the enclosed estate of Viliscordon, with the use of the adjoining forest for the benefit of the enclosure and of the houses there, and all else that you possess there; the village [Col. 1056D] of Bretinolis with all its appurtenances and the parochial right you possess in it; the tithe of Cavannis; half the tithe of the oven of Maanes; whatever you possess at Fontanas; the village of Fontaney with all its appurtenances; the church of Pomaeus with half of all its revenues; whatever you possess at Valcheri; whatever you possess at Melcharaldus; whatever you possess at the village of Generia; whatever you possess at Ulmus; the forest called Fais; the church of Bois with half the dues of that village; and all the tithes which you possess in that parish and its other dependencies, two parts of the lesser tithe of that parish, from lambs, wool, and pigs; the village of Villader with all its dependencies; the chapel of Saint Martin; the two [Col. 1057A] vineyards which you possess in the valley of Aliniac, with the meadows and other things which you possess there; the dependent priory of Chasneium with all its dependencies, and the village of Belregart; the church of Saint Aricius with half of all its revenues; the dependent priory of Molummis, which is of your freehold, with all its dependencies; the church of that village, in which you possess half of all the revenues; the territory of Maort; the dependent priory of the valley of Dosia, with woods, meadows, a mill, and all other dependencies, all of which are of your freehold; half the tithe of that same village, in which you possess half of all the revenues; and the church of Colummeria.

In the bishopric of Autun: the dependent priory of Luciac, with meadows, fisheries, a mill, and pasturage also through all [Col. 1057B] the meadows of that riverbank at all times for the riding horses of the prior of the same place. We likewise confirm to you the church of that village with half of all its revenues and certain tithes, and whatever you possess at Cervon. Moreover, we confirm to you by apostolic authority the liberty which you possess in temporal matters, and all those things which your monastery is known to possess by the gift of Hervaeus, lord of Donzy, of good memory, as contained in the document of his donation. We likewise confirm to you the reasonable and ancient customs which your monastery is known to possess.

Furthermore, by this present decree we firmly prohibit bishops, their vicars, or any other persons from having authority to take away from you, or to appropriate, the goods and possessions of your priests which they have acquired from the benefices of the churches [Col. 1057C] belonging to you, except those which bishops have voluntarily left to them. Accordingly, we establish that no bishop may, on account of an offence committed by you or those belonging to you, place your lands or churches under interdict, or forcibly take away what belongs to you by right, until you are prepared to render justice in the presence of the same bishop or of the metropolitan.

We also decree and establish by the authority of the Apostolic See that no one shall answer for violation of your cemetery except to you and your church. Your churches and chapels shall be free and exempt from every exaction, [Col. 1057D] except the customary episcopal *parata* and jurisdiction over priests who have offended against the dignity of their order; the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical jurisdiction of the diocesan bishop being, of course, preserved. You may also choose priests in your churches, provided that they receive the cure of souls from the bishops without payment; that they answer to the bishop concerning the care of the people; and that, concerning temporal goods belonging to the monastery itself, they render you due subjection. Certainly, no one may presume to exact tithes from you on the produce which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or from the sustenance of your animals.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may [Col. 1058A] rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things be preserved intact, for the complete benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, without prejudice in all things to the obedience due to the abbot of Cluny, to whose right and ownership your monastery is known to belong. If, therefore, anyone in the future, etc.

I, Anastasius, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Callixtus. I, Hicmarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Hugh, bishop of Ostia. I, Cencius, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. [Col. 1058B] I, Radulphus, cardinal deacon of Saint Lucy in Septa. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Joannes, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Hubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Manfredus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Pastor. I, Jordanus, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Susanna and Felicitas. I, Octavianus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Astaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Prisca. I, Gerardus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, Henricus, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. [Col. 1058C] I, Joannes, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of May, in the second indiction, in the year 1154 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Anastasius IV.

## LXV. He confirms the judgment delivered by Eugenius III in the dispute between the canons of Saints Alexander and Vincent at Bergamo. (Lateran, April 21.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia Sacra*, IV, 462.]

[Col. 1058D] ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons LANFRANC, provost, and the other canons of the church of Saint Alexander of Bergamo, in perpetuity, etc.

Just as it is equitable and fitting to a religious office to decide controversies arising among ecclesiastical persons by a reasonable conclusion, so the force of equity requires that matters reasonably decided be entrusted to written record and, lest they later be disturbed by anyone’s opposition, be strengthened by apostolic authority. Therefore, desiring to provide for your peace and tranquillity, we also confirm by this charter of our own attestation, and decree to remain valid and unshaken forever, the judgment which our predecessor Pope Eugenius of happy memory, [Col. 1059A] after sufficient examination in his presence and that of his brethren of the same cause, and after taking counsel with them, pronounced between you and the canons of Saint Vincent concerning certain matters over which litigation between you and them had long continued.

He decreed that the priests of the bishopric of Bergamo who were ordained after the judgment issued by Pope Innocent, our predecessor of happy memory, or who shall subsequently be ordained, shall render fealty to both churches; and that, should the canons of Saint Vincent perhaps refuse to receive it, they shall nevertheless be bound to render it to your church. Concerning penances, he ordered this observance between you: whenever priests of the whole bishopric of Bergamo bring their parishioners to penance for public crimes, [Col. 1059B] they shall endeavor to summon both parties; and no penance shall be imposed upon those offenders without the presence of your provost or one of the priests of your church.

He also added that, at the bishop’s table, the provost of your church shall occupy the first place on the left side and shall have his clerics beside him. He further established that whenever, in the customary processions for celebrating the solemnities of Mass, the canons of Saint Vincent come to your church, they shall peacefully occupy the four walls of the choir in that church; and that on the vigils and feast of Blessed Viator, and likewise in the Gregorian litanies, you shall honorably receive the same canons through your representatives, with incense and holy water and with bells rung. But when they assemble with you in that church for the funeral rites of the dead or on other days, you shall occupy the entire choir of your church together with them. Whenever you meet with them at solemnities or funerals, whether in the church of Saint Vincent or elsewhere, [Col. 1059C] the provost of your church shall occupy the first place on the left side of the choir; the remaining brethren shall sit jointly with those clerics.

Likewise, he decreed that the chaplains of the churches of Saint Saviour, Saint Agatha, Saint John, Saint Grata, and Saint Vigilius shall assemble at your church for the principal Masses on Sundays and major feasts. On the Lord’s Supper, at Baptism, and at other solemnities, you shall observe in peace at all times the manner in which you have customarily celebrated the divine [Col. 1059D] offices.

Furthermore, since certain priests create delays in rendering to you the aforesaid fealties and presume to defer them by evasions, we establish by apostolic authority that, according to the ancient custom of your church, they shall render them to you immediately upon receiving orders; and if they disdain to render them at once, they shall be excluded from the orders they have received until they do render them. By this present decree we also establish that the bishop of Bergamo shall impose upon you no undue or unusual burden, but shall leave you and your church in your ancient liberty.

Therefore, lest you be wearied anew by recurrent litigation concerning matters decided between you by the judgment of the Apostolic See, [Col. 1060A] and lest one party thereby bring the other to expense and labor, concerning which perpetual silence has by judicial order been imposed upon both parties, we forbid by apostolic authority any person whatsoever to presume to act against the judgment of our aforesaid predecessor or against this charter of our confirmation and constitution by rash daring. Whoever presumes to attempt this shall incur the indignation of almighty God and of His apostles, Blessed Peter and Paul. Amen. Amen. Amen.

Place of the seal. KEEP ME, O LORD, AS THE APPLE OF THE EYE.

I, Aribertus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Pastor, have subscribed. I, Bernard, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement. I, Jordanus, cardinal priest of Saints Susanna and Felicitas, have subscribed. I, Astaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Prisca, have subscribed. [Col. 1060C] I, Gerardus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill, have subscribed. I, Joannes, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius, have subscribed. I, Henricus, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus, have subscribed. I, Joannes, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Sylvester and Martin, have subscribed. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Rodulfus, cardinal deacon of Saint Lucy in Septasol, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Joannes, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, [Col. 1060D] have subscribed. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest of the holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the second day before the Kalends of May, in the second indiction, in the year 1154 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Anastasius IV.

## LXVI. Bull for the monastery of Saint Salvius of Montreuil. (Lateran, April 24.)

[*Gallia Christiana*, X, Documents, 314.]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons EUSTACHIUS, abbot of the monastery of Saint Salvius of Montreuil, and his brethren, etc. . .

In these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names. [Col. 1061A] The altar of St. Mary of Darnestal, and the whole tithe in the village of Monsterol; the altar of St. Winwaloe, free from every exaction. In the same village, the altar of St. Peter with the whole tithe; the altar of St. Judoc and the whole tithe; the altar of St. Wulflagius and the whole tithe; the altar of St. Martin of Escuignecourt and the whole tithe; the altar of St. Peter of Wally; the altar of St. Mary of Airon; the tenants, woodland, and land; the altar of St. Vedast of Escuir and the whole tithe. In the same village, tenants and arable land, and the woods called Sudoye, Osanne, Caisnoy, and Vellegny, by gift of Count Herlewin; the altar of St. Albin and half the allod, as it was granted to you free of charge; likewise the allod of Walter Hurupel and a fourth part of the wood called Waltestrens; the tithe [Col. 1061B] of Abboltineil; the altar of St. Crispin of Campengnol; at Vilernel, a third sheaf of the tithe.

In the aforesaid village of Monsterol: allods, mills, butchers’ stalls, an oven, the passage at Novaevilla, and sixty shillings at the king’s gate; also the fishery from Altim to Brimoniacum, the fishpond of Escuriol, the lower meadow, and the whole Marest as far as Escuir; the altar of St. Winwaloc of Belmery and the whole village, with its mill, marshy places, cultivated and uncultivated lands, and woods; a fourth part of Concil and a sixth part of Arry; and the whole village called Long Meadow, with its tenants, woods, meadows, cultivated and uncultivated lands, and a third part of fifteen saltworks in the village called Rua, with arable land; and in Nigromont [Col. 1061C] three and a half saltworks.

In the village of Maire, one tenant; at Maregni, part of the allod of Baldwin the clerk; at Verton, tenants, saltworks, arable land, and the right to gather wood, by gift of Robert, king of the French, from the feast of St. Martin until the middle of May, from all carts and wagons, asses and ships, and from all who sell wood in the same castle, whether townsmen or outsiders; likewise a fourth part of the allod of Dourriers (otherwise Daminois) and of Fraisnis; the comital jurisdiction throughout all your land between Quantia and Alteia, and beyond Alteia, as Count Wido granted it to you; likewise the land of Albin, a mill, and woodland.

In the parish of Thérouanne: the altar of St. Martin of Caveron and the whole [Col. 1061D] tithe; the altar of St. Winwaloe and the whole tithe; the altar of St. Dionysius of Walbertcort; and the altar of St. Vedast; also the entire village of Caveron, with two mills, cultivated and uncultivated lands, meadows and woods, and comital jurisdiction; a fourth part in the village called Ghisi, with woods and meadows; likewise a sixth part of Contis. In the holding of Galami, a third part both of the village and of the mill, woodland, and arable land; at Montegny, three holdings; at Tigny and Colinas, a third part of two tenants; at Novavilla, land for half a plough-team and meadows; the village of Silviniacum; and, in the village of Judei, one holding; and one church in the village called Farnerias, with three resident householders and arable land; a certain part of the village of Totendal with [Col. 1062A] woodland. In the village of St. Mary, tenants, arable land, and woodland; in the village of Hodie, half of one mill and arable land, likewise the land of Frenc and comital jurisdiction; in the village of Cormunt, one tenant; at Botin, one tenant; at Wis, two tenants; at Staplas, four tenants, three water-rights, and two nets; at Boxin, the allod of Ramelm; in the town of London, the altar of St. Lawrence with many tenants, and in the territory of that city the chapel of Cochenech with land for two plough-teams; and at Cochessella and Stambriga, the tithe from the land of Wiard Pointel; in the parish of Norwich, part of the manor of Wirham with its church, arable land, sake and soke, and the chapel of the same village; in the village of Fillebi, land yielding twenty shillings, and two thirds of the whole [Col. 1062B] tithe of the holding of Honestanestone; and in the diocese of Lincoln, the right of passage at Gernic. The governance of all the schools of Monsterol and the anointing of the sick of the same town. We therefore decree, etc.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Roland, cardinal-priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the eighth day before the Kalends of May [24 April], in the second indiction, in the year 1154 from the Incarnation of the Lord, in the first year of the pontificate of Pope Anastasius IV.

## LXVII. He receives under protection the charitable hospital of Piacenza and confirms its goods and privileges.  
*(Lateran, 24 April.)*

[CAMPI, *History of Piacenza*, II, 353.]

[Col. 1062C] ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons OTTO, rector of the Hospital of Mercy, and his successors to be regularly appointed, in perpetuity.

Although by the kindness and goodwill of the apostolic see we ought to protect all the children of the Church, we are especially bound to provide more attentively for those known to minister humbly and devoutly to almighty God in the service of the poor and pilgrims, and to fortify their establishments with the shield of our protection, lest they be troubled by the molestations of wicked men. Thus, just as by God’s ordinance we are called fathers in name, so also may we be proved such in deed. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, [Col. 1062D] we graciously grant your just requests and, following the example of our predecessor of holy memory, Pope Eugenius, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid hospital over which, by God’s grace, you are known to preside, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same hospital now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, God being favourable, through grants of popes, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these, we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The place in which the hospital itself is situated, with all its appurtenances; the mill; and [Col. 1063A] the lands which you possess around that place; and the house which you hold beyond the Po in the diocese of Lodi, with its appurtenances. Moreover, we confirm and decree shall remain firm and unshaken, by authority of the apostolic see, for you and your successors and for the same house, the laudable rule known to have been established in that house by Hugh, its founder of good memory, and by other prudent and discerning men, and confirmed by Arduino, bishop of Piacenza, of good memory. We likewise confirm what the aforesaid bishop granted to the said hospital: namely, that no one from the Church of Piacenza shall in any way demand an oath of fealty from the priests dwelling there and in the church of St. Giles, which belongs to that hospital. Further, no one whatsoever shall presume to demand tithes from you on newly cleared lands (novalia) which your brethren hereafter cultivate with their own hands or at their own expense, or from the increase of your animals.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid hospital, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that everything be preserved intact for your use and for the use of Christ’s poor, for whose governance and support these things were granted, and wholly serve those purposes, the authority of the apostolic see being preserved. If anyone therefore in future, etc.

I, Anastasius, bishop of the catholic Church, [Col. 1063C] have subscribed.

*(The subscriptions of the cardinals follow; they are omitted for the sake of brevity.)*

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Roland, cardinal-priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the eighth day before the Kalends of May [24 April], in the second indiction, in the year 1154 from the Incarnation of the Lord, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Anastasius IV.

## LXVIII. He confirms the possessions and goods of the monastery of St. Peter of Flavigny.  
*(Lateran, 24 April.)*

[PÉRARD, *Collection of Documents Serving the History of Burgundy*, p. 236.]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son RAINALD, abbot of the monastery of St. Peter [Col. 1063D] of Flavigny, and to his brethren, present and future, professed in perpetuity in the religious life . . . . . . . .

Both the force of equity and the order of reason require that just requests be granted effect, especially when piety assists the petitioners’ wish and truth does not desert it. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously grant your just requests and, following in the footsteps of our predecessor of blessed memory, Pope Calixtus, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the monastery of St. Peter of Flavigny, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions or goods the aforesaid monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, God being favourable, through grants [Col. 1064A] of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these, we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

Namely, the church of St. George of Colticum and its borough; the church of St. Mary of Sinemur; with its parish; the church of the Holy Trinity of Prisciac; the church of St. Genesius of Flavigny and the revenues of the litanies belonging to the same monastery; the church of St. Symphorianus of Griniac; the church of St. Germanus of Vitellum; the church of St. Bandelius of Vuabra; the church of St. Benignus of Sirriac; the church of St. Martin of Massiniac; the church of St. Regina of Joliac; the church [Col. 1064B] of St. Martin of Villiac; the church of St. Benignus of Darriac; the church of the Holy Saviour of Magtinile; the church of St. Anhymus of Cancellis; the church of St. Marcellus of Glennone; the church of St. Sulpicius of Fontanis; the church of St. Martin of Chichiac; and the church of St. Peter of Puteoli, with the tithes belonging to those churches.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the same monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that everything be preserved intact and fully benefit the uses of those for whose support and governance these things were granted, with, to be sure, the canonical rights of the diocesan [Col. 1064C] bishops reserved. Upon the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it by any cunning or violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall provide to be elected, from their own community or, if possible, from another, according to God and the Rule of St. Benedict. If anyone therefore, etc.

I, Anastasius, bishop of the catholic Church. I, G. G., cardinal-priest of the title of St. Calixtus. I, Guido, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Chrysogonus. I, Ubaldus, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Praxedes. I, Manfredus, cardinal-priest of the title of St. [Col. 1064D] Sabina. I, Aribertus, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Anastasia. I, Guido, cardinal-priest of the title of Pastoris. I, Jordanus, cardinal-priest of the title of SS. Susanna and Felicitas. I, Gerardus, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, Joannes, cardinal-priest of the title of SS. John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius. I, Hicmarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Cincius, bishop of Porto and St. Rufina. I, Gregorius Miron, bishop-elect of the church of Sabina. I, Rodulphus, cardinal-deacon of St. Lucy in Septasol. [Col. 1065A] I, Joannes, cardinal-deacon of SS. Sergius and Bacchus.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Roland, cardinal-priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the eighth day before the Kalends of May [24 April], in the second indiction, in the year 1154 from the Incarnation of the Lord, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Anastasius IV.

## LXIX. Bull issued to Alan, bishop of Auxerre—It confirms his right concerning the abbot of St. Germanus.  
*(Lateran, 25 April.)*

[*Gallia Christiana*, XII, 123.]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother ALAN, bishop of Auxerre, and to his successors canonically appointed, in perpetuity.

[Col. 1065B] We desire that matters known to have been carried out by our predecessors through judgment or agreement should remain in their stability, so that henceforth they may obtain greater force through the protection of our confirmation. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Bishop Alan, favourably granting your just petitions, we, following in the footsteps of our predecessor of holy memory, Pope Eugenius, confirm by the authority of the apostolic see the agreement which he is known to have made concerning the dispute over the monastery of St. Germanus between Hugh, your predecessor of good memory, and our beloved son Peter, abbot of Cluny, and the monks of St. Germanus. We command that in the abbey [Col. 1065C] of St. Germanus no abbot shall in any way be elected without the counsel of the abbot of Cluny; but you and your successors shall have full authority canonically to approve or reject the person elected and, if he is worthy, to bless him as abbot. Once blessed, he shall promise obedience to the bishop of Auxerre. His deposition too, if—God forbid—he should prove to be such a person as requires it, shall be carried out by judicial procedure; and the canonical correction both of the abbot and of the monks shall likewise belong to you. The abbot and monks of St. Germanus shall receive from the bishop of Auxerre, as their diocesan, chrism, holy oil, the consecration of altars or churches, and the ordination of monks or clerics to be advanced to holy orders, until they obtain the favour of the apostolic see.

Moreover, following the enactments of our aforesaid predecessor Pope Eugenius, we confirm by the text of this present writing that what the aforesaid abbot of Cluny has done for the abbot of St. Germanus concerning investiture by the staff shall not hereafter prejudice you or your church, or bring it any harm; and we forbid any future abbot of St. Germanus to receive investiture by the staff from the abbot of Cluny. But if anyone knowingly and rashly attempts to act against the text of this our confirmation, let him incur peril to his rank and office, or suffer final punishment, unless he corrects his presumption by suitable satisfaction.

I, Anastasius, bishop of the catholic Church. [Col. 1066A] I, B., cardinal-priest of the title of St. Calixtus. Guido, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Chrysogonus. Umbaldus, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Praxedes. Aubericus, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Anastasia. Julius, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Marcellus. Jordanus, cardinal-priest of the title of SS. Susanna and Felicitas. I, B., cardinal-priest of the title of St. Stephen on the Caelian Hill. Joannes, cardinal-priest of St. John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius. Joannes, cardinal-priest of the title of SS. Silvester and Martin. Imarus, bishop of Tusculum. [Col. 1066B] Hugo, bishop of Ostia. Censius, bishop of Porto. Gregorius, cardinal-deacon and bishop-elect of Sabina. Rodulphus, cardinal of the title of St. Lucy in Septasol. Guido, cardinal-deacon of St. Mary in Portico. Joannes, cardinal-deacon of SS. Sergius and Bacchus. Oddo, deacon of St. Nicholas in the Tullian Prison.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Roland, cardinal-priest and chancellor of the Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Kalends of May [25 April], in the second indiction, in the year 1154 from the Incarnation of the Lord, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Anastasius IV.

## LXX. He confirms the privileges and possessions of the Church of Bordeaux.  
*(Lateran, 25 April.)*

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 783.]

[Col. 1066C]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers GAUFRID, archbishop of Bordeaux, and his suffragan bishops of Agen, Angoulême, Saintes, Poitiers, and Périgueux, and to all abbots established throughout the same province, present and future, in perpetuity.

Whenever, through the provision of Catholic rulers, any church is freed from the servile conditions imposed by secular men and is granted welcome liberty, it especially devolves upon the Holy Roman Church, mother of all Christ’s faithful, to take care and act diligently so that what is known to have been done for the honour of God and the welfare of his Church may be strengthened by apostolic authority in such a way that the Church of God, which seemed to have been restored to freedom, is not again burdened by anyone’s wickedness with renewed servile conditions. Accordingly, just as the catholic mother Church, etc., we, following in the footsteps of our predecessors of blessed memory—the Roman pontiffs Innocent, Lucius, and Eugenius—confirm by the assurance of our favour and command that it be observed as valid and inviolate in future times: namely, that both at the see of Bordeaux and in the other episcopal [Col. 1067A] churches and abbeys of the same province you shall enjoy canonical freedom in the elections of bishops and abbots, without an obligation of homage, oath, or a pledge of faith given by hand.

Further, we decree by apostolic authority, just as our predecessors established in general councils, that the property, goods, and all possessions of archbishops of Bordeaux, suffragan bishops, or abbots who die shall alike be preserved unimpaired and inviolate for the use of their successors. We also add that all churches within the aforesaid province shall possess their estates, possessions, and all things belonging to them whole and inviolate, in accordance with their privileges, legal rights, and good customs; and that, as stated, you shall enjoy canonical liberty in all matters concerning all their churches, their ministers, and your possessions, with the authority of the apostolic see reserved. Therefore no person may lawfully rashly disturb you or your churches concerning this our constitution, or inflict upon you any opposition arising from it. But if anyone with rash presumption attempts to oppose this our constitution, unless he suitably amends his offence, let him lose the dignity of his power and rank, incur the indignation of almighty God and of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul, and be subject to excommunication. Those who observe it, however, shall obtain the blessing and favour of those same apostles. Amen.

I, Anastasius, bishop of the catholic Church, have subscribed. [Col. 1067C] I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum, have subscribed. I, Cynthius, bishop of Porto and St. Rufina, have subscribed. I, W., cardinal-priest of the title of Calixtus, have subscribed. I, Hubaldus, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Praxedes, have subscribed. I, Manfredus, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Sabina, have subscribed. I, Aribertus, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Anastasia, have subscribed. I, Julius, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Marcellus, have subscribed. I, Rodulphus, cardinal-deacon of St. Lucy, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal-deacon of St. Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Oddo, cardinal-deacon of St. Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Roland, cardinal-priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, [Col. 1067D] on the seventh day before the Kalends of May [25 April], in the second indiction, in the year 1154 from the Incarnation of the Lord, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Anastasius IV.

## LXXI. To the archbishops of Besançon and Lyons—That they enforce the sentence of excommunication and interdict judicially pronounced by him against the abbot and brethren of Miratoire.  
*(Lateran, 25 April.)*

[D. BOUQUET, *Collection*, XV, 661.]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers H[UMBERT], archbishop of Besançon, and the archbishop of Lyons, salvation and the apostolic blessing.

[Note: [Col. 1067] Eraclius, who settled the lawsuit in the year 1155, as may be seen in the Sebusian Library.]

[Col. 1068A] Matters concluded in the Roman Church by judicial procedure ought to remain stable; and those who presume to violate them or in any way hinder their execution ought without doubt to be subject to severe punishment. Concerning the case being litigated between our beloved son Peter, abbot of Cluny, and Eustorgius, abbot of Miratoire, you should know that we have pronounced the following sentence by judicial procedure. We have adjudged that the abbot of Miratoire must repay to our aforesaid son, the abbot of Cluny, a sum of seventeen thousand shillings in Lyons currency. But because the aforesaid abbot of Miratoire, aggrieved by the sentence mentioned above, departed without obtaining leave, we have decreed, in order that our sentence may be fulfilled, that the same abbot of Miratoire and his brethren shall restore that money to the abbot of Cluny by the Kalends of August [1 August]. Otherwise, from that time, you are to know that both the abbot himself and his prior are bound by the bond of anathema, and that divine offices are interdicted in their church and among all their brethren and lay brothers, wherever they may be. Therefore, by apostolic letters we command you to ensure that the sentence of excommunication and interdict is firmly observed throughout your provinces until our command has been fulfilled.

Given at the Lateran on the seventh day before the Kalends of May [25 April], in the first year of our pontificate.

## LXXII. He affirms for the canons of St. Alexander their possession of the church of St. Michael of Virgis.  
*(Lateran, 30 April.)*

[LUPUS, *Diplomatic Codex of Bergamo*, II, 1127.]

[Col. 1068C]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons LANFRANC, provost, and the other canons of Blessed Alexander of Bergamo, salvation and the apostolic blessing.

If, in consequence of the care of all churches entrusted to us by God—who, although unworthy, are successors of blessed Peter, keeper of the keys of the kingdom of heaven and answerable to the Most High for all churches and ecclesiastical persons—we ought especially and willingly to confirm those things which our predecessors have reasonably decreed and to provide diligently lest they be changed in future times. For one who does not wish his own acts to be altered by successors ought to preserve inviolate the works and enactments of his predecessors and strengthen them by the protection of his approval. Moved therefore by the obligation of this reasoning, beloved sons in the Lord, favourably granting due assent to your reasonable requests, we also grant the church of St. Michael of Virgis, with all its appurtenances, which our predecessor Pope Innocent of venerable memory confirmed by his writing, and give it to be administered and governed perpetually under your authority. In recognition of this our grant and gift received from [Col. 1069A] the apostolic see, you shall pay to us and our successors each year twelve denarii of old Milanese currency. But if anyone knowingly attempts to act against this text of our grant and donation, after a second or third warning, unless he makes suitable satisfaction, if he is a cleric, let him be deposed from the office of his order; if a layman, let him be bound by the bond of excommunication.

Given at the Lateran, on the second day before the Kalends of May [30 April].

A lead bull is suspended on silken cords.

## LXXIII. Bull to Peter, bishop of Marseille.  
*(Lateran, 1 May.)*

[*The Antiquity of the Church of Marseille*, I, 473.]

[Col. 1069B]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother PETER, bishop of Marseille, salvation and the apostolic blessing.

A prudent and wise man strives to honour the ministry entrusted to him and to discharge the episcopal office committed to him in such a way that he is held blameless by all. But you, recently returning from the apostolic see, burdened the churches of our beloved sons, the brethren of the monastery of Marseille, apparently under the pretext of hospitality. For you tried to seek out your sheep not as a bishop but as a soldier, surrounded by a great crowd of soldiers and others, etc. Consequently, some of them, observing the burdens imposed on the others, were compelled to pay you an excessive sum of money and burden their churches so that they might be freed from your exactions. They add also [Col. 1069C] . . . that, although free burial has been granted to the same monastery by the apostolic see, you rashly forbade your priests to administer the Eucharist to anyone unless they had first, by an oath or surety, bound themselves never to be buried at the monastery of Marseille. Whether these are the acts of a bishop, consider for yourself from the statutes of the holy fathers; ask your elders, and rather learn from them matters in which, as the outcome of events clearly shows, you appear by no means to have been instructed, etc.

Given at the Lateran, on the Kalends of May [1 May].

## LXXIV. To William, bishop of Toulon, and Peter, bishop of Marseille.  
*(Fragment.) (Lateran, 1 May.)*

[Same source.]

[Col. 1069D]

ANASTASIUS, etc. . . . For they complain that you place their churches and the brethren dwelling in them under interdict, and compel them to come to your synods, although they are endeavouring to send to you their own priests who minister divine things to the people. Therefore, by these present letters we command you that, so long as they are willing to render you justice or send their priests to you when summoned, you are in no way to place their churches under interdict or compel [Col. 1070A] their monks to attend your councils.

Given at the Lateran, on the Kalends of May [1 May].

## LXXV. To Peter the Venerable—He revokes Peter’s grant or donation of certain priories and revenues to specified persons.  
*(Lateran, 1 May.)*

[*Bullarium Cluniacense*, 65.]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons PETER, abbot, and the whole chapter of Cluny, salvation and the apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1070B] From the customary clemency of the apostolic see and the good repute diffused from the manner of life of your predecessors, it has come about that the most holy Roman Church readily hears your church when it petitions, and, even when it does not petition, freely bestows gifts upon it as upon a special daughter. Yet we have learned from certain religious men that you, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot—at which we are greatly astonished—have conferred upon certain persons, partly by commendation and partly by gift, priories and certain revenues belonging to the conventual table, without the counsel and consent of your brethren: namely, upon our beloved son P . . . . ., abbot of Vézelay, the priory of Silviniac; upon the abbot of Clusinum, the priory of Cariloc; and upon the archdeacon [Col. 1070C] of Lyons, the priory of Vilereis. You are also said to have granted Master W . . . of Mutim. ten pounds in the chapel of the borough of Cluny, and Master O . . . . of Autun ten pounds in the priory of Magobrium.

Since we are the less willing to permit your church to sustain a diminution and loss of its goods because we see that your predecessors laboured more diligently for its advancement, we command you by these present letters to recall as speedily as possible to your uses and control all those revenues and priories that are found not to have been granted by your common counsel or consent, and to restore to their former state all things that have been unlawfully granted. We indeed annul such grants by apostolic authority, [Col. 1070D] and do not wish your revenues, especially those known to be assigned to your table, to be diverted without reason to others’ uses. Rather, we command that they be kept fixed and unchanged in their present condition; and, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot, by apostolic authority we forbid you henceforth to presume to attempt anything of this kind concerning those priories or revenues. Otherwise, fear that you will incur our displeasure and a grave loss of your office. We wholly remove from your successors any power to redirect revenues hitherto assigned to the brethren’s table to other uses without their consent.

Given at the Lateran, on the Kalends of May [1 May].

## LXXVI. To Theobald, prior of Blessed Mary of Prato at Donzy—He forbids anyone to establish a cemetery or baptismal font within the parish boundaries; and confirms the right held by the priory in the church of St. Caradoc.  
*(Lateran, 7 May.)*

[*Bullarium Cluniacense*, 66.]

[Col. 1071A]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son THEOBALD, prior of St. Mary of Prato, and to his successors regularly appointed, in perpetuity.

Whenever a request is made of us which is known to accord with reason and propriety, it is fitting that we grant it willingly and give suitable support to the petitioners’ desires. Therefore, beloved sons in [Col. 1071B] the Lord, granting your prayers, we utterly forbid by the authority of the apostolic see that any person shall ever be permitted to establish a cemetery or baptismal font within the boundaries of your parish. Moreover, we likewise confirm for you and your successors whatever you have hitherto justly and canonically possessed in the chapel of St. Caradoc, and decree that the monastery entrusted to you shall be preserved in future times. Therefore no cleric or layperson may rashly violate this text of our constitution or in any way oppose it. But if anyone presumes to attempt this, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his offence by suitable satisfaction, let him lose the dignity of his power [Col. 1071C] and rank; let him know that at the final judgment he stands guilty of the wrong committed; let him be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ; and let him incur the indignation of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul. Amen.

I, Anastasius, bishop of the catholic Church.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Roland, cardinal-priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the Nones of May [7 May], in the second indiction, in the year 1154 from the Incarnation of the Lord, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Anastasius IV.

## LXXVII. Privilege for the monastery of St. Eusebius, diocese of Apt.  
*(Rome, at St. Peter’s, 18 May.)*

[*Gallia Christiana*, new ed., I, in the text, p. 377.]

[Col. 1071D]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, greetings to the beloved abbot of St. Eusebius [Bertran], etc.

We decree that no archbishop or bishop whatsoever may extend the hand of excommunication or interdict against that monastery, its abbot, or its monks; rather, by the grace of almighty [Col. 1072A] God, the monks and monastery, together with the village, shall always remain peaceful, free, and exempt from every episcopal exaction or burden. We decree that whatever possessions or goods the same monastery now possesses, or may hereafter acquire, God being favourable, through grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure for you and your successors. Among these, we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The church of St. Michael of Avollaron and a fourth part of that castle; the church of St. Ferriol of Cavaillon; St. Mary of Costa, with chapel and village; St. Brice with its village; St. Saviour of Roura, with chapel, tithe, and village; St. Peter of Dena; St. Martin of Nogaret; St. Clement of Antrannis; St. Mary of Tudon; and a fourth [Col. 1072B] part of the castle called Villa Calcaria. The tithes of Signione, of the castle of Holy Cross, and of Codols. Further, we forbid by apostolic authority that any abbot or monk may presume to alienate, dispose of, pledge, or grant as a fief, rent, or benefice to any knight the treasures, honours, and possessions now held or hereafter to be acquired through the Lord’s bounty, etc.

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, through the hand of Roland, cardinal-priest and chancellor, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of June [18 May], in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1152 from the Incarnation of the Lord, in the year . . . of the pontificate of Pope Anastasius IV.

[Note: [Col. 1071D] The chronological notes must be corrected here: for the eleventh indiction one should read the second. This error perhaps arose because the number II, which in Roman arithmetical characters signifies two, denotes eleven in Arabic arithmetical notation. For [Col. 1072D] the year 1152 one should likewise read 1154, which corresponds to the second indiction. Certainly Anastasius IV could not have fortified the abbey of St. Eusebius with a privilege in 1152, since it is established that he did not ascend the see of St. Peter before 1153.]

## LXXVIII. He confirms the possessions and goods of the church of Blessed Mary of Reno.  
*(Lateran, 20 May.)*

[TROMBELLI, *Historical Memoirs of Reno*, 369.]

[Col. 1072C]

ANASTASIUS, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GUIDO, prior of the church of Blessed Mary of Reno, and his brethren, present and future, professed in the regular life, in perpetuity.

Religious persons who choose the religious life ought to have apostolic protection at hand, lest perhaps an attack of anyone’s rashness either call them back from their purpose or—God forbid—weaken the strength of sacred religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, following in the footsteps of our predecessors of blessed memory, Innocent, Lucius, and Eugenius, we graciously assent to your just requests and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid church of the Blessed Mother of God and ever-Virgin Mary, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this present document. First, indeed, we establish that the canonical order according to the Rule of Saint Augustine shall be observed there inviolate for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions or goods that same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, with God’s favor, acquire through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The church of Saint Saviour in the city of Bologna; at Turicella, the church of Saint Andrew; the church of Saint Domninus near Bagnum; the church of Saint Mary at Raticosa with its appurtenances; the church of Saint James called Casa Dei, with its appurtenances; and the bridge situated beside your church over the Reno, with its possessions.

We also forbid any brother, after making profession there, to dare to leave that cloister without the willing permission of the prior or the congregation; and let no one whatsoever receive one who departs without a common letter of authorization. But if any of those brothers should dare to remain outside the cloister without the aforesaid permission, and, having been admonished a second or third time, should perhaps scorn to repent, the prior of that place may pronounce upon him, as upon one professed to him, a sentence of excommunication. You shall also have free authority, without anyone’s objection, to receive for conversion clerics or free laymen living in the secular condition. Certainly, concerning the produce which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or the increase of your animals, let no one at all presume to exact tithes from you.

Receive holy oil and the ordinations of clerics to be promoted to sacred orders from the diocesan bishop, provided that he is Catholic, enjoys the favor and communion of the Apostolic See, and is willing to furnish these things freely and without any improper exaction. Otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what is requested. Upon the death of you, the present prior of that place, or of any one of your successors, let no one be put in charge there through any contrivance of fraud or violence, except one whom the brothers by common consent, or the sounder part of the brothers’ counsel, shall, according to the fear of God and the Rule of Saint Augustine, provide to be elected.

To this we further add and establish that it shall not be lawful for any archbishop, bishop, or any person whatsoever to make exactions in the aforesaid church of Blessed Mary or to impose burdens upon the prior and brothers. We also grant that the burial-place of that house shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict, while the right of the mother church is nevertheless preserved.

Therefore we decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb that church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but let all things remain whole and unimpaired, for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop.

If anyone therefore in the future, etc.

I, Anastasius, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum, have subscribed. I, Cinthius, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal priest of the title of Calixtus, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus, have subscribed. I, Hubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes, have subscribed. I, Manfredus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina, have subscribed. I, Aribertus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia, have subscribed. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Pastor, have subscribed. I, Bernardus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement, have subscribed. I, Octavianus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia, have subscribed. I, Astaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Prisca, have subscribed. I, Gerardus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, of Pammachius, have subscribed. I, Henry, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Sylvester and Martin, have subscribed. I, Rodulfus, cardinal deacon of Saint Lucy in Septa Solis, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed.
