The church of Boneio; the chapel of Doolvilla; and both the altar-gifts and the greater and lesser tithes of those same churches. The church of Purveis, with its altar and one half both of the tithes and of the alms given for the dead. Moreover, one half of everything offered at the altar on the Nativity of St Mary, both at the vigil and on the feast. The church of Blaviniacum, with its endowment, three chapels, and the altars of Monz, Magaicum, and Bibiniacum. At Blaviniacum, all tithes, greater and lesser alike; at the Nativity of the Lord, Easter, and the feast of St Medard, two parts of the offerings. At Monz, all tithes, except the tithes of three persons.

[Col. 1386A] At Biliniacum and at Jaiacum, one half of all tithes. The church of Parniacum above the Moselle, with its altar, four parts of the greater tithes of that church, and one half of the lesser tithes. Also, from the endowment of that church, one half of the annual offerings and one half of the alms for the dead. The church of Luzda, with its altar, a third part of all tithes, and one half of its endowment. The church of Beverone, with its altar, its endowment, and the rents of the churchyard, together with three whole parts of the tithes of that church. The church of Odelincurt, with its altar and one half of all tithes, endowment, and rents of the churchyard.

From the gift of Duke Simon and his wife Aleidis, with the consent of their son Matthew: the allod of Monce, with the mill constructed there; the vineyards which the three brothers Drogo, Arnulf, and Herbert, and their nephew Theodoric, a cleric, granted to that monastery out of pious regard. From the gift of Rainald Rufus, the vineyard of Marsillin. Moreover, we decree that the holding on which the monastery itself stands shall be peaceful, exempt from every exaction, and free from every secular ban, so that no bishop or other person may have the right to impose upon it any new or unlawful burden or exercise any vexation.

By apostolic authority we likewise forbid anyone, ecclesiastical or secular, ever to transfer from the place where it is now held the annual market-fair celebrated in the meadow adjoining your monastery on the feast of St Mansuetus. [Col. 1386C]

Therefore we decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; rather, all things shall be preserved whole and intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop.

If anyone therefore, etc.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum. [Col. 1386D] I, Gregory, bishop of Sabina. I, Guy, cardinal-priest of the title of St Chrysogonus. I, Hybald, cardinal-priest of the title of St Praxedes. I, Aribert, cardinal-priest of the title of St Anastasia. I, Subald, cardinal-priest of the title of the Holy Cross. I, Senrica [uncertain reading], cardinal-priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. I, John, cardinal-priest of the title of Saints Sylvester and Martin. I, Guy, cardinal-deacon of St Mary in Portico. I, John, cardinal-deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. [Col. 1387A] I, Gerard, cardinal-deacon of St Mary. I, Odo, cardinal-deacon of St Nicholas in the Prison.

Given at Rome, at St Peter’s, through the hand of Roland, cardinal-priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Ides of February, in the third indiction, in the year 1154 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Adrian IV.

XVII. He grants to Henry, patriarch of Grado, and his successors primacy over the archbishopric of Zadar and the right to consecrate its archbishop. (Rome, at St Peter’s, 22 February.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 821.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, patriarch of Grado, and his successors canonically appointed: for ever.

Lest all churches everywhere and without distinction arrogate everything to themselves, authority, after the prudent and useful deliberation of the holy Fathers, decreed that some should excel others by a prerogative of dignity and should preside over them both with authority to judge and with power to correct. But above all, by the ordering of heavenly counsel, the most holy Roman Church has been established, to whose judgment the affairs of all churches should be referred and whose statutes the whole multitude of the faithful should follow. From the privilege granted to it from the first foundation of the Church in Blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, it has with provident consideration ordered the condition of all churches, [Col. 1387C] and whenever it judged expedient, has decreed that some should take precedence over others in order to exercise a more extensive care for them.

Accordingly, considering your integrity, prudence, and the sincerity of devotion which you are known always to have shown toward the most holy Roman Church, and lest the church of Grado entrusted to your governance and direction—which enjoys the prerogative of honour through the benevolence of the Apostolic See—should, because of the limited extent of its patriarchate, come to be regarded by the less discerning as inferior and lowly: for the increase of its dignity, by apostolic authority we grant it primacy over the archbishopric and bishops of Zadar. We decree that both you and your successors shall preside in the dignity of primacy over the archbishop of Zadar [Col. 1387D] and his bishops at any given time, and shall confer the gift of consecration upon that archbishop, while reserving to the Roman pontiff the conferral of the pallium.

Therefore, so that this our constitution may remain firm and unshaken for ever, we fortify it by the text of this writing and confirm it by apostolic authority.

We decree that no one may ever infringe this document of our constitution and confirmation, or oppose it in any manner, saving in all things the authority of the Apostolic See.

But if anyone presumes to attempt this, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his offence by fitting satisfaction, let him forfeit the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; and at the last judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Gregory, bishop of Sabina. I, Guy, cardinal-priest of the title of St Chrysogonus. I, Hubald, cardinal-priest of the title of St Praxedes. I, Manfred, cardinal-priest of the title of St Sabina. I, Aribert, cardinal-priest of the title of St Anastasia. I, Julius, cardinal-priest of the title of St Marcellus. I, Guy, cardinal-priest of the title of the Shepherd. I, Astald, cardinal-priest of the title of St Prisca. I, Gerard, cardinal-priest of the title of St Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, Henry, cardinal-priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. [Col. 1388B] I, John, cardinal-priest of the title of Saints Sylvester and Martin. I, Guy, cardinal-deacon of St Mary in Portico. I, John, cardinal-deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Gerard, cardinal-deacon of St Mary in Via Lata. I, Odo, cardinal-deacon of St Nicholas in the Tullian Prison.

Given at Rome, at St Peter’s, through the hand of Roland, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the eighth day before the Kalends of March, in the third indiction, in the year 1154 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Adrian IV.

XVIII. To the archbishop of Zadar.—He informs him of what he had arranged: that he should recognize the patriarch of Grado as his primate. (Rome, at St Peter’s, 22 February.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 822.]

[Col. 1388C]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother [LAMPRIDIUS], archbishop of Zadar, and to his suffragan bishops: greeting and the apostolic blessing.

Because the most holy Roman Church is the head and mother of all churches, it is sometimes unable, as it ought, readily to provide for the needs of certain churches, whether owing to the obstacle of distance between lands or to the impediment of many affairs. It has therefore customarily called discerning and prudent men, appointed over other churches so that they might devote a more extensive care to those churches, to share in its solicitude. Moved by this consideration—both because we judged it fitting to enlarge the dignity of the church of Grado, and because we foresaw that it would be useful to you temporally and spiritually to have near you someone from whom you might receive instruction in doubtful matters and support in need—we have decreed that our venerable brother Henry, patriarch of Grado, shall be your primate, and have declared that henceforth the dignity of the church of Grado shall preside in primacy over your churches. [Col. 1389A]

Therefore, by these present letters we command you henceforth humbly to acknowledge that patriarch as your primate and to render him the obedience and honour due to your primate. It will conduce greatly to your benefit, by the Lord’s favour, if you receive his teaching with a devout mind and strive by the performance of your works to fulfil what he shall beneficially command.

Given at Rome, at St Peter’s, on the eighth day before the Kalends of March, in the first year of our pontificate.

XIX. He receives the monastery of Corvey (diocese of Paderborn) into protection and confirms its goods and rights, at the request of Abbot Wibald. (Rome, at St Peter’s, 25 February.)

[MARTÈNE, *Amplified Collection*, II, 616.]

ADRIAN, bishop, to his beloved sons WIBALD, etc.

[Col. 1389B] The authority of our office admonishes and invites us to concern ourselves for the condition of churches, etc. Therefore, beloved in Christ, Wibald, carefully considering the devotion which you show toward the Apostolic See, and following in the footsteps of our predecessor Pope Eugenius of holy memory, we too wish, by the Lord’s help, that the dignity transmitted to your predecessors through the privileges of our predecessors, the Roman pontiffs, be preserved unimpaired. Accordingly, by the authority of this decree we grant you, on the principal solemn feasts, the use of sandals and dalmatic; the right to sit beside the altar; and the right to instruct the people entrusted to the monastery or its cells in matters pertaining to the salvation of their souls, as was granted to [Col. 1389C] your predecessors by our predecessors, the Roman pontiffs.

Moreover, we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and of ourselves the monastery of Corvey itself, over which, by the Lord’s direction, you are known to preside, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, God granting, acquire by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and undiminished for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The tithe, namely, from the estate of Luithardessen; the tithe [Col. 1389D] from the estate of Beverungen; the tithe from the estate of Dasburg; the tithe from the estate of Mullenhusen; the tithe from the estate of Buthelestorp; the tithe from the estate of Munden; the tithe from the estate of Bodowicke; the tithe from the estate of Munchusen; the tithe from the estate of Beldernichusen; the tithe from the estate of Buwelage; the tithe from the estate of Homourstelde; the tithe from the estate of Nienstede; the tithe from the estate of Bolckmaressen; the tithe from the estate of Luitheressen; the tithe from the estate of Erclen; the tithe from the estate of Brumelinchtorp; the tithe from the estate of Leziazi; the tithe from the estate of Castinaci; the tithe from the estate of Hottepe; the tithe from the estate of Nuthlon; the tithe from the estate of Kefflike; the tithe from the estate of Nen; the tithe from the estate of Croppenstede; the tithe from the estate of Hemmentorp; the tithe from the estate of Holthusen; the tithe [Col. 1390A] from the estate of Groninge. In Frisia, a certain estate called Merten, and in that same place the church of Linguerd; the island of Rugia; the fishery of Hocwar.

We further decree that this monastery itself shall on no pretext whatsoever be granted as a benefice to any person, but shall always remain under the protection of the Roman pontiffs and the defence of emperors or kings. We add that the monastery of Heresburg, together with the tithes around the mountain for two Saxon *rastae*, as is known to have been conferred by Pope Leo of blessed memory at the request of Emperor Charlemagne, who had captured that mountain; likewise the monastery at Groninga and the monastery at Kemnade, shall never be alienated from the aforesaid monastery of Corbie, [Col. 1390B] but shall always be governed by the abbot of that place and beneficially ordered under the rule of monastic discipline. Nor shall anyone have authority, without the consent of the brethren residing in those monasteries and with the approval of the chapter of Corbie, to exchange, grant as a benefice, or alienate anything from the goods of those three monasteries which pertain to the use and prebend of those serving the Lord there.

We also will that the provostship of the clerics of the church of St. Paul, called the New Church, shall always remain, as hitherto, under the direction of the abbot of Corbie; nor shall it be lawful for the abbot or provost, without the agreement of the clerics, to confer, exchange, or dispose of the canons’ prebends as benefices.

[Col. 1390C] Moreover, we establish that within the circuit of the wall of the said monastery of Corbie no cleric or layman shall at any time possess any dwelling by right of property or benefice; rather, the entire enclosure of that place shall be available for the needs and dwellings of the abbot, monks, and other religious persons. We prohibit any bishop other than the Roman pontiff from exercising any jurisdiction in that monastery, so that, unless invited by the abbot of this monastery, he may not presume even to celebrate the solemnities of Mass there. Therefore, that all the matters stated above may retain their full force hereafter, as they are contained in the authentic privileges of our predecessors, we confirm them, both for you and for your successors, by the authority [Col. 1390D] of our favour.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, remove its possessions, retain possessions removed, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved unimpaired and entire, for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See.

If anyone therefore, etc.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of St. Chrysogonus. [Col. 1391A] I, Ubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of St. Praxedes. I, Manfredus, cardinal priest of the title of St. Sabina. I, Ubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross. I, Astaldus, cardinal priest of the title of St. Prisca. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Portico. I, Gerardus, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Via Lata.

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Kalends of March, in the indiction [lacuna]. In the year [Col. 1391B] of the Lord’s Incarnation 1155; in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Adrian IV.

Wibald also obtained from Adrian another diploma for the collegiate church of Herford, given at Sutri through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of June, in the third indiction, in the year 1155 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Adrian IV.

XX. He commands the bishops of Scotland to obey Roger of York. (Rome, at St. Peter’s, 27 February.)

[WILKINS, *Concilia*, I, 481.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brethren H., bishop of Glasgow; Christian, bishop of Whithorn; [Col. 1391C] R., bishop of St. Andrews; M., bishop of Dunblane; G., bishop of Dunkeld; T., bishop of Brechin; G., bishop of Aberdeen; W., bishop of Moray; S., bishop of St. Peter’s at Ross; and A., bishop of Caithness: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Whenever, by the ordering of divine clemency, such a pastor is appointed in any church that we have good confidence in his discernment and prudence, we are filled with all the greater joy on that account, inasmuch as we must be zealous for the advancement of all churches. We have therefore received with due kindness our venerable brother Roger, archbishop of York and your metropolitan; we have granted him the pallium—that is, the fullness of pontifical authority; and, while he remained for some time with us, we honourably treated him as one whom we love with sincere affection of heart and with special favour, and held him dear among our brethren and fellow bishops, as was fitting. Accordingly, as he returns, under the Lord’s guidance, to his church with the grace of the Apostolic See and the support of our letters, we earnestly commend him to your brotherhood. By the authority of the present letter we command and enjoin you to take care to love and honour him as your metropolitan, and, setting every pretext aside, to render him the obedience and reverence due by metropolitan right. If you do not do this and refuse to obey him, we wish you to know that, by God’s authority, we shall hold ratified the sentence canonically pronounced by that same our brother [Col. 1392A] against any one of you on this account.

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, on the third day before the Kalends of March.

XXI. He commends to the prelates of the diocese of Piacenza Bishop Hugh, whom he himself has consecrated. (Rome, at St. Peter’s, 4 March.)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXI, 820.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, all provosts, abbots, priors, archpriests, parish priests, chaplains, and other prelates of churches in the bishopric of Piacenza: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Gazing with eyes of mercy upon the tribulations and straits of the Church of Piacenza, we have taken pity on its misfortunes. Therefore, we have granted you as bishop of Piacenza our most dear son Hugh, a man indeed prudent, noble, and energetic, whom your beloved sons, your envoys, elected; and we have taken pains to consecrate him as bishop of the Church of Piacenza with our own hands, as though they were the hands of Blessed Peter. Sending this same our brother to you with the full grace of the Apostolic See, we have thought fit earnestly to commend him to your whole body, commanding you by apostolic letters to extend to him such aid as may enable him to discharge the debts with which the church entrusted to him is known at this time to be burdened. Thus, perceiving your devotion and generosity, he may always [Col. 1392C] hold you dearer; and we may rightly rejoice over the devotion which we shall see you show toward him. We likewise command you to honour more earnestly the aforesaid our brother and, as to a father and bishop of your souls, to strive to render him the obedience and reverence due to him; so that you may be seen to fulfil, in all humility and patience, what belongs to you, and he may be able and bound to be solicitous for your salvation and give you that care of provision which a spiritual father is ever accustomed to keep in mind for good sons.

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, on the fourth day before the Nones of March.

XXII. He commends Bishop Hugh to the clergy and people of Piacenza. (Rome, at St. Peter’s, 4 March.)

[CAMPI, *History of Piacenza*, II, 354.]

[Col. 1392D]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the clergy and people of Piacenza: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Moved by pity for the hardships of the Church of Piacenza, compassionating it with fatherly affection, at the request of your envoys we have granted you our beloved son Hugh as bishop and taken pains to consecrate him bishop of Piacenza with our hands, as though they were the hands of Blessed Peter. Therefore, sending this same our brother to you and to the church entrusted to him with the fullness of our favour, we have thought fit [Col. 1393A] earnestly to commend him to you, commanding you by apostolic letters to strive to receive, with great honour and reverence as is fitting, your father and the ruler of your souls; and, rendering him the obedience due, in all humility to endeavour to please him as your spiritual father in all things and through all things. Thus, while you remain obedient to him, he may be able to minister to you as to his own children spiritual nourishment in due season, so that, under the Lord’s guidance, he may attain with you to the heavenly homeland.

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, on the fourth day before the Nones of March.

XXIII. He grants Uberto, provost of Prato, the right of appeal to the Apostolic See. (Rome, at St. Peter’s, 10 March.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, III, 332.]

[Col. 1393B]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son UBERTO, provost of the Church of Prato: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The clemency of the Apostolic See has always been accustomed to love devoted and humble sons with special affection and to foster them by the protection of the Apostolic See, lest they be harassed by the molestations of evil men. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves your person, together with the goods, both ecclesiastical and temporal, which you now justly and canonically possess or may hereafter, by the Lord’s favour, acquire; and we strengthen them by the safeguard of this document. We establish that, should you find yourself oppressed by anyone, you may freely appeal to the Apostolic See. Therefore no person whatsoever, etc.

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, on the fourth day before the Ides of March.

XXIV. Privilege for the Church of St. Mary in Porto, Ravenna. (Rome, at St. Peter’s, 14 March.)

[FANTUZZI, *Monuments of Ravenna*, II, 131.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son MANFRED, prior of the Church of St. Mary in Porto, and to his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

The authority of the Apostolic See committed to us exhorts us [Col. 1393D] to grant the protection of guardianship to places and persons which duly seek its assistance with devotion. For just as no effect ought to be granted to those who make unjust requests, so the petition of those seeking what is lawful and just ought not to be delayed—especially of those who, through uprightness of life and a praiseworthy ordering of conduct, rejoice in serving almighty God.

Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Prior Manfred, granting with due kindness our favourable assent to your just petitions, we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves, after the example of our predecessor Pope Innocent of happy memory, the Church of the Blessed Mary, Mother of God, over which, by God’s will, you are known to preside, with all things belonging to it; and we strengthen it with the privilege of this document. [Col. 1394A] We establish that whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, with God’s favour acquire, shall remain firm and inviolate to you and your successors in perpetuity. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their own names:

Whatever you acquired by emphyteusis from Sipoto, abbot of the monastery of St. Andrew and St. Mary of Cereto in the regions of Istria; likewise, whatever was reasonably granted to that church by the bishops of Cervia, Cesena, and Rimini; the water-mill with its redemption payment and appurtenances outside the Gate of St. Lawrence at Ravenna, where you constructed a mill beside the bridge which is seen to stand over the water [Col. 1394B] flowing before that gate. We grant this, on the upper and outer side of the same bridge, as belonging to the right of Blessed Peter, to you under an annual rent of one denarius of Luccan coin, payable by your church to us and our successors. We also confirm whatever was bestowed upon your church by Walter, formerly archbishop of Ravenna, of blessed memory, for the sake of divine piety: with lands, meadows, vineyards, woods, rights of use, and pastures in woodland and plain; waters and mills; roads and paths; and all their other liberties and immunities.

You may also receive into your community, without the objection or molestation of any bishop or provost, clerics fleeing the world in order to embrace conversion. No bishop or provost shall dare to forbid you to admit laypersons from any parishes into your fellowship, by your own act, for conversion to the discipline of the rule, unless perhaps they are bound by some lawful obligation. Nor shall any brother of the same church, after making profession among you, have leave to depart from your cloister or house on any pretext without the permission of the prior of your church or the common consent of the community. Should any professed cleric or layperson depart from your cloister or house and, after admonition, disdain to return to the prior then governing that church, the latter shall have authority by apostolic warrant [Col. 1394D] to suspend and excommunicate such a person from his offices. No bishop or abbot shall presume to receive or retain one who has been suspended, interdicted, or excommunicated. We grant all these things by apostolic authority, provided that the observance of the canonical order shall, by God’s favour, continue among you.

Moreover, by our grant you may regularly confer the clerical tonsure in your place upon those who wish to live under the rule through profession. You shall also have leave to receive the ordinations of your clerics from whatever Catholic bishop you prefer. If at any time the Church of Ravenna should have no bishop, or if he who is in it is found not to be Catholic, no bishop or episcopal minister shall dare demand from you the tithes which your brethren collect anywhere through their own labours and expenses. We also decree that burial in sacred places shall be wholly free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who resolve to be buried there—unless they are excommunicated or interdicted.

Furthermore, by the authority of the present privilege we establish that your aforesaid church, with all its possessions wherever situated, shall be exempt from every extraordinary public burden. Thus, should it happen that the archbishop of Ravenna, or any other bishop in whose parish you have a church or possession, or, upon the archbishop’s death, clerics or laypeople of that church, must travel to the Roman pontiff or emperor concerning any matter, they shall not dare impose upon you any levy [Col. 1395B] in money, riding-horses, or any other contributions from the resources of that church, nor inflict any burden whatsoever by lodging there. Furthermore, if war arises and the citizens of Ravenna, or people of other cities or places, impose a levy for soldiers, for fortifying a city, or for a castle, we command that your said church shall be exempt from every exaction.

We therefore decree that no human person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away or diminish its possessions, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved entire, to benefit in every way those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See.

[Col. 1395C] If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person [should violate this, etc.]

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Ubaldus, cardinal priest of the Holy Roman Church, of the title of St. Praxedes. I, Manfredus, cardinal priest of the Holy Roman Church, of the title of St. Sabina. I, Aribertus, cardinal priest of the title of St. Anastasia. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of St. Marcellus. I, Astaldus, cardinal priest of the title of St. Prisca. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul. I, Henry, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Sylvester and Martin. I, Rodulfus, cardinal deacon of St. Lucy in Septa Solis. [Col. 1395D] I, Guido, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Portico. I, John, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus.

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Ides of March, in the third indiction, in the year 1154 of the divine Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Adrian IV.

XXV. To the nuns of the monastery of Horreo. He forbids anyone to prevent them from living in enclosure. (Rome, at St. Peter’s, 14 March.)

[MARTÈNE, *Amplissima collectio*, I, 833.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, the sisters of the monastery of St. Mary at Horreo [Note: [Col. 1395D] Horreo, or the monastery of Horreum, in the city of Trier, was founded by St. Irmina. It still continues under the Rule of St. Benedict, is commonly called St. [Col. 1396D] Irmina’s, and is open only to noble virgins.]: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Whenever a request is made of us which is known to accord with religion and uprightness, it is fitting that we grant it willingly and afford suitable support to the desires of the petitioners. Therefore, beloved daughters in the Lord, assenting to your prayers, we establish and decree by the present document that no person, great or small, secular or ecclesiastical, shall prevent you from serving the Lord under the same Rule of Blessed Benedict, under which, in the time of our predecessor Pope Eugenius of holy memory, by his command, you promised to serve the Lord as enclosed women. No person whatsoever may rashly [Col. 1396B] violate this page of our constitution or oppose it by any means. If anyone presumes to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the wrath of almighty God and of the apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, on the second day before the Ides of March.

XXVI. He takes the Camaldolese congregation under his protection. (Rome, at St. Peter’s, 14 March.)

[MITARELLI, *Annals of Camaldoli*, III, Appendix, 475.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons RODULF, prior of the Camaldolese, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

The authority of our office admonishes and invites us [Col. 1396C] to labour for the condition of churches and, with the Lord’s help, beneficially provide for their quiet and tranquillity. It is indeed held worthy and consonant with propriety that we who, by God’s ordering, have been appointed to their governance should both protect them from the malice of evil persons and fortify them by the patronage of Blessed Peter and the Apostolic See.

Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions. Following in the footsteps of our predecessors, the Roman pontiffs Paschal, Eugenius, and Anastasius, of happy memory, we command and decree by the authority of the present document that no person whatsoever—cleric, monk, or layperson, of whatever order or dignity, in present or future times—may in any way divide from its subjection and unity those congregations [Col. 1396D] and places which have accepted the discipline and order of the Camaldolese hermitage or monastery and which are today subject to its governance. These places and congregations, for the preservation of unity, have been thought fit to be entered under individual names.

In the bishopric of Arezzo: the monastery of St. Saviour of the Berardingi; St. Peter at Rota; St. Mary at Agnano; St. Quirinus at Rosa; the hermitage of Fleri; the monastery of St. Virianus; and St. Bartholomew at Anglare. Near Bagno: the monastery of St. Mary at Trivio. In Galiata: the monastery [Col. 1397A] of St. Mary on the Island. In the bishopric of Montefeltro: the monastery of Monte Ercole. In the bishopric of Forlimpopoli: Almericus’s hospital. In the bishopric of Pesaro: the monastery of St. Decentius and the hermitage of Fajoli. In the bishopric of Bologna: the monastery of the Holy Archangel near the castle of Britti, and St. Felix. In the bishopric of Florence: the monastery of St. Peter at Luco and St. Saviour near the city. In the bishopric of Fiesole: the monastery of St. Mary at Poplena and the church of St. Margaret. In the bishopric of Volterra: the monastery of St. Peter at Fontiano, St. Mary at Policiano, St. Peter at Cerreto, and St. Justus near the city. In the bishopric of Pisa: the monastery of St. Mary of Morrona, the monastery of St. Stephen at Cinctoria, [Col. 1397B] and St. Sabinus at Montione. In the city itself: the monasteries of St. Michael, St. Fridianus, and St. Zeno. In the bishopric of Lucca: the monastery of St. Saviour at Cantiniano and St. Peter at Puteoli.

Likewise, in Sardinia, in the archbishopric of Torres: the monastery of the Holy Trinity of Saccaria; the church of St. Eugenia at Samanar; the church of St. Michael and St. Lawrence at Vanari; the church of St. Mary and St. John at Altasar; the church of St. Mary at Contra; the church of St. John and St. Simeon at Salvenaro; the church of St. Nicholas of Trulla; the church of St. Peter at Scano; the church of St. Paul at Contrognano; and the church of St. Peter at Olim.

Likewise, in Tuscany, in the bishopric [Col. 1397C] of Chiusi: the hermitage of Vivo on Mount Amiata, with all appurtenances of the above-mentioned places; furthermore, the estate of Mojona, which you bought from Provost Henry and the other canons with all its appurtenances; and the estate of Montione, which you bought from the abbot of St. Flora, as is contained in your charters and as was adjudged to you through justice by our predecessor Pope Anastasius of good memory and confirmed by the judgment of his document.

We establish and decree by the authority of the Apostolic See that all the aforesaid monasteries, with everything belonging to them, shall remain for all time as one body under one head—that is, under the prior of the Camaldolese hermitage—and shall persist in the observance of his discipline, under that prior, namely, who shall have been regularly elected, by God’s favour, by the abbots or priors of the congregation itself and by the hermits. Furthermore, we decree that the congregation itself shall be permanently entrusted to the protection of the Apostolic See, such that no bishop may, without the consent of the prior or licence of the Apostolic See, excommunicate or interdict from divine offices anything belonging to these monasteries. The brethren themselves shall be free to receive the sacraments of consecration or ordination from whatever Catholic bishop they prefer.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid Camaldolese hermitage, remove its possessions, retain possessions removed, diminish them, or harass it with any other vexations; but that all things shall be preserved intact for the benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishops.

If anyone therefore in the future, etc.

**MY EYES ARE EVER TOWARD THE LORD. ST. PETER, ST. PAUL, POPE ADRIAN IV.**

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Ubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of St. Praxedes. I, Aribertus, cardinal priest of the title of St. Anastasia. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of St. Marcellus. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, the title of Pammachius. I, Henry, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Nereus [Col. 1398B] and Achilleus. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Sylvester and Martin. I, Rodulfus, cardinal deacon of St. Lucy in Septa Solis. I, Wido, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Portico.

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Ides of March, in the third indiction, in the year 1154 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Adrian IV.

XXVII. He commands the monks of St. Sylvester of Monte Suavi to obey the Camaldolese prior. (Rome, at St. Peter’s, 15 March.)

[Ibid., p. 494.]

[Col. 1398C]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the monks of the monastery of St. Sylvester of Monte Suavi: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our predecessor Pope Eugenius of holy memory gave and granted to our beloved son, the prior of the Camaldolese, and to his successors, the monastery in which you chose to serve the Lord. This monastery belongs spiritually to the right and property of the Prince of the Apostles; and the grant was made so that monastic order might firmly be observed there according to the custom of the Camaldolese brethren, that the monastic order might be reformed under his discipline and governance, and that the Rule of Blessed Benedict might be firmly observed.

Yet, although at that time some of you, in the presence of our said predecessor, promised our aforesaid son the prior to render him full obedience, you now look backward. By withholding from that aforesaid our son the prior the obedience due according to the custom of the Camaldolese brethren, both you and they oppose the observance of the Rule of Blessed Benedict. This action gives sufficient indication that you are not concerned either for the observance of religion or for the salvation of your souls, or that you do not wish, with diligent zeal, to do what is pleasing to God. Therefore, lest you incur the indignation of almighty God and of ourselves, we command and enjoin you by the present letter to obey humbly the aforesaid our son the prior [Col. 1399A] in all things according to God, the Rule of Blessed Benedict, and the custom of the Camaldolese. If you refuse to fulfil this within one month, know that from that time you are bound by the bond of anathema.

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, on the Ides of March.

XXVIII. He entrusts the government of the Church of St. Potentiana at Rome to the Church of St. Mary of Reno. (Rome, at St. Peter’s, 17 March.)

[TROMBELLI, *Memoirs of Reno*, 404.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son GUIDO, prior of the Church of St. Mary of Reno, and to his brethren, present and future, living canonically: in perpetuity.

The splendour of the house of the Lord must be cherished, and the place where his glory dwells must be honoured with attentive diligence and reverence.

For the Church of God, which journeys upon earth not without much grief and toil, because of love and longing for him in whose heavenly realm it shall enjoy the reward of everlasting and uninterrupted joys, reveres and loves with particular care religious persons who have devoted themselves to the service of our Creator. We likewise, to whom the Lord, the provider of all good things, has entrusted, by his own ordering, the care of the universal Church, labour, as required by our office, to establish religion pleasing to God and to preserve it once established with exact diligence. This is especially so in the city of Rome, where, just as it was formerly the head of all error, so, in the age of Christianity, it is surely fitting that the light of all holiness should shine forth.

Moved, therefore, by the force of this consideration, and assenting to the prayers of our most dear son Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Pastor, we commit the Church of St. Potentiana itself, by authority of the Apostolic See and with the counsel of our brethren, to you and your successors for ordering and governance. We establish that a canonical order shall be instituted there through you, by God’s favour, and shall be preserved there inviolate for all time according to the institution and observance of your rule. Furthermore, in accordance with the disposition of our aforesaid son Guido, cardinal priest, we confirm to your canons residing in the same church one half of all the possessions which that church now reasonably possesses, together with one half of the vineyards and rents belonging to it. So long as the canonical order according to the Rule of Blessed Augustine shall, by the Lord’s favour, flourish in that place, we establish that these shall remain for the use and disposal of the brethren serving the Lord there. Among these possessions, we have decreed to record the following by their own names:

At Marana, three *pedicae*; at Favaralo, three *pedicae* and three small plots; at Salone, one *pedica*; at St. Genesius, one *pedica* and eight plots of vineyard; six gardens around the church; and the church of St. John [Col. 1400A] at Petroiolo with its appurtenances. No person whatsoever may lawfully violate this document of our constitution and confirmation by rash presumption or disturb it by any molestations.

If anyone presumes to attempt this, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his presumption by due satisfaction, let him incur loss of his rank and office, or be punished with the penalty of excommunication. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Hubaldus, cardinal priest of St. Praxedes. I, Manfredus, cardinal priest of the title of St. Sabina. I, Aribertus, cardinal priest of the title of St. Anastasia. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of St. Marcellus. [Col. 1400B] I, Hubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Astaldus, cardinal priest of the title of St. Prisca. I, Guido, cardinal priest of Pastor. I, Gerardus, cardinal priest of the title of St. Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, John, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, the title of Pammachius. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Sylvester and Martin. I, Rodulfus, cardinal deacon of St. Lucy in Septa Solis. I, John, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. [Col. 1400C] I, Girardus, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Via Lata. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of St. Nicholas in the Tullian Prison.

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of April, in the third indiction, in the year 1154 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Adrian IV.

XXIX. He commends the Camaldolese of Berardingorum and of St. Peter at Rota to Wibald, abbot of Stavelot. (Rome, at St. Peter’s, 19 March.)

[MARTÈNE, *Amplissima collectio*, II, 589.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 1400D] son, the abbot of Stavelot: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Although the care and solicitude of all churches rests upon us, and although we must defend them universally, it especially becomes us to foster religious places with attentive care and render them more gracious services: for those who have forsaken their own possessions have chosen to remain lowly and despised in the house of the Lord rather than dwell in the tents of sinners. In the bishopric of Arezzo there are known to be certain monasteries, namely Berardingorum and St. Peter at Rota, in which religious men, Camaldolese brethren, diligently strive to serve the Lord. Although poor in temporal things, they are believed nevertheless to abound in an unfailing treasure.

For their sake, therefore, we earnestly entreat the affection of your brotherhood. By apostolic letters we command your discretion, for the love of God and in reverence for Blessed Peter and ourselves, to exert your influence with our most dear son Frederick, illustrious and Catholic king of the Romans, so that the aforesaid brethren may not suffer loss of their goods at the hands of those in the army; but rather, whenever they bring a complaint before that most Christian prince, they may be able to obtain full justice from him.

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of April.

XXX. He confirms the privileges of the monastery of Pomposa. (Rome, at St. Peter’s, 9 April.)

[MURATORI, *Italian Antiquities*, V, 166, where only the date and subscriptions are printed.]

[Col. 1401B]

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Ides of April, in the third indiction, in the year 1155 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Adrian IV.

After the bishops subscribe:

I, Guido, priest cardinal of the title of Saint Chrysogonus. I, Hubald, priest cardinal of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Matthias, priest cardinal of the title of Saint Sabina. [Col. 1401C] I, Julius, priest cardinal of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, Octavian, priest cardinal of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Girard, priest cardinal of the title of Saints Nereus and Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, John, priest cardinal of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius. I, John, priest cardinal of the title of Saints Sylvester and Martin. I, Rodulf, deacon cardinal of Saint Lucy in Septisolium. I, Gerard, deacon cardinal of Saint Mary in Via Lata. [Col. 1401D] I, Odo, deacon cardinal of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison.

XXXI. To E[raclius], archbishop of Lyons, and H[umbert], archbishop of Besançon: he commands that they not permit the monastery of Tournus to suffer injuries from G[irard], count of Mâcon. (Rome, at St Peter’s, 14 April.)

[JUENIN, *New History of Tournus*, Documents, p. 166.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brethren E[RACLIUS], archbishop of Lyons, and H[UMBERT], archbishop of Besançon: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Those who presume to invade the goods of churches and to burden religious persons and their lands with harsh and unlawful [Col. 1402A] exactions ought to be admonished more earnestly by the prelates of the Church, so that they may themselves receive the fruits of their possessions in full, and so that those who, by plundering churches, plainly seem to depart from justice into sins may be corrected by the exhortations of their pastors. For our beloved son P[eter], abbot of the monastery of Tournus, has shown us in his account that the nobleman G[irard], count of Mâcon, burdens its lands and the people dwelling on them with unlawful and unprecedented exactions to such an extent that he is unable not merely to derive the customary income from them, but is even frequently compelled to contemplate the loss of those possessions themselves. Therefore, since we neither ought nor can permit the abbot or his monastery to suffer harm, [Col. 1402B] by these present letters we command you strictly to warn the said count to abstain entirely from such exactions upon the lands and persons of the aforementioned monastery, and to allow the brethren dwelling there to serve the Lord in complete peace. But if he should perhaps refuse to do this and should decide to oppose your warnings—and perhaps he will not—then administer such full justice concerning him and against his [lacuna] that, at least through fear of punishment, he may unlearn [perhaps: cease] harassing the goods of the said monastery or imposing unlawful exactions upon its lands.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of May.

XXXII. He commands the canons of Chalon to restore a certain church to the monastery of Tournus. (Rome, at St Peter’s, 14 April.)

[Ibid., p. 165.]

[Col. 1402C]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the canons of the Church of Chalon: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Good sons ought not to undo what they have seen their father establish by reasonable foresight. Of blessed memory, (Walter), formerly bishop of Chalon, gave a certain church, out of pious regard, to our beloved sons P[eter I], abbot, and the monks of the monastery of Tournus. As our beloved son P[eter II], abbot of that same [Col. 1402D] monastery, has endeavoured to show us in his complaint, you have unjustly taken it from them. Therefore, lest you may deservedly be proved destroyers of good works, by these present letters we command you, if his complaint is supported by the truth, not to delay in any way in restoring that church to our same son. We have indeed commanded our venerable brother G., your bishop, to admonish you to restore that church. And if you believe that you have any right against them, either in that same church or in other matters, you may obtain your justice in the presence of our venerable brother E[raclius], archbishop of Lyons. Otherwise, we wish you to know that, with God as author, we shall punish your presumption and disobedience in such a way that those to whose ears [Col. 1403A] the report of the punishment comes will not dare to attempt similar acts.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of April [read: May].

XXXIII. He receives the monastery of Benediktbeuern under his protection and confirms its rights. (Rome, at St Peter’s, 17 April.)

[MEICHELBECK, *Chronicle of Benediktbeuern*, I, 99.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons WALTER, abbot of Saint Benedict of Burin, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

The duty of our office admonishes us, with the Lord’s help, beneficially to provide for tranquillity. For it is recognized as worthy [Col. 1403B] and fitting to honour that we who, by the Lord’s disposition, have been appointed to govern churches should both protect them from the wickedness of evil persons and strengthen them by the patronage of blessed Peter and of the Apostolic See. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously grant your just requests and, following the example of our predecessor Pope Eugene of happy memory, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this document. We decree that whatever possessions or goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, with the Lord’s aid, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors.

And because, as we have learned from the rescript of the letters of Lothair, Roman emperor of illustrious memory, that same monastery, once enriched with many possessions and riches, was stripped of them by the necessities of the realm and impending emergencies, it pleased that emperor to endow it with liberty and to decree that it should be immune from all injuries and exactions. We therefore confirm that same liberty by apostolic authority and decree that it shall remain inviolate for ever. Moreover, as that emperor decreed, no advocate shall be installed there except one whom the abbot of that place, with the counsel of the brethren, has chosen. If such a person, contrary to his right, should lay hands upon the property of the church against the abbot’s will, the abbot shall have authority, according to the tenor of the letters of the emperor already mentioned, to reject him. Upon the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any one of your successors, no one shall be set over it through any craft of deception or violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall provide to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of Saint Benedict. We also grant that the burial-place of the same house shall be free, so that no one may oppose [Col. 1404A] the devotion and final wish of those who have decided to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict, saving, of course, the canonical right of the mother church.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, remove its possessions, retain what has been removed, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved unimpaired and whole for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If anyone therefore, etc.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Imar, bishop of Tusculum. [Col. 1404B] I, Cinthius, bishop of Porto and Saint Rufina. I, Gregory, bishop of Sabina. I, Guido, priest cardinal of the title of Saint Chrysogonus. I, Hubald, priest cardinal of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Manfred, priest cardinal of the title of Saint Sabina. I, Octavian, priest cardinal of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Astald, priest cardinal of the title of Saint Prisca. I, John, priest cardinal of the title of Saints Sylvester and Martin. I, Odo, deacon cardinal of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Guido, deacon cardinal of Saint Mary in Portico. I, John, deacon cardinal of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Gerard, deacon cardinal of Saint Mary in Via Lata.

[Col. 1404C] Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, by the hand of Roland, priest cardinal of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of May, in the third indiction, in the year 1155 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Adrian IV.

XXXIV. He receives under protection the church of Saint Mary at Czerwińsk and confirms its goods. [Note: [Col. 1403D] From an authentic parchment charter preserved in Warsaw in the library of the illustrious Count Zamojski; it now lacks the lead bull formerly attached by threads of blue-grey, green, and red, though a notarial parchment copy of the year 1404 in the same library attests that it was formerly furnished with this bull. Pope Eugene IV [Col. 1404D] confirmed this bull of Adrian in the year 1143; a copy of his confirmation is found in the collection of Czerwińsk privileges, p. 35 ff.] (Rome, at St Peter’s, 18 April.)

[RZYSZCZEWSKI, *Polish Diplomatic Codex*, I, 8.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GUIDO, prior of the church of Blessed Mary at Cirvenzk [Note: [Col. 1404D] Czerwińsk, a parish town in the territory and region of Płock, situated on the Vistula.], and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

[Col. 1404D] The authority of our office admonishes and invites us to labour for the condition of churches and, with the Lord’s help, to provide beneficially for their peace and tranquillity. For it is recognized as worthy and fitting to honour that we who have been appointed to govern churches should both protect them from the wickedness of evil persons and strengthen them with the patronage of blessed Peter and of the Apostolic See. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously grant your just requests and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church, in which you are devoted [Col. 1405A] to divine service; and we fortify it by the patronage of this document. We decree that whatever possessions or goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God being favourable, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have judged it proper to specify the following by their proper names:

At Płock [Note: [Col. 1405C] The city of Płock, capital of the province bearing its name.] the prebend of Zaxichow [Note: [Col. 1405C] In the notarial copy of this bull drawn up in 1404, and in the privilege of the apostolic legate Opiso of 1154, presented below as no. XLIII, this village is called Zaskow or Saskow. Zaskow is a village in the parish of the town of Nur, in the territory of Ostrołęka, situated near other goods of the monastery.]; at Czerwińsk, the tenth and ninth market, the tenth and ninth mark, the tenth and ninth boat, the tenth *poletrum*, and the tenth day in the enclosure [Note: [Col. 1405C] The apostolic legate Opiso, in the privilege mentioned above, speaks not of the tenth day but of the tenth night in the enclosure, and describes more fully each of the donations mentioned here.]; the whole of Łomna [Note: [Col. 1405C] Łomna, a royal parish village in the Warsaw region.] with its appurtenances; Gostezlaw [Note: [Col. 1405D] Undoubtedly the village of Gocław in the Płock region, belonging to the parish of Letowo. The old copy reads Gotslaw.] [Col. 1405B] with its appurtenances; [Scol]atowe [Note: [Col. 1405D] Here we restore, within brackets and according to the tenor of the copy, words which a crack damaging the charter prevents from being read. Skolatowo is a parish village in the Płock region.] with its appurtenances; Targoscine [Note: [Col. 1405D] Targosczine in the copy, but neither Targoscina nor any other village with a similar name is found in this region. It seems more likely that this concerns the village of Kargoszyn, not far from Nasielsk, in the territory and region of Przasnysz, belonging to the parish of Ciechanów.] with its appurtenances; Nasielzk [Note: [Col. 1405D] Nasielsk is a parish town in the territory and region of Pułtusk.] with its appurtenances; Caccubum in Segovend [Note: [Col. 1405D] Both Segovend and Sgovantka, which occur in the notarial copy of the bull of 1404 and in Opiso’s privilege, are entirely unknown in these regions. Yet there is the parish village of Zgłowiątka, or Zgłowieg(e)zka, in the Kuyavian territory, Brest region, near the town of [Col. 1406C] Lubraniec; likewise, there is a stream called Zgowigtka in Długosz (I, 14, 26), whose source is the lake called Orle, situated between the towns of Lubraniec and Piotzkowo, and whose mouth is near Włocławek in the River Vistula.]; Garvolionem [Note: [Col. 1406C] Garwolewo, a royal village in the Płock region, belonging to the parish of Czerwińsk.], which Count Bartholomew, with his wife and son, gave to the church of Blessed Mary out of devotion for the redemption of his soul and confirmed by his charter; a [market] at Cohow [Note: [Col. 1406C] Two villages of this name seem to have been in the monastery’s possession. One is usually cited together with Kobylnica and lies in the Podlachian province, the region of Żelechów, and the parish of Maciejowice, not far from Kobysnica. The other, of the same name, is found in the Sandomierz region, in the parish of Strzyżowice. This latter seems likely to be meant here, from a decree of the Sandomierz court issued in 1373 in a case between the monastery of Czerwińsk and the possessor of the neighbouring village of Strzyowiyzce, preserved in the book of privileges of this monastery, pp. 4–5.] by gift of Duke Henry; the whole of Chrominna; Scriseva with the lake; Chomissina [Note: [Col. 1406D] Cromnova in the copy; Kromnow—one Polish and the other German—is a royal village in the Masovian province, Sochaczew region, parish of Brochów. Struzewo, however, is situated in the Płock region, parish of Wrona; and there too is the village of Komsin, belonging to the parish of Czerwińsk.]; Guidua [Note: [Col. 1406D] Called Siudva in the copy. This village, along with Wilkowiec, Olsyny, Golawice, Pomnichowo, and many other possessions near the monastery, is said in the privilege of Casimir the Great of 1361, printed below, to have been situated in the former district of Zakroczym; it cannot be found either on maps or in the index of places in the kingdom of Poland.]; Parlin [Note: [Col. 1406D] Parlin is a royal village in the Płock region, belonging to the parish of Czerwińsk.].

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church of Czerwińsk, remove its possessions, retain what has been removed, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all shall be kept whole for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance [Col. 1405C] and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See [Col. 1406A] and the canonical right of the bishop of Masovia.

If anyone therefore, etc.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. (“Fare well,” in the monogram.) I, Guido, priest cardinal of the title. I, Imar, bishop of Tusculum. I, Odo, deacon cardinal of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Gregory, bishop of Sabina. I, Aribert, priest cardinal of the title of Saint Anastasia. I, Julius, priest cardinal of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, Odo, deacon cardinal of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. [Col. 1406B] I, Octavian, priest cardinal of the title of Saint Cecilia.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, by the hand of Roland, priest cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the Kalends of May, in the third indiction, in the year 1155 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Adrian IV.

XXXV. To T., bishop of Paris.—Concerning the investiture of certain *personatus*. (Rome, at St Peter’s, 20 April.)

[MARTEN, *Amplified Collection*, II, 639.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother T. [Note: [Col. 1406D] Theobald, who, from being prior of Saint-Martin-des-Champs, became bishop of Paris.], bishop of the Parisians: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1406C] Our venerable brother Henry, bishop of Beauvais, appearing before us, set forth in our hearing [Col. 1407A] that, while a dispute concerning the *personatus* of certain churches was being conducted between our beloved son O. [Note: [Col. 1407] Odo, who succeeded Abbot Suger in the government of the abbey of Saint-Denis.], abbot of Saint-Denis, and the chancellor of the church of Beauvais, that abbot, while the case was pending, invested a certain clerk with those *personatus*. Afterwards that clerk came to the Apostolic See and obtained letters of confirmation from Pope Anastasius, our predecessor of happy memory, who was unaware of this affair. Therefore, since that which is known to have been obtained unknowingly from the Apostolic See ought not to prejudice the other party, by these present letters we command your brotherhood to summon both parties before you and, having diligently heard and fully learned the arguments of each party, to decide the same dispute [Col. 1407B] without evasion through appeal, justice acting as mediator. But if it should happen that the aforesaid abbot prevails in this case, since our aforesaid brother maintains that the investiture of those same *personatus* belongs to him by right, we command you to summon both him and the aforesaid abbot before you at a suitable place and time, and, having heard, carefully considered, and fully understood the arguments of both, to bring the case to a canonical conclusion, excluding appeal, so that neither party shall have any ground to complain of any diminution of its right.

Given at Saint Peter’s, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of May.

XXXVI. To O., abbot of Saint-Denis.—Concerning certain *personatus* and their investiture. (Rome, at St Peter’s, 20 April.)

[Ibid., col. 640.]

[Col. 1407C]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to our beloved son O., abbot of Saint-Denis: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our venerable brother Henry, bishop of Beauvais, coming to the Apostolic See, asserted that a dispute was being conducted between you and the chancellor of his church concerning certain *personatus*, and between you and himself concerning the investiture of those same *personatus*. But, wishing to remove every cause for litigation, we have committed the decision of the same case to our venerable brother T., bishop of Paris. Therefore, by these present letters we command your belovedness [Col. 1407D] that, when you are summoned by him on this matter, you shall appear before him and accept and observe, without appeal, what he judges between you.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of May.

XXXVII. To An., canon of Beauvais.—For the case pending between Henry, bishop of Beauvais, and An., canon.

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother AN., canon of Beauvais: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have committed for decision to our venerable brother T., bishop of Paris, the case being litigated between you and our venerable brother Henry, bishop of Beauvais, concerning the *personatus* of certain churches [Col. 1408A] which our beloved son O., abbot of Saint-Denis, is said to have granted to you. Therefore, by these present letters we command you that, when you are summoned by him, you shall appear before him and accept and observe, without appeal, what he judges between you.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s.

XXXVIII. He receives the monastery of Floreffe under protection and confirms its goods and privileges. (Rome, at St Peter’s, 22 April.)

[MIRAEUS, *Diplomatic Works*, IV, 20.]

[Col. 1408B] ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GERLAND, abbot of Floreffe, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

Following in the footsteps of our predecessors, Innocent and Eugene, Roman pontiffs of happy memory, we graciously grant your just requests and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church of Floreffe, in which you are devoted to divine service, together with all that belongs to it; and we fortify it by the privilege of this document. We decree that whatever possessions or goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter acquire, through grants of [Col. 1408C] pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, with the Lord’s help, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you. Among these we have judged it proper to specify the following by their proper names:

The estate, etc.; likewise the church of Leffe with its prebends. Moreover, no one shall exact tithes from you on your newly cleared lands, which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or upon the fodder of your animals.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, remove its possessions, retain what has been removed, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance [Col. 1408D] and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop.

If anyone therefore, etc.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Imar, bishop of Tusculum. I, Centius, bishop of Porto. I, Rufinus, bishop. I, Gregory, bishop of Sabina. I, Guido, priest cardinal of the title of Saint Chrysogonus. I, Manfred, priest cardinal of the title of Saint Sabina. [Col. 1409A] I, Albert, priest cardinal of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, John, priest cardinal of Saints Peter and Paul, of the title of Pammachius. I, Henry, priest cardinal of the title of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Guido, deacon cardinal of the title of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Girard, deacon cardinal of Saint Mary in Via Lata. I, Odo, deacon cardinal of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, by the hand of Roland, priest cardinal of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the tenth day before the Kalends of May, in the third indiction, [Col. 1409B] in the year 1155 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Adrian IV.

XXXIX. He confirms the privileges of the monastery of Rosenfeld at the request of Abbot Bruno. (Rome, at St Peter’s, 1 May.)

[LAPPENBERG, *Hamburg Charters*, I, 189.]

XL. He receives under protection the church of Saint Hippolytus of Bibbiena and confirms its goods. (Rome, at St Peter’s, 2 May.)

[MITARELLI, *Camaldolese Annals*, III, Appendix, 479.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ANTONY, parish priest of Saint Hippolytus of Bibbiena, [Col. 1409C] and his brethren, present and future, to be canonically appointed: in perpetuity.

A devout request ought to be fulfilled by an effect corresponding to its wish, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth praiseworthily and the requested benefit may undoubtedly acquire force. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously grant your just requests and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this document. We decree that whatever possessions or goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God being favourable, [Col. 1409D] shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have judged it proper to specify the following by their proper names.

The churches of Saint Blaise and Saint James of Bibbiena, which are known to belong freely, with all their rights, to your parish church; the tithes of that same castle and of the surrounding villages; the church of Lontrina; the church of Saint Mary of Cursolone; the church of Monteclo; the church of Saint Nicholas of Vignole; Saint Flora’s of Sarna; the church of Campi; the church of Querceto; Saint Bartholomew’s of Catarsina; the church of Saint Angel and Saint Donatus, with the tithe of the ash-burners of Banzena; the church of Saint Zeno; the church of Saint John of Tremojano; Saint Clement’s of Petra; the church of Ossignano; [Col. 1410A] the church of Saint Mary of Monte, with the ancient and due income from Correzzo owed to you; the church of Saint Giles of Frasseneto; the church of Saint Lawrence of Ceresiolo; the church of Montesatuclo, with the whole tithe of the adjacent village called Gage; the church of Saint Sylvester of Jompareta; and the church on Mount Sylvester, with the income of twelve sextaries of grain that are owed to you by ancient and due right. Moreover, whatever is known to belong to your right in the ancient and due tithes and revenues of the aforesaid churches, we confirm to you by apostolic authority.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, remove its possessions, retain what has been removed, diminish them, [Col. 1410B] or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved unimpaired and whole for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See.

If anyone therefore, etc.

MY EYES ARE EVER TOWARD THE LORD. SAINT PETER, SAINT PAUL, POPE ADRIAN IV.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Imar, bishop of Tusculum. I, Cencius, bishop of Porto and Saint Rufina. I, Gregory, bishop of Sabina. I, Guido, priest cardinal of the title of Saint Chrysogonus. I, Julius, priest cardinal of the title of Saint Marcellus. [Col. 1410C] I, Ubald, priest cardinal of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Octavian, priest cardinal of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Gerard, priest cardinal of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, John, priest cardinal of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius. I, Henry, priest cardinal of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. I, Odo, deacon cardinal of the title of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Rodulf, deacon cardinal of the title of Saint Lucy. I, Guido, deacon cardinal of the title of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Odo, deacon cardinal of the title of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison.

[Col. 1410D] Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, by the hand of Roland, priest cardinal of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the sixth day before the Nones of May, in the third indiction, in the year 1145 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Adrian IV.

XL–XLI. To Henry, bishop of Beauvais.—That a certain prebend be restored to the Knights Templar. (Rome, at St Peter’s, 2 May.)

[MARTEN, *Amplified Collection*, II, 647.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, bishop of Beauvais: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Both the habit of religious profession and the office of the pontificate you have undertaken [Col. 1411A] admonish you to take diligent thought for the relief of religious persons. We have recently learned from the representation of our beloved sons, the Knights Templar, that your brotherhood has taken from them a certain prebend which O., your predecessor of good memory, granted them for the salvation of his soul, with the assent of his canons, in the church entrusted to you. Although Pope Eugene of blessed memory requested your brotherhood to restore that prebend to them, you have delayed doing so until now. Therefore, adding our own request to the prayers of that same predecessor of ours, we ask your brotherhood in apostolic letters, for the love of God and in commendation of your office, to restore that same prebend to them at our intervention, and to allow them to hold it peaceably according to the grant [Col. 1411B] of your aforesaid predecessor.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, on the sixth day before the Nones of May.

XLII. Privilege for the church of Saint Mary at Marturi. (Rome, at St Peter’s, 6 May.)

[LAMI, *Monuments of the Florentine Church*, IV, 11.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons DEODERIC, parish priest of the church of Saint Mary at Marturi, and his brethren, present and future.

A devout request ought to be fulfilled by an effect corresponding [Col. 1411C] to its wish, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth praiseworthily and the requested benefit may undoubtedly acquire force. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, graciously granting your just requests and following in the footsteps of our predecessors of happy memory, Nicholas, Alexander, Calixtus, and Anastasius, Roman pontiffs, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this document. We decree that whatever possessions or goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God being favourable, may acquire [Col. 1411D], shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have judged it proper to specify the following by their proper names:

Namely, the chapel of Saint Andrew of Papiano; the chapel of Saint Michael in the same castle; whatever right you possess in the chapel of Saint Martin of Luco; the chapel of Saint Peter of Maregnano; whatever right you possess in the chapels in the castle of Stuppli—namely, the chapel of Saints Philip and James, the chapel of Saint Justus, and the chapel of Saint Lucy—and in the chapel of Saint Lawrence in the field, and in the chapel of the Holy Cross in the castle of Marturi. Likewise, whatever right you possess in the bishopric of Siena, within the parishes of the church of Saint Agnes, and in the bishopric of Volterra, [Col. 1412A] both in tithes and in possessions. Finally, whatever Casilia, a noblewoman, is known to have granted to that church, both in houses and in lands. Moreover, we will that the Bridge of Sapeco and the hospital house located near the borough of Marturi, saving the right of the Roman Church, shall remain under your authority and jurisdiction for the honour of God, the relief of the poor, and their support, as Matilda, countess of good memory and special daughter of blessed Peter, decreed, and as Count Guidoguerra confirmed by the attestation of his charter. Furthermore, we likewise confirm to you the first fruits of that church, the full shares of tithe, and whatever our aforesaid predecessor Pope Nicholas of good memory is known to have justly and canonically granted to the said church, whether in the wills of the dead, in clothing, or in offerings, and likewise whatever in the borough or outside the borough of Marturi. [Col. 1412B] We also decree that the bishop of Florence shall never presume to burden the aforesaid church with unlawful or undue exactions. We add, moreover, that within the boundaries of the parish of your church no one shall dare, without your counsel or assent, to build a church or chapel. We further decree that no abbot or anyone else shall dare to bury any of your parishioners, except with the right of your church preserved; nor shall anyone presume in any way to receive a person who has left your church through the rashness of his own will.

We therefore decree that no person may rashly disturb the aforesaid [Col. 1412C] church, remove its possessions, retain what has been removed, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be kept whole for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop.

If anyone therefore, etc.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Imar, bishop of Tusculum. I, Gregory, bishop of Sabina. I, Guido, priest cardinal of the title of Saint Chrysogonus. I, Adubald, priest cardinal of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Manfred, priest cardinal of the title of Saint Sabina. I, Adibert, priest cardinal of the title of Saint Anastasia. [Col. 1412D] I, Odo, deacon cardinal of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Rodulf, deacon cardinal of Saint Lucy in Septem Solium. I, Guido, deacon cardinal of Saint Mary in Portico. I, John, deacon cardinal of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Bernard, priest cardinal of the title of Saint Clement. I, Octavian, priest cardinal of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Astald, priest cardinal of the title of Saint Prisca. I, John, priest cardinal of the title of Saints Martin and Sylvester.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, by the hand of Roland, priest cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Nones of May, in the third indiction, in the year 1155 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Adrian.

XLIII. He receives the monastery of Saint Saviour of Majella under protection and confirms its possessions. (Rome, at St Peter’s, 5 May.)

[*Vatican Bulls*, I, 55.]

[Col. 1413A]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ALEXANDER, abbot of the Hermitage of Majella, and his brethren, present and future, professing the eremitical life: in perpetuity.
