To assent to the just desires of religious persons and graciously to grant their reasonable petitions is urged upon us both by the authority of the Apostolic See, which, by the Lord’s bounty, we serve, and by the unity of fraternal charity. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Alexander, prior [Col. 1413B], we graciously grant your just petitions; and, following in the footsteps of our predecessors of holy memory, Paschal and Eugene, Roman pontiffs, we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and of ourselves the church of Saint Saviour, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that the wilderness of your dwelling-place shall remain free from the right and power of all persons, and that you may enjoy complete tranquillity for the Lord’s service. Moreover, whatever possessions and goods that same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by the Lord’s favour, acquire through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The church of Saint Saviour of Augre Castellare, with the dependent height of Cefalia; the church of Saint Martin at Ranchano [Note: [Col. 1413C] Eugene adds a byname to the church of Saint Martin, concerning which we have spoken above in the notes to Alexander III’s bull, calling it the church of Saint Martin at Ranclano. [Col. 1413D] We do not know the precise site of this place; although it appears to be situated in nearer Abruzzo. From our documents, whose series we shall produce in the dissertation we have promised, we have gathered that this very church, described by the same particular byname, had already been granted to the monastery of Majella in the year 1054.] [otherwise, Ranclano], with its cells; the church of Saint Pancras with its cells [Note: [Col. 1413D] By “cells,” Du Cange, under *cella*, states that one should understand certain private houses situated on rural estates, to which little chapels or oratories were sometimes attached. The monks withdrew to these houses either when they were away from the monastery to gather produce, or when they resorted there in order to devote themselves more earnestly to solitude and prayer, removed from the crowd and company of others.]; the altar of Pinua, with the dependent height of Famoclanum; the church of Saint Mary of Lavella, with its cells; the church of Saint Angel and Saint Peter of the castle of Larome; the church of Saint Clement, with its cells; [Col. 1414A] the monastery of Saint Andrew, with its cells; the church of Saint Blaise; the church of Saint Agatha; the church of Saint Procopius; the church of Saint Nicholas; the church of Saint Helena of the castle of Saint Angel in Trifinio; and there the *villani* [Note: [Col. 1413D] *Villanus* denotes a rural person—not just any such person, but one bound to the service of cultivating the land. Their service, therefore, was not voluntary but wholly compulsory; since the cultivation of the lands had been entrusted to them, they could never be separated from them. Thus, when an estate or holding passed into another lordship [Col. 1414D], they themselves followed the holding. Consult Du Cange’s *Glossary*.], together with landed and vineyard properties.

Likewise, at Fara: *villani*, mills, landed and vineyard properties, and the church of Saint Cantiana. At Vacrum: the church of Saint Agatha and the church of Saint Nicholas, with their lands, vineyards, and possessions. At Praetorum [Praeturum]: the church of Saint Candida, the church of Saint Nicholas, *villani*, mills, and landed and vineyard properties. At Castellione: the church of Saint Justa and Saint Agnes, with *villani*, lands, and vineyards. At Boulanium: the church of Saint Mary [Col. 1414B] of Mirebello, the church of Saint Mary of Bassano, the church of Saint James, *villani*, a mill, and landed and vineyard properties. At Saint Vitus: the monastery of Saint Angel, with cells, *villani*, lands, mills, and vineyards. At Gipsum de domo: the church of Saint Mary, with *villani*, lands, and vineyards; and the church of Saint Mary of Calderari, with its cells. At Mount Moriscum: the church of Saint Helena. At Atessa [Note: [Col. 1414D] Atessa is a town not far from the city of Anxanum. Medieval writers give it various names, among whom Tazze, Atissa, and Atessa are equivalent forms. Among the places subject to the abbey of Majella, Emperor Lothair, in his diploma issued in 1137, which is entered in Corrado’s codex under letter C, fol. 9, lists Taize—that is, as we think, Atessa itself, because of the similarity of the name. In the vicinity of this town Adrian places the church of Saint Juliana, as Corrado the visitor confirms in the codex cited above, fol. 11. The fate undergone by that church is indicated by a description extracted from folio 178 of the volume entitled *Index of Collations*, etc., which reads as follows: “The said church [of Saint Juliana] is near the said settlement, outside the walls of Saint Anthony, and only traces of it are visible.”], the church of Saint Juliana. At Cosulem: the estate called Colle Milonis, with its appurtenances; one hospital at Plazanum. At Septem: the church of Saint Pastor and one hospital. At Lanzonum: one hospital. At Rocca Morici: the church of Saint Mary and Saint Nicholas. At Ursonia: the church of Saint [Col. 1414C] Martin. At Ylice: the church of Saint Angel, with its cells, *villani*, lands, and vineyards; at the bank of Corvaria, the church of Saint Victorinus, with lands and vineyards.

You shall receive chrism, holy oil, the consecration of altars or churches, and the ordination of clerics to be promoted to sacred orders from the diocesan bishop, provided that he is Catholic, is in the favour and communion of the Apostolic See, and is willing to furnish these things freely and without any improper exaction. Otherwise, you may approach whichever bishop [Col. 1415A] you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what is requested.

We decree, therefore, that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid wilderness, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass them in any manner; but that all things shall be preserved whole and undiminished for the benefit of those for whose governance and support they have been granted, and shall in every way serve their use—saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishops. As a token of this liberty received from the Roman Church, you and your successors shall pay one gold piece annually to us and our successors.

If any person, therefore, etc.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. [Col. 1415B] I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Gregory, bishop of Sabina. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus. I, Hubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul of Pammachius. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, John, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Gerard, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata. I, Oddo, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison [Col. 1415C].

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the Nones of May, in the third indiction, in the year 1155 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Pope Adrian IV.

XLIV. He confirms the monastery of Baume to Peter, abbot of Cluny, and to his successors. (Rome, at Saint Peter’s, 7 May.)

[*Bibliothèque de Cluny*, p. 1115.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ PETER, abbot of Cluny, and to his successors canonically appointed [Col. 1415D], in perpetuity.

The glorious and admirable majesty of divine providence established diverse ranks and orders in its Church for this purpose: that, while inferiors render due obedience and reverence to superiors, one bond might arise from diversity, and the administration of each office might be ordered aright. But just as obedient children ought to be cherished at the gracious breasts of mother Church’s consolation, so rebellious and proud persons, who through their disobedience incur a crime like the sin of divination and idolatry, must be more strictly restrained by the disciplines of ecclesiastical severity. Therefore the monastery of Baume, which, through the brethren gathered there, ought to have shone and flourished in the fragrance of good repute and the beauty of religion [Col. 1416A], wasted away in its sins, at the devil’s persuasion, because they followed the old man with his deeds. Thus it had been grievously diminished in both spiritual and temporal matters.

But when it pleased Him who disposes all things from eternity to put an end to such great evils and mercifully to recall that place to His service, He willed that the faces of those brethren should be filled with shame, so that thereby they might seek His name and return, even unwillingly, to the way of rectitude. Justice therefore having gone before, beloved son in the Lord, Peter, abbot, following in the footsteps of our predecessors, the Roman pontiffs Eugene and Anastasius of venerable memory, we confirm in perpetuity to you and your successors, and through you to the church of Cluny, the monastery of Baume with all that it now justly and canonically possesses or may hereafter, by the Lord’s favour, acquire by reasonable means [Col. 1416B]. This is on the condition that the monastic Order shall be preserved there inviolate in future times according to the institution of the brethren of Cluny; and that, because of the rebellion, contumacy, and offence which the abbot and brethren of the monastery of Baume committed against the holy Roman Church, whoever for the time being obtains governance in that place through you shall never bear the title of abbot, but only that of prior.

Among its goods and possessions we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: the dependency (*obedientia*) of the monastery of Visan [Col. 1416C]; the dependency of Strabona; the dependency of Grandifons with its appurtenances; the dependency of Galda with its appurtenances; and the church of Saint Leodegar, which is in the village called Bavinans; the church of Beliac; the church of Wilari Rostanni; the church of Fragiac; the church of Vadriac; the church of Montibus; the dependency of Saint Lautenus; the dependency of Breriac with all its appurtenances; Baerna in that borough; the dependency of Cavaniac; the dependency of Poloniac with all its appurtenances; and the chapel of Saint Savinus; three burgesses in the borough of Ledo, called Wanirant; the dependency of Dola; the dependency of Benevant; the dependency of Saint Maurice; the dependency [Col. 1416D] of Saoneres; the dependency of Bivillac; the dependency of Saint Agnes; the dependency of la Fracte; the dependency of Munet; the dependency of Ponte Arleti, with their appurtenances and with the church of Pinctis; the church of Blaterans; the church of Wilari Rodulfi; the dependency of Capella; the dependency of Sinziciac, with their appurtenances; the church of Cornavo; the church of Corlant; the church of Fay, with tithes and their appurtenances; the church of Freboans with its tithes; and the dependency of Saint Rannebert with its appurtenances.

We decree, therefore, that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass them by any vexations; but [Col. 1417A] that all things shall be preserved whole for the benefit of those for whose governance and support they have been granted, and shall in every way serve their use. In all things the authority of the Apostolic See is reserved, as is the canonical right of diocesan bishops in the churches named above.

If any person, therefore, etc.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Ymarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Cencius, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina. I, Gregory, bishop of Sabina. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus. I, Hubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Maimedus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, Bernard, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement. [Col. 1417B] I, Octavian, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Astaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Prisca. I, Girardus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, John, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul of the title of Pammachius. I, Henry, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Sylvester and Martin. I, Odo, dean and cardinal of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Rodulfus, cardinal deacon of Saint Lucy in the Septa Solis. I, Guido, dean and cardinal of Saint Mary in Portico. [Col. 1417C] I, John, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Girardus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the Nones of May, in the third indiction, in the year 1155 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Pope Adrian IV.

XLV. He commends L. and G., canons of Orléans, to Louis, king of the Franks. (Rome, at Saint Peter’s, 9 May.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 810.]

[Col. 1417D] ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his dearest son in Christ LOUIS, illustrious king of the Franks, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our beloved sons L. and G., canons of Orléans, having come to the Apostolic See, conducted themselves in the matter for which they had come in such a way that they appear not to have offended you or our beloved son Philip, your brother, the archdeacon, in any word whatsoever. We therefore admonish your magnificence by apostolic letters that, should the envoys of that same son of ours or anyone else seek to report anything unfavourable concerning them to you, you should by no means acquiesce in his allegations; but, as a discerning and wise man, refute unjust accusations and malicious statements.

[Col. 1418A] Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, on 9 May.

XLVI. He receives the convent of Herford under protection and confirms its privileges and goods. (Sutri, 17 May.)

[SCHATEN, *Annals of Paderborn*, I, 801.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, Judith, abbess of the monastery of Herford, and her sisters, both present and future, professing the canonical life, in perpetuity.

A devout petition ought to be fulfilled with an effect corresponding to its wish, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth commendably and the benefit sought may undoubtedly acquire force [Col. 1418B]. Therefore, beloved daughter in Christ Judith, abbess, carefully considering the devotion which you bear toward the Apostolic See, we too, by God’s favour, desire that the dignity bestowed upon your predecessors by the privileges of our predecessors, the Roman pontiffs, shall be preserved unimpaired. We receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, God being propitious, acquire by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful [Col. 1418C] means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and those who succeed after you.

We further enact that the monastery itself shall never under any pretext be granted in benefice to any person whatsoever, but shall always remain under the protection of the Roman pontiffs and the defence of emperors or kings. Moreover, we establish that within the circuit of the wall of the aforesaid monastery of Herford no cleric or layperson shall at any time possess any dwelling by right of ownership or benefice; rather, the entire enclosure of that place shall be open for the use and habitation of the abbess, the sisters, and other religious persons. We prohibit any bishop, other than the Roman pontiff, from exercising any jurisdiction in that monastery, so that, unless invited by the abbess of the same monastery, he may not even presume to celebrate the solemnities of Mass [Col. 1418D]. Therefore, in order that all these provisions may have full force hereafter, as they are contained in the authentic privileges of our predecessors, we confirm them for you and those succeeding after you by the authority of our favour.

We decree, therefore, that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass them by any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole for the benefit of those for whose governance they have been granted and shall in every way serve their use, saving [Col. 1419A] the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop.

If any person, therefore, etc.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Hubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Manfredus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, Octavian, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Sylvester and Martin. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. [Col. 1419B] I, John, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Gerardus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison.

Given at Sutri through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of June, in the third indiction, in the year 1155 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Pope Adrian IV.

XLVII. He receives the monastery of Stavelot under the protection of the Apostolic See and confirms all its possessions and privileges. (Sutri, 17 May.)

[MARTENE, *Amplissima Collectio*, II, 129.]

[Col. 1419C]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons WIBALD, abbot of Stavelot, and his brethren, both present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

Whenever we are asked for something recognized as fitting for religion and honour, it is proper for us gladly to grant it and to afford suitable assistance to the petitioners’ desires. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, we graciously grant your just petitions; and, following the example of our predecessors of blessed memory, Celestine, Lucius, and Eugene, Roman pontiffs, we receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid church over which, by God’s appointment, you are known to preside, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing, etc. [Col. 1419D]

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Hubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Manfredus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, Octavian, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Henry, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. [Col. 1420A] I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, John, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Gerardus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison.

Given at Sutri through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of June, in the third indiction, in the year 1155 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Pope Adrian IV.

XLVIII. He receives the church of Goslar under protection and confirms its possessions. (Sutri, 17 May.)

[HEINECCIUS, *Antiquities of Goslar*, 152.]

[Col. 1420B]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the canons of the church of Goslar, present and future, canonically appointed, in perpetuity.

The force of equity and the order of reason require that just petitioners be granted their requests, especially where piety supports their wish and truth does not fail them. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously grant your just petitions, receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid church in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by the Lord’s favour, acquire through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors [Col. 1420C]. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

Namely, the property which you possess in Slanstesten, which our predecessor Pope Victor II of blessed memory confirmed by his privilege to you and your predecessors among the other possessions of your church; and likewise the property in Wischeribe, which Conrad II, king of the Romans, of illustrious memory, granted to you and your successors, for the use of the brethren serving the Lord there and for the remedy of his soul. We confirm these by the authority of the Apostolic See [Col. 1420D].

We decree, therefore, that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass them by any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole and unimpaired for the benefit of those for whose governance and support they have been granted, and shall in every way serve their use—saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop.

If any person, therefore, etc.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. [Col. 1421A] I, Hubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Manfredus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, Octavian, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Henry, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, John, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Gerardus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison.

[Col. 1421B] Given at Sutri through the hand of Roland, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of June, in the third indiction, in the year 1155 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Pope Adrian IV.

XLIX. To the archbishop of Tours.—He declares void the settlement made by the abbot of Fontaines and urges an amicable settlement with the bishop of Dol; otherwise he orders him to come to the Apostolic See. (Sutri, 17 May.)

[MARTENE, *Thesaurus Anecdotorum*, III, 898.]

ADRIAN, pope, to the archbishop of Tours.

The church of Dol, coming into the presence of our apostolic office [Col. 1421C], worn down by many labours and harassed by troubles, humbly petitioned us to grant to our venerable brother Hugh, archbishop of Dol, the fullness of his pallium. It requested this both by the terms of the agreement which it acknowledged had been made between you and him and by ancient custom. Your envoys also came against him, unanimously requesting confirmation of a certain settlement which, they asserted, had been made by the abbot of Fontaines concerning the suffragans there. They said, moreover, that the same church, together with its aforesaid archbishop, had renounced the suffragans in that settlement; adding that our predecessor Pope Lucius of good memory had so determined it by the common counsel of the brethren, as was contained in his writing.

In reply, the church of Dol stated that the settlement was altogether null; and further maintained that the judgment of the Roman pontiff itself was not binding, because he [Note: [Col. 1421] This was Godefridus le Roux, who, having been called from the archdeaconry of Dol to the episcopal dignity, was later transferred by Innocent II to the see of Capua.] who then held the office of bishop had employed fraud and deceit, since the church of Dol had not been present at the examination and he was zealously aspiring to the archbishopric of Capua, which he later obtained through the intrusion of the king of Sicily. Therefore, since he alleged nothing in that proceeding advantageous to the church of Dol, and since we could not obtain full knowledge of the matter, because the other party persisted in denial and asserted that it had absolutely no mandate to carry these matters out, [Col. 1422A] we made no determination on the matter. Nevertheless, we have entirely annulled the aforesaid settlement and decree by the authority of the Apostolic See that it shall henceforth have no force.

In accordance with the petition of that same church, we have judged the pallium, the insignia of the episcopal office, to be granted to our said brother. Sending him back with the blessing of the Apostolic See and the fullness of our favour, we will that the rights of the great church over which he presides remain whole and unimpaired, inasmuch as it is fitting that we, by reason of our entrusted office, should provide more diligently for ecclesiastical interests. Therefore, mercifully providing for the consolation of the church of Dol, lest it complain that the most holy Roman Church is negligent or remiss in enforcing its right, we command your fraternity by apostolic letters either to reach an agreement with him or to present yourself before our apostolic presence by the next feast of Saint Michael, 29 September, prepared both to render and to receive full justice. In the meantime, you must not presume for any reason to burden our same brother or his clerics with a sentence of excommunication or interdict [Col. 1422B].

Given at Sutri, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of July [read: June].

L. He commends Hugh, archbishop of Dol, to Geoffrey, son of Oliver, etc. (Sutri, 21 May.)

[Ibid., col. 900.]

[Col. 1422C]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GEOFFREY, son of Oliver, and his brothers ROLAND of Dinan, BERTRAND, RODULF the viscount, WILLIAM [otherwise, OLIVER] of Montfort, RADULF of Fougères, and ROBERT of Vitré, greeting and apostolic blessing.

By the Lord’s ordering, although unworthy, we are seen to sit in the place of the prince of the apostles so that we may, through the urgency of our exhortation, summon the people committed to us by His gift to those things through which, by divine grace’s bounty, they may attain the reward of the heavenly blessedness. Since obedience is so perfect and efficacious a virtue that it brings a person to the prize [Col. 1422D] of the heavenly calling, we command and exhort all of you in the Lord by apostolic letters that you render our venerable brother Hugh, archbishop of Dol, in all things the obedience due to him, as you are shown to have rendered it to his predecessors; and that you presume to be rebellious or contumacious against him in nothing. If any of your people is known to hold any possessions belonging to his right, cause them promptly to be restored to our aforesaid brother, or cause full justice to be done to him. Otherwise, whatever sentence he may canonically pronounce against that person, we decree by apostolic authority that it shall remain valid and firm [Col. 1423A].

Given at Sutri, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of June.

LI. To the archbishop, archdeacon, and dean of the church of Rouen.—That they shall cause possessions of the church of Dol violently seized in Normandy to be restored. (Sutri, 21 May.)

[Ibid., col. 901.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother archbishop and beloved sons, the archdeacon and dean of Rouen, greeting and apostolic blessing.

By the office of the supreme pontificate enjoined upon us by God and the obligation of the stewardship we have undertaken, we are prompted to preserve whole and unimpaired the rights of all Christ’s churches and, insofar as divine grace permits, to attend more earnestly to their interests [Col. 1423B]. Our venerable brother Hugh, archbishop of Dol, appearing before our apostolic presence, represented to us that the church of Saint Samson at Rillio, other churches, and certain possessions which his predecessors had justly and canonically possessed in Normandy had been violently occupied by some persons. We therefore command you by apostolic letters to take care diligently to admonish those who presume unjustly to hold those churches and possessions, that they restore them without evasion and allow him hereafter to possess them in peace and quiet, as his predecessors are known to have possessed them; or that they do not delay in rendering him full justice in your presence. If they judge fit to treat your admonition with contempt, keep them bound by the bond of excommunication until they repent [Col. 1423C].

Given at Sutri, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of June.

LII. He commands [Geoffrey] of Langres, [Henry] of Autun, [Geoffrey] of Nevers, and [Alan] of Auxerre to excommunicate the count of Nevers unless, after being warned, he repairs within thirty days the damages inflicted upon the monastery of Vézelay. (Sutri, 21 May.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 813.]

[Col. 1423D] ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brethren of Langres, Autun, Nevers, and Auxerre, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The malice of the count of Nevers, as your fraternity does not fail to know, has now grown so great against the special daughter of the Apostolic See, the church of Vézelay, that it would doubtless seem an exceedingly grave fault if his wickedness remained unpunished. Besides the evils which he long ago rashly inflicted upon it, both by inciting the burgesses to persecute it and in diverse other ways, he has recently stationed his soldiers and the men of his enemies in Vézelay and, contrary to the right of his predecessors, has usurped lordship in that town according to his own will. He also presumes to encourage the burgesses in their conspiracy and perjury against our beloved son Pons, abbot of Vézelay [Col. 1424A].

Indeed, our predecessor Pope Eugene of blessed memory, compassionating with paternal affection the afflictions and distresses of that church and duly inflamed against the malice of the aforesaid count, cut him off with the sickle of the divine word from the body of Christ, which is the Church, and forbade divine offices to be celebrated in his land. Since, therefore, that same count has been so given over to a reprobate mind and has so turned the eyes of his mind away from the prospect of eternal damnation that he could not be restrained from his wickedness even when scourged for it, we command you by these present letters, under obedience, to admonish him strictly: that he remove his guards from the town of Vézelay; make amends for the wrongs inflicted on the church; restore to the aforesaid abbot the charter of settlement extorted in violation of the privileges of our predecessors and of the church’s liberty; give the burgesses no aid or favour in their conspiracy against him; and promise on oath that he will provide that commune with no further support. But if within thirty days after your admonition he scorns to fulfil the foregoing, renew against his person the sentence of excommunication and against his land the sentence of interdict, and command both sentences to be firmly observed by all [Col. 1424B].

Given at Sutri, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of June.

LIII. He commands the bishops of Gaul to excommunicate the burgesses of Vézelay, unless they make satisfaction to the monastery for the wrongs inflicted, and to subject them to various penalties. (Sutri, 21 May.)

[Ibid.]

[Col. 1424C]

ADRIAN, to the bishops of Gaul.

The Vezelay townsmen have conspired with great wickedness against their mother and lady, the Church of Vézelay; how fiercely they have ravaged her and her property has come to your brotherhood’s knowledge, and we are by no means unaware of it. Indeed, Pope Eugenius, our predecessor of happy memory, moved by their pride and the Church’s affliction, bound those same sacrilegious persons with a sentence of ecclesiastical severity. Yet, estranged and turned backward, they by no means ceased from their wickedness, but passed [Col. 1424D] into the desire of their heart and presumed continually to commit graver offenses against their mother, becoming like those of whom the prophet says: “You struck them, and they did not grieve; you crushed them, and they refused to receive correction” (Jer. 5).

For, to pass over for the present the other acts previously committed by them against the Church of Vézelay, they recently made an attack, ransacked the Church’s workshops, broke open the casks, poured out the wine, plundered everything, and even presumed to lay violent hands upon the monks themselves. In all this we grieve for those wretched people, who have fallen into a pit of perjury, sacrilege, robbery, and many sins. We also grieve because we see none of you take up the shield of justice and rise to her aid, [Col. 1425A] so that we may mourn and say with the prophet: “There is none to comfort her among all her loved ones” (Lam. 1).

Therefore, since we, to whose guardianship and protection the aforesaid Church has special recourse, can neither ignore nor ought to ignore her afflictions, by these present letters we command you: laying aside all lukewarmness, hasten strictly to admonish these burgesses, that they restore what they have taken to the aforesaid abbot and his brethren, make good the damage inflicted, render fitting satisfaction for the wrongs done, and return to the fidelity and lordship of the Church. But if, without any delay after your admonition, they contemptuously refuse to perform what we have said, excommunicate, without remedy of appeal, all who are the authors of this wickedness, [Col. 1425B] and those whom the aforesaid abbot shall report to you. Wherever any of these burgesses may come within your dioceses, forbid the celebration of divine offices there for as long as he is present; and if it happen that any one of them dies, let him be deprived of Christian burial.

And lest they escape corporal punishment as well, strictly enjoin upon all your parishioners that they admit them in no way to their fairs and presume to have no association with them, whether in merchandise or in other matters; but let them avoid them as excommunicated persons, seize them wherever they find them, and, from love of justice, not cease to strip them of their goods, so that at least against their will they may be compelled to return to the subjection and fidelity of their lord. [Col. 1425C] For new remedies must be prepared for new diseases.

Given at Sutri, 12 Kalends of June [21 May].

### LIV. He exhorts Louis, king of the Franks, to pursue the burgesses of Vézelay by armed force, so that they may submit to the abbot as their lord. (Sutri, 21 May.)

[Ibid., col. 809.]

There is no need to admonish you at length concerning the protection of religious men and reverence for holy places. For that fire which the Lord came to cast upon the earth has sufficiently kindled your mind to this end, even without admonition, so that among all the rulers of the world there is none deemed more worthy of praise in the sight of the whole Church [Col. 1425D] in this respect.

Indeed, although you extend the protection of your power to all churches established in your kingdom, we desire you to show yourself all the more attentive to the Church of Vézelay, because it belongs more specially to the right of blessed Peter and because it suffers greater troubles and oppressions through the treachery of its own burgesses. Your prudence is not unaware how, some years ago, having conspired against our beloved son Pontius, abbot of Vézelay, under the patronage of the count of Nevers, they presumed to plunder the Church’s property and even to expel the abbot himself from it. For this they deserved to become outcasts from the body of the Lord, which is the Church.

Recently, moreover, making an assault upon the church itself, they broke down the doors, ransacked [Col. 1426A] the workshops, poured out the wine, plundered the monks’ garments, carried off the ornaments of the sacristy, and with rash audacity laid violent hands even upon the monks and the household servants. Since their wickedness has not yet been restrained by the severity of ecclesiastical judgment, it awaits the restraint of your hand and needs to be corrected by your force—what has hitherto remained uncorrected under the equitable discipline of canonical censure.

We therefore ask, admonish, and exhort your Magnificence in the Lord, and enjoin this upon you for the remission of your sins: inflamed with zeal for justice, stirred by the affliction of the aforesaid monastery and by our exhortations, go to Vézelay with a strong hand. Compel the burgesses to renounce the commune which they have established and to return to the fidelity and [Col. 1426B] subjection of our beloved son Pontius, abbot of Vézelay, as their lord. Make them restore what they have taken and repair the damage they have caused; and inflict upon those who are the chief authors of this wickedness such punishment that their successors, considering their punishment, may not dare to raise their heads against their lord or commit similar treachery in the sanctuary of the Lord.

Given at Sutri, 12 Kalends of June [21 May].

### LV. Privilege for the monastery of Cluny. (Sutri, 21 May.)

[Bullar. Cluniac., 68.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son PETER, abbot of Cluny, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

The office of the apostolate entrusted to us by God, and consideration for the welfare of the Church, urge and admonish us to love with fuller charity those churches which we see to be more fervent in the observance of holy religion and which we know to flourish in uprightness and religion, and continually to show them greater honor and favor. Therefore, beloved son Peter in the Lord, following in the footsteps of our predecessors, we sincerely and tenderly love your church, as a daughter of the Apostolic See specially devoted in every respect; and we have judged it fitting to grant assent to your petitions.

We therefore grant you and your successors in perpetuity that in parishes [Col. 1426D] belonging to your jurisdiction no order or religious community other than the Cluniac shall in future be established—namely, lest the goods or rights granted to your church through the generosity of the Roman pontiffs be diminished or taken away under the pretext of any new or subsequently introduced religious order. We likewise decree that no one shall presume to establish a cemetery within the boundaries of your parishes without your consent. Therefore let no person whatever be permitted to infringe the tenor of this our decree or rashly disturb it.

Should any ecclesiastical person hereafter, etc.

Given at Sutri, through the hand of Roland, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, 12 Kalends of June, in the third indiction, in the year 1155 of the Lord’s Incarnation [Col. 1427A], in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Adrian IV.

### LVI. He commends the monastery of Saint Antimo to [Arnold], archbishop of Cologne, [Henry], bishop of Constance, and [Wibald], abbot of Stavelot. (Sutri, 28 May.)

[MARTEN., *Ampl. Coll.*, II, 590.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers the archbishop of Cologne and bishop of Constance, and to his beloved son the abbot of Stavelot, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The order alike of reason and equity demands, and the office of the administration you have undertaken invites you, to grant the aid of your protection to pious and religious places [Col. 1427B] and by every means to support them in their justice. Therefore by apostolic letters we command your prudence to take care, for reverence toward blessed Peter and ourselves, to uphold the monastery of Saint Antimo in its rights. According as is known to be contained in the privileges granted to that monastery by the Roman emperors, labor, as you judge expedient, to preserve its liberty; so that it may be our duty to render you fitting thanks and, not without cause, to commend in this matter the zeal of your devotion.

Given at Sutri, 5 Kalends of June [28 May].

### LVII. He directs a certain archbishop, [Eberhard], bishop of Bamberg, and Wibald, abbot of Corvey, to commend Farfa monastery to Frederick, king of the Romans. (Sutri, 1 June.)

[MARTEN., *Ampl. Collect.*, II, 592.]

[Col. 1427C]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable archbishop . . . and bishop of Bamberg, and to his beloved son WIBALD, abbot of Corvey, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Because Farfa monastery belongs specially to the ordering and disposition of the Apostolic See, we have thought fit to request our dearest son Frederick, illustrious king of the Romans, that, for reverence toward blessed Peter and ourselves, he love our beloved son R., abbot of that monastery, and the monastery itself, and send to him letters of his goodwill, in which he may show his favor and benevolent will toward that abbot. In those same letters we have also made petitions to this same most glorious son of ours concerning other matters, which, if carried into effect, are known beyond doubt to concern the benefit and restoration of that monastery.

We therefore command you by these present letters to induce the king’s mind to this end: that the petitions which we have made to him in this matter may, through your efforts and with God’s aid, be swiftly fulfilled; and that he may thus provide, in word and deed, the aforesaid monastery with the salutary support of his aid, so that the said abbot and his brethren may find that our petitions have benefited them and may know that they possess in him a benevolent and effective defender.

[Col. 1428A] Given at Sutri, on the Kalends of June [1 June].

### LVIII. He commends his envoys to the emperor to [Wibald], abbot of Stavelot. (Sutri, 1 June.)

[Ibid.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son the abbot of Stavelot, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The sincerity of your devotion toward the most holy Roman Church, already proved in many matters, leaves no room for doubt in our mind that you are vigilant and diligent in matters concerning her honor. We have determined to send into the presence of our dearest son Frederick, most illustrious king of the Romans, concerning urgent affairs, our beloved sons G., priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Pudentiana; J., priest-cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul; and G., deacon-cardinal of Saint Mary in Portico—prudent, honorable, and learned men, [Col. 1428B] whom we hold very dear.

We therefore admonish and exhort your love in the Lord to assist them diligently before that same son of ours as you would ourselves, and to employ every care so that they may successfully discharge the business entrusted to them for the honor of the most holy Roman Church.

Given at Sutri, on the Kalends of June [1 June].

### LIX. He receives the monastery of Saint Mary of Carcere under protection and confirms its property. (Viterbo, 4 June.)

[MITARELLI, *Ann. Camald.*, III, 481.]

[Col. 1428C]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons DOMINIC, prior of the church of Blessed Mary of Carcere, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

The authority of the Apostolic See, in which by the Lord’s bounty we serve, and the bond of fraternal charity urge us graciously to assent to the just desires of religious persons and their reasonable petitions. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, moved by the prayers of our venerable brother John, bishop of Padua, we graciously assent to your just petitions. We receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the church of Blessed Mary of Carcere, in which you are devoted to divine [Col. 1428D] service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing.

First, we decree that the canonical order known to have been established in that place according to God and the Rule of Blessed Augustine shall be observed there inviolate for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions or goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future, by grant of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, obtain through the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we consider it proper to specify by name: the church of Saint Andrew of Curteroduli with its appurtenances; the tithes of all newly cleared lands which have already been, and shall forever be, made in the place called Carracetulum; and [Col. 1429A] those in Agucciano, throughout Scodassia, in Fracta, in Montagnana, and in Vighizzolo.

We likewise confirm whatever was canonically granted to you by Bellinus and Senebald, former bishops of Padua, of good memory. We also confirm and decree to remain valid the judgment lawfully pronounced by the aforesaid Bishop Bellinus concerning the dispute between you and the clerics of Saint Thecla of Este over the person of Hugh Ballistarius, his sons, and his property.

We therefore decree that no person whatever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, [Col. 1429B] or harass it with any vexations; but that all things be kept intact and whole, to benefit in every way the use of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See.

Should any person therefore, etc.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Manfred, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Sabina. I, Julius, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, Ubald, priest-cardinal of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Gerard, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, Henry, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. [Col. 1429C] I, John, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints Sylvester and Martin. I, Gerald, deacon-cardinal of Saint Mary in Via Lata.

Given at Viterbo, through the hand of Roland, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, 2 Nones of June [4 June], in the third indiction, in the year 1155 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Pope Adrian IV.

### LX. He receives under protection the monastery of Hardehusen, founded by Bernard, bishop of Paderborn, and confirms its property. (Near the city of Castello, 11 June.)

[SCHATEN, *Annal. Paderb.*, I, 805.]

[Col. 1429D]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons VOLBERT, abbot of the monastery of Herswitheleusen, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

Whenever a request is made of us that is known to accord with religion and uprightness, it is fitting that we grant it willingly and afford suitable assistance to the petitioners’ desires. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, moved by the prayers of our venerable brother Bernard, bishop of Paderborn, who built your church at his own expense, we receive the same church under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing.

We decree that whatever possessions and goods [Col. 1430A] that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future, by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, obtain through God’s favor, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. No one whatever shall presume to demand tithes from you on the new lands which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or from the sustenance of your animals.

We therefore decree that no person whatever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things be preserved whole for the use of those for whose governance and support they were granted, to benefit them in every way, saving the authority of the Apostolic See.

Should any person therefore, etc.

Given near the city of Castello, through the hand of Roland, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the third Ides of June [11 June], in the third indiction, in the year 1155 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Adrian IV.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Imar, bishop of Tusculum. I, Guy, deacon-cardinal of Saint Mary in Portico. I, John, deacon-cardinal of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Gerard, deacon-cardinal of Saint Mary in Via Lata. [Col. 1430C] I, Odo, deacon-cardinal of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Guy, priest-cardinal. I, Hubald, priest-cardinal of Saint Praxedes. I, Manfred, priest-cardinal of Saint Sabina. I, Julius, priest-cardinal of Saint Marcellus. I, Bernard, priest-cardinal of Saint Clement.

### LXI. To Henry, bishop of Beauvais—concerning money to be repaid to a certain person. (In the territory of Magliano, 12 June.)

[MARTEN., *Ampl. Collect.*, II, 640.]

[Col. 1430D]

ADRIAN, bishop, etc., to his venerable brother HENRY, bishop of Beauvais, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have recently learned from the complaint of A., bearer of these letters, that he formerly lent forty-one marks of silver to two brothers residing in your court, namely Hu. and R. of Noello, after receiving their oath that they would repay it at the stipulated date; but although that date has now passed, they have made no repayment whatsoever. We therefore command your brotherhood by apostolic letters diligently and urgently to admonish them, within twenty days after receiving these letters, to pay the said sum in full to the aforesaid creditor within two months after [Col. 1431A] your admonition. Should they perhaps refuse to do so, do not delay in applying canonical sentence against them and subjecting all their land to interdict.

Given in the territory of Magliano, 2 Ides of July [read: June; 12 June].

### LXII. Privilege for the Church of Trier. (In the Nepi plain, 15 June.)

[GUENTHER, *Cod. diplom. Rheno-Mosell.*, I, 356.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HILLIN, archbishop of Trier, and to his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

[Col. 1431B] The office of the apostolate entrusted to us by God, and consideration for the welfare of the Church, urge and admonish us to love with fuller charity our brother bishops whom we know to flourish in uprightness and religion, and continually to show them greater honor and favor. For then they can truly be concerned for the welfare of those subject to them and can more effectively apply themselves to fulfilling their office, when they themselves perceive that we bestow more abundant honor upon them and love them with a more devoted affection of charity.

Accordingly, beloved brother Hillin, archbishop in the Lord, having regard for the devotion and sincere affection of the Church of Trier, over which by God’s ordering you are known to preside, and for the due goodwill shown by your predecessors toward blessed [Col. 1431C] Peter, our predecessors, and ourselves, we apostolically confirm for you and your successors, and strengthen by the privilege of this present writing, the dignities, honors, and liberties granted to that Church by our predecessors, the Roman pontiffs John XIII, Benedict VII, Leo IX, Victor II, Innocent, and Eugenius, of happy memory, or by emperors or kings.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Guy, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Chrysogonus. I, Hubald, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Gregory, bishop of Sabina. I, Manfred, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Sabina. I, Julius, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Marcellus. [Col. 1431D] I, Hubald, priest-cardinal of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Guy, priest-cardinal of the title of Pastor. I, Bernard, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Clement. I, Gerard, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, John, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul, the title of Pammachius. I, Henry, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. I, John, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints Sylvester and Martin. I, Guy, deacon-cardinal of Saint Mary in Portico. I, John, deacon-cardinal of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. [Col. 1432A] I, Gerard, deacon-cardinal of Saint Mary in Via Latina. I, Odo, deacon-cardinal of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison.

Given in the Nepi plain, through the hand of Roland, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Roman Church, 17 Kalends of July [15 June], in the third indiction, in the year 1155 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Adrian IV.

### LXIII. He entrusts to Wichmann, archbishop of Magdeburg, the settlement of a case concerning tithes between the bishop of Osnabrück and Abbot Wibald. (In the territory of Tusculum, 11 July.)

[MARTEN., *Ampl. Collect.*, II, 578.]

[Col. 1432B]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother WICHMANN, archbishop of Magdeburg, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have learned from the report of our beloved son Wibald, abbot of Corvey, that the tithes of his villages in Northland, which were formerly unjustly taken from the monastery entrusted to him, are being retained by our venerable brother Philip, bishop of Osnabrück, and certain others in his name. We therefore command your brotherhood by these present letters to summon both parties before you. Having diligently heard the arguments of both sides and examined them with the requisite care, judge what is just in the matter, [Col. 1432C] and cause your judgment to be carried out without obstacle of delay.

Given in the territory of Tusculum, 5 Ides of July [11 July].

### LXIV. He receives the monastery of Heidenheim under protection and confirms its discipline and possessions. (In the territory of Tivoli, 11 July.)

[FALCKENSTEIN, *Cod. diplom.*, 36.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ADELBERT, abbot, and all the brethren of Heidenheim, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since neither the union of charity can safely endure nor service pleasing to God be rendered without the observance of true religion, it is fitting that we, with the Lord’s cooperation, establish the observance of holy religion in all churches and preserve what has been established with exact diligence. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, concurring in assent with your just petitions, we receive your monastery under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and strengthen it by the protection of this present writing.

First, we decree that the monastic order known to have been established in that monastery by the command of Pope Eugenius, our predecessor of happy memory, through the care and foresight of our venerable brother Eberhard, bishop of Bamberg, and our beloved son Adam, abbot of Ebrach, [Col. 1432D] shall be observed there inviolate for all time. Moreover, whatever goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter reasonably obtain by the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors.

We therefore decree that no person whatever may rashly disturb that monastery, take away or diminish its possessions, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things be kept unimpaired and whole, for the benefit of your use and that of your community, saving, of course, the canonical right of the diocesan bishop.

If anyone should presume to attempt this, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not correct his presumption by fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and office, and know himself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed. But upon all who preserve their rights to that place, may there be the peace of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, [Col. 1433B] so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the severe Judge the rewards of eternal life.

Given in the territory of Tivoli, 5 Ides of June [the date prints June, though the heading gives 11 July].

### LXV. Privilege for Hillin, archbishop of Trier. (In the territory of Tivoli, 13 July.)

[GUENTHER, *Cod. diplom. Rheno-Mosell.*, I, 358.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HILLIN, archbishop of Trier, and to his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

Placed by the Lord’s ordering on the lofty watchtower of the Apostolic See, we ought to love our brother bishops with fraternal charity and provide with paternal care for the churches entrusted to them by God. Therefore, beloved brother Hillin, archbishop in the Lord, having regard to your devotion and the sincere fidelity of the Church of Trier toward blessed Peter and ourselves, we strengthen by apostolic authority, and fortify with the page of this writing, the rights and ancient canonical customs known to have existed in your church from long past times.

Namely, we confirm for you and your successors the visitation, in every fourth year throughout your bishopric, for consecrations of churches, confirmations of persons, and correction of offenses according to synodal justice. For the expenses of this labor, we likewise confirm to you and your successors the whole tithe in that fourth year, or a fourth part in each year, [Col. 1433D] as has been established by the sacred canons. Furthermore, we forbid any archdeacon of your church to presume, without your consent, to entrust the care of souls in churches situated within your bishopric to anyone, as our predecessor Pope Eugenius of holy memory is known to have granted to your predecessor Albero, of good memory, and to you.

We therefore decree that no person whatever, etc.

Given in the territory of Tivoli, through the hand of Roland, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, 3 Ides of July [13 July], in the third indiction, in the year 1155 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Adrian IV.

### LXVI. He subjects the monastery of Werbe to Wibald, abbot of Corvey, and his successors. (In the territory of Tusculum, 15 June.)

[MARTEN., *Ampl. Collect.*, II, 619.]

[Col. 1434A]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son WIBALD, abbot of Corvey, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Whenever the most holy Roman Church has seen a church specially belonging to its jurisdiction so worn down in temporal and spiritual matters that it could not be restored to its proper condition unless it received the greater care of another person, it has been accustomed to entrust its own responsibilities for that church’s care to persons who seemed bound to it by sincere devotion and appeared honorable and competent in knowledge to restore its condition.

Therefore, having regard to your worthiness, beloved son Wibald, abbot in the Lord, and to the devotion which you are known to bear toward your mother, the most holy Roman Church, we entrust to you—and through you to the monastery of Corvey committed to your care—the monastery of Werbe, which belongs specially to the jurisdiction of blessed Peter and is known to have been not a little diminished in temporal and spiritual matters, together with its advocacy and all its appurtenances. We decree that it shall remain under your rule and that of your successors for all time, on this condition: that you shall pay two gold pieces from it each year to us and our successors. [Col. 1434C]

Let no person therefore be permitted rashly to infringe the text of this our confirmation and grant, or to oppose it through any molestations. If anyone presumes to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of his apostles, blessed Peter and Paul.

Given in the territory of Tusculum, on the Ides of July [15 July].

### LXVII. He commands [Arnold], archbishop of Mainz, to protect Werbe monastery from the injuries of Count Bobbo. (In the territory of Tusculum [?], July.)

[Ibid., col. 620.]

[Col. 1434D]

ADRIAN, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son in Christ, the bishop of Mainz, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Following in the footsteps of our predecessors, we have entrusted the abbey of Werbe, specially belonging to the right and property of blessed Peter, to our beloved son Wibald, abbot of Corvey, to govern and protect, hoping that, by God’s aid, it may prosper through his prudence. But because Count Bobbo, who asserts that he is advocate of its advocacy, has threatened to harass Werbe monastery and the aforesaid abbot with various disturbances, we command and enjoin your strictness to admonish him rigorously to cease from molesting the abbot and monastery. If he stubbornly and proudly refuses to obey your admonitions, take care to restrain him with canonical censure. [Col. 1435A]

### LXVIII. He grants to Rainer, bishop of Siena, an estate on Mount Bonizi for building a church, subject to an annual rent. (Near the city of Castello, 21 July.)

[MURATORI, *Antiq. Ital.*, V, 811.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother RAINER, bishop of Siena, and to his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

Since, by the office of the supreme pontificate entrusted to us by God, we ought to show ourselves favorable to all Christ’s faithful and hear them in their petitions, we must especially provide with paternal concern for our brother bishops and love them with fuller affection of charity in the performance of their work. Therefore, venerable brother Rainer, bishop in Christ, favorably receiving your just petitions, we have thought fit to grant your brotherhood that, on the estate which our beloved son, the noble Count Guy, is known to have granted on Mount Bonizi to blessed Peter and to ourselves, who, though unworthy, exercise his office, you may build a church; consecrate it when built without any opposition; place clerics in it at your discretion; and freely appoint them.

And, that this our grant may have greater force in future, [Col. 1435C] we have thought fit to confirm it by the protection of our authority and strengthen it with the page of this present writing. We decree that whoever from your diocese goes to that place shall be answerable in all spiritual matters solely to you and your successors, and that you shall retain the same authority as before. Moreover, as a sign of this grant and confirmation, you shall pay one bezant each year to us and our successors.

We therefore decree that no person whatever may rashly infringe the text of this our grant and confirmation or in any way oppose it.

Should anyone indeed, etc.

[Col. 1435D] I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Hubald, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Manfred, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Sabina. I, Ubald, priest-cardinal of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, John, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints John and Paul, the title of Pammachius. I, John, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints Sylvester and Martin. I, John, deacon-cardinal of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Bernard, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Clement.

[Col. 1436A] Gerard, deacon-cardinal of Saint Mary in Via Lata.

Given near the city of Castello, through the hands of Roland, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, 12 Kalends of August [21 July], in the third indiction, in the year 1155 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Adrian IV.

The lead bull is missing.

### LXIX. He grants certain privileges to the monks of Saint Bertin of Sithiu.

(See Iperius, *Chronicle of Saint Bertin*, in MARTEN., *Thesaurus Anecdotorum*, III, 647.)

### LXX. He receives the monastery of Saint Michael of Pisa under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. (Ferentino, 4 October.)

[MITARELLI, *Ann. Camaldul.*, III, Appendix, 482.]

[Col. 1436B]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the abbot of the monastery of Saint Michael, situated in the city of Pisa, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

The authority of our office admonishes and invites us to be concerned for the condition of the Churches and, with the Lord’s help, to provide beneficially for their peace and tranquillity. For it is recognized as worthy and consonant with propriety that we, who by the Lord’s ordering have been appointed to govern them, should protect them from the wickedness of evil men and fortify them by the patronage of blessed Peter and of the Apostolic See [Col. 1436C]. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the monastery in which you are devoted to divine service, strengthening it by the privilege of this present document. First, indeed, we establish that the monastic order which is known to have been instituted in that monastery according to God, the Rule of blessed Benedict, and the customary statutes of the Camaldolese, shall there be preserved inviolate in times to come. Moreover, whatever possessions and goods that monastery at present justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by the grant of popes, the generosity of kings or princes [Col. 1436D], the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, with God’s favour, be able to acquire, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these, we have thought fit to specify the following by name:

The church of St Lawrence of Rivolta, with its hospital and appurtenances; the church of St Cecilia; your right in the church of St Christopher of Colignola, with its entire parishes and dioceses; whatever you possess in the villages of Ghezzano, Colignola, Mezzano, Leona, and Bottano, and within Marceto; whatever you possess in the church of St Peter in Grado—saving the customary due payable to the present archbishop—and whatever you possess near the walls of the city, both in lands and vineyards: all this we likewise confirm to you.

[Col. 1437A] We also grant that the same monastery shall have free burial, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict; nevertheless, the right of the mother church is reserved. You shall receive the ordinations of your monks or clerics who are to be promoted to sacred orders from the diocesan bishop, provided that he is Catholic, possesses the favour and communion of the Apostolic See, and is willing to confer them upon you freely and without the depravity of simony. Otherwise, you may approach whichever bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what is requested. You shall also have free authority to receive clerics or free laypersons who wish to return to you for the sake of conversion. [Col. 1437B] Furthermore, by the assurance of this present decree we establish that no one shall presume, within the bounds of your parish or of your churches, to build any church without the consent of the diocesan bishop and yourselves.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole and unimpaired, for the full benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See.

If anyone therefore, etc.

[Col. 1437C] **MY EYES ARE EVER TOWARD THE LORD.**

Peter and Paul; Pope Adrian IV. I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Imar, bishop of Tusculum. I, Cencius, bishop of the Church of Porto. I, Guido, priest-cardinal of the title of St Chrysogonus. I, Aribert, priest-cardinal of the title of St Anastasia. I, Astaldus, priest-cardinal of the title of St Prisca. I, Guido, priest-cardinal of the title of Pastor. I, Bernard, priest-cardinal of the title of St Clement. I, Gerard, priest-cardinal of the title of St Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, John, priest-cardinal of the title of SS. Sylvester and Martin. [Col. 1437D] I, Oddo, deacon-cardinal of the title of St George at the Golden Veil. I, John, deacon-cardinal of the title of SS. Sergius and Bacchus. I, Oddo, deacon-cardinal of the title of St Nicholas in the Tullian Prison.

Given at Ferentino through the hand of Roland, priest-cardinal of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on 4 October, in the fourth indiction, in the year 1155 of the Lord’s Incarnation [Col. 1438A], in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Adrian IV.

**LXXI.** He announces to Stephen of Metz, Henry of Toul, and A[lbert] of Verdun, bishops, that Hillin, archbishop of Trier, has been appointed legate of the Apostolic See throughout the whole German kingdom. (Alatri, 7 October.)

[D. Bouquet, *Recueil*, XV, 672.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers S., bishop of Metz, HENRY, bishop of Toul, and A., bishop of Verdun; and to his beloved sons, the abbots, provosts, deans, and all ecclesiastical persons, and to the other faithful of God established throughout the archbishopric of Trier: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1438B] The more our venerable brother Hillin, archbishop of Trier, has from the time of his promotion rendered greater reverence and submission to the most holy Roman Church, the more we, though unworthy ministers therein, have judged it right to honour him especially among the other sons of the Church and, as the actual effect of his works demonstrates, to love him with a fuller bond of charity. Therefore, after taking counsel with our brethren, we have granted him our vicariate throughout the whole German kingdom, that he may there exercise the office of legate by authority of the Apostolic See, receiving from us full power to correct whatever needs correction and to order whatever he sees needs ordering.

[Note: [Col. 1437D] Arnold of Mainz had resented this authority and the power attached to the new dignity. Concerning him see John Latomus, in the *Catalogue of the Archbishops of Mainz*, under the year 1155, edited by Mencken, vol. III of the *German Writers*, p. 502: “When the envy of certain persons harassed Arnold, and Hillin, prelate [Col. 1438D] of Trier, claimed jurisdiction over Arnold of Mainz and the other bishops of Germany, Arnold was compelled to lay before the Roman pontiff the injuries done to him. Received honourably by the pope, he also obtained the Apostolic legation; and in that capacity he was introduced into Mainz amid great rejoicing.”]

Since, moreover, by metropolitan right you ought to be subject and obedient to that same brother [Col. 1438C] of ours, and to show him every devotion and reverence, we command your whole body by apostolic letters that, as legate of the Apostolic See—and as one to whom we have judged our authority in this matter should be entrusted—you endeavour to obey him, by right of legation, more particularly and diligently than others, as you would ourselves; and that you in no way presume to oppose those things which he may wish to correct or order in your bishoprics or parishes.

Given at Alatri, 7 October.

**LXXII. To the abbot and brothers of Vézelay.** (Benevento, 21 November.)

[Mansi, *Concilia*, XXI, 815.]

[Col. 1438D]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the abbot and all the brothers of Vézelay: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The more specially your monastery is known to belong to the right of blessed Peter, the more attentively it is fitting for us to labour to direct and enlarge its condition. It has come to us, beloved son in the Lord, abbot, that at the beginning of your prelacy, when the tenor of the same privileges had not yet become known to you, you granted Simon of Silviniac a moneychangers’ table [Col. 1439A], contrary to the tenor of the privileges of the Apostolic See, despite the objections of your brothers. Therefore, since we do not permit the goods of your monastery to be diminished through any thoughtlessness, nor the privileges of our predecessors to be violated, we command you by these present letters: if the matter concerning the table is so, swiftly restore it to your own hands and to the property of the Church; and do not presume in any way to give, sell, or otherwise alienate those things which belong to the property of the monastery. Otherwise, know that severe punishment will be exacted from you.

Given at Benevento, 21 November.

**LXXIII. To the archbishop of Tours—That he settle amicably with the bishop of Dol.** (Benevento, 20 December.)

[D. Bouquet, *Recueil*, XV, 672.]

[Col. 1439B]

The office of the supreme pontificate has, by the Lord’s ordering, been entrusted to us for this purpose: that we should foster all Christ’s faithful, insofar as we are able with God, in their rights, and that we ought to preserve to each person his own justice. Therefore, wishing, with justice as mediator and God’s favour, to settle the controversy long pursued between you and our venerable brother H. [Hugh], archbishop of Dol, concerning the suffragan bishops, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters either [Col. 1439C] to reach an amicable agreement with the aforesaid brother of ours, the archbishop, regarding the suffragans; or to appear before us by the coming feast of All Saints, intending to render or receive full justice; or, without delay, to send the dean of your church and other adequate representatives by the next appointed date. For we desire that, with our judgment intervening, each party may obtain its justice in our hearing.

Given at Benevento, 20 December.

**LXXIV. To all clerics and laypeople established throughout the province of Dol—He confirms the sentence issued by Archbishop Hugh against evildoers and occupiers of ecclesiastical property.** (Benevento, 20 December.)

[Ibidem, p. 673.]

[Col. 1439D]

Whenever a sentence is promulgated by our brothers the archbishops or bishops, or by other prelates of churches, against evildoers and those who occupy ecclesiastical rights, it is fitting that we should hold that sentence ratified; and, that it may be observed more firmly at all times, we ought to confirm it by the authority of the Apostolic See. Therefore we wish it not to be unknown to you all that we regard as ratified and firm the sentence of excommunication which our venerable brother Hugh, archbishop of Dol, has canonically pronounced—or shall pronounce—against John of Dol and the other persons who violently usurp the rights of his archbishopric [Col. 1440A]; and we decree that it shall possess the force of perpetual validity until due satisfaction has been made.

Given at Benevento, 20 December.

**LXXV. He commands [Baldwin], king of Jerusalem, to order restitution to the citizens of Genoa both of money and of a ship taken by his men.** (Benevento, November–December.)

[Caffaro, *Annals of Genoa*, in Muratori, *Writers of Italian Affairs*, VI, 266.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the illustrious king of Jerusalem: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1440B] By the disposing grace of God we have been placed upon the exalted watchtower of the Apostolic See so that we ought to extend the eye of our concern to all parts of the world, and more diligently amend those things known to have been done contrary to the path of justice and the order of right. Our beloved sons, the citizens of Genoa, recently set forth to us in a complaint that your men had violently taken from them, without any reasonable cause, money and the ship in which that money was being carried, and, as we are told, still presume to hold them. If the prudent judgment of your nobility had considered what losses, how many inconveniences, and even what scandals might arise for your land and the kingdom entrusted to you [Col. 1440C] from the occasion of this robbery—since the city of Genoa is glorious, renowned, and deemed most powerful in far-off regions of the world—you ought, even without our admonition, to have ensured that all things unjustly taken by robbery were restored in full to the aforesaid Genoese.

Therefore, lest these Genoese and others should have further cause to complain against you or your faithful, we command your nobility by apostolic letters, strictly ordering that, as you desire to retain the blessing and favour of your most holy mother, the Roman Church, you cause both the money and the ship to be restored to the said Genoese without any diminution. For if any repeated complaint about this affair reaches our ears, we shall be unable to refrain [Col. 1440D] from taking more severe action against your land because of the continued detention of this plunder. We also command your affection by the authority of these presents that henceforth you allow them to possess peacefully and without any disturbance the viscounty of Accaron and the other rights known to belong by right to the Genoese.

Letters to the same effect were written to the count of Tripoli and the prince of Antioch, under penalty of excommunication; he also commanded the patriarch of Antioch by apostolic letters to excommunicate the prince of Antioch unless he fulfilled the aforesaid requirements. He also wrote to the bishop of Bourges [Note: [Col. 1439D] Read: bishop of Béziers.], Agde, and Nîmes, that they should bind Bernard Aton, the men of Béziers, and the men of Agde with the bond of excommunication [Col. 1441A], so that they might restore in full the money taken from our Genoese. And when the Genoese legate sought leave from the pope, the pope handed him a certain ring and said: “Let this be a token of love and favour, on the part of ourselves and the Apostolic See, between us and the Genoese for ever; and let this aforesaid ring, held by you as legate, be a pledge of apostolic friendship and favour.”

**ABOUT THE YEAR 1155.**

**LXXVI. To Henry II, king of England—He grants a privilege for the occupation of Ireland.**

[Mansi, *Concilia*, XXI, 788.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his dearest son in Christ, the illustrious king of the English: greeting [Col. 1441B] and apostolic blessing.
