Therefore we decree that, so long as you remain in the observance of canonical discipline, it shall be lawful for absolutely no person rashly to disturb your church, take away its possessions, retain possessions taken away, diminish them, or harass it by oppressive public services or reckless vexations; but that all things be preserved whole for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted. We further forbid either bishop or archbishop, or indeed any person, to divert the goods of your community to private use, grant them to others in benefice, or alienate them by any other means from the prebend of the brethren or from the common good. [Col. 1467C] Leases, exchanges, or investitures of the aforesaid goods shall never be carried out without the common counsel of the brethren; nor shall this right be usurped by a bishop or by any persons whatsoever, while the canonical reverence due to the Catholic bishops of Bergamo remains intact.

If in the future any archbishop, bishop, emperor, king, duke, prince, count, viscount, or any ecclesiastical or secular person, etc.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Guy, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus. I, Hubald, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Humbald, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross [Col. 1467D] in Jerusalem. I, Octavian, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius. I, Henry, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Sylvester and Martin. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Guy, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison.

Given at Benevento through the hand of Roland, [Col. 1468A] cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the sixth Ides of June, in the fourth indiction, in the year 1156 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Adrian IV.

### CI. He confirms the judgment of Eugenius III concerning the dispute between the canons of Saint Alexander and Saint Vincent of Bergamo. (Benevento, 9 June.)

[LUPI, *Codex diplomaticus Bergomensis*, I, 1151.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons LANFRANC, provost, and the other canons of Saint Alexander of Bergamo and their successors, in perpetual memory.

Whatever is known to have been reasonably established by our predecessors concerning disputes of causes ought to be strengthened by the protection of the Apostolic See. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, wishing to provide for your peace and tranquillity, we strengthen by the protection of this present writing the judgment which Pope Eugenius, our predecessor of happy memory, after sufficient examination in his own presence and that of his brethren of the controversy long contested between you and the canons of Saint Vincent concerning certain matters, promulgated after taking counsel with his brethren, and which Pope Anastasius of blessed memory confirmed by a charter of his own affirmation; and we decree that it shall remain valid and unshaken for all time.

For he ordained that the priests of the bishopric of Bergamo who were ordained after the judgment given by Pope Innocent of happy memory, our predecessor, and those who shall hereafter be ordained, shall render loyalty to both churches; and, even if the canons of Saint Vincent should perhaps refuse to receive it, they must nevertheless render it to your church. Concerning penances, moreover, he commanded that the following be observed between you: whenever priests throughout the bishopric of Bergamo bring their parishioners to penance for public crimes, they shall endeavour to summon both parties, and no penance shall be imposed upon those offenders without the presence of your provost or of one of the priests of your church. He further added that, at the bishop’s table, the provost of your church shall occupy the first place on the left-hand side [Col. 1468D] and shall have his clerics beside him.

He further decreed that, whenever the canons of Saint Vincent come to your church in the customary processions for celebrating the solemnities of Mass, they shall peaceably occupy the four walls of the choir in that church; and that, on the vigil and feast of Blessed Viator, as also in the Gregorian Litanies, you shall honourably receive those canons with incense and holy water, the bells being rung, through your own personnel. But whenever they assemble with you in that church for funeral rites or on other days, you shall occupy the whole choir of your church together with them. Whenever, however, you assemble with them at solemnities, at funeral rites for the dead, or on other occasions, the provost of your church shall occupy the first place on the left-hand side of the choir [Col. 1469A]. The remaining brethren shall sit in common with those clerics.

Likewise, he decreed that the chaplains of the churches of Saint Saviour, Saint Agatha, Saint John, Saint Grata, and Saint Vigilius shall assemble at your church for the principal Masses on Sundays and the chief feast days. But on the Lord’s Supper, at baptism, and at other solemnities, you shall at all times peaceably observe the manner in which you have customarily celebrated the divine offices.

Moreover, since certain priests were contriving delays in rendering you the aforesaid acts of loyalty, and presumptuously postponing them by certain evasions, our predecessor Pope Anastasius of good memory established by apostolic authority that, according to the ancient custom of your church, they shall render them to you immediately after receiving orders. And if they disdain to render them at once, they shall be excluded from the orders they have received until they do render them. By his decree he also ordained that the bishop of Bergamo shall impose upon you no undue or unusual burden.

Therefore, lest you again be wearied by renewed litigation concerning matters decided between you by the judgment of the Apostolic See, and lest one party thereby bring the other into expenses and labours, [lacuna] it is agreed that perpetual silence has been judicially imposed upon both parties. By apostolic authority we have forbidden anyone whatsoever to presume to act against the constitution or decree of the aforesaid Pope Eugenius, our predecessor, [lacuna] and of the aforementioned Pope Anastasius, which we strengthen by the protection of our own affirmation [Col. 1469C], or [lacuna] to oppose our confirmation. Should anyone presume to attempt this, let him incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul. Amen.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus. I, Hubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, Hubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Octavianus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, John, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius. [Col. 1469D] I, Henry, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison.

Given at Benevento by the hand of Roland, cardinal priest of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifth day before the Ides of June, in the year 1156 of the Lord’s Incarnation, the fourth indiction, and the second year of the pontificate of our lord Pope Adrian IV.

## CII. He confirms the peace made with William, king of Sicily, through envoys. (Benevento?, June.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 801.]

[Col. 1470A]

Adrian, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his dearest son in Christ, WILLIAM, illustrious and glorious king of Sicily, and to his heirs whom he shall appoint to the kingdom by his voluntary disposition, in perpetuity.

Although, by the office of the apostolate entrusted to us by God, we ought to embrace all Christ’s faithful in the arms of paternal love and invite them to peace and concord, we ought nevertheless to love and honour kings and all persons of the highest rank all the more [Col. 1470B], and to exhort them toward the good of peace all the more earnestly, because a greater spiritual and temporal benefit is known thereby to accrue to the Church of God and to Christian believers.

It is evident, dearest son in Christ William, glorious king of Sicily, that among the kings and more exalted persons of this world you shine in distinguished achievements, power, and wealth. Thus, through the force of justice which you preserve in the land placed under your rule, through the security of peace in which all who live therein rejoice, and through the terror which by magnificent deeds you have instilled into the enemies of the Christian name, the fame of your name and your glory extend to the farthest corners.

As we, most beloved and eminent son in Christ William, have more diligently considered this, and have likewise considered how great an advantage may come to the Roman Church if your Highness is joined to it in firm peace and concord, we determined, while we were safe and free in the city of Benevento with our brethren, to apply ourselves with earnest zeal to making peace with you. We therefore sent to your Excellency certain of our brethren, namely, as above.

> [Note: [Col. 1469] Thus in the Vatican codex, from which Baronius copied this letter.]

Through them we set forth our desire for the good of peace and concord; and we earnestly invited and exhorted your Excellency to peace. And, through the inspiration of Him who, when about to ascend to heaven, said to His disciples: “Peace I give to you; my peace I leave to you” (John 14), we found your disposition such as was fitting in a son of peace and a Catholic prince. [Col. 1470D] And through the mediation of the aforesaid our sons, etc., as above, we came by our free and spontaneous will to the following form of peace: namely, concerning those articles about which there is a dispute between us and your Excellency, in every respect, etc.

And in order that what we have said above may retain perpetual force both in our own time and in that of our successors, and may not in your time or that of your heirs be disturbed by anyone’s presumption, we, with the common counsel and will of our brethren, confirm these things by apostolic authority, strengthen them by the charter of this present writing to remain valid for ever, and ordain that they shall be observed in perpetuity both by us and by our successors.

[Col. 1471A] Therefore let no one at all be permitted to infringe this charter of our grant and confirmation or rashly oppose it. But if anyone should attempt this, let him incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul. Amen, amen, amen.

Given in the year 1156 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the month of June, the fourth indiction.

## CIII. He commands the bishops of the churches of Agrigento, Mazara, and Malta, established as suffragans of the Church of Palermo, to obey Archbishop Hugh. (Benevento, July 10.)

[PIRRI, *Sicilia sacra*, I, 94.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the elect of AGRIGENTO, MAZARA, and MALTA, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Lest the fullness of sacred ministries should be lacking to Christian believers in any province, the authority of the holy Fathers ordained that every province should have a metropolitan see, which should preside over the others both in the administration of government and in the authority of office. Seeing that Sicily lacked this, we have decreed that the city of Palermo, which until now was held to be a metropolis almost in name alone, shall be established in the full dignity of a metropolitan see; and we have ordained that your cities shall be subject to it by metropolitan right in perpetuity. Therefore, by these apostolic writings, we command you humbly to obey our venerable brother Hugh, archbishop of that place, [Col. 1471C] as your metropolitan, and diligently to render him continual reverence and honour.

Given at Benevento, on the sixth day before the Ides of July.

## CIV. He receives the monastery of Huysburg under protection and confirms its goods. (August 8.)

[*Velle Mitth. a. d. Geb. hist. ant. Forsch.* IV. I, 10.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, etc., to RICHARD, abbot of the monastery of Huysburg, etc. Besides the possessions granted by his predecessors, he confirms the following:

In the district of Halberstadt: estates at Bodesleve, Uplinge, Deleve, Vogelstorp, Tingelstede, Serkestede, [Col. 1471D] Tietevorde, Erkestede, Ricbertiggerode, Anderbeke, Nieustede, and Fleischzehuten in Kowelle, etc.

In the year 1156, fourth indiction, second year of Pope Adrian IV’s pontificate.

## CV. He informs all the clergy and people of Mainz that he has graciously received Archbishop Arnold, “coming into the presence of the Apostolic See out of devotion,” and that he has “released his person, together with his whole bishopric and his suffragan bishops, from the right of legation of Hillin, archbishop of Trier, legate of the Apostolic See”; he commends Arnold. (Narni, August 11.)

[See *Archive für Kunde Österreichischer Geschichtsquellen*, 1850, II, p. 61.]

## CVI. He receives the Church of Balne under protection and confirms its goods and rights. (Narni, August 13.)

[MITARELLI, *Annals of Camaldoli*, III, Appendix, 489.]

[Col. 1472A]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ALBERT, archpriest of the church of Balne, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

Both the force of equity and the order of reason require that effect be granted to just petitioners, especially when mercy aids the wishes of those present and truth does not abandon them. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, receive the aforesaid church, in which you are devoted to divine service, under the protection of blessed Peter and our own, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing.

First, we ordain that the canonical order known to have been established in that place according to the Rule of blessed Augustine and the institution of Saint Frigdianus shall be preserved there inviolably for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future acquire, by grant of popes, gift of kings or princes, offering of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these, we have thought it right to specify the following by their own names:

A garden and mill in the place called Pantanus [Col. 1472C], possessions at Batipalla, and whatever you hold by right in the estate of Castelline.

Likewise, we confirm to you the definitive judgments which our predecessor Pope Innocent of happy memory is known to have canonically pronounced and confirmed by the charter of his writing concerning the controversy between your church and the church of Trevi over chapels, tithes, offerings both of the living and the dead, and the remaining parochial right. We have seen those judgments set out in the privilege of that same predecessor in the following terms:

“Long ago, beloved son in the Lord John, archpriest, you frequently complained to us of the injuries and oppressions which, you said, were inflicted on the church of Balne entrusted to you. Among other matters which you laid before us concerning these burdens, you complained grievously against the abbot of Trevi, asserting that he was violently taking away from the church of Balne twelve chapels, together with their tithes, offerings both of the living and the dead, and the remaining parochial right. Therefore we sent our messenger into your region to investigate the matter diligently [lacuna]; accordingly [lacuna] to summon him, on the next Kalends of June, to plead the aforesaid case before us.

“At that appointed time, both parties having appeared before us, the aforesaid abbot produced in support of his case a certain document in the name of Pope Paschal, our predecessor of blessed memory. On examining it more carefully, we discovered by close scrutiny that it was suspect [Col. 1473A] and falsified, because certain erasures were found in it and other words had been written in place of others. For it is clearer than daylight, both by the authorities of the holy canons and by the general custom of the Church, that every chapel ought to be subject to its parish church and answer to it concerning tithes and other matters pertaining to parochial right. It is manifest that this same parish church is situated within the estate of Saint Peter, prince of the apostles, and stands by proprietary right under his own lordship.

“Having therefore heard the allegations of both parties, it seemed good to us and to our brethren to pronounce definitive judgments in this dispute. But the abbot, desiring to prolong the proceedings and seeking an evasion, requested a long adjournment, promising that he would appear at a date fixed for him more fully prepared for the case and would bring certain documents which he had left at home. Yet, lest we should appear to decide anything precipitately, we granted him an adjournment until the Octave of Saint Martin, commanding him in the meantime to deal in good faith with that same church, which he acknowledged to be subject to Saint Peter, and to pay it the shares, offerings, and tithes of those chapels.

“When the appointed time arrived, the abbot returned to us and produced a certain old volume, in which we could find nothing relevant to the advantage of his case. When repeatedly questioned by us, he also replied that the aforesaid chapels were situated within the parishes of that same parish church. He added that the ministers [Col. 1473C] of those chapels customarily visited that parish church every year with litanies and offerings, and that both the parish church itself, the chapels, and the whole territory of Balne were held to belong to Saint Peter.

“Therefore, having considered the authority of the holy canons and taken counsel with our brethren and with many wise archbishops, bishops, abbots, and others who were present, since the aforesaid abbot could produce no authentic document concerning his acquisition of them, we restore and grant by judgment to you, beloved son in the Lord John, archpriest, and through you to the church of Balne, all the tithes of the aforesaid chapels—whose names are these: Saint Saviour, Saint Nicholas, Saint Paul, Saint Apollinaris, Saint Martin, Saint Paternianus, Saint Hilary, Saint Flora, Saint Margaret, Saint Andrew, Saint Blaise, and Saint Angel [Col. 1473D]—together with all parochial right in those chapels. Thus you shall henceforth have in those chapels the same authority which you exercise in others subject to the aforesaid parish church: namely, to appoint or remove priests, to suspend them, to restore them to office, and to receive the due shares from offerings both of the living and the dead, as well as whatever else pertains to the mother church and to your office. You are further granted authority to dispose and administer, according to the ordinances of the holy canons, all tithes collected at any time from parishioners from the estates of the aforesaid chapels, or received from the whole territory of Balne.”

Following in the footsteps of our predecessor Pope Innocent, we confirm to you, by authority of the Apostolic See, the judgment reasonably and canonically promulgated by him, as we have said, and declare that it shall remain valid and firm for all time. Following in every respect the example of our aforesaid predecessor, we further forbid any ecclesiastical person to receive or possess, in the aforesaid chapels or other places mentioned, or in any others situated within the territory of Balne, any tithes, offerings, or other things belonging to the administration or property of the mother church of Balne, without the consent of that parish church.

Upon the death of you, the present archpriest of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be installed there by any artifice of fraud or violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall have provided to be elected according to God and the Rule of blessed Augustine [Col. 1474B]. We grant you the right, for ordinations both in your church and throughout the whole parish belonging to your parish church, to summon whichever Catholic bishop you prefer from the province of the Roman Church. We further ordain that this parish church and the clergy of that place shall be answerable in nothing to anyone except the Roman pontiff alone. Nor may anyone build a church within the bounds of the parish of that church without the consent of us or our successors.

[Col. 1474C] We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all shall be preserved whole and intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted.

If anyone therefore, etc.

**MY EYES ARE EVER TOWARD THE LORD.**

Saint Peter, Saint Paul, Pope Adrian IV. I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus. I, Ubaldus, of the title of Saint Praxedes. [Col. 1474D] I, Manfred, cardinal priest of Saint Sabina. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, Ubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Bernard, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Sylvester and Martin. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Centius, bishop of Porto and Saint Rufina. I, Gregory, bishop of Sabina. I, Hyacinth, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. [Col. 1475A] I, Octavian, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico.

Given at Narni by the hand of Roland, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the Ides of August, in the fourth indiction, in the year 1156 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the second year of the pontificate of our lord Pope Adrian IV.

## CVII. He receives the Church of Mondoñedo and all its inheritances under the protection of the Apostolic See. (Narni, August 18.)

[FLOREZ, *España sagrada*, XVIII, 345.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother PETER, bishop of Mondoñedo, and to his successors to be canonically appointed in perpetuity.

Since, by the office of the apostolate entrusted to us by God, through which by the Lord’s authorship we have pre-eminence over all Christ’s faithful, we ought to devote ourselves to the peace and tranquillity of each, we must especially be solicitous for the peace of those who are endowed with pastoral dignity and raised to pontifical office. For unless, by attending to their interests, we preserve their rights intact as far as God permits us, and defend them by apostolic authority from the attacks of wicked men, they cannot truly be solicitous for the salvation of those whom the Lord has entrusted to their governance [Col. 1475C].

Therefore, venerable brother in Christ Peter, bishop of Mondoñedo, graciously assenting to your just petitions, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the church of Saint Mary, in which the episcopal see is situated and over which, by the Lord’s appointment, you are known to preside; and we fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. We ordain that whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future acquire by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought it right to specify the following by their own names:

[Col. 1475D] The castle called Goia, with the possessions and people belonging to it; Froxera and Grallial; the monastery of Villanueva, with its churches, inheritances, and people belonging to that monastery; the monastery of Petroso; the monastery of Saint Martin of Neda; the monastery of Saint James of Silva, together with the other monasteries, parishes, possessions, inheritances, and people belonging to the bishopric of Mondoñedo.

Likewise, the churches which you have scattered through various dioceses: namely, in the bishopric of Ourense, ten churches with their possessions and people in the place called Castella; in that of Lugo, ten churches with possessions and people in the place called Deza; in Taveirolos, ten churches with their possessions and people; in Asma, ten churches with their possessions and people; and in Aviancos and Sarria, fifteen churches with all things belonging to them [Col. 1476A].

Moreover, we likewise confirm by apostolic authority that donation which you are known to have made to the church of Saint Martin, where the episcopal see was formerly located—namely, half of all the goods which you possessed there and certain other things—where, that is, with the common counsel of your brethren, you placed Regular Canons.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all shall be preserved whole and intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving, of course, the authority of the Apostolic See.

If anyone therefore, etc.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Guido, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Chrysogonus. I, Ubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Manfred, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cosmas [Col. 1476C]. I, Ubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Bernard, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Clement. I, Octavian, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Gerald, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen. I, John, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius. I, Imarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Centius, bishop of Porto and Saint Rufina. I, Gregory, bishop of Sabina. [Col. 1476D] I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Silverius and Martinianus. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Hyacinth, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, John, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Prison.

Given at Narni by the hand of Aldebrand, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of September, in the fourth indiction, in the year 1156 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the second year of the pontificate of our lord Pope Adrian IV.

In place of the leaden seal.

## CVIII. At the request of Peter, abbot of Cluny, he commands S[tephen], archbishop of Vienne, and C. [Heraclius], archbishop of Lyons, not to permit the monastery of Celsiniac to be harassed by Eustace. (Narni, August 19.)

[D. BOUQUET, *Recueil*, XV, 674.]

[Col. 1477A]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brethren S[tephen], archbishop of Vienne, and C. [HERACLIUS], archbishop of Lyons, greeting and apostolic blessing.

> [Note: [Col. 1477D] Correct E., that is, Heraclius of Montboissier, who himself had formerly been badly harassed by his brother Eustace and was reconciled through Peter’s intervention; from letter 4, book III, of the same Peter.]

Our beloved son Peter, abbot of Cluny, is grievously harassed by his brother Eustace on account of three hundred marks of silver which he demands from him, although Peter declares that he has been prepared to render him, through judicial process, whatever is just. Eustace seizes the men of the aforesaid church, plunders their goods, and continually afflicts them in every way he can [Col. 1477B].

Therefore, because we desire to oppose, with exact diligence both personally and through our brethren and fellow bishops, those who disturb the Church of Cluny, we command you by these present letters to admonish the aforesaid E[ustace] strictly to refrain from harassing the aforementioned monastery and its people and to restore what has been unjustly taken away. But if he should disdain to obey your admonitions, bind him with the bond of excommunication and cause him to be diligently avoided as excommunicated until he comes to his senses.

If indeed he has any claim of right against the Church of Cluny or its dependencies, assemble together, summon the parties before your presence, carefully hear and fully ascertain the arguments on both sides, judge whatever may be just in the matter, and ensure by active enforcement that it is carried out.

Given at Narni, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of September.

## CIX. He receives the Church of Saint Constantius at Orvieto under protection and confirms its goods and privileges. (At Orvieto, October 15.)

[MONTEMARTE, *Chronicle of Orvieto*, II, 231.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ROCCO, provost of Saint Constantius at Orvieto, and his brethren, present and future, canonically appointed.

In order that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth worthily and the advantage sought may unquestionably acquire strength. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, [lacuna] we graciously assent to your just petitions, receive the aforesaid church, in which you are devoted to divine service, under the protection of blessed Peter and our own, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. We ordain that whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future acquire by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God being propitious, [Col. 1478A] shall be [lacuna] secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought it right to specify the following by their own names:

The church of Saint Lawrence with its appurtenances; the church of Saint Bartholomew with its appurtenances; the church of Saint Matthew and the hospital with their appurtenances; the church of Saint Julian and the hospital with their appurtenances; the church of Saint Anastasia with its appurtenances; likewise the estate called Ferosellum with its appurtenances; Mezzana; the field on the bank of Transmarinus; the field before the church of Saint Constantius; the parish church of Saint Peter of [lacuna], with its appurtenances; the parish church of Saint John of Vallelacus with its appurtenances; the parish church of Saint Smiraldus and Saint Stephen of Montelongo with their appurtenances [Col. 1478B]; the parish church of Saint Terentianus with its appurtenances; the parish church of Saint Mary of Miniano with its appurtenances; and the hospital on the bank of Acquapendente, with its church and appurtenances.

Moreover, we likewise confirm to you whatever you justly and canonically possess in tithes, first-fruits, and offerings. We also decree that the burial ground of that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the final-devotional wish of those who have decided to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict, while preserving, nevertheless, the just right of the churches from which they were taken.

And we decree that no one may be permitted to disturb the aforesaid church rashly, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations [Col. 1478C]; but that all things shall be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving, of course, the canonical right of your bishops.

If anyone therefore, etc.

**MY EYES ARE EVER TOWARD THE LORD.**

Saint Peter, Saint Paul. Pope Adrian IV. I, John, cardinal deacon of the title of Saints Gregory and Bacchus. I, Ubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Manfred, cardinal of the title of Saint Sabina. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, Ubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lucy. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Bernard, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill [Col. 1478D]. I, Henry, cardinal priest of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. I, John, cardinal priest of Saints Sylvester and Martin.

Given at Orvieto by the hand of Roland, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the Ides of October, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1156 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the second year of Pope Adrian IV’s pontificate.

## CX. He receives the Church of Belluno under protection and confirms the goods and rights of its canons. (At Orvieto, October.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, V, 150.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ANNO, archpriest of the Church of Belluno, and his brethren, present and future, canonically appointed, in perpetuity.

Both the force of equity and the order of reason require that effect be granted to just petitioners, especially when mercy assists the petitioner’s will and truth does not abandon it. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we willingly assent to your just petitions, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the aforesaid church in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it with the protection of this present writing. We ordain that whatever possessions and goods the same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future acquire by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes [Col. 1479B], offerings of the faithful, or other means, through the Lord’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought it right to specify the following by their own names:

The church of Saint Bartholomew, situated in the place called Agrae, with the hospital building there; the hospital house established in the place called Vedana, and the church founded there; Mount Premezze, with its tithes and appurtenances; land in the estate called Formeganum; and also the estates and possessions, especially those tithes which Aymo, bishop of Belluno of good memory, granted to the same church out of piety, situated in the eastern part of the city of Belluno beyond the river called Ardo. These we likewise confirm to you and, through you, to your church [Col. 1479C].

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any exactions; but that all shall be preserved whole and intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving in all things the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of your bishop, etc.

If anyone therefore, etc.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic See. I, Ubaldus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes. [Col. 1479D] I, Manfred, cardinal priest of Saint Sabina. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, Henry, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. I, John, cardinal deacon of the title of Saints Sergius and Bacchus.

Given at Orvieto by the hand of Roland, cardinal priest of the Holy Roman Church; in the year 1155 [1156] of the Lord’s Incarnation, the fifth indiction, on the third day of October, and in the second year of Pope Adrian IV’s pontificate.

> [Note: [Col. 1479D] The date formula is erroneous.]

## CXI. He receives the Church of Acqui under protection and confirms the goods and rights of its canons. (Lateran, November 12.)

[MORIONDI, *Monumenta Aquensia*, I, 59.]

[Col. 1480A]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons UBERTO, archdeacon of the Church of Acqui, and his brethren, present and future, in perpetuity.

The authority of our office exhorts us, by the Lord’s grant, to make wholesome provision for the peace and welfare of churches; nor is any service ever rendered more pleasing to God, if, proceeding from the root of charity, it is preserved in the purity of religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions [Col. 1480B], receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing; decreeing that whatever possessions and goods that same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by the grant of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or by other just means, through the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The parochial right which you possess in the city and suburb of Acqui, both in tithes and first-fruits, in the penances of the sick and the burials of the dying, and whatever you possess within the boundaries of that place [Col. 1480C], in churches, houses, lands, [lacuna], woods, mills; the parish church of Calamagna; whatever you possess in Plaxano; the parish church of Campali and the tithe of that same place; the whole church of St. Martin of Septebrio and whatever you possess in that place; the church of St. George in Wiwliola and whatever you possess in that place; whatever you possess in Pradasco and Cassinellis; whatever you possess in Ursaria or Ripalta; whatever you possess in Montebono or Casanova; whatever you possess in Tercio and Bestagno, in Melagio and Cartonio, Veredino and Cavatore, in Vidixone and Cascinis; whatever you possess in the land of the lords of Barberio; the rent from the churches of Gamondi, in money and candles; the oil-rent of Codolet; the oil-rent of Albenga; the rent from the church of St. [Col. 1480D] Thomas of Canello.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things be preserved unimpaired and entire, for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of your bishop.

If anyone therefore, etc.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Guido, priest-cardinal of St. Chrysogonus. I, Ubaldus, priest of the Church of St. Praxedes. [Col. 1481A] I, Octavianus, titular priest of St. Cecilia. I, Oddo, cardinal-deacon of St. George. I, Guido, cardinal-deacon of St. Mary in Portico. I, Odo, cardinal-deacon of the Tullian Prison. I, Henry, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Roland, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the second Ides of November, in the fifth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1156, in the second year of the pontificate of our lord Pope Adrian IV.

## CXII. He receives the Church of St. Mary of Pineta into protection and confirms its goods and rights.

*(Lateran, November 30.)*

[Lami, *Ecclesiastical Monuments of Florence*, I, 81.]

[Col. 1481B]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons in Christ, HUGH, parish priest of the church of Blessed Mary at Pineta, and his brethren, present and future, canonically appointed, forever.

The authority of our office admonishes and invites us to labor for the condition of churches and, with God’s help, to make wholesome provision for their peace and tranquillity. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that same church now justly and canonically [Col. 1481C] possesses, or may hereafter acquire by the grant of pontiffs, the gifts of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names.

The church of St. Martin of Strata with all its appurtenances; the church of St. [lacuna] (Mary) in the castle of Monte Acuto; the church of St. Mary of Carpineta with all its appurtenances; the church of St. Justus of Mazzaena with all its appurtenances; the church of St. Peter in Jerusalem with all its appurtenances; the church of St. Stephen of Patholatico with all its appurtenances [Col. 1481D]; the church of St. Lawrence of Lerose with all its appurtenances; the church of St. Peter of Muliermala with all its possessions; the church of St. Martin of Bagnoio with all its appurtenances; the church of St. Stephen of Bifonicae with all its appurtenances; the church of St. Andrew of Lujano with all its appurtenances; the church of St. Romulus of Bopsi with all its appurtenances; the church of St. Martin of Caffari with all its appurtenances; the church of St. George of Pineta with all its appurtenances; the church of St. Christopher of Strata with all its possessions; the church of St. Christina of Panicole with all its possessions; the church of St. Hilary of Pitiliano with all its [Col. 1482A] possessions; the church of St. Lawrence of Collina with all its possessions; the church of St. Michael of Daethano with all its appurtenances; the church of St. Minias of Quintulo with all its possessions; and twelve tithe-churches.

You may appoint clergy to those chapels and establish fit priests in them, who shall humbly render you the due obedience and reverence. Moreover, the people living within the territory of your parish shall, without anyone’s opposition, pay you what is legally due in tithes, first-fruits, offerings, burials, wills, and mortuary garments, as well as in other matters, as is known to be contained in the privilege of Pope Nicholas, our predecessor of blessed memory. [Col. 1482B] Furthermore, by apostolic authority we prohibit anyone whatsoever from building any church or hospital within the boundaries of your parish without your consent and that of the bishop, or from daring to subject a building already erected to another’s authority. Nor may anyone presume to build any house in the cemeteries of the aforesaid churches. No one shall receive your parishioners for burial unless your right, which belongs to you by the ordinance of the sacred canons, is preserved for you in its entirety.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things [Col. 1482C] be preserved unimpaired and entire, for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop.

If anyone therefore, etc.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Centhius, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina. I, Gregory, bishop of Sabina. I, Guido, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Chrysogonus. I, Hubaldus, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Praxedes. I, Julius, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Marcellus. I, Manfredus, priest-cardinal of St. Sabina. I, Bernard, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Clement. [Col. 1482D] I, Octavianus, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Cecilia. I, Gerardus, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, John, of the title of Saints John and Paul, of Pammachius. I, Odo, cardinal-deacon of the title of St. George at the Golden Veil. I, Hyacinth, cardinal-deacon of St. Mary in Cosmedin. I, Hildebrand, cardinal-deacon of St. Eustace beside the Temple of Agrippa.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Roland, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Kalends of December, in the fifth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1156, in the second year of the pontificate of our lord Pope Adrian IV.

## CXIII. Bull for the Church of Nîmes.

*(Lateran, December 10.)*

[*Gallia Christiana*, vol. VI, Documents, 198.]

[Col. 1483A]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother ALDEBERT, bishop of Nîmes, and to his successors canonically appointed.

Placed, by the Lord’s disposition, on the lofty watchtower of the Apostolic See, we ought to love our brother bishops, whether near or far away, with fraternal charity, and to preserve for the churches in which they are known to serve the Lord their rights. Therefore, beloved brother in the Lord, Bishop Aldebert, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves the church of Nîmes of the Blessed Mother of God and ever-virgin [Col. 1483B] Mary, over which, by God’s ordinance, you are known to preside; and we strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods you now justly and canonically possess, or may hereafter acquire by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God being favorable, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names.

Within the walls of that city: the monastery of St. Saviour of the Fountain; the church of St. Martin of the Sands; the church of St. Thomas; the church of St. Vincent; the church of St. Stephen of the Capitol; the church of St. [Col. 1483C] Lawrence; the castle called the Arles Gate; one third of all market and fair tolls; one third of the *sextarius*, *corde*, and *quintal*; and one third of all stalls, saving in this the right of the canons. Outside the city: the abbey of Cendrac; the monastery of Tornac; the castle of St. Martial with its church; the castle of St. Bonitus with its church; the castle of Leguas with its church; the castle of Montpesat; the church of St. Stephen of Garons with its village and territory; the church of St. Gervasius with its village; the church of Amiglau with the village situated on the hill; the church of St. Mary of Gaujac with its village; the church of Dorbia with its chapels; [the churches] of Valle Garnita and Rocafolio. In the diocese of Uzès [Col. 1483D], the village of Rovoreto; and likewise all other churches, possessions, and other things known to belong to your right, we confirm to you and your successors.

We decree that the agreement reasonably made between you and the canons of your church, by the counsel of wise and discerning men, shall remain valid and be observed as is contained in the writings drawn up concerning it. Furthermore, inclined by the prayers of your fraternity, we confirm by apostolic authority to those who profess the regular life, and to their successors, all churches, possessions, and goods which they justly and canonically possess through your grant or that of other faithful of God, or may hereafter acquire by reasonable means, God being favorable. Among these we have thought fit to note the following by their proper [Col. 1484A] names.

Within the walls of that city: the church of St. Mary Magdalene; the church of St. Eugenia; the church of St. Stephen between the two churches; the church of St. John. Outside the city: the church of Margarita; the church of Agarna; the church of Costaballenis; the church of Carto; the church of St. Perpetua; the church of Polvereries; the church of Bollanicis; the church of Fonte Cooperto; the church of Liveriis; the church of Brociano; the church of Codol; the church of Melignanicis; the church of Geneirac; the church of Bellovicino; the church of Poscheriis; the church of Olodanicis; the church of Carrugeriis; the church of Galadanicis with its chapels; St. Guiraldus of Villetella; St. Mary of Ponte Ambrosio; and St. Cosmas; [Col. 1484B] the church of Cavairac; the church of St. Cosmas; the church of St. Dionysius; the church of Anagia; the church of Bosseriis; the church of Bizac; the church of Calvitione; the church of Liveriis; the church of St. Mary of Congénies; the place of St. Mary of Bonaur; the church of St. Andrew of Congénies; the church of Saumanicis; the church of Podiis; the church of Leuc; the church of Bordet; the church of Sumène; the church of Rocaduno; the church of Vissec; the church of Aulatis; the church of Daveda; the church of St. Romanus. In the diocese of Uzès: the church of Calmetis; the church of Roveria; the church of Montinianicis; the church of Guillano. In the diocese of Mende: the church of Melosa. We therefore confirm the aforementioned churches, with their chapels and all [Col. 1484C] their appurtenances, to the same canons as we have said above, while preserving the canonical right of you and your successors, and of the other bishops within whose parishes those churches are situated.

We further prohibit anyone from presuming to establish an oratory or cemetery within the parish of the church of St. Mary, the see of Nîmes, and the monastery of St. Baudilus without the consent of the bishop and canons. We also decree that, with your assent, monks and canons shall place priests in the parish churches which they hold; and, if such priests are suitable, you shall entrust them with the care of the parish, so that priests of this sort may answer to you concerning the care of the people, while rendering due subjection to those monks and canons in temporal matters. We further prohibit [Col. 1484D] anyone from receiving for burial parishioners of the Church of Nîmes without your and the canons’ consent, unless they themselves have determined to be buried in some venerable place.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things be preserved entire, for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See. But if any ecclesiastical or secular person knowingly [lacuna] this page of our constitution, etc.

Place of the seal.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. [Col. 1485A] I, Ymarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Lentius, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina. I, Gregory, bishop of Sabina. I, Guido, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Chrysogonus. I, Ubaldus, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Praxedes. I, Manfredus, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Sabina. I, Julius, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Marcellus. I, Otho, cardinal-deacon of the title of St. George at the Golden Veil. I, Guido, cardinal-deacon of St. Mary in Portico. I, Hyacinth, cardinal-deacon of St. Mary in Cosmedin. I, Hildebrand, cardinal-deacon of St. Eustace.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Roland, priest-cardinal of the Holy Roman Church, of the chancery, on the fourth Ides of December, in the fifth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation [Col. 1485B] 1156, in the third year of the pontificate of our lord Pope Adrian IV.

## CXIV. He confirms the privileges and possessions of the monastery of St. Denis.

*(Lateran, December 18.)*

[Doublet, *History of Saint-Denis*, 501.]

[Col. 1485B]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son ODON, abbot of the monastery of the Blessed martyr Dionysius, situated at Paris, and to his successors regularly appointed, forever.

Although, by the office of the apostolate entrusted to us by God, we judge ourselves indebted to all churches and ecclesiastical persons, it especially becomes us to provide with a more earnest concern of charity for those known to be familiars of Blessed Peter and [Col. 1485C] the Holy Roman Church. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Odo, whose fidelity and devotion to Blessed Peter and the Holy Roman Church we have proved by certain evidence, we gladly assent to your reasonable petitions. We decree, therefore, that whatever dignity has been granted to that place by the authentic privileges of our predecessors, the Roman pontiffs Zacharias, Stephen, Leo, Alexander, Paschal, Calixtus, Innocent, and Eugenius; whatever goods are known to belong to that monastery through the lawful offerings of Catholic kings or other faithful persons; and whatever it may hereafter acquire by the grant of pontiffs, the gifts of kings or princes, or other just means, through the Lord’s bounty, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your [Col. 1485D] successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

In the district of Metz, the new cell with all its appurtenances, namely Hulsperc, Ausminge, Enmelingas, the church of Fulcreia, the saltworks and salt-pans at Marsal; the monastery of Argenteuil, situated in the district of Paris on the River Seine, with its appurtenances. In the diocese of Orléans: the field of Mainetii, Villare, Vendrous, Villammeium, Feienis, Liuns. In the diocese of Laon: the altar of Caadursa, the altar of St. Gobert, the altar of Pirolis, the altar of Sairiac with the chapel of St. Denis at Ribemont. In the valley of Vison: the altar of Sorbais, the altar of Altrepia, the altar of Rochiniis, the altar of the Serene Springs. [Col. 1486A] In the diocese of Cambrai: the altar of Solesmes, the altar of Vertiniolo, with their tithes and all appurtenances. In the diocese of Rouen: the church of Calvomon with its appurtenances, which our venerable brother Hugh, archbishop of Rouen, with the consent of our dearest son Louis, king of the Franks, gave to you. In the diocese of Paris: the cell of Blessed Mary situated near Corbeil on the River Essonne, with its appurtenances. By the gift of the aforesaid king: whatever he had in the village of Tropis, except the annual lodging when he should stay there, and the *tallia* which he gave you at Cergy in the Vexin and at Cormelles. By the gift of Geoffrey, bishop of Chartres, of good memory: the altars of Monarville and Rubrido. By the gift of Aluisius, bishop [Col. 1486B] of Arras: the altar of Anechin. By the gift of the illustrious memory of Edward and William, kings of England: Deerhurst, situated on the River Severn; Taunton and More; Rulias with its appurtenances; the church of Berno; the church of Bosia; the church of Vico Pleno; the church of Chasanoy; the church of Aldo; the church of Pelolio and the demesne field lying near the church; the church of Nopsiac; the church of Malliac; the church of Duobus Casis; the church of Stivaliculis; the church of Giveretis; the church of Argentearia; the church of Vallo [otherwise, “of the valleys”]; the church of Lanatico; the church of Vimreziac; the church of Noto; the church of Archiniac; Leuraam [otherwise Lebraham] in Germany, with all its appurtenances. In the diocese [Col. 1486C] of Le Mans: Saint Gaburge (*the priory of St. Gaulburge*), with all its appurtenances; the chapel of Gastinel (*the chapel of Gastineau*); the church of Allennes (*Notre-Dame d’Aleines*); the church of Malo Stabulo (*of Mallétable*); Castrum Novum, with all its appurtenances; Furnellos in Spain, with all its appurtenances; the church of St. Martin; the church of Arcolio; the church of Marniac with its appurtenances.

We likewise confirm to you the vicariate, every form of jurisdiction, and full liberty around the village of St. Denis, as distinguished by the following boundaries: namely, from the River Seine, from the mill commonly called Bayard, as far as the upper end of the village called Habervillare, which the aforesaid King Louis, acknowledging it to belong by right to St. Denis, restored to it. [Col. 1486D] Furthermore, we confirm by the protection of our authority, so that you may possess them peacefully forever, every power, every jurisdiction, and all the customs of the proclaimed fairs which have been granted you by the liberality of that same king.

We decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with rash vexations; but that all things be preserved entire for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted. When you, the present abbot of that place, or any one of your successors dies, no one [Col. 1487A] shall be placed over it by any cunning of fraud or by force, except the person whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, shall elect according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict. The person elected shall be consecrated either by the Roman pontiff or by whichever Catholic bishop he prefers. You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars and basilicas, and ordinations of monks or clerics belonging to the same monastery from Catholic bishops, as was established by the privileges of canonical equity of our predecessors. We prohibit public Masses from being celebrated or a station held in that monastery without the abbot’s consent; nor do we allow bishops or their ministers the power to impose an interdict upon, excommunicate, or summon to a synod either the abbot or the monks of that place. [Col. 1487B] Moreover, we grant both you and your successors leave to appeal to the Apostolic See in graver cases; nor shall any injury be done to those who appeal before the case is concluded, so that, with God as author, you may remain peaceful and diligent in the pursuits of holy religion.

If anyone hereafter, etc. To all, etc.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Hubaldus, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Praxedes. I, Manfredus, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Sabina. I, Hubaldus, priest-cardinal of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. [Col. 1487C] I, Astaldus, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Prisca. I, Girardus, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Stephen. I, John, priest-cardinal of the title of Pammachius. I, Centhius, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina. I, Gregory, bishop of Sabina. I, Odo, cardinal-deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil. I, Guido, cardinal-deacon of St. Mary in Portico. I, Hyacinth, cardinal-deacon of St. Mary in Cosmedin. I, Hildebrand, cardinal-deacon of St. Eustace. I, Odo, cardinal-deacon of St. Nicholas in the Tullian Prison.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Roland, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman [Col. 1487D] Church, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of January, in the fifth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1156, in the third year of the pontificate of our lord Pope Adrian IV.

## CXV. He receives the monastery of St. Bavo of Ghent into protection and confirms its goods.

*(Lateran, December 31.)*

[Miraeus, *Diplomatic Works*, IV, 21.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons BETTO, abbot of the monastery of St. Bavo, and his brethren, present and future, regularly appointed, forever.

It is fitting that apostolic protection be [Col. 1488A] at hand for those choosing the religious life, lest perhaps an attack of any rashness either turn them back from their resolve or, God forbid, weaken the strength of sacred religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, strengthening it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper [Col. 1488B] names:

The altars of St. Bavo, free from every personal benefice (*personatus*); the altar of Waterlos; the altar of Aspera with its appurtenances; the altar of Gremmine; the altar of Dorla; the altar of Poesela; the altar of Canenchein; the altar of Vinderholt; the altar of Lathem; the altar of Eckerchem with its appurtenances; the altar of Everchem; the altar of Christi-Kercka with its appurtenances; the altar of Rodemburch with its appurtenances; the altar of Vondeslo; the altar of Danckenam; the altar of Murcoka; the altar of St. Bavo within the diocese of Cambrai; the altar of Swalma with its appurtenances; the altar of Holthem; the altar of Esscha; the altar of Rothem; the altar of Flethersele with its appurtenances; the altar of Selleka; [Col. 1488C] the altar of Cobbenchem; the altar of Bocholt with its appurtenances; the altar of Fonnethe.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things be preserved unimpaired and entire, for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop.

If anyone therefore, etc.

I, Adrian [Pope IV]. I, Hubaldus, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Praxedes. I, Gregory, bishop of Sabina. [Col. 1488D] I, Hyacinth, cardinal-deacon of St. Mary in Cosmedin. I, Hildebrand, cardinal-deacon of St. Eustace. I, Henry, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Roland, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the second day before the Kalends of January, in the fifth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1156, in the third year of the pontificate of our lord Pope Adrian IV.

## CXVI. Privilege for the monastery of St. Peter of Aldenburg.

*(Lateran, December 31.)*

[*Chronicle of the Monastery of Aldenburg*, Appendix, 94.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons HERMANN, abbot of St. Peter of Aldenburg, [Col. 1489A] and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, forever.

Both the force of equity and the order of reason require that just petitioners be granted their requests, especially when piety supports the petitioners’ desire and truth does not oppose it. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and especially receive under the protection of Blessed Peter and ourselves the monastery in which you are devoted to divine service, strengthening it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by the grant of pontiffs, the gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s favor, [Col. 1489B] shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

One third of the tithe of the whole parish of Aldenburg; furthermore, one third of the tithe, all offerings, and whatever proceeds from the altar of St. Mary, except the benefices belonging to the priesthood. All these things, under an annual rent of eight pounds and eleven solidi, which you are bound to pay annually, as is contained in the privileges of the Church of Tournai, we confirm to you by apostolic authority: the tithe of Herneghem, and the land which you possess at Aldenburg.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may [Col. 1489C] rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things be preserved unimpaired and entire, for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop.

If anyone therefore, etc.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Roland, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the day before the Kalends of January, in the fifth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1156, in the third year of the pontificate of our lord Pope Adrian IV.

## CXVII. He confirms the election of Archbishop Berengar.

(*Gallia Christiana*, VI, Documents, 40.)

[Col. 1489D]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son B., elect of the Church of Narbonne, greetings and apostolic blessing.

The Church of Narbonne, deprived of its own shepherd, sought to elect you as its father and archbishop, and wished to present its election to the holy Apostolic See. [Note: [Col. 1489D] Some word is missing here.] Concerning this, after it had been somewhat discussed in our presence by our brethren, because we believe that through you the state of that Church can, by the Lord’s agency, be reformed for the better, we have thought fit to confirm that election. Therefore, by this present writing we command you that, when you have been requested by our sons, the clerics of the Church of Narbonne, [Col. 1490A] you shall go to the aforesaid church and, trusting in the abundant mercy of the Almighty, undertake the episcopal burden.

## CXVIII. He confirms for the hospital house of Canterbury the church of Northborne, granted by Silvester, abbot of St. Augustine’s, for the relief of pilgrims and the poor.

*(Twisden, *Historical Writers of England*, II, 2110.)*

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons SILVESTER, abbot, and all the monks of the church of St. Augustine, greetings and apostolic blessing.

“Concerning these works, etc.” Below: From inspection of your letters, since we have learned through the report of our beloved son R., your fellow brother, that you have granted, out of regard for mercy, the church [Col. 1490B] of Northborne, with its chapels, tithes, and all appurtenances, to the hospital house built before your gate, for the relief of pilgrims and the poor: and since you requested that this your grant be strengthened by our patronage, we, at your petition, confirm it by apostolic authority and strengthen it by the protection of this present writing, as it is known to have been reasonably made by you and confirmed by the text of your document, etc.

## CXIX. A.D. 1154–1157. At the request of Theobald, bishop of Paris, he confirms the agreement concluded between Stephen, his predecessor, and Theobald the archdeacon.

(See Petit, *The Penitential of Theodore*, II, 718.)

[Col. 1490C]

## CXX. He settles the controversy between Lanfranc, bishop of Lodi, and Berard, abbot of the monastery of St. Sixtus of Piacenza, concerning the church of St. Michael at Castronovo.

(Campi, *History of Piacenza*, II, 354.)

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother LANFRANC, bishop of Lodi, greetings and apostolic blessing.

Matters established between ecclesiastical men by reasonable provision through the mediation of a settlement or agreement ought to remain stable, and it is necessary that they be strengthened by the protection of the Apostolic See so as to have greater [Col. 1490D] firmness in the future. Therefore, venerable brother in the Lord, Bishop, we have thought fit to strengthen by the authority of the Apostolic See the agreement reasonably made in our presence, with the consent of each party, between you and our beloved son Berard, abbot of the church of St. Sixtus of Piacenza, concerning the church of St. Michael of Castronovo, over which a dispute had arisen between you; our beloved son Giufredus, your envoy, acting jointly in this matter with that abbot, having been granted full authority by you concerning it. That settlement was made as follows, as is set out below.

The priest who is to be installed in that church of St. Michael [Col. 1491A] shall be chosen by the abbot and presented to you; if found suitable, he shall receive from you the care of souls and promise obedience, which he shall render to you in the care of souls. He shall answer to you and your successors concerning the care of the people, but to the abbot and his successors concerning temporal matters. Moreover, you shall claim in that church all episcopal rights except a share of the tithes and first-fruits; and every fourth year, when you come to that church, sufficient necessities for dinner or supper must be supplied to you, twelve persons, and as many mounts. The abbot, or the priest then serving there, shall annually pay twelve Milanese denarii of the old coinage from the aforesaid church to you and your successors on the feast of St. Martin as a rent. [Col. 1491B] Except for these things set out above, nothing else shall be owed in that church. That the aforesaid settlement made between you may be observed inviolate in future times, we confirm it by apostolic authority and strengthen it by the protection of this present writing. We decree that no person whatsoever may infringe this page of our confirmation or in any way act against it, etc.

## A.D. 1157.

## CXXI. He orders [Silvester], abbot of St. Augustine’s at Canterbury, to render obedience to [Theobald], archbishop, within thirty days.

[Gervase’s *Chronicle*, in Twysden, *Historical Writers of England*, II, 1379.]

[Col. 1491C]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son, the abbot of St. Augustine’s, Canterbury, greetings and apostolic blessing.

The more our venerable brother, the Archbishop of Canterbury, legate of the Apostolic See, is known always to have been faithful and devoted to the most holy Roman Church from the very time of his elevation, the more earnestly ought we to love him and the Church entrusted to him, and to preserve for it its rights unimpaired and entire. Therefore we command your belovedness by apostolic letters that, just as it is established that some predecessor of yours [Col. 1491D] rendered obedience at some time to a predecessor of this same brother of ours, the archbishop, so, setting aside every appeal and excuse, you shall not delay to render that obedience to him within thirty days after receiving this letter.

### CXXII. He grants the convent of St. Mary at Caramagna to Anselm, bishop of Asti. (Jan. 4.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, IV, 365.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother ANSELM, bishop of Asti, greeting and apostolic blessing.

What is done by reasonable foresight of our predecessors, the Roman pontiffs, we desire to endure in its stability [Col. 1492A] and, lest it be altered in future times, to be strengthened also by our protection. The monastery of Blessed Mary, situated at the place called Caramagna, stands under the protection and disposition of the Apostolic See and is known to belong to its right by an ancient offering. Therefore, bestowing care, by provision of the Apostolic See, upon its improvement and recovery, we entrust this same place to you, dearest brother and fellow bishop Anselm, and to your successors, after the example of Pope Callixtus, our predecessor of blessed memory, so that you may act there in our stead in the appointment and consecration of abbesses and in the other episcopal administrations, while in all things preserving the right and reverence of the Roman Church and the annual payment to the Lateran [Col. 1492B] palace of one gold piece.

For, as we have learned from the report of religious brethren, the same monastery has been greatly diminished both spiritually and temporally, and, through your particular diligence, may, with the Lord’s aid, be restored to a better condition and defended from the power and attacks of wicked persons. Therefore let no person whatsoever have authority to withdraw the aforesaid monastery from your oversight and subjection, or with any rashness to remove what has been established by us; rather, by God’s grace, you shall freely discharge our office in all things, as stated above, for the honor of God, the salvation of our souls, and the inward and outward increase and improvement of the place. But if anyone [Col. 1492C] should with audacious rashness act against this our commission, let him incur danger to his rank and office, or be punished by severance through excommunication, unless he restrains his presumption by fitting satisfaction.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church.  
I, Otto, cardinal-deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil.  
I, Manfred, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Sabina.  
I, Guido, cardinal-deacon of St. Mary in Portico.  
I, Ymanus, bishop of Tusculum.  
I, Hyacinth, cardinal-deacon of St. Mary in Cosmedin.  
I, Cencius, bishop of Porto and St. Rufina.  
I, Oddo, cardinal-deacon of St. Nicholas in the Tullian Prison.  
I, Octavian, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Cecilia.  
[Col. 1492D] I, Ardicio, cardinal-deacon of St. Theodore.  
I, John, cardinal-deacon of SS. John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius.  
I, Boso, cardinal-deacon of SS. Cosmas and Damian.

Given through the hand of Roland, cardinal-priest of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the second day before the Nones of January, in the fourth indiction, in the year 1156 from the Incarnation of the Lord, in the third year of the pontificate of our lord Pope Adrian IV.

### CXXIII. To Wibald, abbot of Stavelot.—That he should urge the emperor to remain in reverence for the Apostolic See. (Lateran, Jan. 19.)

[MARTEN., *Ampl. Collect.*, II, 597.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 1493A] son WIBALD, abbot of Stavelot, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Considering the devotion which, while you were present, your prudence showed us, we judge nothing concerning your person except what befits an upright man and a devoted son. Hence, although very many endeavor to maintain that, in Greece, contrary to the opinion we hold of you, you devised many schemes against us and against your mother, the most holy Roman Church, we nevertheless do not wish to give credence to that assertion, because the devotion which you displayed to us in our presence does not permit us to believe such things.

Moreover, because, as a certain wise man says, life judges concerning what came before, we consider from future events what we ought to believe concerning the matters aforesaid. Since, therefore, there are said to be certain persons about our dearest [Col. 1493B] son Frederick, emperor of the Romans, who labor by every means to extinguish in his mind devotion toward the most holy Roman Church, we command your belovedness by apostolic letters that, according to your prudence, you resist their wicked suggestions and admonish the aforesaid emperor to remain, as he ought, in reverence for the Apostolic See, so that he may in no way be moved from sound and upright judgment by anyone’s suggestions. For by this we shall be able to know what we may hold without any doubt concerning the devotion of your mind.

Given at the Lateran, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of February.

### CXXIV. He receives the convent of St. Zacharias at Venice under his protection. (Lateran, Feb. 18.)

[CORNELII, *Ecclesiae Venetae*, XI, 374.]

[Col. 1493C]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ GISELDRUDA, abbess of the monastery of St. Zacharias, and her sisters, present and future, regularly appointed, in perpetuity.

It befits the clemency of apostolic governance to cherish religious persons and defend their places by the safeguard of pious protection. Therefore, beloved daughters in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to the divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this document, [Col. 1493D] establishing first that the monastic order known to have been instituted there according to God and the observance of the brethren of Cluny shall be observed inviolate in perpetuity.

Moreover, whatever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, God being favorable, through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and those who succeed you. Among these we have considered the following worthy of expression by their proper names:

The estate situated in the village called Petriolo, with the church of St. Thomas and all [Col. 1494A] its appurtenances; the estate situated in the place called Cona, with the church of St. Mary and all its appurtenances; and whatever is held at Sacco, Lupa, Liquentia, and Laurentiaca, together with their appurtenances. We likewise confirm to you the tithes of all the tenants of those same estates which you lawfully possess. We further prohibit the admission henceforth of any sister into the same monastery who presumes in any manner to possess private property.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; rather, let all things remain whole and unimpaired, serving in every way the uses for which they were granted—for the governance and support of those concerned—while preserving the authority of the Apostolic See [Col. 1494B] and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop.

If anyone therefore, etc.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church.  
I, Ubald, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Praxedes.  
I, Manfred, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Sabina.  
I, Octavian, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Cecilia.  
I, Actald, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Prisca.  
I, Gerard, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Stephen on the Caelian Hill.  
I, John, cardinal-priest of SS. John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius.  
I, Aldiprand, cardinal-priest of the Basilica of the Twelve Apostles.  
I, Odo, cardinal-deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil.  
[Col. 1494C] I, Rodulf, cardinal-deacon at the Septa Solis.  
I, Guido, cardinal-deacon of St. Mary in Portico.  
I, Bonadies, cardinal-deacon of St. Angelo.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Roland, cardinal-priest of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of March, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1156 from the Incarnation of the Lord, in the third year of the pontificate of our lord Pope Adrian IV.

### CXXV. He receives under his protection the monastery of the Scots, St. James at Regensburg, confirms its possessions and privileges, and imposes upon the monks an annual payment of one bezant. (Lateran, March 19.)

[RIED, *Codex diplomaticus Ratisbonensis*, I, 224.]
