ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 1494D] sons GREGORY, abbot of the monastery of St. James situated in the suburb of Regensburg, and his Scottish brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

A pious request ought to be fulfilled by the resulting effect, so that the sincerity of devotion may appear praiseworthy and the benefit requested may undoubtedly gain force. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests and, following in the footsteps of our predecessors of blessed memory, the Roman pontiffs Calixtus and Eugenius, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this document. First, we establish that [Col. 1495A] the monastic order known to have been instituted in that place according to God and the Rule of blessed Benedict shall there be preserved inviolate in perpetuity.

Moreover, whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, God being favorable, through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. We also decree that the burial-place of that house shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last wish of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict, while preserving the right of the mother church. As an acknowledgment of this protection granted by the Apostolic See [Col. 1495B], you shall pay one bezant each year to us and our successors.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery; take away, retain when taken, diminish, or harass with any vexations the watercourse lawfully granted to you by the abbot of Prüfening, or its other possessions. Let all things remain whole, serving in every way the uses for which they were granted—for the governance and support of those concerned—while preserving the canonical right of the bishop of Regensburg.

If anyone therefore, etc.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church.

Then follows the subscription of five cardinals.

[Col. 1495C] Given at the Lateran through the hand of Roland, cardinal-priest of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of April, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1156 from the Incarnation of the Lord, in the third year of the pontificate of our lord Pope Adrian IV.

Lead seal: Adrian, Pope IV.

### CXXVI. He receives under his protection the monastery of St. Vitalis at Ravenna and confirms its goods. (Lateran, April 5.)

[MARGARINI, *Bullarium Cassinense*, II, 177.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ALBERIC, abbot of the monastery of St. Vitalis at Ravenna, and his brethren, present [Col. 1495D] and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

For those choosing the religious life, it is fitting that we provide with careful consideration lest an occasion of any necessity make them negligent or, God forbid, weaken the strength of their sacred manner of life. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this document. We establish that whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, [Col. 1496A] or other lawful means, by the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have considered the following worthy of expression by their proper names:

The church of Holy Cross and St. Nazarius, with its possessions; the church of St. Lawrence in Pannonia and St. John in Consule; the church of St. Mary in the vineyard of Taliata. In the diocese of Faenza, the church of St. John at Ronco with its possessions; the church of St. Lawrence at Auriclania with its possessions; and, with the same villages, your people and demesnes, mills, and whatever you possess at Taurise. The hospital of St. James of Carossa, with its church and possessions; whatever you possess in the church of St. Mary in Prata; [Col. 1496B] the holding which you possess at Gunfo, Fossula, Vigazolo, Flexo, Badarzolo, and Blancana. Whatever you possess at the church of St. Peter and St. Saviour—people, a mill, and demesnes—situated at Albereto on both sides of the river. Whatever you possess in the estate of St. Basil; and the church of St. Peter at Ponticello with its possessions; people and demesnes situated at Ponticello and Abrulia with their lands. Whatever you possess in the city of Faenza; the whole estate of Visiliani and Cerreti; the estate of Aviliani with all its appurtenances; and the properties situated on both sides of the river; the church of St. Peter at Casaliclo with its possessions, which lies in the diocese of Forlì. Whatever you possess in the county of Cunii. Whatever you possess in [Col. 1496C] the county of Bagnae Caballi; the church of SS. Gervasius and Protasius with its possessions. In the diocese of Bologna, the church of St. Lawrence at Galeria with its possessions. In the diocese of Ferrara, the church of St. Vitalis with its possessions; the estate of St. Lawrence at Scornio with all its possessions—everything situated in the territories of Ferrara and Adria. Whatever you possess in the city of Argenta, in lands, waters, marshes, and fisheries on both sides of the Po. In the diocese of Cervia, whatever you possess, both in saltworks and buildings; the church of St. Theodore with all its possessions, in lands, vineyards, woods, and marshes—everything situated in the diocese [Col. 1496D] of Cervia and in the diocese of Cesena. Whatever you possess in the estate of Saliani and in the diocese of Cesena. In the diocese of Rimini, the church of St. Mary at Gauriolo with all its possessions, woods, banks, and hills; whatever you possess in the same diocese in the parish of St. Archangel and in the parish of St. Vitus. The castle of Marignano, with the church of St. John and all its appurtenances. Whatever you possess in the diocese of Senigallia, both in the city, near the city, and outside it.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; rather, let all things remain whole and unimpaired, serving in every way the uses for which they were granted [Col. 1497A] for the governance and support of those concerned, while preserving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical rights of the diocesan bishops.

If anyone therefore, etc. But to all, etc.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church.  
I, Cencius, bishop of Porto and St. Rufina.  
I, Gregory, bishop of Sabina.  
I, Manfred, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Sabina.  
I, Julius, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Marcellus.  
I, Bernard, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Clement.  
I, Octavian, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Cecilia.  
I, Gerard, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Stephen on the Caelian Hill.  
I, Henry, cardinal-priest of SS. Nereus and Achilleus.  
[Col. 1497B] I, Ildebrand, cardinal-priest of the title of the Basilica of the Twelve Apostles.  
I, Oddo, cardinal-deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil.  
I, Guido, cardinal-deacon of the title of St. Mary in Portico.  
I, Hyacinth, cardinal-deacon of St. Mary in Cosmedin.  
I, Bonadies, cardinal-deacon of the title of St. Angelo.  
I, Ardicio, cardinal-deacon of the title of St. Theodore.  
I, Albert, cardinal-deacon of the title of St. Adrian.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Roland, cardinal-priest of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the Nones of April, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1157 from the Incarnation of the Lord, in the third year of the pontificate of our lord Pope Adrian IV.

### CXXVII. He receives under his protection the church of St. Peter at Guastalla and confirms its goods and rights. (Lateran, May 13.)

[AFFO, *Istoria di Guastalla*, I, 341.]

[Col. 1497C]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons RAINALD, archpriest of the church of Blessed Peter situated in the district of Guastalla, and his brethren, present and future, canonically appointed, in perpetuity.

Since without the worship of true religion neither can the unity of charity endure nor service pleasing to God be rendered, it is fitting for apostolic authority to cherish religious persons and especially to foster by the protection of the Apostolic See religious places which belong by right to Blessed Peter and pertain particularly to the Roman [Col. 1497D] Church. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests and receive under the protection of that prince of the apostles and ourselves the aforesaid church—known to belong to the right of the Roman Church, raised by our predecessor Pope Gregory V, of blessed memory, from a chapel to a parish church, and confirmed by the privileges of his successors, the Roman pontiffs Paschal, Innocent, and Eugenius, of holy memory—and fortify it by the protection of this document.

We establish that whatever possessions, goods, or tithes the same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, through grants of pontiffs, generosity of kings, gifts [Col. 1498A] of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, by the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. We grant you free permission to receive chrism, holy oil, ordinations of clerics, and consecrations of churches from whichever Catholic bishop you prefer. We further decree that no one may presume to build a church within the bounds of your parish without your permission, except one which ought to be subject to you. We also establish that the chapels of St. George, St. Martin, and St. James, belonging to the right of your church and confirmed to you by our aforesaid predecessors, shall remain perpetually under your subjection. As an acknowledgment of this protection received from the Apostolic See [Col. 1498B], you shall pay three bezants annually to us and our successors.

We therefore decree that no archbishop, bishop, abbot, duke, marquis, captain, judge, *castaldio* [official], or any other person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any other vexations; rather, let all things remain whole, serving in every way the uses for which they were granted for the governance and support of those concerned, while preserving in all things the authority of the Apostolic See.

If anyone therefore, etc.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church.  
I, Gregory, bishop of Sabina.  
[Col. 1498C] I, Odo, cardinal-deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil.  
I, Rodulf, cardinal-deacon of St. Lucy at the Septa Solis.  
I, Manfred, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Lucy.  
I, Julius, cardinal-priest of St. Marcellus.  
I, Octavian, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Cecilia.  
I, John, cardinal-priest of SS. John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius.  
I, Aldebrand, cardinal-priest of the title of the Basilica of the Twelve Apostles.  
I, Guido, cardinal-deacon of St. Mary in Portico.  
I, Hyacinth, cardinal-deacon of St. Mary in Cosmedin.  
I, Ardicio, cardinal-deacon of St. Theodore.  
I, Boso, cardinal-deacon of SS. Cosmas and Damian.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Roland, cardinal-priest of the Holy Roman [Col. 1498D] Church and chancellor, on the third day before the Ides of May, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1157 from the Incarnation of the Lord, in the third year of the pontificate of our lord Pope Adrian IV.

### CXXVIII. Privilege for the monastery of Canossa in the district of Reggio. (Lateran, May 15.)

[TIRABOSCHI, *Memorie Modenesi*, III, 33.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons MANFRED, abbot of the monastery of Canossa situated in the parish of Reggio, and his brethren, present and future, regularly appointed, in perpetuity.

A pious request ought to be fulfilled by the resulting effect, [Col. 1499A] so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth praiseworthily and the benefit requested may undoubtedly gain force. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and, after the example of our predecessors of blessed memory, the supreme pontiffs Honorius and Innocent, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the monastery of Blessed Apollonius, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this document; establishing that whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, God being favorable, through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure [Col. 1499B] and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have considered the following worthy of expression by their proper names:

One half of the castle of Canossa, with the chapel of St. Martin and its other appurtenances; the castle of Sarzano with its chapel and estate; the castle of Filica with its estate and two chapels; the New Castle with chapel and estate; the monastery of St. Michael with its appurtenances; the church of Roarolo; the church of St. Abundius; the church of St. John of Gurgo; the church of St. Peter of Bagnolo; the church of St. Euphemia of Casula; the chapel of St. George of Fano; the church of St. Euphemia of Plazola; likewise the holding at Fano, which Emperor Henry of revered memory is known to have granted to your church out of pious regard; [Col. 1499C] also the tithes from the demesnes which belonged to Marquis Boniface of good memory, or from the monastery’s own demesnes in the estate of Canossa, Paterno, Bibianello, Caviliano, Cargnoni, Pantano, and from the demesne of Gnasiani, Sorzani, Cavello Nuovo, and Filina, while preserving the rights of the parish churches; and the tithe of Foresto in the estate of Canossa, as our venerable brother Albert, bishop of Reggio, is known canonically to have granted those tithes to the aforesaid monastery and confirmed them by the text of his document.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it by any molestations; rather, let all things remain whole, serving in every way the uses for which they were granted, for the governance and support of those concerned, while preserving in all things the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of diocesan bishops in the aforesaid churches. As an acknowledgment of this liberty received from the Apostolic See, you shall pay annually to us and our successors twenty solidi [lacuna].

If anyone therefore, etc.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church.  
I, Manfred, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Sabina.  
I, Octavian, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Cecilia.  
I, Guido, cardinal-deacon of St. Mary in Portico.  
I, Bonadies, cardinal-deacon of St. Angelo.  
[Col. 1500A] I, Henry, cardinal-priest of the title of SS. Nereus and Achilleus.  
I, Otto, cardinal-deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil.  
I, Oddo, cardinal-deacon of St. Nicholas in the Tullian Prison.  
I, Albert, cardinal-deacon of St. Adrian.  
I, Ildeprand, cardinal-priest of the title of the Basilica of the Twelve Apostles.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Roland, cardinal-priest of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the Ides of May, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1156 from the Incarnation of the Lord, in the third year of the pontificate of our lord Pope Adrian IV.

### CXXIX. Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary at Pontigny. (Lateran? May 18.)

[MARTENI, *Thesaurus Anecdotorum*, III, 1231.]

[Col. 1500B]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son GUIZARD, abbot of the monastery of St. Mary of Pontigny, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

It is fitting readily to grant consent to religious desires, so that faithful devotion may attain a swift effect. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this document. [Col. 1500C] We establish that whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter reasonably acquire by the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have considered the following worthy of expression by their proper names:

The abbey of Pontigny with all its appurtenances; Grange, St. Porcaire, Bunion, Crecey, Challiac, Burs, Vilers, Algremont, Champ-Inventé, Folcheries, and Aiglisoles, with all their appurtenances in woods, plains, meadows, and waters; likewise rights of use throughout the whole Othe and in the woods belonging to the archbishop of Sens [Col. 1500D] and the bishop of Troyes, as these have been piously granted to you by them and are known to have been confirmed by the text of their document.

We also establish that within the boundary of your granges no one whatsoever may presume to seize a person, commit theft or robbery, or exercise violence. We further add that no ecclesiastical or secular person whatsoever may have authority, without your knowledge and permission, to construct a new dwelling-house within a space of half a league around your granges, and especially around the grange of Seveia. If anyone should presume to attempt this, let him be struck by canonical sentence. Moreover, no one shall presume to demand tithes from you on your newly cleared lands, which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or on the fodder of your animals. [Col. 1501A]

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; rather, let all things remain whole and unimpaired, serving in every way the uses for which they were granted for the governance and support of those concerned, while preserving the authority of the Apostolic See.

If anyone therefore, etc.

ST. PETER, ST. PAUL, POPE ADRIAN IV.

Place of the monogram.

MY EYES ARE EVER TOWARD THE LORD.

### CXXX. He receives under his protection the convent of St. Mary at Carolicastrum and confirms its goods. (Lateran, May 18.)

[BÉATRIX, Countess of Châlons, p. 128.]

[Col. 1501D]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ PERONELLA, abbess of the monastery of St. Mary at Carolicastrum, and her sisters, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

It is fitting that our protection be present for virgins dedicated to God, who, having rejected marriage, abandoned the world and its pomps, and wholly devoted themselves to the service of their Creator, strive under the religious habit and profession of holiness, with the flesh mortified and lamps kindled, to enter with Christ the Lord into the heavenly banquet; and that an apostolic safeguard be applied against the storms of worldly [Col. 1502A] waves, so that, fenced about by apostolic protection, they may be made secure from every trouble and rejoice that they have recovered in Christ the help which they left in the world.

Therefore, beloved daughters in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church of Carolicastrum, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the protection of this document. We establish that whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or which you may hereafter acquire, God being favorable, through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure [Col. 1502B] and unimpaired for you and those who succeed you. Among these we have considered the following worthy of expression by their proper names:

The church of Molar; the church of Nores; the church of Salaman; the church of St. Peter of Mura; the church of Plaseio; the church of Rento; the church of Artai; and the church of St. Saphorin, with all their appurtenances. Moreover, since William, count of Burgundy and Mâcon, entered upon the way of all flesh, his wife Countess Adalasia, together with their sons Stephen and Gerard, in the presence of our venerable brother Hubert, archbishop of Besançon, renounced, out of pious regard for the aforesaid church, the third part of the village called Faisses, together with the tallages and other profits which they unjustly levied there; and Tibert of Montmoret, for the remedy and salvation of his soul, in the presence of certain nobles, remitted the bread-tallage, capon-tallage, and sheaf-tallage which he exacted from certain men of your church, and the seven denarii which he annually exacted from the church of Carolicastrum from every holding on the feast of St. Martin. We confirm these same renunciations by the privilege of this document [Col. 1502C] and establish that they shall remain unshaken in perpetuity.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church of Carolicastrum, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any molestations; [Col. 1502D] rather, let all things remain whole, serving in every way the uses for which they were granted for the governance and support of those concerned, while preserving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of diocesan bishops. As an acknowledgment of this protection received from the Apostolic See, you shall always pay to us and our successors ten pounds of bronze in every seventh year.

If anyone therefore, etc.

### CXXXI. He receives the church of Geneva under his protection and confirms the peace made between Bishop Arducius and Amadeus, count of Geneva. (Lateran, May 21.)

(SPON, *History of Geneva*, II, 14.)

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother ARDUCIUS, bishop of Geneva, greeting [Col. 1503C] and apostolic blessing.

[The supplied source ends here.]

Whenever such requests are made of us by our brethren the bishops as accord with equity and do not depart from the path of reason, it becomes us to grant them willingly; and we ought to fulfil their wishes by carrying them into effect. Therefore, venerable brother bishop in Christ, concurring with ready assent in your just petitions, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves your person and the church entrusted to you, and fortify them by the safeguard of this present writing.

Moreover, at the urgency of your request, we confirm by apostolic authority to you, and through you to the Church, the agreement reasonably concluded, with the assent of both parties, between you and our beloved son, the nobleman Amedeus, Count of Geneva, in the presence of our venerable brethren S., Archbishop of Vienne, E., [Col. 1503D] Archbishop of Lyon, and P., Archbishop of Tarentaise, J., Bishop of Grenoble, and William, Bishop of Belley, and certain religious abbots, concerning certain disputes being conducted between you. The tenor of this agreement, as contained in the instrument drawn up concerning it, is appended below.

For our aforesaid brother Peter, Archbishop of Tarentaise, and our beloved sons Almaric, precentor of the Church of Geneva, William Alberic, dean, Lambert of Anassy, dean, and Artold, dean, Walter, canon and chaplain, Pontius of Fillinges, canon, [Col. 1504A] Master Peter of Toulon, canon, Aymo, vidame of Geneva, Amedeus of Nangy, Peter of Nangy, Aymericus of Nangy, Falco Turumbertus, and Cono of Ruppe, beginning with the burdens imposed upon you by the Count through priests and deacons, since you had complained of this matter, settled it between you as follows: if priests or deacons held a fief or land of the Count, they should render him equal service; but if they wished to relinquish his land, they should relinquish the investiture and render the *usamentum* according to what they had held from him, and thus remain in all things peacefully subject to the bishop and Church of Geneva.

Since the Count had also made complaint against you concerning persons of his servile condition whom you had ordained, it was settled on this point [Col. 1504B] that those who had been ordained priests or deacons previously should be left to you in peace, and that thereafter you should by no means ordain the Count’s serfs, or those of his men, without their consent.

The Count also complained concerning the fief of tithes; but because you maintained that the Count had made a settlement with you concerning those tithes, it was established that you should prove that such a settlement had been made, and that it should be maintained. Otherwise, you should relinquish the fief of tithes to the Count, while preserving episcopal right and the mandate of the Apostolic See.

After this you brought forward another complaint concerning castles recently built by the Count upon Church land, and concerning William of Marvello, whose men the Count had unlawfully taken and thereby alienated from the Church of Geneva, to which William ought in every respect to belong. [Col. 1504C] Accordingly, the aforesaid arbiters settled concerning the castles that any built by the Count upon Church land, if this could be proved, should be wholly demolished; otherwise, if they had been erected upon the Count’s land, they should remain intact, provided nevertheless that they harmed the Church’s property in no respect.

Further, concerning William of Marvello, it was ordained that, since he was a nobleman, if he wished he should relinquish the Count’s fief and, after rendering the Count’s homage void, return to the lordship of the Church of Geneva and of the bishop. If he preferred to retain the Count’s fief and lordship, he should peacefully relinquish the Church’s fief; and thereafter the Count should exact nothing from the Church on this account.

The Count’s further complaint concerned [Col. 1504D] the son of Maynerius, whom you had taken from him. You gave an entirely sufficient answer: namely, that the mother belonged to the household of the Church of Geneva and had therefore given the son of Maynerius a fief of the Church, because he had acquired it on his mother’s side and it belonged to him. It was accordingly settled that, if the Count wished to have that son of Maynerius, he should peacefully relinquish the Church’s fief, and that neither the Count nor anyone else should on this account bring any burden upon the Church.

Furthermore, concerning the men and lands of the Church seized and appropriated by the Count and his men, a complaint having been lodged by you, it was declared by the common counsel of the arbitrators that, in those districts of the bishopric of Geneva where such controversy existed, in order to ascertain the truth concerning the boundaries of places, [Col. 1505A] four men of good repute and natives of the area from your side and four from the Count’s side should be compelled by ecclesiastical censure to swear an oath; and what they should attest, touching the most holy relics, concerning the lawful possession of the Church or the Count, should thereafter be firmly maintained by you both.

Among the other matters contained in the agreement made at Seyssel were the following: that the memoranda made after the oath by the men of the bishop and the Count—namely Almaric, cantor and canon of Geneva, William Born., dean, Richard, vidame, and William of Bosco—as recited with the common assent of you and the Count in the presence of the aforesaid Peter, Archbishop of Tarentaise, and Amedeus, Bishop of Lausanne, [Col. 1505B] and of the abbots of the whole bishopric of Geneva—Rudolph of Hautecombe, Stephen of Chézery, Moses of Bonmont, Borch. of Abondance, Pontius of Sixt, as well as Rudolph, Abbot of Agaune—and many religious and honourable men present in the episcopal house at Geneva, should be firmly observed by both parties as to what belonged to the bishop and what to the Count in the lordship and jurisdiction of the city of Geneva.

These are the memoranda: the ban of all Geneva, in all matters and wholly, belongs to you alone; the jurisdiction and lordship over every person, whoever he may be, pertain solely to you; strangers also, once they have resided at Geneva for a year and a day, belong to you alone; the Count, however, ought to take no men anywhere in [Col. 1505C] Geneva. You ought to possess as lord the right of hospitality, the general court, wine dues, *coroddam* [uncertain term], and transfers of houses when the lord has died. The market of the whole town and market jurisdiction pertain to you alone; likewise the river toll and the pastures. The Count, either personally or through any of his men, ought not to levy any riding-service in the pastures of Geneva; the coinage belongs solely in your hands.

If any thief is captured, you ought to have him and all his goods. The Count’s residence at Geneva shall be subject to your cognizance, provided that neither the Count nor his household harms the Church, the citizens, or ecclesiastical goods. Neither the Count nor any of his men shall impose their pledges by force upon anyone, unless they are of equal value; and they shall release them only upon satisfaction of the creditor. Thus far are the episcopal rights.

The following, however, appear to belong to the Count: he is Count and ought to be a good advocate under the bishop. Finally, by reason of affection, he ought to enjoy such familiarity in the episcopal household that, at changes of offices in that household, if any question should arise from this, he ought there to have *druulia* [sic; uncertain]. You likewise, if you are provoked or angered against any member of his household, that person shall have recourse to the Count; and until he has given you suitable satisfaction, the Count may retain him. In the same manner, any member of the Count’s household shall in every respect be held by you.

Although the disposition regarding a thief shall be as stated above, if he is assigned for condemnation or for the execution of any justice arising from the matter, [Col. 1506A] he shall nevertheless be delivered to the Count for carrying out the justice. Likewise concerning monasteries: if they should at any time make false coin, the Count shall administer justice at your command.

Since, therefore, the Count, exceeding all bounds, had inflicted many and very great losses upon you and likewise upon the canons, and had demolished and destroyed the houses of your men, the arbiters declared that the Count should pay forty pounds toward reparation of the damage; but should make good the canons’ damage according to their discretion and mercy. In restoring the houses, the Count should also make compensation to the men whose houses they were, to their satisfaction.

It was further declared that he should restore peace to all your men whom the Count, out of the ill will existing between himself and you, had hated; [Col. 1506B] and likewise that you yourself should make peace with the Count’s men, except those who had taken your goods—namely, goods which the Count had not possessed. Concerning these it was declared that the Count should do you justice until the goods taken had been restored in accordance with your will; but if you yourself should administer your justice on that account, the Count should in no respect oppose you.

You had previously also complained concerning fishing. It was settled that your men should always peacefully enjoy the good customs which they had held from ancient times in that place. You also complained concerning the fishing-day on the Venna which the Count had taken away. The arbiters declared that, whenever you wished to summon the Count, he should come to your court and abide peacefully by the court’s decision.

Concerning Rudolph of [Col. 1506C] Saint-Gervais, because the Count had complained on that matter, it was settled that the Church’s investiture should remain; and if the Count wished, he should come before your court concerning this, and each party should possess his right according to what had been said or might yet be said.

If anyone should rashly attempt to violate this peace or agreement, the arbiters declared that you should administer justice concerning it, and that the Count should not, within forty days, oppose you because of the justice so administered.

Therefore, that this agreement may be inviolably observed in future times, we have judged it fitting to confirm it by the authority of the Apostolic See and to secure it with the present privilege.

[Col. 1506D] We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever to infringe this page of our confirmation or in any way oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his presumption by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know that he stands guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity he has committed; and at the last judgment let him be subject to severe vengeance.

But to all who observe it, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Gregory, bishop of the Church of Sabina. [Col. 1507A] I, Manfred, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina. I, Girard, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, Henry, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Rodolph, cardinal deacon of Saint Lucy in the Septa . . . . . I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Ardicio, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore. [Col. 1507B] I, Boso, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Albert, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Roland, cardinal priest of the holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of June, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1157 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Adrian IV.

### CXXXII. He confirms to the Church of Geneva the goods bestowed by Emperor Frederick. (Lateran, 21 May.)

[*Ibid.*, p. 20.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother ARDUCIUS, bishop of the Church of Geneva, [Col. 1507C] and to his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

Since, by the office of the apostolate entrusted to us by God, through which by the Lord’s authorship we have precedence over all Christ’s faithful, we ought to give attention to the peace and tranquillity of each, we must especially be solicitous for the repose of those endowed with pastoral dignity and raised to the episcopal office. For unless, by attending to their interests, we preserve their rights unimpaired as far as God permits us, and defend them by apostolic authority from the assaults of the wicked, those who, by the Lord’s ordering, are entrusted to them for governance cannot truly be solicitous for their salvation.

[Col. 1507D] Therefore, venerable brother bishop of Geneva in Christ, we grant favourable assent to your just petitions and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid Church of Geneva, over which, by God’s authorship, you are known to preside; and we fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that those things pertaining to royal right which our dearest son in Christ Frederick, Emperor of the Romans, is known, out of pious regard, lawfully to have bestowed upon you and your Church, within and outside the city of Geneva, and to have confirmed by the text of his document—as is contained in that document itself—we confirm in their entirety to you and your successors by the authority of the Apostolic See, and strengthen by the protection of this privilege.

Furthermore, whatever possessions and whatever goods that Church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, through the Lord’s favour, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors.

[Col. 1508A] We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid Church, remove its possessions, retain what has been removed, diminish them, or harass them with any vexations; rather, all shall be preserved unimpaired and intact for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and maintenance they were granted, the authority of the Apostolic See being preserved in all things.

If anyone therefore, etc.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. [Col. 1508B] I, Manfred, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina. I, Gregory, bishop of the Church of Sabina. I, Girard, cardinal of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, Almericus, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. I, Otto, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Rodolph, cardinal deacon in the Septa of Saint Lucy. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. [Col. 1508C] I, Ardicio, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore. I, Boso, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Albert, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Roland, cardinal priest of the holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of June, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1157 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Adrian IV.

### CXXXIII. Privilege for the nunnery of Remiremont. (Lateran, 3 June.)

[*Gallia Christiana*, XIII, Instruments, 509.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, JUDITH, abbess of the monastery of Remiremont, and her sisters, present and future, professing the Rule.

Although by the office entrusted to us we ought to have care for all Churches, we must nevertheless be more solicitous for those Churches which belong especially to the right of blessed Peter. Therefore, beloved daughters in the Lord, granting favourable assent to your reasonable petitions, we receive under the guardianship and protection of the Apostolic See the monastery of Remiremont, in which you are dedicated to the divine service; we fortify it by the privilege of this present writing; and we decree that the same monastery, according to the venerable decrees of our predecessors, shall always remain under the special right of the Apostolic See. Whatever possessions it now [Col. 1509A] justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means through the Lord’s favour, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The territory which the monastery of Remiremont possesses at Adocei; the revenues of Mandasmei which William of Arches relinquished; the estate of Goherey Candarau; the point of Gaudricourt; Bussoncourt; Guislovillard; and the lands of Mandasmei; the holding in the city of Toul which Hugh of Gondricourt held; the vineyards which you possess at Barro; and the land which you possess in the district of Toul.

Moreover, lest access of the popular assembly be open within the enclosures of the nuns, we prohibit any bishop from celebrating public masses there or making dispositions of the affairs of that place, unless invited thereto by the abbess of the place or the community of sisters. [Col. 1509B] You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and the ordinations of clerics to be promoted to sacred orders, from whatever bishop you prefer, provided that he enjoys the favour and communion of the Apostolic See. If a bishop, having been requested, should at any time come to the monastery, it shall not be lawful for him to claim for himself anything, great or small, from its ornaments, vessels, or any goods whatever. Nor do we permit an archbishop, archdeacon, the diocesan bishop himself, or any person whatsoever to exercise authority in that monastery.

We also prohibit anyone, within one league of the monastery, from making any invasion or taking away its goods. Upon the death of you, the present abbess of that place, or of any of those who succeed you, no one shall be placed there by fraud, guile, or force, save one whom the sisters by common consent—or the sounder part of their counsel—shall, according to the fear of God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict, provide to be elected [from chapter 64 of the Rule of Saint Benedict]. The woman elected shall be presented to the Roman pontiff to receive the mysteries of blessing; if she should perhaps depart from the regular path, she shall be subject to the corrections of the Apostolic See. [Col. 1509D] A bishop, however, shall not presume to exercise any disciplinary action against her without the Roman pontiff’s permission.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass them with any vexations; but all shall be preserved wholly unimpaired and intact for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and maintenance they were granted, the authority of the Apostolic See being preserved in all things. Moreover, as a token of liberty received from the Roman See, within each period of four years you shall pay to us and our successors a white horse with an *astrolinum* cloth.

If, therefore, in future any archbishop or bishop, [Col. 1510A] emperor or king, prince or margrave, count, viscount, judge, or any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowingly attempts rashly to contravene this page of our constitution, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his presumption by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know that he is guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let him be subject to severe vengeance. But to all who preserve the rights of that venerable place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards [Col. 1510B] of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Apostolic Church. I, Manfred, cardinal priest of Saint Sabina. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, Hubald, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lucy. I, Astald, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Prisca. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen. I, John, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Damasus. I, Henry, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. I, Gregory, bishop of Sabina. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Guido, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Bonadies, cardinal deacon of Saint Angelo. I, Ardicio, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore. I, Boso, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Albert, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Roland, cardinal priest of the holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the third day before the Nones of June, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1157 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Adrian IV.

### CXXXIV. He receives under protection the monastery of Saint Blasius in the Black Forest, and confirms its goods and rights. (Lateran, 8 June.)

[GERBERT, *History of the Black Forest*, III, 82.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son GUNTHER, abbot of the monastery of Saint Blasius, situated in the bishopric of Constance, namely in the place called the Black Forest, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

The authority of the Apostolic See, which by the Lord’s bounty we serve, and the unity of fraternal charity exhort us to assent to the just desires of religious persons and mercifully to grant their reasonable requests. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Gunther, granting favourable assent to your just requests, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid monastery of Blessed Blasius, over which, by God’s authorship, you are known to preside, after the example of our predecessor Pope Innocent of happy memory, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and whatever goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means through God’s favour, shall remain firm and [Col. 1511B] unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The cell of Ochsenhausen, with the churches belonging to it: Rainstesten, Mittilbuc, the church of Berichem, the church of Banhem, the church of Arta, the church of Horsenhusen, the church of Wolpach, and other churches with their appurtenances.  
[Note: [Col. 1511C] This cell, with the churches here expressly named as its own, has been independent since the fifteenth century.]

The cell of Berowa, with the churches belonging to it, namely Berowa.  
[Note: [Col. 1511C] The nunnery of Berowa, with the parish church bearing the same name as the monastery, still belongs to it. Nuchilca, or Neukirch, in the district of Schaffhausen; Oningen, now Hocheminingen; and Wurmlingen in the chapter [district], formerly belonged to it. See vol. I, p. 394 ff.]

Nuchilca, with the other churches of the same cell; the cell of Witinova, [Note: [Col. 1511D] We gave above the charter of the donation of the church at Wittnau to the monastery of Saint Blasius; it had already been converted into a cloister by Abbot Ulto. It now belongs, with its churches, to the Margraves of Baden, as does likewise the cell of Bürgel here listed.] with its churches, namely Viselat and Tennibero; the cell of Burgulum, with its churches—namely Eggenheim, Sicenchilcha, and Chaltenbach—with that right and authority in receiving tithes and in other matters which our venerable brother Hermann, Bishop of Constance, is known reasonably to have granted to the monks of [Col. 1511C] Burgulum and confirmed by his writing; the cell of Wiziluichovin.  
[Note: [Col. 1511D] We have discussed the cell of Wislikofen in the Swiss district and canton of Zurich, vol. I, p. 411. The bull of Innocent II, issued 28 November 1138, by which he ratifies the donation of this cell, is printed in S. Herrgott, vol. II, pt. I, p. 157.]

Also the churches of Batemaringin, [Note: [Col. 1511D] The churches listed here are situated in various places and did not belong to the cells; some are still subject to the monastery, while others have been withdrawn from it. Of this kind are Bertimaringen, or Betmaringen, mentioned above, a parish church with its daughter church Manchen; [Col. 1512C] Grisheim, or Griessen, in Klettgau; Sneisanc, or Scheneissengen, in Switzerland; and Chilotorf, or Ckirchdorf, a regular church neighbouring it, [Col. 1512D] recently received by exchange from the abbey of Elchingen; no. LI and others. Many more are added in the bull of Antipope Calixtus III, issued at Foligno, 26 April 1173 (vol. I, p. 392), namely the cell of Sizzenchilcha, here still called a church rather than a cell (see above no. LII), and the churches of Louha, Wrimos, Mintriedin, Altriechsrieth, Loppinhusen, Utrinwilare, Howidorf, Teigingin—perhaps the same as Tougingin—Wilare, Blochingen, Ritte, Huginilo, Omingin, Imindingen, Bacheim, Gundilwanc, here called Gudelwanc, Bernowa, Schonowa, Gerispach, Warnowa, Tullinchovin, Cuiringin, Blansingin, Wisintowa, Chernis, Nuheim, Steinhusin, Rebistal, Stallinchovin, Birbonnistorf, Stadiln, and Hachinswanda. Of all these parish churches, many are no longer under our jurisdiction, having passed to others through the various vicissitudes of time. Bernowa, Schonnowa, and Hachinswanda will be mentioned again below.]

—with the church of Moucheim subject to it; Steina; Brambach; Richeim; Everingin; Hougelheim; Rotwilo; Grizheim; Sneisanc; Stallinkovin; Chilotorf; Tougingin; Guldelwanc; Nallingin; Plochingin; Buron; Brunnon; Luvingin; Entilibouch; Schwercin; Waremundisriet; and the remaining churches with all their appurtenances.

No one whatsoever shall presume to exact tithes from you on your newly cleared lands which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or on the increase of your animals. [Col. 1512A] We also decree that, in the parish churches which you hold, you shall choose suitable priests and present them to the bishop; if they are suitable, the bishop shall commit the care of souls to them without objection, so that they shall render account to the bishop for the care of the people, while showing to you due subjection in temporal matters belonging to the monastery itself.

You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, ordinations of monks to be promoted to sacred orders, and the other matters belonging to episcopal office from the Bishop of Constance, in whose diocese you are situated, provided that he is Catholic, enjoys the favour and communion of the Apostolic [Col. 1512B] See, and is willing to provide them freely and without improper exaction. Otherwise, it shall be lawful for you to approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer and receive from him the sacraments of consecration; supported by our authority, he shall grant what is requested.

We further decree that burial at the same place shall be wholly free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who have determined to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict, while preserving nevertheless the rights of the mother church. No opposition of any bishop or provost shall prevent you from receiving free and unbound clerics or laypersons into conversion [the religious life].

Upon the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed there by fraud or force unless he whom the brothers, by common consent, or the sounder part of the brothers’ counsel, elect according to God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict. We also confirm to your monastery the cell of Silva Swarzwalt, founded by Saint Reginbert, with all its possessions, estates, and lands belonging to it.

Moreover, we likewise confirm the ordinance concerning the liberty and advocacy of your monastery established by Henry IV, emperor of good memory, and King Lothair, and ratified by our predecessors, the Roman pontiffs Calixtus, Honorius, and Innocent, of happy memory, with the deliberation of bishops and cardinals: [Col. 1513A] namely, that in choosing an advocate the abbot, with the counsel of his brothers, shall have free authority to choose one whom he knows to be good and useful for defending the monastery’s liberty, and who desires to possess and administer that advocacy well, not for earthly gain but for the love of God, forgiveness of his sins, and the reward of eternal blessing.

But if, being rather a plunderer than an advocate, he should seize the monastery’s goods rather than defend them, and, after a first and second warning, should in no way make amends, the abbot, with the counsel of the brothers, shall have authority to appoint for himself another, more useful advocate. Thus, as was determined by judgment of the aforesaid Emperor Henry and King Lothair, the liberty of your monastery shall in every respect be separate from the jurisdiction of the Church of Basel. As a token of the protection received from the Apostolic See and of the liberty granted to your monastery, you shall pay one gold piece each year to us and our successors.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, remove its possessions, retain what has been removed, diminish them, or harass them with any vexations; rather, all shall be preserved intact for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and maintenance they were granted, the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishops being preserved.

If anyone therefore, etc.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Gregory, bishop of Sabina. I, Manfred, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Sabina. I, Julius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, Hubald, cardinal priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Octavian, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Gerard, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill. [Col. 1513D] I, Henry, cardinal priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. I, Ildebrand, cardinal priest of the Basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, Odo, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Boso, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Albert, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian.

Given at the Lateran by the hand of Roland, cardinal priest of the holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the sixth day before the Ides of June, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1157 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Adrian IV.

### CXXXV. He confirms for the monastery of Saint Blasius the churches of Bürgel, Eggenheim, and Chaltenbach. (Lateran, 8 June.)

[*Ibid.*, p. 88.]

[Col. 1514A]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GUNTHER, abbot of the monastery of Saint Blasius, and his successors: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Those things known to have been reasonably done by our brethren the bishops ought to remain in their stability; and, lest they can in future be altered through anyone’s rashness, they should be secured by the authority of the Apostolic See. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, concurring with favourable assent in your just requests, we confirm by the authority of the Apostolic See, after the example of Pope Innocent of happy memory, that which was established concerning the cell of Bürgel and the chapel of Saint John situated in the place called Eggenheim by Ulrich, Bishop of Constance, of good memory, and by his successor Ulrich, with the consent of the archpriest and the other priests of that parish. That is: the aforesaid cell of Bürgel and church of Saint John, which were built, with the consent of the aforesaid bishops, on the freehold which Werner and Wipert, upon entering religious life, canonically offered with its appurtenances to the monastery of Saint Blasius, in which you are dedicated to divine service, shall henceforth belong in perpetuity to the right of the said abbey.

Nevertheless, [Col. 1514C] you shall freely and without anyone’s opposition serve the Lord in the aforesaid cell of Bürgel; and the people in the church of Saint John at Eggenheim, built at the foot of the mountain, shall receive the divine sacraments, and each shall remain within its own boundaries, as is known to have been established by the aforesaid bishops. Furthermore, we confirm by the authority of the Apostolic See the church of Chaltenbach with all its rights and resources, as our venerable brother Hermann, Bishop of Constance, is known to have granted it to your monastery and confirmed it by his writing.

Let it therefore be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to infringe this page of our confirmation or in any manner oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty [Col. 1514D] God and of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, by the hand of Roland, cardinal of the holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the sixth day before the Ides of July [read: June], in the fifth indiction, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Adrian IV.

### CXXXVI. He receives the monastery of Engelberg under protection and confirms its possessions and rights, imposing upon the monks an annual payment of one gold piece. (Lateran, 8 June.)

[*Ibid.*, p. 85.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son FROWIN, abbot of the monastery of Saint Mary, situated in the bishopric of Constance, in the place called [Col. 1515A] Mount of the Angels, and to his successors regularly appointed in perpetuity.

To grant effect to just petitions is required by the force of equity and the order of reason, especially when piety supports the petitioners’ wish and truth does not abandon it. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Frowin, we graciously assent to your just requests, and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery, over which, by God’s authority, you are known to preside, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by the grant of popes, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, by God’s favor, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The church of Stans; the church of Buoches, with all their appurtenances. Indeed, no one whatsoever shall presume to exact tithes from you upon your newly cultivated lands which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or upon the increase of your animals. Moreover, in the parish churches which you hold, you may, without anyone’s opposition, choose suitable priests and present those chosen to the diocesan bishop. If they are suitable, the bishop shall commit the care of souls to them, so that they may render account to the bishop for the care of the people, but show to you due subjection in temporal matters belonging to the same monastery. Further, we confirm to you by apostolic authority the right which you are known to have received from Oudalric and Hermann, bishops of Constance, in receiving tithes, together with the other things which they are known to have granted and confirmed to your monastery. You shall receive chrism, holy oil, the consecration of altars or churches, the ordination of your monks who are to be promoted to sacred orders, and the other things belonging to the episcopal office, from the bishop of Constance, in whose diocese you are situated, provided that he is Catholic, enjoys the favor and communion of the Apostolic See, and is willing to provide these things freely and without corruption. Otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer and receive from him the sacraments of consecration; supported by our authority, he shall grant what is requested. [Col. 1515D] We also decree that the burial-place of that site shall be entirely free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who choose to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict, while the rights of the mother church are nevertheless preserved. You may also receive into conversion clerics fleeing the secular life, or free laymen, provided they are not excommunicated, without anyone’s opposition. Upon the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed over it by any device of surreptitious intrusion or by force, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren’s counsel, shall provide to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of St Benedict. [Col. 1516A]

Further, we confirm by authority of the Apostolic See that arrangement concerning the liberty of your monastery and the election of its advocate which Henry IV, of good memory, established, and which Pope Innocent, of happy memory, confirmed by his privilege: namely, that the abbot, with the counsel of his brethren, shall elect a useful advocate, who may desire to hold and administer that advocacy well, not for earthly gain but for the love of God and forgiveness of his sins; and that it shall never pass to anyone by hereditary right. But if he proves to be a harasser rather than an advocate, seizes the monastery’s goods rather than defending them, and, having been warned once, twice, or three times, does not amend, the abbot, with the counsel of his brethren, shall have power to appoint another, more useful advocate for himself. [Col. 1516B] As a token of this protection and liberty received from the Apostolic See, you shall pay each year one gold piece to us and our successors.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain possessions taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; rather, all things shall be preserved whole and intact, to benefit in every way the uses for which they were granted, namely the governance and support of those concerned, without prejudice to the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishops.

If anyone therefore, etc.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Gregory, bishop of Sabina. [Col. 1516C] I, Manfred, cardinal-priest of the title of St Sabina. I, Julius, cardinal-priest of the title of St Marcellus. I, Hubald, cardinal-priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Octavian, cardinal-priest of the title of St Cecilia. I, Gerard, cardinal-priest of the title of St Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, Henry, cardinal-priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. I, Hildebrand, cardinal-priest of the title of the Basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, Odo, cardinal-deacon of St George at the Golden Veil. [Col. 1516D] I, Bobo, cardinal-deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Albert, cardinal-deacon of St Adrian.

Given at the Lateran, by the hand of Roland, cardinal-priest of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the sixth Ides of June, in the fifth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1157, in the third year of the pontificate of Pope Adrian IV.

### CXXXVII. To Henry, Patriarch of Grado.—He confirms the patriarchal dignity and primacy over the archbishopric of Zadar. (Lateran, June 31.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 822.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, Patriarch of Grado, and to his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

We are shown to perform usefully the office of apostolic dignity entrusted to us, and the duty of stewardship, when we preserve with provident concern the dignity conferred upon each church, and strive to keep intact and whole the rights of individual churches; just as the Apostolic See ought not to grant anyone, beyond his deserts, anything by the favor of grace. Therefore, the greater the prerogative by which you have been exalted through the regard of heavenly grace, the more diligently you must take heed that, in correcting subjects, reason may have more power with you than authority; that the good may find you gentle, and the evil merciful, as a corrector; that you may love persons and pursue the faults of those subject to you. Otherwise, should you perhaps wish to act differently, correction may turn into cruelty and you may lose those whom you desire to amend. Thus you ought to cut away a wound without wounding what is sound; lest, if the iron be applied more than the case requires, it harm the one whom you hasten to benefit. Rather, let each be tempered by the other, so that the good, by loving, may have what they must avoid, and the evil, by fearing, what they must love. [Col. 1517B]

Therefore, venerable brother in Christ, Patriarch Henry, willingly assenting to your petitions, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the Church of Grado, over which, by God’s authority, you are known to preside, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. Accordingly, following in the footsteps of our predecessors of happy memory, Pelagius, Alexander, and Urban II, and preserving the tenor of that principal constitution which our most holy predecessor Pope Leo IX confirmed both by synodal judgment and by a document of privilege, we grant to you and your successors canonically appointed the patriarchal dignity, and confirm your authority to govern the Church of Grado within those boundaries which are known to have been established for that church by our aforesaid predecessors. We also grant that the cross may be carried before you, except when you are in Rome, or in the presence or company of the Roman pontiff. We likewise bestow upon your brotherhood, from the generosity of the Apostolic See, the pallium—that is, the fullness of the pontifical office. Remember to use it within your own church for the solemn celebration of Mass on those days on which we do not doubt your predecessors used it: [Col. 1517D] namely, at the Nativity of the Lord, Epiphany, the three feasts of Holy Mary, the Lord’s Supper, Holy Saturday, the Resurrection of the Lord, the Ascension, and Pentecost; on the Nativity of St John the Baptist and of All the Apostles; also on the feasts of St Mark, St Stephen the Protomartyr, St Lawrence, St Martin, the solemnity of All Saints, and the principal feasts of your church; likewise at the consecrations of churches, bishops, and other clerics, and on the anniversary of the consecration of your diocese.

Moreover, lest the aforesaid Church of Grado, entrusted to your governance and administration, which enjoys the prerogative of honor from the benevolence of the Apostolic See, should, because of the brevity of its patriarchate, be regarded by the uninformed as inferior and more lowly, and in order to increase its dignity, we grant it by apostolic authority primacy over the archbishopric of Zadar and its bishoprics. We establish both you and your successors as presidents, by the dignity of primacy, over the archbishops of Zadar and their bishops for the time being, and grant to you the office of conferring consecration upon that archbishop, while reserving to the Roman pontiff the conferral of the pallium. We decree also that whatever goods and possessions the same Church of Grado justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by just means, by God’s favor, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. Further, we freely confirm to you and your successors the churches offered to the Church of Grado by religious bishops and established throughout your patriarchate, so that no bishop may, without your consent, celebrate consecrations in them or forbid divine offices to priests serving the Lord in those churches so long as they remain in those places. [Col. 1518B]

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain possessions taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; rather, all things shall be preserved intact and whole, to benefit in every way the purposes for which they were granted, namely the governance and support of those concerned, without prejudice in all things to the authority of the Apostolic See.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, etc. [Col. 1518C]

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Ymarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Cintius, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina. I, Guido, cardinal-priest of the title of St Chrysogonus. I, Ubald, cardinal-priest of the title of St Praxedes. I, Manfred, cardinal-priest of the title of St Sabina. I, Julius, cardinal-priest of the title of St Marcellus. I, Ubald, cardinal-priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Octavian, cardinal-priest of the title of St Cecilia. [Col. 1518D] I, John, cardinal-priest of Saints John and Paul, title of Pammachius. I, John, cardinal-priest of the title of Saints Sylvester and Martin. I, Oddo, cardinal-deacon of St George at the Golden Veil. I, Guido, cardinal-deacon of St Mary in Aquiro. I, Hyacinth, cardinal-deacon of St Mary in Cosmedin.

Given at the Lateran, by the hand of Roland, cardinal of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the Ides of June, in the fifth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1157, in the third year of the pontificate of Pope Adrian IV.

### CXXXVIII. To the same.—That he may ordain and consecrate bishops at Constantinople and in other cities of the Constantinopolitan Empire in which the Venetians possess several churches. (Lateran, June 13.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, col. 824.]

[Col. 1519A]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, patriarch: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Among all the stars of heaven, which divine wisdom formed in the beginning for the adornment of the world and the use of humankind, he willed the sun to surpass them in the brightness of its light, so that by its rising it might pour day upon the earth and drive away the darkness of night. For it was fitting that it should be regarded as more excellent than the other stars, since, at the very beginning of creation, it received from the gift of the heavenly Creator the special office of ruling the day alone. Thus indeed our Redeemer, when he had spread churches like shining stars more widely through the various regions of the world, ordained that the most holy Roman Church—whose ruler was blessed Peter, prince of the Apostles—should stand above all as a splendid sun, and that all individual churches, as members, should be subject to it as to their head. This is more plainly declared by those words in which the Lord addressed Peter himself: “If you love me, feed my sheep” (John 21). And elsewhere: “You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church” (Matthew 16). But the rock upon which it is read to have been founded admits no fissures and suffers no divisions. [Col. 1519C] This is shown again when it is said: “Whatever you bind on earth shall be bound in heaven; and whatever you loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven” (ibid.). To Peter himself both steadfastness of his own and the strengthening of another’s faith were given, when he deserved to hear from the Master: “I have prayed for you, Peter, that your faith may not fail; and when you have turned, strengthen your brethren” (Luke 22). By these and other reasons, therefore, the holy and apostolic Church, which by heavenly privilege holds primacy among the others, has received from the Lord Jesus Christ himself, its head, such a prerogative that it has singular authority to provide for all churches throughout the world and, by discerning consideration, to establish in them what it recognizes ought to be established.

It is therefore incumbent upon us, who, though with insufficient merits, have undertaken to discharge in the holy Church the office of the prince of the Apostles, to provide diligently and act so that, according to the dignity and condition of each church, due honor may be bestowed upon it, and provident care may be shown to our brethren together with the salvation of the people. Accordingly, venerable brother in Christ, Patriarch Henry, inclined by this consideration to your just petitions, we grant a favorable assent; and, wishing to have regard both for your devotion and for the honor and advantage of the Church of Grado, over which, by God’s authority, you are known to preside, we have determined by apostolic authority to grant to you and your successors that, in the city of Constantinople and in other cities situated solely within the Constantinopolitan Empire, in which the Venetians possess several churches and where their multitude is accustomed continually to assemble, you may ordain a bishop and confer upon him the office of consecration without anyone’s opposition. [Col. 1520A] Therefore, that this our grant may be observed inviolably for all time, we strengthen it by the safeguard of our authority and fortify it with the protection of this present writing. We decree that no person whatsoever may infringe this document of our grant and confirmation, etc. If anyone, therefore, etc. But for all who observe it, etc. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Ymarus, bishop of Tusculum. I, Cinthius, bishop of Porto and St Rufina. [Col. 1520B] I, Guido, cardinal-priest of St Chrysogonus. I, Ubald, cardinal-priest of the title of St Praxedes. I, Manfred, cardinal-priest of St Sabina. I, Julius, cardinal-priest of the title of St Marcellus. I, Ubald, cardinal-priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Octavian, cardinal-priest of the title of St Cecilia. I, John, cardinal-priest of Saints John and Paul, title of Pammachius. I, John, cardinal-priest of the title of Saints Sylvester and Martin. I, Oddo, cardinal-deacon of St George at the Golden Veil. I, Guido, cardinal-deacon of St Mary in Aquiro. I, Hyacinth, cardinal-deacon of St Mary in Cosmedin.

[Col. 1520C] Given at the Lateran, by the hand of Roland, cardinal-priest of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the Ides, in the fifth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1157, in the third year of the pontificate of Pope Adrian IV.

### CXXXIX. He commends Henry, Patriarch of Grado, to the bishops, doge, and people of Venice. He announces to him that the archbishop of Zadar has promised obedience. (Lateran, June 13.)

[Ibid., col. 825.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers the bishops, beloved sons, the majesty of the doge, and all the people of Venice: greeting [Col. 1520D] and apostolic blessing.

We received our venerable brother Henry, Patriarch of Grado, when he came to the Apostolic See, with the kindness proper to one whom we love with true affection in the Lord and embrace in the arms of sincere charity. Bestowing upon him the honor due to him, we have taken care to grant his requests, both because of the worthiness and integrity of his person and because of the office of dignity entrusted to him, and also because we love your city, noble and renowned as it is, and intend to honor you by every means which we can according to God. Sending him back to you in a special manner, as to special and devoted sons, with the blessing of the Apostolic See and the fullness of our favor, we earnestly commend him to you all, commanding you by apostolic letters to receive him honorably, treat him with respect, and show him in all things the obedience and reverence due to him as spiritual prince and ruler of your souls. [Col. 1521A]

Further, we wish your discernment to know from this present notice that our brother, the archbishop of Zadar, in the presence of ourselves and our brethren, voluntarily promised obedience to our aforesaid brother the patriarch and to his successors as to his primate, and that we caused this promise to be set down in a public instrument. But you, as men valiant and renowned, should labor by every means to enlarge the boundaries of the Church of Grado, your mother church, and apply yourselves effectively to its advancement. For when the opportunity arises, we shall take care to honor that church by whatever means we can with God, and to provide diligently for its exaltation and advantage. [Col. 1521B]

Given at the Lateran, on the Ides of June, in the third year.

### CXL. To Rodulph, prior of Camaldoli, and his successors: he confirms the monastery of Pratalia, bestowed by Jerome, bishop of Arezzo. (Lateran, June 15.)

[MITARELLI, *Annals of Camaldoli*, III, Appendix, 496.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons RODULPH, prior of Camaldoli, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity. [Col. 1521C]

Whenever a request is made of us which is recognized as fitting religion and integrity, it is proper for us to grant it willingly and to afford suitable support to the petitioners’ wishes. You have asked us, beloved sons in the Lord, to strengthen by apostolic authority the donation of the monastery of Pratalia and its grant to you and, through you, to the Church of Camaldoli, canonically made to you by our venerable brother Jerome, bishop of Arezzo. From the tenor of that bishop’s letters which he sent to us, having fully learned that the donation was canonically made, we confirm it by apostolic authority and decree that this confirmation shall remain valid and unshaken for all time. [Col. 1521D]

Therefore, confirming to you the aforesaid monastery, with its churches and all its appurtenances, under the protection of the Apostolic See, we receive it under the special protection of the Apostolic See and ourselves and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing.

First, we decree that the monastic order which is known to be established there according to God, the Rule of blessed Benedict, and the order of the Camaldolese brethren shall be observed inviolate in that place for all time.

Moreover, whatever possessions and goods the same monastery presently justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by grant of popes, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s assistance, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and to those who strive in that monastery to serve the Lord. We also grant that the burial-place there shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who choose to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict, while the rights of the mother church are preserved. Indeed, no one shall presume to exact tithes from the newly cultivated lands of that monastery, cultivated by its own hands or at its own expense, or from the increase of your animals. [Col. 1522A]

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain possessions taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; rather, all things shall be preserved intact and whole, to benefit in every way the purposes for which they were granted, namely the governance and support of those concerned, without prejudice to the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop.

If anyone therefore, etc.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Gregory, bishop of Sabina. I, Manfred, cardinal-priest of the title of St Sabina. I, Julius, cardinal-priest of the title of St Marcellus.
