I, Hubald, cardinal-priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Guido, cardinal-priest of the title of the Shepherd. I, Octavian, cardinal-priest of the title of St Cecilia. I, Bernard, cardinal-priest of the title of St Stephen on the Caelian Hill. [Col. 1522C] I, John, cardinal-priest of Saints John and Paul, title of Pammachius. I, Hildebrand, cardinal-priest of the title of the Basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, Oddo, cardinal-deacon of St Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Oddo, cardinal-deacon of St George at the Golden Veil. I, Bonadies, cardinal-deacon of St Angelo. I, Boso, cardinal-deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian.

Given at the Lateran, by the hand of Roland, cardinal-priest of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of July, in the fifth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1157, in the third year of the pontificate of Pope Adrian IV. [Col. 1522D]

### CXLI. Privilege for the Church of Ravello. (Anagni, September 11.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, I, 1185.]

ADRIAN IV, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother John, bishop of Ravello, and his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

A petition of pious will ought to be fulfilled by a corresponding effect, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth commendably and the requested advantage may undoubtedly acquire strength. Therefore, venerable brother in Christ, Bishop John, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid Church of Ravello, over which, by God’s authority, you are known to preside. We fortify it by the privilege of this present writing, decreeing that whatever possessions and goods the same church presently justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by grants of popes, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, by God’s favor, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. We also confirm to you and your successors in perpetuity the entire district of the Church of Ravello, as it was reasonably possessed by your predecessors. [Col. 1523A]

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain possessions taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; rather, all things shall be preserved whole and intact, to benefit fully the purposes for which they were granted, namely the governance and support of those concerned, without prejudice to the authority of the Apostolic See.

If anyone therefore, etc.

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Hubald, cardinal-priest of the title of St Praxedes. I, Hubald, cardinal-priest of the title of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, James, cardinal-priest of Saints John and Paul, title of Pammachius. I, Arditio, cardinal-deacon of St Theodore. I, Boso, cardinal-deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian.

[Col. 1523C] Given at Anagni, by the hand of Roland, cardinal-priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the third Ides of September, in the fifth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1157, in the third year of the pontificate of Pope Adrian IV.

### CXLII. Privilege for the Church of Benevento. (Orvieto, September 28.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, VIII, 117.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, archbishop of Benevento, and his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

Both the order of reason ordains, and consideration of ecclesiastical advantage persuades, that fuller favor and honor should be bestowed upon our brethren and fellow bishops, and that the churches committed to their governance should be fortified against the assaults of secular wickedness by the protection of the most holy Roman Church, so that they may always be more diligent in the salvation of their subjects and the discharge of their office, in proportion as they see themselves to possess a stronger bulwark of apostolic protection against the audacity of the wicked. Therefore, venerable brother in Christ, Archbishop Henry, we graciously assent to your just petitions and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the Church of Benevento, over which, by God’s authority, you are known to preside. We fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same church presently justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire by grants of popes, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, by God’s favor, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these, we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: the bishoprics of Avellino, Monte Marano, Frequentino, Ariano, Monte di Vico, Bovino, Ascoli, Lucera, Fiorentino, Tortibolo, Montecorvino, Vulturara, Civitate, Dragonara, Larino, Termoli, Guardia, Trivento, Bojano, Alife, Telese, and Sant’Agata; [Col. 1524A] within the city of Benevento, the church of St Paul, the church of St Mary of the Glorious Gate, the church of St Peter Paccadosso, the church of St Thecla, the church of St Martin, the church of St Mary *ante horam* (“before the hour”), the church of St Peter situated beside the church of Peter de’ Medici, the church of St Mary of Ancona, the church of St Arthellais, the church of St Januarius of the Greeks, the church of St Marinus, the church of St Paschasius, the church of St Angelo, situated beside the church of St Cassian, and the church of St Mary Rotunda; outside the city of Benevento, the church of St Mary of Rocca, the church of St Mary of Venticano, the church of St Peter of Cardito, the church of St Peter of Planisio, the church of St Theodora, the church of St Mary in Geldone, the abbey of St Mary in Strata, the abbey of St Mary of Corate, the church of St Mary in Gradellis, and whatever right you possess in the castle of Monte Sarculo and the Caudine Valley. [Col. 1524B]

Moreover, in accordance with custom, we grant you the use of the pallium for the solemn celebration of Mass, and the right to have the cross carried throughout your whole province. You may use the pallium on the Nativity of the Lord, on St Stephen’s Day, Epiphany, the Purification of St Mary, her Annunciation, Laetare Jerusalem Sunday, the Lord’s Supper, Holy Saturday, the Paschal feasts, the Ascension of the Lord, and Pentecost; on the feast of St John the Baptist and the feasts of the blessed Apostles; on the Assumption and Nativity of the blessed Virgin Mary; on the two translations of Blessed Bartholomew; on the dedication of your archbishopric and the anniversary day of your consecration; at assemblies and consecrations of bishops, ordinations of clerics, consecrations of churches, and on the feasts of the principal churches of your province. [Col. 1524D]

We further decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain possessions taken away, or harass it with any vexations; rather, all things shall be preserved intact, to benefit in every way the purposes for which they were granted, namely the governance and support of those concerned, without prejudice in all things to the authority of the Apostolic See. If any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowingly attempting rashly to act against this document of our constitution, does not make suitable satisfaction and amendment after being warned a second or third time, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honor, recognize himself or herself liable before the divine judgment for the aforesaid iniquity, be excluded from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and be subject to severe punishment at the final judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of this place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good conduct and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen. [Col. 1525A]

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Hubald, cardinal-priest of the title of St Praxedes. I, Manfred, cardinal-priest of the title of St Sabina. I, Hubald, cardinal-priest of the title of the Holy Cross. I, Octavian, cardinal-priest of the title of St [lacuna]. I, Gerard, cardinal-priest of the title of St Stephen on the Caelian Hill. [Col. 1525B] I, Henry, cardinal-priest of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. I, John, cardinal-priest of the title of Saints Sylvester and Martin. I, John, cardinal-deacon of the title of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Oddo, cardinal-deacon of St Nicholas in the Tullian Prison.

Given at Orvieto, by the hand of Roland, cardinal-priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Kalends of October, in the fifth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1157, in the third year of the pontificate of Pope Adrian IV.

### CXLIII. He reproaches Frederick, emperor of the Romans, because, disregarding his admonitions, he has still allowed the sacrilegious seizure of Eskil, archbishop of Lund, to go unpunished. He recalls that he bestowed the imperial crown upon him, etc. (About October.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 789.]

[Col. 1525C]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son FREDERICK, illustrious emperor of the Romans: greeting and apostolic blessing.

A few days ago, we recall, we wrote to Your Imperial Majesty, calling to your attention that dreadful and execrable crime and sacrilegious outrage committed in our time in the German regions—an act, as we believe, never previously attempted—and expressing no small astonishment that you have until now permitted the savagery of so destructive a crime to pass without the severity of a worthy punishment. For Your Most Serene Highness knows how our venerable brother E., archbishop of Lund, while returning from the Apostolic See, was captured in those regions by certain impious and wicked men—something which we cannot recount without great sorrow of heart—and is still kept in custody; how also, during that same seizure, men of impiety, evil seed, wicked sons, drew their swords and violently raged against him and his companions, stripped them of all things, and treated them most shamefully and dishonorably. The report of so great a crime has already reached regions far distant and remote. [Col. 1526A]

To avenge this most grievous deed, you ought, as one whom we believe to be pleased by good and displeased by evil, to have risen more resolutely; you ought to have directed against the necks of the wicked the sword which, by divine providence, has been granted to you for the punishment of evildoers and the praise of the good, and to have crushed the presumptuous offenders most severely. Yet you are said to have so disregarded the matter and neglected this outrage that those men have no reason to repent of having committed the crime, because they now already perceive that they have found impunity for the sacrilege which they carried out. We are wholly ignorant of the cause of this disregard and negligence, since no scruple of conscience accuses us that we have in any way offended the glory of Your Serenity. Rather, we have always loved your person with sincere charity as our dearest and special son and as a most Christian prince, whom we do not doubt is, by God’s grace, firmly established upon the rock of apostolic confession; and we have treated you with the affection of due kindness. [Col. 1526B]

For, most glorious son, you ought to call to mind how gladly and joyfully, in the previous year, your mother, the most holy Roman Church, received you; with what affection of heart she treated you; how great a fullness of dignity and honor she bestowed upon you; and how, most willingly conferring the insignia of the imperial crown, she strove to cherish the summit of your exalted rank in her most kindly bosom, doing absolutely nothing that she knew might oppose the royal will even in the least. Yet we do not regret having fulfilled in every respect the desires of your will. Rather, if Your Highness had received still greater benefits from our hand, if that were possible, considering how much advancement and advantage might thereby come to the Church of God and to us through you, we should rightly rejoice. [Col. 1526C]

But now, because you seem to neglect and disregard so immense a crime, which is known to have been committed also in contempt of the universal Church and of your empire, we indeed suspect and fear that perhaps your mind has been led into this disregard and negligence because, through the prompting of a perverse man sowing tares, you have conceived—God forbid!—some indignation or resentment against your most merciful mother, the most holy Roman Church, and against ourselves.

For this reason, therefore, and because of all the other matters which we know to be impending, we have thought fit at present to send to Your Serenity from our side two of the best and dearest men whom we have about us: namely, our beloved sons Bernard, priest of St. Clement’s, and Roland, priest-cardinal of St. Mark’s and our chancellor—men distinguished, indeed, for religion, prudence, and integrity. We earnestly ask Your Excellency to receive them as honourably as kindly, to treat them with due respect, and, without any hesitation, to accept what they shall set before Your Imperial Dignity on our behalf concerning this matter and other matters pertaining to the honour of God and of the most holy Roman Church, and also to the glory and exaltation of the Empire, as though it proceeded from our own mouth; nor should you hesitate to give credit to their words as though it were we ourselves who uttered them. [Col. 1526D–1527A]

### CXLIV. He confirms the possessions of the Hospital of St. Blaise near Monza. (Lateran, 4 November.)

[GIULINI, *Memorie di Milano*, VI, 529.]

### CXLV. He confirms to the Milanese monastery of St. Dionysius all its rights and possessions. (Lateran, 10 November.)

[MURATORI, *Antiq. Ital.*, V, 1035.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons WILFRED, abbot of the monastery of St. Dionysius at Milan, and to his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: for ever.

It is fitting that the just desires of religious persons should readily receive favourable consent, so that faithful devotion may attain a notable effect. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, Abbot Wilfred, we graciously assent to your just requests; and we take under the protection of blessed Peter, our predecessor, and under our own protection, the monastery of St. Dionysius, over which, by God’s ordering, you preside, and we fortify it by the privilege of this present document. We decree that whatever possessions or goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, acquire by the Lord’s favour, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors.

Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: namely, the church of St. Michael of Pescallo, in which you have authority to establish a monastery if expedient, as has been granted to you by the reasonable provision of our venerable brother Oberto, archbishop of Milan; the entire parish of the suburb of the gate called Porta Nuova, as it has been lawfully adjudged to you by the sentence of that same archbishop; the church of St. Mary in Solario, now called St. Fidelis; the church of St. Lawrence, which is beside the house of Tasso, with all their appurtenances; the estate of Melate, with its three chapels—namely, those of St. Bartholomew, St. Dionysius, and St. Mary of Sabioncello—and the two castles, namely Melate and Sabioncello; the estate of Lierni, with two chapels, namely those of blessed Maurice and blessed Michael; a third part of the estate of Talamona with the tithe, and your right in the two chapels situated upon that estate, namely St. Mary’s and St. Martin’s, with all that belongs to them; the chapel of St. Martin of Gradi, with all its possessions; the church of blessed Michael of Pescallo, with all its appurtenances; the tithe of the lands lying near the monastery itself, and of those lands which are situated on either side around the river Seveso, throughout all the holdings of persons dwelling in the gate called Porta Nuova and in the eastern gate, which are now cultivated or were cultivated formerly, as it was canonically granted to you and confirmed in his document by Eribert, archbishop of Milan, of good memory; and the possessions which you hold at Sacrate, Sesto called Giovanni, Affori, Ponte Curione, Gorgonzola, Aronio, Pescallo, Lomacio, Casalego, Calutate, Romano, Quinto, Surdi, and Casale, of Casinis and Valle Saxia, with all the liberties and customs of the aforesaid possessions, as you have hitherto held them peaceably through royal cession and as they have been confirmed to you by the charter of the aforesaid Archbishop Oberto. [Col. 1527B–1528A]

Furthermore, the four clerics of this monastery, who belong to the order of the Decomani of the Milanese Church, shall be installed and ordained in that Church by the abbot holding office at the time, for the honour of God; and they shall be obedient to him as their father and lord, as they are known hitherto to have been and as is contained in the document of the archbishop already mentioned. We decree that in the aforesaid churches of Saints Lawrence and Fidelis you may appoint priests, with the assent of the aforementioned archbishop, without any contradiction.

We also prohibit anyone, without your consent, in the parish of the suburb of Porta Nuova, which is under your jurisdiction, from visiting the sick, burying the dead, or celebrating divine offices for the people that pertain to parochial right. Moreover, whatever Adalbert, the aforesaid abbot and usurper of that monastery, unlawfully alienated from the same church of St. Dionysius by sales, pledges, infeudations, investitures, charters, exchanges, leases, or in any other manner whatsoever, we decree to be void; and we grant you authority to reclaim it for the church of Blessed Dionysius, just as this was lawfully adjudged and confirmed by the judgment of the Milanese consuls for Archbishop Rubald of good memory.

No one may presume to exact tithes from you on your newly cleared lands which you cultivate with your own hands or resources, nor on the fodder of your animals. We likewise confirm to you the tithes which you canonically possess. [Col. 1528B–1528C]

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole and unimpaired, to serve in every way the uses of those for whose governance and support they have been granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the archbishop of Milan.

If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing of this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he correct his presumption by fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself to be guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most holy body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer; and at the last judgment let him be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen. [Col. 1528D–1529A]

I, Adrian, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Gregory, bishop of Sabina. I, Hubald, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Praxedes. I, Julius, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Marcellus. I, Octavian, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Cecilia. I, Henry, priest-cardinal of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus. I, Odo, deacon-cardinal of St. George at the Golden Veil. I, Guido, deacon-cardinal of St. Mary in Portico. I, Odo, deacon-cardinal of St. Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Bonadies, deacon-cardinal of St. Angelo. [Col. 1529A–B]

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Albert, deacon-cardinal of St. Adrian, acting in place of Lord Roland, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the fourth Ides of November, in the sixth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1157, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Adrian IV. [Col. 1529B–C]

### CXLVI. Privilege for the convent of the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete. (Lateran, 1 December.)

[*Opp. Abaelardi*, 353.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ HELOISE, abbess, and the others devoted to divine service in the oratory of the Holy Spirit, situated in the district of Troyes, etc. [as in the preceding letter of Eugenius].

Moreover, the places of Pomario, Triagnello, Leavalle, Neforto, and St. Flavit, as they have reasonably been granted to you, we confirm to you by apostolic authority, etc.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Albert, deacon-cardinal of St. Adrian, acting in place of Lord Roland, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the Kalends of December, in the eleventh indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1157, in the third year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Adrian IV. [Col. 1529C–D]

### CXLVII. He receives the church of St. Rupert at Salzburg under protection and confirms its possessions and rights. (Lateran, 30 December.)

[HANSIZII, *Germ. sacra*, II, 254.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons HUGH, provost of the Church of St. Rupert at Salzburg, and to his brethren, present and future, professing the canonical life: for ever.

Whenever something is requested of us which is recognized to accord with religion and uprightness, it is fitting for us gladly to grant it and to afford suitable support to the desires of the petitioners. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests. Following in the footsteps of our predecessors of happy memory, the Roman pontiffs Calixtus, Honorius, Innocent, and Eugenius, we take under the protection of blessed Peter and our own protection the church of St. Rupert, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this present document.

First, we decree that the canonical order which, according to the Lord, the Rule of Blessed Augustine, and the institution of our venerable brother Conrad, archbishop of Salzburg of good memory, is known to have been established there, shall be observed inviolate there for all time. We also enact that no one shall dare remove you from the place in which you have been established or impose upon you the rule of another profession.

Furthermore, whatever possessions or goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, through the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, acquire by the Lord’s favour, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify by their proper names: Longow, with all its appurtenances; Krencecar, with all its appurtenances; Saldorf, with all its appurtenances; Hoerdingen, with all its appurtenances; the saltworks at Halle, with estates, serfs, and their other appurtenances; in the eastern region, vineyards, fields, estates, dependent households, with all their appurtenances; Arnstorff, with all its appurtenances; Peberar, with all its appurtenances; and those things which you appear justly and lawfully to possess in the district of Salzburg, in fields, meadows, and newly cleared land; the church of St. James, situated in the city of Salzburg beside your monastery, with all its appurtenances; and Pongau Hopfgart with all its appurtenances. [Col. 1530A–C]

We prohibit any of you, cleric or layman, after making profession, from daring to possess private property or to leave the community of the cloister without the permission of the abbot or congregation. We also prohibit any advocate of your church from appointing a substitute for himself or presuming to harass you with unjust vexations. Nor may any bishop impose upon you or your church forced services or other new exactions contrary to your canonical freedom and religious life.

Upon the death of you, the present abbot of the same place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it by any trickery of fraud or force, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall, according to God and the Rule of Blessed Augustine, provide to be elected.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid Church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole and unimpaired, to serve in every way the uses of those for whose governance and support they have been granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical reverence due to the archbishop of Salzburg.

If anyone therefore, etc. But upon all, etc.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Roland, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Kalends of January, in the sixth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1157, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Adrian IV. [Col. 1530C–1531A]

### CXLVIII. To the archbishops and bishops of Germany: he complains of injuries inflicted by Emperor Frederick upon his legates. He orders them to strive that the emperor procure satisfaction from Chancellor Rainald.

[MANSI, *Concil.*, XXI, 790.]

Whenever something is undertaken in the Church against the honour of God and the salvation of the faithful, concern ought to be shown by our brethren and fellow bishops, especially those who are guided by the Spirit of God, so that acts wrongly performed may receive correction pleasing to God. At this time, however—to say it without profound grief is impossible—our most beloved son Frederick, emperor of the Romans, has done something such as we do not read that he did in the times of his predecessors.

For when we had sent to his presence two of our best brethren, Bernard, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Clement, and Roland, our chancellor, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Mark, he seemed at first, when they arrived before him, to receive them gladly. But on the following day, when they returned to him and our letter was read in his hearing, he seized upon the occasion of a certain expression contained in its text, namely, “we bestowed upon you the benefaction of the crown,” and burst into such agitation of mind that it is grievous even to hear and lamentable to recount the insults which he is said to have hurled against us and our legates, and how disgracefully he compelled them to withdraw from his presence and swiftly to leave his territory.

As they departed from his presence, he is said to have issued an edict that no one from his kingdom should approach the Apostolic See; and to have placed guards along all the borders of the kingdom, who were forcibly to turn back those wishing to come to the Apostolic See. Although we are somewhat disturbed by this act, we nonetheless receive greater consolation within ourselves from the fact that it did not proceed from your counsel and that of the princes. We therefore trust that he may readily be recalled from the agitation of his mind by your counsel and persuasion.

Accordingly, brethren, since in this affair not only our own cause but yours and that of all Churches is clearly at stake, we admonish and exhort your charity in the Lord to stand as a wall for the house of the Lord, and to endeavour to bring our aforesaid son back as speedily as possible to the right path. Apply the most earnest care to ensure that he causes Chancellor Rainald and the Count Palatine—who presumed to vomit forth grave blasphemies against the aforesaid legates and against your mother, the most holy Roman Church—to offer satisfaction so substantial and manifest that, just as the bitterness of their words offended the ears of many, so their satisfaction may likewise bring many back to the right path. [Col. 1531B–1532A]

Let that same son of ours not yield to the counsels of the wicked. Let him consider the end and the past, and let him walk by the path by which Justinian and the other Catholic emperors are known to have walked. By their example and imitation he can accumulate for himself both honour on earth and blessedness in heaven. You also, if you bring him back to the straight path, will render welcome service to blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, and will preserve liberty for yourselves and your Churches.

Otherwise, let the aforesaid son of ours learn from your admonition, and from the truth of the Gospel promise, that the most holy Roman Church, founded by God upon the firmest rock, however violently shaken by the storm of winds, will, under the Lord’s protection, remain steadfast for ever and ever. Nor, as you know, was it fitting for him to have attempted so arduous a course without your counsel. We therefore believe that, having heard your admonitions, he can most readily, as a discerning man and a Catholic emperor, be recalled to the fruit of sounder conduct. [Col. 1532A–C]

### CXLIX. He grants certain fiefs to Aldebrandino and Bernardino, sons of Count Ubolino of Calmaiare.

[MURATORI, *Antiq. Ital.*, I, 631.]

In the name of the Lord, etc. I, Adrian IV, pope of the holy Apostolic See, with the consent and will of my brethren—namely, Ubald, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Praxedes; Ubald of the title of Holy Cross; Julius of the title of St. Marcellus; Henry of the title of Saints Nereus and Achilleus; Boso, deacon-cardinal of Saints Cosmas and Damian and our chamberlain; and Albert, deacon-cardinal of St. Adrian—grant to you Aldebrandino and Bernardino, sons of the late Count Ubolino of Calmaiare, and to your legitimate sons and daughters, the following. But if you die without legitimate sons and daughters, the lands named below which we grant you shall freely remain under the right and lordship of blessed Peter; namely, Fracta of Adzo’s son, etc., as above.

The aforesaid lands are situated in the bishoprics of Soana, Orvieto, Todi, and Chiusi, within the jurisdiction of blessed Peter and the holy Roman Church. You are to hold, use, enjoy, improve, possess, and retain them, as stated, because you have done homage to us and sworn fealty to us, to our Catholic successors, and to the holy Roman Church; and because you have sworn and promised to observe the highway at all times and for all persons, except public robbers and enemies of the Roman Church and of yourselves—provided, however, that they do not bear the dress of pilgrims—and to swear and observe the truce if your other peers swear and observe it.

We grant the keeping of the Rocca of St. Stephen to Scarlatano of Radicofano, his brother Orlandino, and the sons of Belizo, provided that they make fealty to us, at your expense for five consecutive years. This is on the condition that, if you commit an offence upon the highway and, when called upon, do not make amends within eight days, the aforesaid Rocca of St. Stephen shall absolutely remain under the right and lordship of blessed Peter. But if you offend against the truce or against Hospitallers, Templars, clerics, or monks, and, when called upon, do not make amends within fifteen days, the aforesaid Rocca of St. Stephen shall remain under the right and lordship of blessed Peter.

You shall cherish and protect the churches, clerics, and monks of your territory as our other faithful men protect their churches, clerics, and monks. You shall not give or alienate this grant, in whole or part, to any other pious place; nor shall you sell or alienate it to any person before offering it to the lord pope holding office at the time and to the holy Roman Church, deducting twelve denarii from the just price for every pound. If he does not wish to buy and receive that alienation, you shall give him the aforesaid advantage, and you shall sell or alienate it without fraud to a person pleasing to us, always preserving the right and lordship of blessed Peter and the holy Roman Church.

You and your sons shall make war and peace, through your persons and the aforesaid lands, at the command of the Roman pontiff and the Roman Church. Your sons and sons-in-law who hold those lands, or a portion of them, shall render to us and to our Catholic successors fealty and homage, and shall make war and peace at our command and that of our successors. They shall swear not to offend against the truce, the highway, churches, Hospitallers, Templars, clerics, and monks. Otherwise, those who fail to do so shall remain excluded from the right conferred by our grant. We and our successors promise to defend you against every person, if necessary, according to our office. [Col. 1532C–1533C]

### CL. He forbids the canons of Calvimont from alienating church property, since it had long ago been decreed that brethren of the monastery of St. Dionysius should be established in their church. (Rome, St. Peter’s, 10 January.)

[DOUBLET, *Hist. de S. Denys*, 502.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the canons of the Church of Calvimont: greeting and apostolic blessing.

What has reasonably been ordered by the authority of the Apostolic See cannot be overthrown by any presumption. It is known that long ago, by decree of the most holy Roman Church, it was established that monks from the monastery of Blessed Dionysius should be placed in your church to perform the divine offices, and that the benefices of deceased canons should pass to their use and administration.

Therefore, lest so praiseworthy an institution be defeated by anyone’s contrivance, we command you by this present writing that you in no way presume to sell or otherwise alienate your prebends and benefices. Otherwise, by apostolic authority we declare those alienations void, and, God being the author, we shall punish you in such a manner that the penalty itself may teach you how serious it is to violate constitutions so holy and praiseworthy. [Col. 1533D–1534A]

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, on the fourth Ides of January.

### CLI. To Henry, bishop of Beauvais: he commends a certain D. (Rome, St. Peter’s, 10 January.)

[MARTEN., *Ampl. Collect.*, II, 638.]

ADRIAN, bishop, etc., to his venerable brother HENRY, bishop of Beauvais, etc.

Because we have the fullest confidence in your devotion and sincerity of heart, we do not hesitate to address requests to you on behalf of those whom we hold dear. Therefore, we earnestly commend to your charity our beloved son D., bearer of the present letter. He has reported to us many things worthy of commendation concerning both your affection towards him and many other matters; and by apostolic writing we ask that, for reverence towards blessed Peter and ourselves, you love and honour him, and, by our intervention and in consideration of his devotion, hold him dearer among those dear to you. Should any affairs arise, let your prudence also diligently defend him with vigour in them. [Col. 1534B]

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, on the fourth day before the Kalends of February.

In the year 1156–58.

### CLII. He exhorts Raymond, bishop of Maguelone, not to dispose at his own discretion of “the goods of the church assigned to the common use of the clerics,” and to restore the tithe of Montpellier to the canons. (Lateran, 27 October.)

[GARIEL, *Series*, I, 199.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to RAYMOND, bishop of Maguelone: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It has come to our notice that you are attempting, contrary to the institution of the Church itself, to dispose at your own discretion of the goods of the church of Maguelone assigned to the common use of your clerics. Further, you have not yet restored to them the tithe of Montpellier, which, as we are informed, belongs to the community of those canons and which you are said to have redeemed from a certain layman.

Since, by the office of apostolic ministry laid upon us, we are bound to correct what needs correcting and to preserve each person’s right, we command and strictly enjoin your brotherhood by apostolic writings not to presume in any way, without the counsel and assent of the archdeacons and the sounder part of the chapter of your church, to make any disposition, contrary to the institution of that church, of property belonging to their community; and to restore in full what you have taken from it. Take earnest care that your clerics may henceforth have no cause for murmuring in these matters and that we not be compelled on this account to write to you with a more severe censure.

Moreover, unless you have already recovered in full the amount which you gave for redeeming the tithe mentioned above, or as soon as you recover it, restore that tithe to your canons, setting aside every excuse and delay. [Col. 1534C–1535A]

Given at the Lateran, on the sixth day before the Kalends of November, [in the fourth year of our pontificate. **Note:** [Col. 1535A] These words appear to have been added by another hand.]

### CLIII. He commends Ansolde, abbot of Compiègne, to Henry, bishop of Beauvais. (Lateran, 29 October.)

[MARTEN., *Ampl. Collect.*, II, 642.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, bishop of Beauvais: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting for us to love and cherish the Church of Compiègne all the more because the Roman Church is known to have taken greater care to plant religious life there. Accordingly, we earnestly ask and admonish your brotherhood in the Lord that, out of reverence for blessed Peter and ourselves, you love and honour our beloved son An., abbot of that place, and afford him aid and protection in his necessities. And because our beloved son Philip, your brother, is said still to retain the treasury of that church, do not cease often to exhort him that the treasury should pass into the hands of the aforesaid abbot.

Furthermore, we command your brotherhood that, concerning those wrongdoers of whom the aforesaid abbot may lodge a complaint before you, you render him such full justice that he may not be compelled further to labour through a failure of justice. [Col. 1535B–C]

Given at the Lateran, on the fourth day before the Kalends of November.

### CLIV. He commands the bishop of Arras to restore to Chancellor Hugh the altar of Aslues which had been taken from him. (Lateran, 1 November.)

[MANSI, *Concil.*, XXI, 807.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother . . . . ., bishop of Arras: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our beloved son Hugh, chancellor of our dearest son Louis, illustrious king of the Franks, has shown us in a report sent to us that he held a certain altar in the bishopric of Arras by the gift of Aluisius, formerly bishop of Arras of good memory. He asserts that he possessed that altar quietly and peaceably until the time when, at our command, he was to receive investiture of the greater archdeaconry in your Church.

But when the day was approaching on which, as we have said, he was to be invested with that archdeaconry according to our command, you are reported to have refused to grant him the investiture unless that altar had first been restored to you, and thus to have extorted the altar itself from him. Since such circumvention is contrary to reason and wholly foreign to the episcopal office, we command and strictly enjoin your brotherhood by apostolic writings that, if the matter stands thus, you restore that altar to our said son Hugh, the chancellor, within forty days after receiving this letter, all appeal being set aside. Should you perhaps delay in doing so, know that we have commanded our venerable brother [Samson], archbishop of Reims and legate of the Apostolic See, not to delay in carrying this out in our stead. [Col. 1535D–1536A]

Given at the Lateran, on the fifth Ides of May.

### CLV. He exhorts Thesbald, bishop of Paris, to grant Chancellor Hugh the first dignity or benefice to fall vacant in the Church of Paris. (Lateran, 1 November.)

[MANSI, XXI, 805.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother, the bishop of Paris: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since we have full confidence in the devotion and sincerity of faith which you are known to bear towards your mother, the most holy Roman Church, and towards ourselves, we do not hesitate to ask your brotherhood concerning those dear and acceptable to us. How devoted and faithful our beloved son Hugh, chancellor of our dearest son, the illustrious king of the Franks, is to your mother, the most holy Roman Church, and to ourselves, and how watchful and solicitous he continues to be for her honour, is known both to us ourselves and, we believe, not unknown to your prudence.

We have therefore thought fit earnestly to commend him to your brotherhood, asking that, out of reverence for blessed Peter and our letters, you grant him the first dignity or benefice which falls vacant in your church. Thus he may find our request effectual for himself, and we may owe you thanksgiving for accepting our request. [Col. 1536B–C]

Given at the Lateran, on the Kalends of November.

### CLVI. He directs the nobleman William and the whole people of Montpellier that, “when five years have elapsed, they are to return the altar of St. Saviour and the offerings into the hands of the prior of the church of Blessed Mary.” (Lateran, 8 November.)

[D. BOUQUET, *Recueil*, XV, 687.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son the nobleman WILLIAM and to the whole people of Montpellier: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Although the sacred canons attribute to laymen no authority to dispose of ecclesiastical property, nevertheless, in view of your devotion, the offerings of St. Saviour have been granted to you for the restoration of that church, so that the work begun through your care may be completed more swiftly and readily. But because it is not fitting for ecclesiastical goods to be wholly removed from the administration of ecclesiastical persons, we wish to set a definite term, after whose completion you are to retain the altar and offerings for a period of five years, and no longer.

Therefore, we command your whole community that, when the five years have elapsed, you return the aforesaid altar and offerings into the hands of the prior of the church of Blessed Mary, so that he may have free authority to dispose of them as of other ecclesiastical property. Therefore, in order that through your work and labour you may merit the joys of eternal blessedness, make provision from those offerings and from the resources granted you by God, and apply yourselves so effectively to completing the work of the Church that, by the Lord’s help, it may be completed within a short time. [Col. 1536D–1537A]

Given at the Lateran, on the sixth Ides of November.

### CLVII. To the archbishop of Reims and his suffragans—concerning the Church of Jerusalem and the Knights Templar. (Lateran, 13 November.)

[MARTEN., *Ampl. Coll.*, II, 647.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother S., archbishop of Reims, legate of the Apostolic See, and to his suffragan bishops: greeting and apostolic blessing. [Col. 1537B]

How greatly the valiant and distinguished lords, namely the knights of the Temple—the new Maccabees under grace—benefit all Christendom, and how they defend against the guile and persecution of the pagans the holy places which our Saviour illumined by his bodily presence, has, we do not doubt, reached not only those who live nearby but also those who inhabit the furthest limits of the world. [Col. 1537C] Therefore, the greater the advantages which come to all Christ’s faithful through them, the more urgently we are bound to take thought and act diligently, that we may endeavour to relieve their needs and, compassionating them with a fatherly affection of charity in their adversities, provide them counsel and assistance.

Recently, however—and we cannot say it without great sorrow and anguish—certain misfortunes befell them; and, through the increasing savagery of the pagans, as sins required, they suffered no small loss and damage both in property and persons. For when the son of the man of blood had come to besiege Bellinacii, which was subject to Christian rule, having assembled an innumerable multitude of faithless men, our dearest son in Christ B., [Note: [Col. 1537D] Baldwin, son of Fulk, king of Jerusalem.] the illustrious king of Jerusalem, hastened swiftly with the brethren of the knighthood of the Temple to drive off the enemies. And when the king had taken up his position opposite the pagan camp, the greater part of his men, leave having been obtained, withdrew, while the brethren of the Temple remained with him. The enemies, clearly recognizing this, hastily attacked the Christians, who resisted them courageously with a strong hand.

But the king and those with him, since they were wholly unable to withstand an innumerable multitude [lacuna], at the advice and urgent, repeated entreaties of those knights of the Temple—who, together with the remaining knights of the king, stayed behind for the battle—returned at last unharmed to their own country, though unwilling and overcome only by much prayer and insistence. [Col. 1538A] Yet the aforesaid brethren, not at all afraid to lay down their lives for Christ’s name and for the salvation of Christians, together with the others who had remained with them, engaged an innumerable host of pagans and joined battle. In that battle our beloved son B., master of the knighthood of the Temple, was captured by the enemies, and with him eighty-seven of the brethren; while three hundred of the other knights were either captured or slain by the sword. They also lost, to an incredible extent, horses, arms, and other spoil.

But after the darkness of this calamity and the confusion of that gloomy time, a season of prosperity shone forth and the desired day of serenity dawned. Accordingly, our aforesaid son the [Col. 1538B] king, having restored his army and assembled a multitude of mounted and foot soldiers, together with our beloved sons, the noble men T., [Note: [Col. 1538D] Theodoric, called of Alsace, who had married the sister of King Baldwin.] count of Flanders, and Rainald of Saint-Valery and their followers—who happened unexpectedly at that time to arrive in those parts—attacked the brutal fury of the arrogant enemies. Having captured some and killed others, he triumphantly drove their army far away from the siege of the aforesaid city.

Meanwhile, to furnish greater joy and a fuller measure of gladness, and also greater consolation amid adversity, about thirty knights of the Temple put to flight two hundred pagans going to a wedding; and, with divine protection accompanying them, they captured some and slew the rest [Col. 1538C] with the sword. Now, therefore, since in so great a desolation and at this crisis of urgent need we neither ought nor can in any way fail the aforesaid brethren and the others who defend those holy places out of pious concern, we ask, admonish, and exhort your brotherhood in the Lord that you strive most diligently to admonish the people entrusted to you; and, by virtue of the office imposed upon you, enjoin upon them, for the remission of their sins, that those who are fit and vigorous for fighting hasten to those places for their liberation and defence. But those who cannot labour in person should endeavour to send thither horses, weapons of war—which are exceedingly necessary in those regions—and other resources from their own means, for the salvation of their souls and for relief against the pagans. [Col. 1538D]

Given at the Lateran, on the Ides of November.

### CLVIII. To the abbots of the diocese of Béziers: he commands them to obey the bishop of Béziers. (Lateran, 13 November.)

[Gallia Christiana, VI, Documents, 138.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the abbots established throughout the parish of Béziers: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We cannot remain unmoved by what has been reported to us by our venerable brother William, bishop of Béziers. For he asserts that you refuse to render him the obedience and reverence due to him, although he is your bishop. Since the character of the habit which you have assumed summons you rather to obedience than to resistance, it is plainly to be understood that you do not carry inwardly in your minds what you outwardly display in your clothing. For it is fitting that you obey your prelate, since, as even your habit shows, you have abandoned your own will for the Lord’s sake.

Therefore, that you may not be shown to bear inwardly anything other than what you outwardly demonstrate by your habit, we command you by apostolic letters, ordering that you, upon whom that bishop lays his hands by his authority, render him, without any contradiction and with appeal set aside, every obedience and reverence which subjects ought humbly to show to their prelates. [Col. 1539A] If any one of you should prove disobedient or rebellious toward him, we shall, by God’s authority, hold ratified by our own authority whatever sentence our aforesaid brother shall have canonically pronounced against one who refuses to obey him.

Given at the Lateran, on the Ides of November.

### CLIX. Privilege for the nunnery of the Holy Spirit of the Paraclete. (Lateran, 25 November.)

[Works of Peter Abelard, p. 354.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, Heloise, abbess of the monastery of the Paraclete, and her sisters: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1539C] Whenever religious persons petition us for things that do not depart from the path of reason, we ought not to be found reluctant to grant what is requested. Therefore, beloved daughters in the Lord, graciously assenting to your just petitions, we grant you by apostolic authority that, if persons who generously bestow from their resources the comforts of charity upon your church are under interdict not for their own offence but for those of others, you may receive them for burial and inter them in your cemetery with the other faithful.

Given at the Lateran, on the eighth day before the Kalends of December.

### CLX. To Henry, bishop of Beauvais: that he should continue to exercise the episcopal office without any hesitation. (Lateran, 1 December.)

[Marten, *Amplissima Collectio*, II, 650.]

[Col. 1539D]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, bishop of Beauvais: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our predecessor Pope Eugenius of holy memory wished you to be appointed bishop of Beauvais, [Note: [Col. 1539D] This took place in the year 1149, when, after the death of Odo, bishop of Beauvais, Henry was appointed in his place by the unanimous vote of clergy and people, with the assent of the metropolitan and of all the suffragans, and also with the approval of the supreme pontiff. On this promotion see Peter the Venerable, book V, letter 8.] [Col. 1540A] hoping that no small benefit for God’s Church would result from your person. In that dignity, indeed, your nobility has thus far conducted itself so prudently, honourably, and circumspectly, divine grace cooperating, that the intention of our predecessor seems to have been fulfilled. Knowing your integrity from the past, we continually conceive greater hope and confidence in the diligence of your brotherhood; and therefore, if you had not been transferred from the repose of contemplation to the labours of action, we should diligently endeavour to bring about such a transfer for the Church’s benefit; nor ought we to bring about the annulment of what has been done.

[Note: [Col. 1539D] For Henry, despising the attractions of court, professed himself a monk at Clairvaux, where with Mary he sat at the feet of Christ the Lord. [Col. 1540D]]

Let not, therefore, a word which you are said to have uttered somewhat incautiously disturb you, for to say that was by no means to abandon your spiritual dignity. [Note: [Col. 1540D] From this you may infer that Henry bore episcopal dignity with reluctance and wished to relinquish it.] [Col. 1540B] Let your prudence therefore diligently exercise the episcopal ministry you have received; strive to instruct the flock entrusted to you, in word and deed, in Christ’s doctrine, so that you need not come empty to the storehouse of the householder, if, through divine grace, you can bring back many sheaves with you. For we neither wish nor could in any way endure that you should relinquish episcopal dignity, unless—God forbid!—we learned that there was such a fault in you that you could not serve the Lord in the episcopal office.

Moreover, show yourself so kind and merciful toward our beloved sons, the brethren of Saint [Note: [Col. 1540D] Saint Lucian’s, a notable monastery of the Order of Saint Benedict in the suburb of the city of Beauvais, in whose church Saint Lucian rests with his companions.] Lucian, that they may pray more fervently to the omnipotent Lord for you.

[Col. 1540C] Given at the Lateran, on the Kalends of December.

### CLXI. To the same: for the church of Saint Lucian. (Lateran, 1 December.)

[Marten, ibid., col. 651.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, bishop of Beauvais: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have thought it right to invite you all the more earnestly to works of piety and mercy because we have greater confidence in your uprightness and religious devotion, and hope that your brotherhood ought to heed our prayers. The religious brethren of the church of Blessed Lucian, concerning certain matters over which a dispute had arisen between you and them, chose rather to submit themselves to your will than to argue in court with your nobility, hoping that humility would bring them more advantage in dealing with you than the conflicts of litigation would provide. Therefore, by apostolic letters we admonish, ask, and exhort your charity in the Lord that, in all matters which they have decided to place within your generosity, especially concerning tithes, meals, and fishing rights, your [Col. 1540D] nobility conduct itself toward the aforesaid brethren in such a manner that you may appear to love and favour religious brethren for Christ’s sake, and that we may be able to offer you abundant thanksgivings. [Col. 1541A]

Given at the Lateran, on the Kalends of December.

### CLXII. To the same: concerning the nephews of a certain canon of Auxerre. (Lateran, 8 December.)

[Marten, ibid., col. 652.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother HENRY, bishop of Beauvais: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We recently received the complaint of our beloved son, a canon of Auxerre, who came into the presence of the Apostolic See: [Col. 1541B] namely, that A., [Note: [Col. 1541D] Arduin, born of an illustrious family, succeeded Abbot Gervase about the year 1147 and died in 1174.] abbot of the church of Saint Germanus of Auxerre, presumes unjustly to retain land which, as we have recently learned, is said to belong by hereditary right to certain nephews of his who have been deprived of paternal support. Since on another occasion the case itself had been committed to our venerable brothers H., archbishop of Sens, and the bishop of Auxerre, for due conclusion, an appeal to the Apostolic See was made during the examination of that business.

But because by the office laid upon us we are compelled to provide beneficially for the rightful claims of wards and orphans, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters that, within fifteen days after receiving these letters, you diligently summon the said abbot, so that [Col. 1541C] he either promptly restore that land to the nephews of the aforesaid L. or render them complete justice in your presence. But if he should prefer to lose the case rather than restore the land in full, then, with both parties appearing before you and the arguments on each side carefully investigated and understood, decide the case by the mediation of justice, all appeal being set aside, in such a way that no complaint concerning it need thereafter be repeated in our hearing.

If the aforesaid abbot is unwilling either to restore the land or to render justice concerning those to whom that land is said to belong, or if he refuses to abide by your judgment in this matter, then by our authority prohibit the celebration of divine offices on the very land in dispute. [Col. 1541D] Moreover, if A., the wife formerly of S. of Merlenmaco, should presume, personally or through another, to obstruct the carrying into effect of either of these measures, pronounce a sentence of excommunication upon her person and a sentence of interdict upon her land.

Given at the Lateran, on the sixth day before the Ides of December.

### CLXIII. To the same: concerning a canon of the church of Auxerre. (Lateran, 8 December.)

[Marten, ibid., col. 553.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable [Col. 1542A] brother HENRY, bishop of Beauvais: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We formerly committed for hearing and due conclusion to our venerable brothers H., [Note: [Col. 1542D] Hugh.] archbishop of Sens, and A., [Note: [Col. 1542D] Alan, formerly abbot of Ripatorium, made bishop.] bishop of Auxerre, the case known to be litigated between our beloved sons R., provost of Liry, and L., canon of the church of Auxerre, concerning a certain prebend. When they had summoned both parties to appear before them, the aforesaid provost R. scorned to attend their summons, but appealed the said L. to the Apostolic See by a frivolous delaying tactic. Since we have great confidence in your discretion, however, we commit the same case to your experience, to be decided by justice with every appeal set aside. [Col. 1542B]

Therefore we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters to summon both parties before you and, after carefully investigating and fully understanding the arguments advanced on either side, decide the same case by a canonical settlement. But if the said provost R. should obstinately refuse to appear at your summons or effectively obey your decision in this matter, then by our authority invest our aforesaid son L. with that prebend, without impediment of appeal.

Given at the Lateran, on the sixth day before the Ides of December.

### CLXIV. To Berengar, archbishop, and the clergy of Narbonne: concerning the prohibition on seizing the goods of deceased bishops. (Lateran, 9 December.)

[Mansi, *Concilia*, XXI, 826.]

[Col. 1542C]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother BERENGAR, archbishop, and to his beloved sons the archdeacons and all the clergy of Narbonne: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since, as God has ordained according to his pleasure, we have undertaken the care of the Apostolic See, it befits us to provide with diligent attention for the tranquillity and peace of all churches, and to confirm by apostolic authority what we see has been done for their peace. Thus, what has once been established for the honour of God, the adornment of his house, and the salvation of the faithful must not through any length of time fall into oblivion and neglect, nor be removed from its stability by any contrivance of evil men. [Col. 1542D]

Now our beloved daughter in Christ, the noble lady Ermengard, lady of Narbonne, wishing, out of love for the divine law and regard for your affection, brother archbishop, to abolish a certain evil custom long established against God and your church, has ordained, for the remission of her sins, that upon the death of you or any of your successors, no prince, castellan, or secular person whatever shall presume to seize, diminish, or disturb episcopal goods; rather, all things are to be preserved unimpaired and whole for the future bishop. We therefore approve her pious intention and hold her renunciation ratified; and we confirm it by apostolic authority, decreeing that it remain firm and inviolate for ever.

Accordingly, when the archbishop then in office dies, neither the ruler of the land, nor any castellan or knight, nor any secular or lay person, under pretext of any custom, may dare to plunder the goods of the church of Narbonne or retain goods already plundered. [Col. 1543A] If anyone should presume to attempt this and does not within forty days amend his presumption by fitting satisfaction, let him incur the indignation of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul; let him know that, as a sacrilegious person, he is deprived of communion with the faithful and bound by the bond of excommunication; and he may be absolved by no one without the permission of the Roman pontiff or of a legate sent from his side.

Given at the Lateran, on the fifth day before the Ides of December.

### CLXV. He confirms the agreement made between the bishop of Béziers and the prior of Cassian. (Lateran, 9 December.)

[Gallia Christiana, VI, Documents, 138.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son JOHN, prior of Cassian: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1543C] What is either settled amicably or reasonably decided concerning the disputes of litigants through the mediation of worthy and honourable men ought to stand in its established state and, lest it be disturbed in the passage of time by anyone’s presumption, ought to be fortified by the document of our authority. When, therefore, a controversy had arisen between you and our venerable brother William, bishop of Béziers, concerning a certain church, and he claimed that the *quartones* were due to him by episcopal right in churches of yours situated in his diocese, the following settlement was made between you through the intervention of our venerable brothers Berengar, archbishop of Narbonne; Aldebert, bishop of Nîmes; Raymond, bishop of Uzès; and Adhemar, bishop of Agde; Pons, provost of Uzès; Roger, archdeacon of Narbonne; [Col. 1543D] and other wise men; and it was confirmed by the assent of both parties.

The bishop of Béziers granted freely to you and to the church of Cassian, to hold in perpetuity: the church of Aureliac, concerning which the dispute had arisen; the church of Saint Victor; the church of Saint Peter of Laspinian; the church of Saint Felix of Calobricis; the church of Saint Martin of Gradano; the church of Saint Andrew of Prolian; the church of Saint Lawrence of Roian; the church of Saint Michael of Padernis; the church of Saint Natalia of Fano; the church of Saint Mary of Rocasels; the church of Saint Severus of Veyran; the church of Saint Andrew of Becses; whatever you possess in the church of Caprilis; and in the church of Clairac. Thus you and your successors, when appointing canons or priests in those churches, shall at all times have authority to do so; while he and his successors shall receive in them episcopal reverence, the synods due to them, and hospitality dues for the needs of the churches, according to canonical ordinances; and the churches shall always be free from every other exaction. [Col. 1544A]

Regarding the fourth portions which he retained in those churches, two modii of grain, measured according to the standard of Béziers, shall be paid every year without opposition by the church of Cassian to him and his successors. Therefore, that this settlement may stand firm and inviolate forever, we confirm it by apostolic authority and strengthen it by the document of this writing. Let no person whatsoever be permitted rashly to violate this page of our confirmation or oppose it. If anyone should presume to attempt this, let him incur the indignation of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul. [Col. 1544B]

Given at the Lateran, on the fifth day before the Ides of December.

### CLXVI. He commands archbishops and bishops to compel the serfs of the monastery of Saint Denis to render the services due from them. (Lateran, 11 December.)

[Doublet, *History of Saint-Denis*, p. 505.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to all venerable brethren, archbishops and bishops, to whom these letters shall come: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1544C] Among the other matters which trouble us in our care for the universal Church, this especially disturbs us: that monasteries known to flourish in religious observance and material wealth should suffer losses in either or both respects. It has come to the knowledge of our apostolic office that the monastery of Saint Denis, noble and very renowned in the kingdom of the Franks, suffers many and great losses through its serfs. For they hide themselves, it is said, in remote corners of the earth and utterly refuse to render the services due to that monastery.

Therefore, lest that monastery be further defrauded of its right through the malice and fraud of its serfs, we command your brotherhood by apostolic letters: should any persons be found in your parishes who are bound to the aforesaid monastery by the bond of serfdom, labour diligently, as the duty of your office requires, that they be wholly subject to the abbot and brethren of that monastery, and endeavour to render them the services due in the house of Saint Denis and every reverence. Otherwise, do not delay to bind them with the bond of excommunication. [Col. 1544D]

Given at the Lateran, on the third day before the Ides of December.

### CLXVII. He commands Godfrey, bishop of Langres, and Alan, bishop of Auxerre, under penalty of excommunication, to exhort Milo of Nugerio to restore to the monks of Reigny the copper found in their land. (Lateran, 13 December.)

[See Lebeuf, *Mémoires d’Auxerre*, II, Preliminary Matter, p. 267.]

### CLXVIII. He commands Hugh, chancellor of the king of the Franks, to reconcile the abbot of Compiègne to the king’s favour. (Lateran, 21 December.)

[Mansi, *Concilia*, XXI, 806.]

[Col. 1545A]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son HUGH, chancellor of the illustrious king of the Franks: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Having full confidence in your devotion and diligence, we confidently urge your prudence to carry into effect those matters which we most earnestly desire to see accomplished. As your discretion knows, the monastery of Compiègne, in which religious life has recently been instituted anew, is shaken by many stormy tempests and troubled by the attacks of wicked men. [Col. 1545B] Indeed, as has been reported to us, our beloved son, [lacuna] abbot of that place, is believed to have fallen from the favour of our dearest son Louis, king of the Franks, because of certain false accusations. We therefore direct your diligence by this present communication, so far as you are able, to restore the said abbot to the favour of our aforesaid son, and to endeavour to offer him and the church entrusted to him welcome and useful counsel.

Given at the Lateran, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of January.

### CLXIX. Papal admonition to the abbot and convent of Saint Vaast. (Lateran, 23 December.)

[Marten, *Amplissima Collectio*, I, 848.]

[Col. 1545C]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to MARTIN, abbot of Saint Vaast, and to the whole convent: greeting and apostolic blessing.

You who have left Egypt and seem now to have crossed the Red Sea dry-shod ought always to lift the eyes of your mind toward what lies ahead and long all the more diligently for the land of promise, the more persons you see remaining in Egypt drowned with Pharaoh and deprived, sooner than they suppose, of Egyptian delights. For those who desire to remain in Egypt beside the pots of meat are cheated of their desire, since in a moment they go down to hell, though they seem to abound in temporal goods and pleasures of the flesh. “I passed by, and behold, he was not”; for although the fool seems to stand firmly rooted, once the sentence of curse has been received, he immediately withers and is wholly removed from glory. [Col. 1545D]

But you, beloved sons in the Lord, who have abandoned even your own wills for the Lord’s sake, must by no means turn your minds to the works of the Egyptians, nor desire in heart to return to Egypt, where Pharaoh is served in mud and brick, from whom you seem separated by the habit of your bodies. For the quality of your garments and the works of charity which you perform seem to signify that you are making for the heavenly homeland, hastening toward it according to the rule set before you, and striving, by the Lord’s gift, to obtain the prize of the heavenly calling.

Yet because the enemy of the human race is accustomed to place stumbling-blocks beside the road for those running in the way of God’s commandments, you must take careful heed, sons, and act so that you endeavour to complete with prudence and foresight the course which you have begun, in order that you may attain the palm of eternal blessedness and be crowned with blessed Benedict in heavenly glory. [Col. 1546A] We, moreover, love with fatherly charity the church entrusted to you and your persons, as special sons of Saint Peter, and always desire to provide you with welcome assistance.

Given at the Lateran, on the tenth day before the Kalends of January.

### CLXX. He commends Hugh, archbishop of Dol, to E., count of Léon and his sons, the viscount of Lamvio, and the sons Iven Gueni and Iven Gualli. (Lateran, 27 December.)

[Marten, *Thesaurus Anecdotorum*, III, 900.]

[Col. 1546B]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the noble men E., count of Léon, and his sons; the viscount of Lamvio [variant: Lautino]; and the sons Iven Gueni and Iven Galli: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The diligence of your nobility ought to direct itself with pious consideration and carefully reflect on how it may increase the churches of God and ever enlarge them with freely bestowed benefits. Among all works of piety through which the prize of eternal blessedness is attained, nothing is more pleasing in the sight of the divine majesty than that one should love and uphold holy churches and strive to preserve their rights unimpaired [Col. 1546C] and whole.

Accordingly, we earnestly commend to your pious concern our venerable brother H., archbishop of Dol, whom we esteem as a prudent, suitable, and honourable man, very dear and acceptable to us, together with the church entrusted to his governance. We greatly ask, admonish, and exhort you in the Lord, and enjoin it upon you for the remission of sins, that you love both him and his church with sincere charity and endeavour to support them in their rightful claims. Moreover, strive to show our aforesaid brother the archbishop, with devout heart and humble will, that honour and devotion which your predecessors were accustomed to render to the archbishop of Dol, so that you may appear in every respect heirs of your forefathers’ virtue. [Col. 1546D] Following the example of your predecessors, furnish him counsel and assistance in his necessities, and ensure that our aforesaid brother holds intact the goods of the church of Dol which lie in your land, and thereafter possesses them quietly and peacefully.

Given at the Lateran, on the sixth day before the Kalends of January.

## Year 1157–1158

### CLXXI. He informs P[eter], bishop, and the canons of Marseilles that he has ordered Pons, archbishop of Aix, to judge between them and the monks of Saint Victor. (Lateran, 30 March.)

[*The Antiquity of the Church of Marseilles*, I, 476.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable [Col. 1547A] brother P., bishop, and to his beloved sons, the canons of the church of Marseilles: greeting, etc. [lacuna]

[lacuna] the case disputed between you and our beloved sons, the brethren of the monastery of Marseilles, concerning the violent removal of a certain body, we commit for hearing to our venerable brother Pons, archbishop of Aix. Therefore we command you by these present letters that, when you have been summoned by the same our brother the archbishop on this account, you appear before him and firmly accept and observe whatever he shall judge between you.

Given at the Lateran, on the third day before the Kalends of April.

### CLXXII. To the canons of Saint Eusebius at Auxerre: concerning confirmation of the grant of the first year’s income of prebends of the cathedral church of Auxerre. (Lateran, 1 June.)

[Marten, *Anecdota*, I, 440.]

[Col. 1547B]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the canons of Saint Eusebius: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Whenever our confirmation is sought by religious men concerning things which they possess justly and lawfully, it is fitting that we grant it willingly and provide appropriate support for the petitioners’ desires, so that the more secure they are from disturbance by others and the more peacefully they possess their goods, the more diligently they may apply themselves to their religious profession and the more earnestly devote themselves to divine offices.

Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your peace and tranquillity, and we confirm by apostolic authority to you, and through you to your church, the benefice of prebends which our venerable brother Alan, bishop of Auxerre, granted to your church and confirmed by the document of his own writing, in accordance with his canonical grant; and we strengthen it by the protection of this present writing. [Col. 1547C] Let no person whatsoever therefore be permitted to violate this page of our confirmation or oppose it in any manner. If anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he shall incur the indignation of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, on the Kalends of June.

### CLXXIII. To N., dean, and the chapter of Soissons: concerning the liberties and customs of the church of Soissons. (Lateran, 1 June.)

[Marten, *Amplissima Collectio*, II, 646.]

[Col. 1547D]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons N., dean, and the whole chapter of Soissons: greeting and apostolic blessing.

By virtue of the office of supreme pontiff entrusted to us by God, it is incumbent upon our care to attend to the interests of churches and provide for their liberties, so that they may remain secure from the harassment of wrongdoers and rejoice that provision has been made for them by our favour. Therefore, desiring to provide beneficially for you and your church, we confirm by apostolic authority to your devotion and to that church the customs and liberties which you are known hitherto to have possessed in the bishopric—namely, the right, without consulting the bishop, to lay your malefactors or their lands under interdict and to absolve them—and strengthen them by the protection of this present writing. We add that whenever your church has ceased from divine offices because of an injury inflicted upon it, the other churches, in accordance with the custom which you are known to have possessed, shall cease from them at your chapter’s command. [Col. 1548A]

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may violate this page of our confirmation or oppose it in any way. If anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he shall incur the indignation of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, on the Kalends of June.

## Year 1158

[Col. 1548B]

### CLXXIV. He receives the church of Saint Mary of Utrecht under protection and confirms its possessions. (Lateran, 3 January.)

[Miraeus, *Opera Diplomatica*, IV, 22.]

### CLXXV. He receives the church of Ferrara under protection and confirms the possessions of its canons. (Rome, at Saint Peter’s, 10 January.)

[Ughelli, *Italia Sacra*, II, 536.]

ADRIAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the beloved sons, the canons of the church of Ferrara, present [Col. 1548C] … etc.

The authority of our office admonishes and invites us to take thought for the condition of churches and, with the Lord’s help, to make salutary provision for their peace and tranquillity. For it is recognized as worthy and consonant with propriety that we, who have been appointed to govern churches, should protect them from the malice of wicked persons and fortify them by the patronage of blessed Peter and of the Apostolic See. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the aforesaid Church of Ferrara, in which you are devoted to divine service; and we strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions, [Col. 1548D] whatever goods, the same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future, with God’s favour, acquire by grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: namely, the estate called Quartisana; the holding opposite the Po; the place Curcula; Caput Redae; the estate called Baniolum; the holding Dundorgum; the estate called Quartiatica; the holding Pecorile; the estate called Fossanova; the chapel of St Mark situated there; the fishery-water called Morticiacum; the church of St Michael with its appurtenances; the chapel of St Stephen with its appurtenances; within the borough of Ferrara, [Col. 1549A] the chapels of St Peter and of the Saviour, situated in the castle of the same Ferrara, with all their appurtenances; the chapel of St Mary Magdalene and St Vitus, which is in the market of Ferrara; the chapels of St Leonard; the whole *Corrigium stadii*; one half of Greater and Lesser Lendenaria; Cocolaria, the fishery-pond (*lama piscatoria*) of Zamedella; a *mansus* at the head of the common *lama*; one half of the holding Gallinarium; one half of the holding Purpurana; the harbour of Caput Redae; likewise the land which belonged to Ajacha, situated in the valley called Zucula; one *mansus* in the holding called Duce; moreover, one half of all property, movable and immovable alike, left for the souls of the faithful departed to the church of St George in the bishopric of Ferrara; one half of the tithe of that same church of St George; the entire tithe of the whole estate called Cocomarium; and all other things which justly belong to the same church—lands, vineyards, meadows, cultivated and uncultivated fields, waters, fisheries, hunting rights, and mills; male and female serfs; and twelve men of that place, who shall carry you by boat wherever your need may require, without any payment.
