LII.—He commands [Godfrey] of Langres, [Henry] of Autun, [Geoffrey] of Nevers, and [Alan] of Auxerre to excommunicate the count of Nevers unless, after being warned, he repairs within thirty days the damage inflicted upon the monastery of Vézelay. 1423  
LIII.—He commands the bishops of Gaul to excommunicate the burgesses of Vézelay, unless they make satisfaction to the monastery for the injuries inflicted, and to punish them with various penalties. 1424  
LIV.—He urges Louis, king of the Franks, to pursue the burgesses of Vézelay by force of arms, so that they may submit to the abbot as their lord. 1425  
LV.—Privilege for the monastery of Cluny. 1426  
LVI.—He commends the monastery of St. Antimo to Arnold, archbishop of Cologne, Henry, bishop of Constance, and Wibald, abbot of Stavelot. 1427  
LVII.—He commands a certain archbishop, Eberhard, bishop of Bamberg, and Wilbald, abbot of Corbie, to commend the monastery of Farfa to Frederick, king of the Romans. 1427  
LVIII.—He commends his envoys to the emperor to Wilbald, abbot of Stavelot. 1428  
LIX.—He takes the monastery of St. Mary of the Prison under protection and confirms its property. 1428  
LX.—He takes under protection the monastery of Hardehausen, founded by Beruhard, bishop of Paderborn, and confirms its property. 1429  
LXI.—To Henry, bishop of Beauvais.—Concerning money to be restored to a certain person. 1430  
LXII.—Privilege for the church of Trier. 1431  
LXIII.—He entrusts to Wichmann, archbishop of Magdeburg, the settlement of the dispute concerning tithes between the bishop of Osnabrück and Abbot Wibald. 1432  
LXIV.—He takes the monastery of Heidenheim under protection and confirms its discipline and possessions. 1432  
LXV.—Privilege for Hillin, archbishop of Trier. 1433  
LXVI.—He subjects the monastery of Werben to Wibald, abbot of Corbie, and his successors. 1434  
LXVII.—He commands Arnold, archbishop of Mainz, to protect the monastery of Werben against the injuries of Count Robbo. 1434  
LXVIII.—He grants to Rainerius, bishop of Siena, an estate on Mount Bonizi for building a church, subject to an annual rent. 1435  
LXIX.—He grants certain privileges to the monks of St. Bertin of Sithiu. 1436  
LXX.—He takes the monastery of St. Michael of Pisa under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. 1436  
LXXI.—He announces to [Stephen], bishop of Metz, Henry, bishop of Toul, and A[lbert], bishop of Verdun, that Hillin, archbishop of Trier, has been appointed legate of the Apostolic See throughout the German kingdom. 1438  
LXXII.—To the abbots and brethren of Vézelay. 1438  
LXXIII.—To the archbishop of Tours.—That he make an amicable settlement with the bishop of Dol. 1439  
LXXIV.—To all clerics and laypeople established throughout the province of Dol.—He confirms the sentence pronounced by Archbishop Hugh against evildoers and occupiers of ecclesiastical property. 1439  
LXXV.—He commands Baldwin, king of Jerusalem, to order the restoration to the citizens of Genoa both of money and of a ship seized by his men. 1440  

## About the Year 1155

LXXVI.—To Henry II, king of England.—He grants a privilege to occupy Ireland. 1441  
LXXVII.—To the monks of Corbigny, concerning the reform of the monastery. 1442  

## In the Year 1156

LXXVIII.—For St. Mary of Frasinaia and St. Peter of Pompeniano. 1443  
[Col. 1694] LXXIX.—He commands Silvester, abbot of St. Augustine’s, Canterbury, to make profession to Archbishop Theobald. 1443  
LXXX.—To the archbishop of Braga.—That he obey the primate of Toledo. 1444  
LXXXI.—He commends Theobald, bishop, C., dean, and the whole chapter of the Church of Paris for having granted to Hugh, the chancellor, the income of a prebend in the Church of Paris. 1445  
LXXXII.—At the request of Bishop John, he confirms the privileges of the church of Olivolo, or Castello, in Venetian territory. 1445  
LXXXIII.—He assures to John, archbishop of Toledo, the primacy of the Spains. 1447  
LXXXIV.—Privilege for the convent of the Paraclete. 1448  
LXXXV.—To Hillin, archbishop of Trier. 1448  
LXXXVI.—He assures to John, archbishop of Toledo, the parish of Alcalá, the primacy of Spain, and the use of the pallium. 1449  
LXXXVII.—He commands John, archbishop of Toledo, to investigate the crimes of the bishop of Pamplona. 1451  
LXXXVIII.—He commands Nigel, bishop of Ely, under penalty of suspension, “that within three months of receiving the letter he shall by no means delay restoring to the condition in which they were when he assumed the governance of the church of Ely those possessions of the church which, contrary to the promise made at his consecration, he is known to have alienated and disposed of.” He also states this in another brief issued to the monks who had complained against him. But when Nigel pleaded the king’s absence, alleging that the king’s presence was necessary for making the restitution, the pope stated in other letters, issued to Theobald, archbishop of Canterbury, at the Lateran on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of April, that he had thought it proper to grant him a postponement for doing this until the next feast of St. Lucy (“I believe that *until the next feast* should be read”). In the meantime, however, he relaxes the sentence of suspension “which,” he says, “we pronounced against him.” 1452  
LXXXIX.—To the leaders of the Roman fraternity.—Arnold, the heresiarch, in the time of Eugenius III, besides other abominable acts which he had ventured against the Roman Church, strove to detach from them the clerics subject to the cardinals. Therefore, to remove this diabolical invention, which had gained strength, Pope Adrian decrees that chaplains shall promise obedience to the heads of the titular churches. 1452  
XC.—He takes the church of Tortosa under the protection of the Apostolic See and confirms its statutes and possessions. 1453  
XCI.—To Hugh, archbishop of Sens, and Henry, bishop of Beauvais.—Concerning the church of Ferrara and certain peasants. 1455  
XCII.—Concerning confirmation of the judgments which King Louis pronounced against Odo, duke of Burgundy. 1456  
XCIII.—He takes the monastery of St. Stephen of Dijon under protection and confirms its possessions. 1456  
XCIV.—He confirms the privileges of the monastery of St. Lambert of Liège. 1461  
XCV.—He commends to the canons of the church of Pisa his chaplain R., concerning the cutting of stones and small columns for use by the canons of the church of St. Rufus in constructing their monastery. 1461  
XCVI.—He takes the monastery of St. Paternianus of Fano under protection and confirms its possessions. 1461  
XCVII.—He takes the monastery of Steingaden under protection and confirms its property. 1463  
XCVIII.—He takes the monastery of St. Afra of Augsburg under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. 1465  
XCIX.—To the clergy of Augsburg.—He declares that Conrad, bishop of Augsburg, is innocent, and condemns his accusers to a severe penalty. 1466  
C.—He takes the church of St. Vincent of Bergamo under protection and confirms its property. 1466  
CI.—He confirms Eugenius III’s judgment concerning the dispute between the canons of St. Alexander and St. Vincent of Bergamo. 1468  
CII.—He confirms the peace made with King William of Sicily through envoys. 1470  
CIII.—He commands the bishops of Agrigento, Mazara, and Malta—constituted suffragans of the Church of Palermo—to obey Archbishop Hugh. 1471  
CIV.—He takes the monastery of Huysburg under protection and confirms its property. 1471  
[Col. 1695] CV.—He informs all the clergy and people of Mainz that he has kindly received Archbishop Arnold, “who came before the Apostolic See out of devotion,” and that he has “released his person, together with his entire bishopric and his suffragan bishops, from the jurisdiction of the legation of Hillin, archbishop of Trier, legate of the Apostolic See”; he commends Arnold. 1471  
CVI.—He takes the church of Bagnoregio under protection and confirms its property and rights. 1472  
CVII.—He receives the church of Mende and all its estates under the protection of the Apostolic See. 1475  
CVIII.—At the request of Peter, abbot of Cluny, he commands S[tephen], archbishop of Vienne, and C. [Heraclius], archbishop of Lyons, not to permit the monastery of Sauxillanges to be harassed by Eustace. 1477  
CIX.—He takes the church of St. Constantius of Orvieto under protection and confirms its property and privileges. 1477  
CX.—He takes the church of Belluno under protection and confirms the property and rights of its canons. 1478  
CXI.—He takes the church of Aix under protection and confirms the property and rights of its canons. 1480  
CXII.—He takes the church of St. Mary of Pineto under protection and confirms its property and rights. 1481  
CXIII.—Bull for the church of Nîmes. 1483  
CXIV.—He confirms the privileges and possessions of the monastery of St. Denis. 1485  
CXV.—He takes the monastery of St. Bavo of Ghent under protection and confirms its property. 1487  
CXVI.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Peter of Aldenburg. 1488  
CXVII.—He confirms the election of Archbishop Berengar. 1489  
CXVIII.—He assures to the hospital house of Canterbury the church of Northbourne, granted by Silvester, abbot of St. Augustine’s, for the relief of pilgrims and the poor. 1490  

## In the Years 1154–1157

CXIX.—At the request of Theobald, bishop of Paris, he confirms the agreement made between Stephen, Theobald’s predecessor, and Theobald the archdeacon. 1490  
CXX.—He settles the dispute between Lanfranc, bishop of Lodi, and Berard, abbot of the monastery of St. Sixtus of Piacenza, over the church of St. Michael at Castronovo. 1490  

## In the Year 1157

CXXI.—He commands Silvester, abbot of St. Augustine’s, Canterbury, to render obedience to Archbishop Theobald within thirty days. 1491  
CXXII.—He grants the convent of St. Mary of Caramagna to Anselm, bishop of Asti. 1491  
CXXIII.—To Wibald, abbot of Stavelot.—That he urge the emperor to remain in reverence for the Apostolic See. 1492  
CXXIV.—He takes the Venetian convent of St. Zacharias under protection. 1493  
CXXV.—He takes the monastery of the Scottish monks of St. James at Regensburg under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges, imposing on the monks an annual payment of one Byzantine coin. 1494  
CXXVI.—He takes the monastery of St. Vitalis of Ravenna under protection and confirms its property. 1495  
CXXVII.—He takes the church of St. Peter of Guastalla under protection and confirms its property and rights. 1497  
CXXVIII.—Privilege for the monastery of Canossa in the district of Reggio. 1498  
CXXIX.—Privilege for the monastery of St. Mary of Pontigny. 1500  
CXXX.—He takes the convent of St. Mary of Charlieu under protection and confirms its property. 1501  
CXXXI.—He takes the church of Geneva under protection and confirms the peace made between Bishop Ardutius and Count Amadeus of Geneva. 1503  
CXXXII.—He assures to the church of Geneva the property bestowed by Emperor Frederick. 1507  
CXXXIII.—Privilege for the convent of Remiremont. 1508  
CXXXIV.—He takes the monastery of St. Blaise in the Black Forest under protection and confirms its property and rights. 1510  
CXXXV.—He assures to the monastery of St. Blaise the churches of Bürgeln, Eggenheim, and Koltenbach. 1514  
CXXXVI.—He takes the monastery of Engelberg under protection and confirms its possessions and rights, imposing upon the monks an annual payment of one gold coin. 1514  
CXXXVII.—To Henry, patriarch of Grado.—He confirms his patriarchal dignity and primacy over the archbishop of Zadar. 1516  
CXXXVIII.—To the same.—That he may appoint and consecrate bishops at Constantinople and in other cities of the Empire of Constantinople, where the Venetians possess several churches. 1519  
CXXXIX.—He commends Henry, patriarch of Grado, to the bishops, duke, and people of Venice. [Col. 1696] He reports that obedience has been promised him by the archbishop of Zadar. 1520  
CXL.—He assures to Rodulph, Camaldolese prior, and his successors the monastery of Pratalia, donated by Jerome, bishop of Arezzo. 1521  
CXLI.—Privilege for the church of Ravello. 1522  
CXLII.—Privilege for the church of Benevento. 1523  
CXLIII.—He reproaches Frederick, emperor of the Romans, because, disregarding his admonitions, he has still allowed the sacrilegious arrest of Eskil, archbishop of Lund, to go unpunished. He recalls that the imperial crown was bestowed upon Frederick by himself, etc. 1525  
CXLIV.—He confirms the possessions of the hospital of St. Blaise near Monza. 1527  
CXLV.—He confirms all the rights and property of the Milanese monastery of St. Denis. 1527  
CXLVI.—Privilege for the convent of the Holy Spirit of the Paraclete. 1529  
CXLVII.—He takes the church of St. Rupert of Salzburg under protection and confirms its property and rights. 1529  
CXLVIII.—He complains to the archbishops and bishops of Germany of injuries inflicted by Emperor Frederick on his envoys. He commands them to strive that the emperor make satisfaction through Chancellor Rainald. 1531  
CXLIX.—He grants certain benefice holdings to Aldebrandinus and Bernardinus, sons of Count Ubolinus of Calmaiare. 1532  
CL.—He forbids the canons of Calvimont from alienating church property; for it had long since been decreed that brethren of the monastery of St. Denis should be established in their church. 1533  
CLI.—He commends a certain D. to Henry, bishop of Beauvais. 1534  

## In the Years 1156–1158

CLII.—He urges Raymond, bishop of Maguelonne, not to “dispose at his own discretion of the property of the church assigned for the common use of the clerics, and to restore to the canons the tithe of Montpellier.” 1534  
CLIII.—He commends Ansold, abbot of Compiègne, to Henry, bishop of Beauvais. 1535  
CLIV.—He commands Godescalc, bishop of Arras, to restore to Hugh the chancellor the abbots’ altar of Aslues. 1535  
CLV.—He urges Theobald, bishop of Paris, to grant Hugh the chancellor the first personate (personal benefice) or dignity which falls vacant in the Church of Paris. 1536  
CLVI.—He prescribes to the nobleman William and all the people of Montpellier that, when five years have elapsed, they return the altar of St. Saviour and the offerings into the hands of the prior of the church of Blessed Mary. 1536  
CLVII.—To the archbishop of Reims and his suffragans.—Concerning the church of Jerusalem and the Knights Templar. 1537  
CLVIII.—He commands the abbots of the diocese of Béziers to obey the bishop of Béziers. 1538  
CLIX.—Privilege for the convent of the Holy Spirit of the Paraclete. 1539  
CLX.—To Henry, bishop of Beauvais.—That he continue to discharge the episcopal office, with no doubt interposed. 1539  
CLXI.—To the same.—Concerning the church of St. Lucian. 1540  
CLXII.—To the same.—Concerning the nephews of a certain canon of Auxerre. 1541  
CLXIII.—To the same.—Concerning a certain canon of the church of Auxerre. 1541  
CLXIV.—To Berengar, archbishop, and the clergy of Narbonne.—Concerning not seizing the property of deceased bishops. 1542  
CLXV.—He confirms the agreement made between the bishop of Béziers and the prior of Cassan. 1543  
CLXVI.—He commands the archbishops and bishops to compel the servants of the monastery of St. Denis to render the services owed to it. 1544  
CLXVII.—He commands Godfrey, bishop of Langres, and Alan, bishop of Auxerre, under penalty of excommunication, to urge Milo of Noyers to restore to the monks of Régnier the copper found on their land. 1544  
CLXVIII.—He commands Hugh, chancellor of the king of the Franks, to reconcile the abbot of Compiègne to the king’s favor. 1545  
CLXIX.—A papal admonition to the abbot and convent of St. Vedast. 1545  
CLXX.—He commends Hugh, archbishop of Dol, to E., count of Léon, and his son; to the viscount of Lamvio and his son; and to Iven Gueni and Iven Gualli. 1543  

[Col. 1697]

## In the Years 1157–1158

CLXXI.—He informs the bishop and canons of Marseille that he has commanded Pons, archbishop of Aix, to render judgment between them and the monks of St. Victor. 1546  
CLXXII.—To the canons of St. Eusebius at Auxerre.—Concerning confirmation of the gift of the first year’s income from the prebends of the cathedral church of Auxerre. 1547  
CLXXIII.—To N., dean, and the chapter of Soissons.—Concerning the liberty and customs of the church of Soissons. 1547  

## In the Year 1158

CLXXIV.—He takes the church of St. Mary of Utrecht under protection and confirms its possessions. 1548  
CLXXV.—He takes the church of Ferrara under protection and confirms the possessions of its canons. 1548  
CLXXVI.—He takes the hospital house of Mercy at Piacenza under protection. 1550  
CLXXVII.—At the request of Henry, duke of Bavaria and Saxony, he takes the church of Ratzeburg under protection and confirms its possessions and rights. 1550  
CLXXVIII.—He takes the church of St. Mary of Gariberto at Piacenza under protection. 1552  
CLXXIX.—He commands the provost and all the clergy of the church of Piacenza to return to canonical discipline and to obey Bishop Hugh. 1553  
CLXXX.—At the request of Henry, duke of Bavaria and Saxony, he takes the monastery of Blessed Pancras of Ranshofen under protection and confirms its property and rights. 1554  
CLXXXI.—He addresses Emperor Frederick in sufficiently mild terms. He explains certain passages of his earlier letter (see above, no. CXLIII). He commends his envoys, sent “at the urging of Henry, duke of Bavaria and Saxony.” 1556  
CLXXXII.—He confirms the possessions and rights assigned for the maintenance of the canons of the church of Blessed Peter at Rome: the churches of SS. John and Paul, St. Martin, St. Stephen Major, and St. Stephen Minor. 1557  
CLXXXIII.—He assures to Archbishop Hugh, Dean William of Vienne, and their successors the privileges granted by King Frederick I. 1562  
CLXXXIV.—He assures to Archbishop Hugh, Dean William of Vienne, and their successors the privileges granted by King Frederick I. 1562  
CLXXXV.—He takes the church of St. Samson of Orléans under protection and confirms its property. 1564  
CLXXXVI.—He takes the convent of Visbeck under protection and confirms its property and privileges. 1565  
CLXXXVII.—Privilege for the monastery of SS. Nazarius and Celsus at Verona. 1567  
CLXXXVIII.—He confirms the property, possessions, and privileges of the church of St. John of Selbode. 1568  
CLXXXIX.—To the archbishops of Tarragona and Narbonne.—He receives Raymond, count of Barcelona, and his dominions under the protection of the Apostolic See. 1570  
CXC.—He takes the church of St. Marcellus of Paris under protection and confirms its property and rights. 1571  
CXCI.—Having settled the dispute between the canons and the bishop of Sutri concerning the church of St. Sylvester, he makes their agreement perpetual by issuing a charter. 1573  
CXCII.—He takes the church of St. Mary of Aachen under protection and confirms its possessions. 1574  
CXCIII.—He assures to Master Adam the mastership of the schools of the church of Meaux, granted by Bishop Manasses of good memory. 1574  
CXCIV.—To Hugh, chancellor of the king of the Franks.—He rejoices that Hugh has rendered useful service in securing peace between the kings of the Franks and the English. 1575  
CXCV.—He urges Prior Gregory and the whole Camaldolese chapter toward virtue and peace. 1576  
CXCVI.—Privilege granted to Hugh, bishop of Piacenza. 1578  
CXCVII.—He does not comply with Emperor Frederick’s request that Guido, subdeacon of the Roman Church, be placed over the church of Ravenna. 1579  

## In the Years 1154–1159

CXCVIII.—He writes to the archbishop of Thessalonica concerning reconciliation of the Greek Church with the Roman Church. He commends Baldwin and Balditzion, couriers sent to Emperor Manuel. 1580  
CXCIX.—He urges the consuls and all the people of Châteauneuf-Grasse to defend the monks of Lérins against Saracens and other enemies. 1581  
CC.—To Louis, king of the Franks.—He commends his exceptional affection toward religious men, which he asks that the Premonstratensian brethren may experience for the reverence of Blessed Peter and of himself. 1582  
CCI.—To Berengar, archbishop of Narbonne, [Col. 1698] Artald, bishop of Elne, and the barons established throughout the bishopric of Elne.—Against Geoffrey, count of Roussillon. 1582  
CCII.—To Walter, bishop of Laon.—That he preserve the benefices of the Church of Prémontré bestowed by his predecessors, and neither inflict nor permit to be inflicted any harassment concerning those benefices. 1583  
CCIII.—To the same.—On the same subject. 1584  
CCIV.—He confirms the property and privileges of the church of St. John in the Vineyards. 1585  
CCV.—To the monks of Pontida.—That they pay the tithes of a certain place. 1586  
CCVI.—He commands Stephen, bishop of Metz, and the bishop of Verdun to declare Matthew, duke of Lorraine, excommunicated. 1587  
CCVII.—He replies to Eberhard, archbishop of Salzburg, that marriages of serfs contracted without their lords’ consent are not to be dissolved. 1587  
CCVIII.—At the request of Bishop Henry, he takes the church of Liège under protection and confirms its possessions. 1587  
CCIX.—He confirms the privileges of the church of St. Omer. 1589  
CCX.—He takes the monastery of St. Michael in Peril of the Sea under protection and confirms its property. 1589  

## In the Years 1155–1159

CCXI.—Privilege granted to Marchward, abbot of Fulda. 1591  
CCXII.—To Hugh, archbishop of Rouen.—Concerning the case of Peter and his mother. 1592  
CCXIII.—He thanks Louis, king of the Franks, for protecting Pons, abbot of Vézelay. He urges him to continue defending the monastery against the count of Nevers and to order the stone houses of the burgesses of Vézelay demolished. 1592  

## In the Years 1157–1159

CCXIV.—He exhorts Abbot Odo and the monks of St. Denis to follow in the footsteps of St. Benedict. 1593  
CCXV.—He confirms to Hugh, chancellor of the king of the Franks, the archdeaconry of Arras. 1593  
CCXVI.—He confirms the privileges of the monastery of St. Denis granted by Kings Robert and Dagobert. 1594  
CCXVII.—To B., Baldwin, bishop of Noyon, and Henry, bishop of Beauvais.—Concerning the cantor of the church of Péronne. 1595  
CCXVIII.—He confirms certain property of the church of St. Ursus of Augsburg. 1596  
CCXIX.—To Henry, bishop of Beauvais.—Concerning Master Nicholas. 1596  
CCXX.—To the archbishop of Reims.—Concerning the same person. 1597  
CCXXI.—To the archbishop of Reims and the bishop of Laon.—Concerning the son of Ramaldus Cottela. 1597  
CCXXII.—To Henry, bishop of Beauvais.—Concerning the cantor of the church of Soissons, that what was taken from him be restored. 1598  
CCXXIII.—He asks Albert, abbot of Nonantola, to grant anew a certain precarial holding to Lot. and Turcl., noblemen. 1598  
CCXXIV.—He confirms the agreement made concerning the subjection of Valmagne to the monastery of Bonnevaux. 1599  
CCXXV.—To the bishops of Saint-Brieuc and Tréguier.—That they prevent their priests from celebrating divine offices against the will of the archbishop of Dol. 1600  
CCXVI.—He commands Eberhard, archbishop of Salzburg, and (Hartwig), bishop of Regensburg, to restore to Abbot Conrad the monastery which he had relinquished because of injuries done by the brethren, and to punish the monks. 1601  
CCXXVII.—He commands the monks of Biburg to obey Abbot Conrad. 1601  
CCXXVIII.—He commands Henry, bishop of Autun, to grant the abbot of Tournus investiture of the church of Petraficta within twenty days. 1602  
CCXXIX.—To the archbishop of Narbonne and his suffragans.—That they defend William, lord of Montpellier, together with his honors and those of his brother, who was journeying on pilgrimage to Jerusalem, against attacks by the wicked, with a sentence of excommunication threatened. 1603  
CCXXX.—To the canons of Holy Cross at Orléans.—He rebukes them because they did not grant Hugh the chancellor the full income of his prebend during his absence. He orders them to do so in the future and to restore what has been withheld. 1603  
CCXXXI.—To Hugh, chancellor of France.—He absolves him from the oath and unlawful condition by which the bishop of Arras had bound him when granting the archdeaconry. 1604  
CCXXXII.—To Godescalc, bishop of Arras.—He informs him that Hugh the chancellor’s oath has been dissolved. 1604  
[Col. 1699] CCXXXIII.—To Samson, archbishop of Reims.—That he restore to Hugh the chancellor the altar which he had taken from him. 1605  
CCXXXIV.—He informs Godescalc, bishop of Arras, concerning the preceding letter. 1606  
CCXXXV.—He commands the dean, cantor, and whole chapter of Paris to grant to Hugh, chancellor of the king of the Franks, the provostship when it becomes vacant in the Church of Paris. 1606  
CCXXXVI.—To the archdeacons of the church of Trier. 1607  
CCXXXVII.—To the clergy and people of Murmirel.—That they obey Hugh, archbishop of Dol. 1607  

## In the Year 1159

CCXXXVIII.—Privilege for the monastery of the Holy Trinity of Monte Sacro. 1608  
CCXXXIX.—He takes the collegiate church of St. Stephen in the city of Constance into the special protection of the Apostolic See. 1611  
CCXL.—Bull confirming the rights and possessions of the abbey of St. Augustine at Limoges. 1613  
CCXLI.—He commends the plan of Louis, king of the Franks, who was considering “hastening into Spain together with Henry, king of England, to subdue the barbarism of the pagans.” Yet he discourages excessive haste and urges him “first to examine and consider the need of that land through the princes of that kingdom; carefully to ascertain the will both of that Church and of the princes and people; and to receive counsel from them as is fitting.” “For,” he says, “the highness of your serenity ought to recall how, when both Conrad, formerly king of the Romans, and you yourself undertook the journey to Jerusalem rather incautiously, without consulting the people of the land, you did not obtain the hoped-for fruit.” Accordingly, he postpones the apostolic exhortation requested by the people through (Rotrou), bishop of Évreux, but takes that kingdom under his protection. 1615  
CCXLII.—Privilege for the Church of Hamburg. 1617  
CCXLIII.—Privilege for the monastery of Jerichow. 1618  
CCXLIV.—To William, bishop of Le Mans.—He entrusts to him for settlement the dispute, long contested between the Cluniac monks and the canons of Périgueux, concerning the church of Roche-Boviscurt. 1619  
CCXLV.—To the monks of Roche-Boviscurt.—He informs them that their case with the canons of Périgueux has been entrusted to the judgment of the bishop of Le Mans for settlement. 1620  
CCXLVI.—He confirms the possessions of the abbey of St. Magloire at Paris. 1621  
CCXLVII.—He takes the monastery of the Valley of St. Mary under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. 1623  
CCXLVIII.—To H., bishop-elect, and the chapter of the church of Soissons.—Concerning Vitto, dean of Soissons. 1625  
CCXLIX.—He takes the monastery of St. Clement of Piscaria under protection and confirms its property and privileges. 1625  
CCL.—He receives the monastery of Muri with its appurtenances into apostolic protection and confirms its property and rights. 1626  
CCLI.—He takes the monastery of Prüfening under protection and confirms its property and rights. 1628  
CCLII.—He takes the monastery of St. John of Blaubeuren under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. 1629  
CCLIII.—He takes the church of St. Opportuna at Paris under protection and confirms its property. 1630  
CCLIII *bis*.—He confirms the agreement made between Hugh, abbot of Prémontré, and Walter, bishop of Laon. 1632  
CCLIV.—To Emperor Frederick.—Concerning the twofold injury inflicted by him upon the Apostolic See. 1635  
CCLV.—He takes the church of Utrecht under protection and confirms its property. 1636  
CCLVI.—He takes the church of St. Mary of Ressens under protection and confirms its property. 1637  
[Col. 1700] CCLVII.—He takes the monastery of Reichersberg under protection and confirms its property. 1639  
CCLVIII.—1640

## John Cirita, Abbot of Tarouca in Spain
Life of John Cirita. 1661

CHAPTER I.—Despising the honours of this world and bidding farewell to temporal military service, he embraces the eremitical life. 1661

CHAPTER II.—He is tempted by a demon in the form of a woman, triumphs marvellously, is appointed abbot over anchorites, and shines with a prophetic spirit. 1662

CHAPTER III.—St John the Baptist appears to our Father Bernard and commands him to send monks into Spain to build a monastery; Blessed John Cirita, forewarned by divine revelation, meets them as they arrive on their journey. 1663

CHAPTER IV.—The monks build the monastery of St John of Tarouca at a place divinely indicated to them by heavenly splendour. 1665

CHAPTER V.—How Blessed John Cirita became a Cistercian monk; and concerning Queen Theresa, who assumed the habit of our Order. 1666

CHAPTER VI.—On the origin of the Order of Avis, which serves under the Cistercian institution and receives its laws and rule from Blessed John Cirita. 1667

CHAPTER VII.—Blessed John Cirita, renowned for a prophetic spirit and various virtues, departs this life and is distinguished by various miracles after death. 1668

Rule of the military Order of Avis. 1669

Form of the oath which the master of the Order of Avis must make. 1671

## Appendix to John Cirita

I.—The Cistercian Order of St Michael in Lusitania is established by King Alfonso under the correction and governance of the abbot of Alcobaça. 1671

II.—Charter granted by Alfonso, king of Lusitania, to the monastery of St John after the Saracens had been driven out in 1122 near the river Távora. 1675
